Nurses described CKRT as a form of technology-embedded relational care requiring simultaneous machine vigilance, humanistic presence, moral judgement, family support, and interprofessional advocacy. CONCLUSIONS: Managing patients receiving CKRT in ICUs requires more than technical competence. It involves emotionally intense, morally complex, and relationally significant nursing work. Structured CKRT education, simulation-based training, advocacy preparation, routine debriefing, psychological support, and staffing models that reflect CKRT workload are needed to sustain safe and person-centred critical kidney care. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.
articles.ai_summary: This qualitative study explored the experiences of critical care nurses managing patients receiving continuous kidney replacement therapy in Saudi Arabian ICUs. Nurses described the complex and emotionally demanding nature of this care, requiring technical, relational, and moral competencies. Four themes emerged from the analysis, highlighting the need for structured education and support.
articles.ai_significance: This study highlights the importance of considering the emotional and relational aspects of critical care, particularly in managing patients receiving CKRT, and underscores the need for structured education and support for critical care nurses.

articles.title: Use of Cytomegalovirus Immunoglobulin with Antiviral Therapy for Cytomegalovirus Infection in Transplant Recipients: A Tertiary Care Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract: UNLABELLED: Background Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality in recipients of hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT), solid organ transplant (SOT), and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy. While antiviral agents remain the cornerstone of treatment, CMV-specific immunoglobulins (CMVIG) have been utilized as adjunct therapy with variable outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the virological response and tolerability of CMVIG in cases of severe or refractory CMV viremia, with or without CMV disease. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective case series of adult recipients of SOT, allogeneic HSCT, and/or CAR-T cell therapy who developed CMV viremia or disease and received at least one dose of CMVIG between May 2017 and May 2023 at our center. Virological improvement within 14 days of starting CMVIG and tolerability of CMVIG are the primary outcome of this study. RESULTS: A total of 33 patients were included. Of these, 29 underwent transplantation [SOT: 48.2%, HSCT: 51.7%], and five underwent CAR-T cell therapy (one post-HSCT). High-risk CMV serostatus was present in 12%. CMV viremia was documented in 32 patients (97%), and tissue-invasive disease was present in 11 patients (33.3%). Virological response, was observed in 65.6% of the cohort. The median time to undetectable CMV viral load following CMVIG initiation was 28 days. CMVIG was well-tolerated. All-cause mortality at 90 days remained high (57%). CONCLUSION: In this case series, CMVIG demonstrated a virological response rate of 65.6% in patients with severe or refractory CMV infection. While CMVIG was well-tolerated with minimal adverse events, the high mortality rate despite virological response suggests that CMVIG may be insufficient for this critically ill population. Our findings should be interpreted as observational data from a small case series, and prospective controlled trials are needed to establish the true benefit of CMVIG in combination with standard antiviral therapy.
articles.ai_key_stats: n=33, virological response 65.6%, median time to undetectable CMV viral load 28 days
articles.ai_summary: This study evaluated the effectiveness of cytomegalovirus immunoglobulin (CMVIG) in treating severe or refractory CMV infection in transplant recipients. The results showed that CMVIG was well-tolerated but had a limited virological response rate of 65.6%. The study also found a high mortality rate despite virological response.
articles.ai_significance: This study highlights the need for further research on the effectiveness of CMVIG in combination with standard antiviral therapy for treating CMV infection in critically ill transplant recipients.

articles.title: C-Reactive Protein-to-Albumin Ratio as a Prognostic Marker in ICU Patients with Pre-Existing Hypertension and Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Background/Objective: The C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) reflects both systemic inflammation and nutritional status and has been proposed as a prognostic marker in critical illness, yet its value in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with pre-existing hypertension is not well defined. Methods: This was a retrospective single-center study of 341 critically ill adults with pre-existing hypertension (June 2001-October 2012) from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III database. CAR was calculated from the first C-reactive protein (CRP) and albumin measurements after ICU admission. Using adjusted Cox proportional hazard models, we examined the association of CAR with 30-day mortality in the overall hypertensive cohort, across hypertension groups, and in patients with coexisting diabetes. Results: Non-survivors had higher CAR than survivors (35.5 vs. 18.1, p = 0.008). CAR showed moderate discriminative ability in the overall hypertensive cohort (AUC = 0.637, 95% CI: 0.543-0.732), with better discrimination in patients with normal/elevated blood pressure (BP) (AUC = 0.748, 95% CI: 0.637-0.858) and a relatively higher AUC in the subgroup with diabetes and normal/elevated BP (0.833, 95% CI: 0.671-0.995). In univariable Cox analysis, high CAR was associated with increased 30-day mortality in the overall hypertensive cohort (HR: 3.02, 95% CI: 1.48-6.17, p = 0.0024), in patients with normal/elevated BP (HR: 8.90, 95% CI: 2.00-39.17, p = 0.0038), and in patients with diabetes and normal/elevated BP (HR: 10.00, 95% CI: 1.20-83.10, p = 0.0331). These associations remained significant after multivariable adjustment in the overall hypertensive cohort (adjusted HR: 3.01, 95% CI: 1.45-6.21, p = 0.0030), in patients with normal/elevated BP (adjusted HR: 10.12, 95% CI: 2.20-46.59, p = 0.0030), and in patients with diabetes and normal/elevated BP (adjusted: HR: 19.41, 95% CI: 1.37-275.28, p = 0.0284). Conclusions: These results suggest that CAR measured early after ICU admission may serve as a practical tool for mortality risk stratification in ICU patients with pre-existing hypertension, particularly those with diabetes.
articles.ai_summary: Researchers studied the C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) as a prognostic marker in ICU patients with pre-existing hypertension and diabetes. They found that higher CAR levels were associated with increased 30-day mortality. CAR may be a useful tool for mortality risk stratification in these patients.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings suggest that CAR could help clinicians identify ICU patients with pre-existing hypertension and diabetes who are at higher risk of mortality, allowing for more targeted care.

articles.title: Critically Ill Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department; Outcome Review in a Tertiary Care Center.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Critically ill patients presenting to the emergency department require prompt recognition and prioritized care due to the severity of their conditions. Reviewing their clinical outcomes helps guide future planning and resource allocation. This study aims to highlight the outcomes of patients triaged as CTAS I and II in the emergency department of a tertiary care center in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted in the emergency department of a tertiary healthcare center, National Guard Health Affairs, in Jeddah. The study provides a comprehensive assessment of factors (including length of stay) and outcomes for a total of 505 critically ill patients (CTAS Levels I and II) who presented to the emergency department from January 2023 to December 2023. RESULTS: A total of 505 patients were included in this study, out of which 325 (64.4%) were males. The most reported co-morbidities were diabetes mellitus 169 (33.5%) and Hypertension 173 (34.3%). The majority of 435 patients (86.1%) were CTAS level 2, while 70 (13.9%) were CTAS 1. The mean ED length of stay was 5.5 hours.347 out of 505 patients required hospitalization (68.7%), and the mean of hospitalization by days was 13 (±23.5%). 8.5% of these patients died of which14.3%were CTAS 1, and 7.6% were CTAS2. CONCLUSION: As demonstrated above, most critical ED cases were comprised of males; this trend may be attributed to higher health risks among them. Furthermore, most critical ED visits were related to cardiac issues, with shortness of breath being the most reported symptom. The mortality rate for these ED patients was 8.5%. Additionally, the average length of stay (LOS) in ED was 5.5 hours. Other studies have demonstrated that this is associated with a lower mortality rate compared to others with longer LOS.

articles.title: Epidemiology, Antimicrobial Resistance, and Seasonal Dynamics of Respiratory Bacterial Pathogens in a Saudi Tertiary Care Hospital (2023-2025).
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly among hospitalized and critically ill patients. The increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) complicates treatment and highlights the need for local surveillance to guide antimicrobial stewardship. This study investigated the epidemiology, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and seasonal trends of respiratory bacterial pathogens in a tertiary care hospital in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted on 5582 respiratory specimens collected between January 2023 and December 2025. Samples included tracheal aspirates, sputum, bronchoalveolar lavage, throat swabs, pleural fluids, ear swabs, and nasal swabs. Bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed using the VITEK® 2 Compact system and interpreted according to CLSI M100-S35 guidelines. Statistical analyses included Chi-square tests and logistic regression. RESULTS: Culture positivity was 38.6% (2154/5582), with tracheal aspirates and sputum accounting for the most positive specimens. The predominant pathogens were Pseudomonas aeruginosa (31.9%), Klebsiella spp. (21.3%), Staphylococcus aureus (10.2%), Serratia marcescens (6.3%), Escherichia coli (5.7%) and Acinetobacter baumannii (5.5%). Culture positivity increased significantly with age (p<0.001), with Gram-negative bacteria predominating in older patients. MDROs were slightly prevalent, including, carbapenem-resistant organisms (22.9%) and ESBL producers (12.3%). The highest MDRO burden occurred in intensive care and other high-acuity wards. Seasonal analysis demonstrated a significant increase in MDRO prevalence during the summer months, with carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative pathogens rising from 18.2% in the winter to 28.7% in the summer (OR 1.82, 95% CI: 1.45-2.28; p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory pathogens in this Saudi tertiary care hospital exhibited a high prevalence of multidrug resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria and in critical care settings. Seasonal increases in resistance during the summer months suggest the need for intensified infection control measures, strengthened antimicrobial stewardship, and ongoing surveillance to reduce MDRO transmission and optimize patient outcomes.
articles.ai_summary: This study investigated respiratory bacterial pathogens in a Saudi hospital from 2023-2025. The most common pathogens were Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella spp. Multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) were prevalent, especially in critical care settings and during the summer months.
articles.ai_significance: This study highlights the need for intensified infection control measures and antimicrobial stewardship to reduce MDRO transmission and improve patient outcomes in critical care settings.

articles.title: Temporal and anatomic determinants of central-line-associated bloodstream infection risk in a tertiary PICU: a 3-year time-to-event and competing-risk analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Central line-associated bloodstream infections remain a major cause of preventable morbidity in pediatric intensive care units, yet most prevention strategies treat infection risk as static over catheter dwell time. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to characterize the temporal and anatomic determinants of central line-associated bloodstream infection in a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit using patient-day survival data. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 300 central venous catheter insertions in children admitted to a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit between January 2020 and December 2022 were screened for eligibility. The daily risk of first central line-associated bloodstream infection was modelled using discrete-time pooled-logistic regression with ridge regularization, incorporating baseline covariates, catheter dwell time (0-14, 15-22, and ≥23 days), time-varying clinical markers lagged by 24 hours, and catheter insertion site (femoral, internal jugular, subclavian). Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models accounted for competing events (catheter removal, discharge, or death). Model performance was evaluated using bootstrap-corrected Harrell's C-index and calibration plots. RESULTS: After exclusions, 270 non-tunneled central venous catheters contributed 4,304 catheter-days. Over 4,304 catheter-days, 13 central line-associated bloodstream infections occurred (incidence 3.0 per 1,000 catheter-days). Compared with dwell time less than 14 days, adjusted odds of infection were 4.33 (95% CI 1.89-9.92) for days 15-22 and 11.71 (95% CI 3.22-42.62) for dwell time of 23 days or more. Right internal jugular insertion was associated with lower adjusted odds relative to femoral access (adjusted odds ratio 0.34; 95% CI 0.14-0.81). Fever in the preceding 24 hours was associated with a threefold higher odds of infection (adjusted odds ratio 3.00; 95% CI 0.94-9.52). The model demonstrated good discrimination (bias-corrected C-index 0.78; 95% CI 0.70-0.86) and acceptable calibration. CONCLUSION: In this tertiary pediatric intensive care unit, central line-associated bloodstream infection risk was strongly phase-dependent, rising sharply after the second week of catheter dwell and particularly beyond 23 days, and was lower with right internal jugular than femoral insertion. These temporal and anatomic findings support time-triggered line-necessity reviews and careful consideration of insertion site within the broader clinical context when seeking to reduce infection risk in critically ill children.

articles.title: Effects of aromatherapy on objective physiological outcomes in adult ICU patients: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aromatherapy has been proposed as a non-pharmacological adjunctive intervention in critical care settings; however, evidence regarding its effects on objective outcome measures remains inconclusive. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of aromatherapy in modulating objective physiological and biochemical markers in adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients. We hypothesized that the controlled ICU environment would facilitate rigorous measurement of both physiological parameters and biochemical stress markers. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted using a novel approach combining lexical database searching (PubMed) and AI-powered semantic search strategies (Elicit, Undermind). Randomized controlled trials examining aromatherapy effects on physiological parameters in critically ill and cardiac patients were included. Outcomes were categorized as cardiovascular, respiratory, and non-cardiovascular/non-respiratory parameters. Subgroup analyses were performed by essential oil type. RESULTS: Eighteen studies comprising 1236 participants were included. Aromatherapy demonstrated moderate effects on cardiovascular parameters (systolic blood pressure: 50% success rate, 5-22 mmHg reductions; diastolic blood pressure: 50%, 3.7-14 mmHg; heart rate: 44%, up to 20 bpm) but limited effects on respiratory parameters (respiratory rate: 25%; peripheral oxygen saturation: 12.5%), with the exception of eucalyptus oil, which showed 75% success for respiratory outcomes in mechanically ventilated patients. Non-cardiovascular/non-respiratory outcomes demonstrated the highest efficacy: anxiety (86%), sleep quality (100%), pain (100%), and sedation outcomes (100%). Subgroup analysis revealed essential oil blends achieved superior cardiovascular and psychological outcomes (100%) compared to lavender alone (64% cardiovascular; 71% anxiety/sedation). Contrary to our hypothesis, no studies measured biochemical stress markers such as cortisol or catecholamines, representing a significant gap in the evidence base. A notable finding was the disparity between evidence certainty: high for anxiety reduction versus low/very low for physiological outcomes, highlighting inadequate control for ICU-specific confounders in existing trials. CONCLUSION: Aromatherapy may serve as a safe adjunctive intervention in critically ill patients, with potential cardiovascular benefits requiring cautious interpretation and strong effects on anxiety and sleep outcomes. The absence of biochemical outcome measurements and inadequate control for ICU-specific confounders limits mechanistic understanding and causal inference.
articles.ai_key_stats: n=1236, systolic blood pressure reductions 5-22 mmHg, diastolic blood pressure reductions 3.7-14 mmHg, heart rate increases up to 20 bpm, anxiety reduction 86%, sleep quality improvement 100%, pain improvement 100%, sedation outcomes 100%
articles.ai_summary: This systematic review evaluated the effects of aromatherapy on physiological outcomes in adult ICU patients. Aromatherapy showed moderate effects on cardiovascular parameters, limited effects on respiratory parameters, and strong effects on anxiety, sleep quality, pain, and sedation outcomes. The review highlights the need for further research to understand the mechanisms of aromatherapy in ICU settings.
articles.ai_significance: These findings suggest that aromatherapy may be a useful adjunctive intervention in critically ill patients, particularly for reducing anxiety and improving sleep quality. However, the evidence is limited by inadequate control for ICU-specific confounders and the absence of biochemical outcome measurements.

articles.title: Occupationally Acquired Polymicrobial Keratitis Caused by Acanthamoeba and Rare Enteric Bacteria Following Gastrointestinal Splash Exposure: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Polymicrobial keratitis is an uncommon but vision-threatening condition, particularly when it involves protozoal and bacterial pathogens. Healthcare workers may be at increased risk due to occupational exposure to hospital-associated microorganisms. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of severe polymicrobial keratitis in a 40-year-old contact lens-wearing nurse who developed acute keratitis following inadvertent ocular exposure to nasogastric secretions while caring for a critically ill child. Contact lens culture and in vivo confocal microscopy identified Acanthamoeba, Enterococcus faecalis, Staphylococcus capitis, and Pantoea species. The patient developed progressive ring infiltrates, stromal haze, and endothelial dysfunction consistent with advanced infectious keratitis. Intensive antiamoebic and targeted antimicrobial therapy resulted in infection control but with significant corneal scarring requiring planned lamellar keratoplasty. CONCLUSION: This case represents a rare example of occupationally acquired polymicrobial keratitis involving Acanthamoeba and multiple healthcare-associated bacteria. It highlights the potential for gastrointestinal and hospital flora to cause severe ocular infection in contact lens users and underscores the need for heightened infection-control awareness among healthcare workers.
articles.ai_summary: A healthcare worker developed severe polymicrobial keratitis after exposure to nasogastric secretions while caring for a patient. The infection was caused by Acanthamoeba and multiple bacteria. The patient required intensive treatment and surgery to control the infection.
articles.ai_significance: This case highlights the risk of occupationally acquired infections in healthcare workers, particularly those who wear contact lenses and are exposed to hospital-associated microorganisms.

articles.title: ICU-acquired infections and mortality in community-acquired pneumonia-induced sepsis: Insights from a transcriptomic analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between ICU-acquired infections and 28-day mortality in pneumonia-induced sepsis and to explore associated immune-related gene expression patterns. METHODS: A secondary analysis was performed using the publicly available GSE65682 dataset, including adult ICU patients with sepsis secondary to community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) or hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP). Patients were stratified based on the development of ICU-acquired infections. 28-day mortality and whole-blood leukocyte gene expression at ICU admission were compared between groups. RESULTS: Among 144 patients, 20 developed ICU-acquired infections. In the CAP subgroup, ICU-acquired infections were associated with numerically higher 28-day mortality compared to those without infection (45.5% vs. 18.2%, p = 0.05), although this finding should be interpreted with caution given the retrospective study design and limited sample size. In HAP patients, a similar pattern was not observed (22.2% vs. 19.6%). Transcriptomic analysis showed significant downregulation of the interleukin-7 receptor (IL7R) in CAP patients who developed ICU-acquired infections, with PRKACB and CD3D also demonstrating a downward trend. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that early immune dysregulation may be associated with an increased susceptibility to secondary infections and potentially worse outcomes among CAP patients. IL7R may represent a candidate signal of immune dysregulation and warrants further investigation and validation in future studies.

articles.title: Assessment of Routine, On-Demand Electroencephalograms for Seizure Detection in the Intensive Care Unit of a Major Saudi Tertiary Center.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the occurrence and characteristics of seizures using routine electroencephalograms (EEGs) in intensive care unit (ICU) patients. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis on routine, portable EEGs of 188 adult ICU patients (53% male) in a large tertiary hospital in Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. We compared variables of interest using a t-test and chi-squared analyses and explored significant associations using binary logistic regression analysis. RESULTS: We found significant associations between the occurrence of seizures on EEGs and several variables, including patient age, ICU admission due to status epilepticus, history of epilepsy or previous neurosurgical procedure, coma state, and convulsions at the time of EEG (p < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis revealed that age, ICU admission due to status epilepticus, and a history of epilepsy were independently associated with the occurrence of seizures on EEG. Epileptiform abnormalities were observed in 14.9% of patients; periodic abnormalities were identified in 14.3%. Electrographic seizures were evident in 11.2% of patients, and 63 comatose patients did not exhibit any evidence of seizures in their EEGs. CONCLUSION: Routine EEGs play a vital role in investigating altered mental status in ICU patients, particularly for seizure evaluation. Age, ICU admission due to status epilepticus, and a history of epilepsy are significant factors associated with seizure occurrence on EEG. Future studies should validate these findings and explore the comparative effectiveness of routine and continuous EEGs in ICU settings.
articles.ai_key_stats: n=188, p < 0.05, 14.9% epileptiform abnormalities, 14.3% periodic abnormalities, 11.2% electrographic seizures
articles.ai_summary: This study analyzed EEGs from 188 ICU patients to see how often seizures occurred and what factors were associated with them. They found that seizures were more common in older patients, those admitted to the ICU due to status epilepticus, and those with a history of epilepsy. Epileptiform abnormalities were seen in 14.9% of patients.
articles.ai_significance: This study highlights the importance of routine EEGs in ICU patients with altered mental status, particularly for seizure evaluation, and identifies key factors associated with seizure occurrence.

articles.title: Candida Albicans Purulent Pericarditis Complicated by Cardiac Tamponade in a Critically Ill Burn Patient: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Journal of the Saudi Heart Association
articles.abstract: Candida pericarditis is a rare, life-threatening complication of invasive candidiasis, associated with high mortality. We report this case of a young woman with 60% body surface area burn, multidrug-resistant polymicrobial sepsis, and multiorgan failure who developed Candida albicans pericarditis complicated by cardiac tamponade. Despite urgent pericardiocentesis and escalation of antifungal therapy, she ultimately progressed to refractory shock and multiorgan failure. This case illustrates the diagnostic challenge and therapeutic limitations of fungal pericarditis in critically ill host, and underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion in burn patients with multisite Candida colonization and prolonged antibiotic exposure.
articles.ai_summary: A young woman with severe burns developed a rare fungal infection of the pericardium, leading to cardiac tamponade. Despite treatment, she progressed to refractory shock and multiorgan failure. This case highlights the challenges of diagnosing and treating fungal pericarditis in critically ill patients.
articles.ai_significance: This case emphasizes the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for fungal infections in burn patients with multisite colonization and prolonged antibiotic exposure, as they can lead to severe complications.

articles.title: The association of empirical treatment with oseltamivir with the outcome of critically ill patients admitted with severe acute respiratory illness (SARI).
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Neuraminidase inhibitors (NAIs) are widely used empirically in critically ill patients with suspected influenza; however, their effect on mortality remains uncertain. This multicenter study evaluates the association between empirical treatment with oseltamivir and the outcome of critically ill patients with Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study conducted in the ICUs of four hospitals in Saudi Arabia, involving adult patients with SARI from September 2012 to December 2018. Data collected were: demographics, comorbidities, clinical presentation, and outcomes among patients treated with oseltamivir and those who were not. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality. The association of oseltamivir and mortality was evaluated adjusting for propensity score. RESULTS: During the study period, 456 patients with SARI were included in the study, 301 were treated with empirical oseltamivir within a median of 1 day from presentation (interquartile range, 0-1 day) and a median of 4 days after symptom onset, while 155 patients were not. No significant differences were observed in baseline characteristics between the two groups. Of the included patients, 334 (73%) were tested for influenza using PCR, and 87 (26%) had a confirmed diagnosis of influenza. Patients on oseltamivir were less likely to require rescue oxygen therapy (22.9% vs. 34.8%, p=0.007), and had shorter hospital stay (20 days vs. 27 days, p=0.01). Patients treated with oseltamivir had significantly reduced 90-day mortality on adjusted analyses (aOR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.81-0.94, p=0.0002). Subgroup analysis revealed that the association with reduced mortality extends to patients >70 years old (aOR: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.89-0.99, p=0.02) and those with negative influenza tests (aOR: 0.81, 95% CI: 0.79, 0.84, p<0.0001). CONCLUSION: Among critically ill patients with SARI, empirical treatment with oseltamivir was associated with lower mortality. These results add to the body of evidence suggesting clinical benefits of oseltamivir in managing critically ill patients with influenza-like illnesses.
articles.ai_summary: This study looked at whether giving oseltamivir to critically ill patients with severe acute respiratory illness (SARI) affected their outcomes. Researchers found that patients who received oseltamivir had lower mortality rates compared to those who did not. The benefits of oseltamivir were seen in patients over 70 years old and those without confirmed influenza.
articles.ai_significance: These findings suggest that oseltamivir may be beneficial in managing critically ill patients with SARI, and clinicians may consider its use in high-risk patients.

articles.title: Blood Stream Infections due to Candida Species: Prevalence, Risk Factors, Mortality, and Susceptibility Profile Over 3-Year Period: A Single Center Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Candida is one of the most common causes of bloodstream infections in critically ill and immunocompromised patients. Understanding the distribution and antifungal resistance patterns of Candida species and the associated mortality rates is critical for tailoring therapeutic measures. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study is to analyze the epidemiology, antifungal resistance trends, and risk factors influencing mortality associated with candidemia in a tertiary healthcare center of Saudi Arabia. PATIENT AND METHODS: The study included all cases of bloodstream infections caused by Candida species from December 2021 to January 2023. The antifungal susceptibility and identification of species were done via standard protocols. Univariate and multivariate statistical analyses were conducted to determine the predictors of 14-day mortality (death within 14 days of the first positive blood culture) and overall (in-hospital) mortality (death during the index hospitalization). RESULTS: Fifty patients were included in the study with a median age of 71 years, with 58% being females. C. albicans accounted for 21.3% of candidemia cases, with a declining trend over time. Candidozyma auris (formerly Candida auris) was the most frequently identified non-albicans Candida species (25%). Fluctuating trends in antifungal susceptibility of non-albicans Candida were observed, with increasing resistance to azoles, while increasing susceptibility to micafungin. The 14-day mortality and overall (in-hospital) mortality rates were 23.4% and 55.3%, respectively. Multivariate analysis revealed older age, cardiac and respiratory disorders, ICU as site of diagnosis, treatment duration of > 48 h, and Candida colonization to be independent predictors of overall (in-hospital) mortality (p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: The continuous rise of antifungal resistance and spread of non-albicans Candida species highlight the need for implementing rigorous control measures in healthcare facilities. Improving candidemia outcomes requires prompt identification of high-risk patients and targeted therapies.

articles.title: Beyond the Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Case Report on Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked recessive genetic disorder characterized by the absence of dystrophin, leading to progressive muscle degeneration and generalized weakness. It primarily affects males in early childhood and progresses to loss of ambulation and cardiac and respiratory complications. CASE REPORT: This case report describes a 26-year-old male with terminal-stage DMD who was admitted to the surgical intensive care unit (SICU) in a critically ill state with multiple-organ failure. He was ventilator-dependent via tracheostomy, hypotensive, anemic, and required cardiovascular support. He also had multiple pressure ulcers, including a Stage IV ulcer with associated edema, acute renal failure managed with continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), and sepsis due to mixed bacterial and fungal infections. Broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy and intensive wound care were provided. This case highlights that advanced-stage DMD is a severe multisystem condition requiring intensive, specialized, and multidisciplinary care. CONCLUSION: This case underscores the critical importance of a multidisciplinary approach in managing complex patient conditions, emphasizing the prevention of secondary complications such as pressure ulcers and pulmonary infections. Adherence to evidence-based guidelines, coupled with psychosocial and ethical considerations related to quality of life, remains essential. Establishing standardized care protocols, enhancing healthcare team training on the specific needs of these patients, and promoting home-based and palliative care services are strongly recommended to ensure comprehensive, coordinated, and patient-centered management.

articles.title: Evidence-Based Guidelines versus Enteral Nutrition Practices in Intensive Care Units: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, enteral nutrition (EN) practices among critical care nurses (CCNs) often vary, leading to suboptimal nutritional delivery. Evidence regarding EN practices in Saudi Arabian intensive care units (ICUs) is limited. This study aimed to assess CCNs' EN practices in Al-Madinah and evaluate their alignment with current evidence-based guidelines. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among CCNs working in adult ICUs of governmental hospitals in Al-Madinah Al-Munawarah, Saudi Arabia, using a census sampling approach. Data were collected using a 61-item self-administered questionnaire comprising three sections: ICU and nurse characteristics (11 items), EN practices (34 items), and assessment and management of EN intolerance and complications (16 items). An online survey was distributed via social media platforms between November 2023 and January 2024. RESULTS: Of 500 eligible nurses, 178 completed the questionnaire (35.6% response rate) and were included in the final analysis. Most reported the availability of EN guidelines (62.4%), performing nutritional assessments (66.9%), initiating EN early within 48 hours or less (87.2%), and using gastric access (98.31%). However, significant inconsistencies were observed in tube placement verification, monitoring and management of gastric residual volume (GRV) and feeding intolerance. Outdated methods for confirming tube placement, such as auscultation, remained common (67.4%). GRV was frequently measured more often than recommended (78.7%), and EN was often withheld at GRV thresholds below recommended (72.5%). Management of diarrhea involved non-recommended practices, although adherence to recommended tube-flushing procedures was high. CONCLUSION: The self-reported EN practices among CCNs showed partial adherence to guidelines, with notable gaps in tube placement verification, GRV and feeding intolerance monitoring and management. These findings underscore the need for standardized protocols, targeted training, and quality improvement initiatives to optimize EN delivery and prevent underfeeding in critically ill patients.

articles.title: Exploring Nurses' Experiences of Autonomy in Intensive Care Units: A Qualitative Descriptive Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nursing autonomy is essential in intensive care units (ICUs). However, there is limited understanding of how nurses perceive autonomy within their practice. AIM: To explore nurses' perception and experience of autonomy in ICUs. DESIGN: A qualitative descriptive study. METHODS: The study was conducted with 14 ICU nurses through interviews from May to August 2025. Nurses' characteristics were described, and interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using a primarily inductive, semantic codebook thematic analysis informed by Braun and Clarke's six-phase framework. RESULTS: Seven main themes and 25 subthemes emerged from the interviews, revealing personal and organizational factors that influence nursing autonomy in ICUs. The themes were as follows: nursing autonomy's definition and perception, clinical practices, facilitators, barriers, perceived influence on patient care, perceived influence on nurse personal and professional development, and future advancements. CONCLUSION: The findings provide insight into ICU nurses' experiences and perceptions of autonomy. Nurses reported that autonomy was influenced by clinical competence, organizational support, and clear guidelines. Nurses perceived that independent nursing care and timely actions undertaken under approved protocols could support patient care, professional confidence, and job satisfaction. Limited decision-making authority, inadequate staffing, and unclear institutional support were reported as barriers. Nursing autonomy could strengthen nurses' confidence and job satisfaction, which nurses perceived as contributing to better patient care. IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING MANAGEMENT: The findings can guide nurse managers in implementing structured competency-based education, reinforcing clearly defined scopes of practice that are consistent with institutional policies, and adopting supportive leadership practices to promote nursing autonomy. Hospital administrators and national policymakers can further use the findings to advance nursing practice through developing organizational and regulatory frameworks required to authorize and safely support expanded autonomous practice.

articles.title: Nurses' Experiences With Artificial Intelligence and the Association Between Clinical Decision-Making and Missed Nursing Care: A Convergent Mixed-Methods Study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being incorporated into clinical nursing practice, but evidence remains limited on how nurses experience AI-supported systems and how decision-making orientation relates to missed nursing care (MNC). AIM: To explore nurses' experiences with AI-supported clinical decision support (CDS) and examine associations among clinical decision-making orientation, professional characteristics, and MNC. DESIGN: A convergent parallel mixed-methods study. METHODS: The study was conducted in six hospitals in Beni Suef Governorate, Egypt. The quantitative sample included 210 intensive care unit (ICU) nurses who completed the Nursing Decision-Making Instrument-Revised 2014 (NDMI-R) and the Missed Intensive Nursing Care Scale (MINCS). Fourteen nurses completed semistructured interviews, and all transcripts were included in the thematic analysis. RESULTS: NDMI-R scores showed a small negative bivariate correlation with MNC (r = -0.178, p < 0.01), but the adjusted association was not statistically significant (β = -0.124, p = 0.063). The regression model explained 16.9% of the variance in MNC (adjusted R2 = 14.5%). Years of experience (β = 0.198, p = 0.004) and bachelor's degree or above compared with a technical nursing diploma (β = -0.255, p < 0.001) were significant predictors. The other education contrast, AI training/support and MISSCARE Reasons were not statistically significant. In interviews, nurses described AI-related tools as potentially helpful for alerts, information review, workflow, and communication while also raising concerns about trust, overreliance, empathy, and training. CONCLUSION: Nurses perceived potential benefits from AI-supported tools, but the quantitative findings did not establish an independent effect of AI or a statistically significant adjusted association between decision-making orientation and MNC. These findings support cautious, nurse-centered implementation and further longitudinal evaluation. IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING MANAGEMENT: Managers should pair any AI-supported CDS implementation with role-specific training, clear accountability, usability monitoring, and safeguards that preserve clinical judgment and humanistic care.

articles.title: Response to "Fragility of Observed Associations in Selection of Empirical Antifungal Therapy for Critically Ill Non-Neutropenic Patients" [Response to Letter].
Feeding practices during high-flow nasal cannula: current evidence and clinical implications for respiratory care.
articles.abstract: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy is increasingly used as a noninvasive respiratory support modality across acute and critical care settings. Although nutritional management is integral to the care of patients with respiratory failure, established guidelines for feeding patients receiving HFNC are lacking, and clinical decisions vary widely, reflecting persistent uncertainty about HFNC's effects on swallowing function, airway protection, and aspiration risk. This narrative review found that HFNC may alter swallowing biomechanics, particularly at flow rates >40 L/min, potentially increasing the risk of choking and aspiration. Evidence on aspiration risk is heterogeneous, deriving largely from healthy volunteers and pediatric bronchiolitis cohorts. Adult evidence is limited to retrospective studies; the largest found no increase in respiratory deterioration with enteral feeding. Most institutions lack formal feeding protocols, and practice is driven by individual clinician judgment. Areas of consensus include the safety of early enteral feeding in hemodynamically stable patients and the avoidance of routine prolonged withholding of nutrition based solely on HFNC use. Disagreement persists regarding routine swallowing assessment, optimal flow thresholds during feeding, and the prioritization of oral versus tube feeding. Safe feeding in patients receiving HFNC requires a multidisciplinary, individualized approach that balances respiratory support against nutritional adequacy. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to define safe flow thresholds, validate bedside assessment tools, and establish standardized feeding guidelines, particularly in adult and critically ill populations.

articles.title: Clinical evaluation of AI Chatbots' performance and safety for total parenteral nutrition planning in critically ill patients: a simulation-based benchmarking study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Total parenteral nutrition (TPN) is essential for critically ill adults unable to meet their nutritional needs via the gastrointestinal tract. Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have sparked interest in their potential to support healthcare providers in complex clinical decisions. Nonetheless, no prior research has systematically compared publicly accessible chatbots to pharmacist-developed reference TPN plans across a diverse patient cohort, using a predefined, guideline-based rubric assessing accuracy, completeness, safety, error types, and numerical precision. This study presents a simulation-based benchmarking to evaluate (i) the accuracy and comprehensiveness of chatbot-generated TPN plans, (ii) their safety, acceptability, and error profiles, and (iii) the numerical agreement and concordance with expert pharmacist references. METHODS: This benchmarking study, based on simulations and cross-sectional analysis, evaluated the performance of four publicly accessible AI chatbots-ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and Perplexity-in formulating TPN plans for critically ill adults. Copilot declined to generate patient-specific TPN plans; this refusal was retained as a performance outcome, while Copilot was excluded from analyses requiring an analyzable TPN prescription. Each chatbot produced one plan for each of 10 standardized clinical cases, resulting in a total of 30 TPN plans. Friedman tests, Kendall's W, and Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used for comparative analyses. RESULTS: ChatGPT produced comprehensive plans for all 10 cases, compared to 6 plans from Gemini and 4 from Perplexity. The median accuracy was 57.7% for ChatGPT, 43.9% for Gemini, and 38.5% for Perplexity, with no statistically significant overall difference (p = 0.124). However, ChatGPT performed better than Perplexity in pairwise comparison (adjusted p = 0.035). There was a significant difference in completeness among the chatbots (p = 0.003; Kendall's W = 0.57), with median scores of 64.6, 41.9, and 32.3%, respectively. All 30 plans had at least one major or critical safety issue, 7 (23.3%) contained a critical concern, and 19 (63.3%) were rejected. The most common errors were related to electrolytes (90.0%), micronutrients (70.0%), and monitoring (66.7%). Recommendations from chatbots often exceeded pharmacist-derived values, with median relative differences of +47% for energy, +120% for lipids, and +100% for potassium. Bland-Altman analysis revealed considerable variability in the agreement. CONCLUSION: ChatGPT produced the most comprehensive TPN plans among chatbots. However, none showed enough accuracy, safety, or concordance for independent use. All plans had critical issues, especially with electrolytes, micronutrients, monitoring, and refeeding precautions. AI chatbots can support education or planning but require review by a well-trained clinician before clinical use.

articles.title: The Impact of 12-Hour Versus 8-Hour Shifts on Intensive Care Unit Nurses' Physical and Mental Well-Being and Job Satisfaction: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Twelve-hour shifts have been widely implemented in intensive care units (ICUs), where nurses work in high-acuity environments requiring sustained clinical attention. However, evidence regarding the impact of shift length on ICU nurses' physical health, mental well-being, job satisfaction and patient-care outcomes remains limited and inconsistent. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the impact of 12-h compared with 8-h shifts on ICU nurses' physical health, well-being and job satisfaction. DESIGN: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251021178). METHODS: A systematic search of CINAHL, Ovid MEDLINE and Embase was conducted in February 2025 and updated in June 2026. Additional searches of Scopus and Web of Science were undertaken in June 2026. Eligible studies included ICU nurses and compared 12-h with 8-h shifts. Risk of bias and methodological quality were assessed using design-specific Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. Findings were synthesised narratively due to the heterogeneity of the included studies. RESULT: Of 815 records identified, five studies met the inclusion criteria. Findings on fatigue, sleep and burnout were inconclusive across studies. Twelve-hour shifts were generally associated with greater roster satisfaction, flexibility and work-life balance, while evidence for sick leave was limited or mixed. CONCLUSION: Evidence did not consistently favour either 12- or 8-h shifts for ICU nurses, with low to very low certainty of evidence. Shift duration should therefore be considered alongside overall roster design, staffing needs and nurses' well-being when planning ICU schedules. IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING MANAGEMENT: Nurse managers should avoid a one-size-fits-all approach to shift duration, as evidence does not clearly favour 12- or 8-h shifts. Shift-length decisions should consider roster design, staffing needs, workload, recovery time and nurses' preferences. Managers should also monitor staff well-being, satisfaction, absenteeism, retention and patient-care outcomes when reviewing shift patterns. Given the low certainty of evidence, ongoing local evaluation is essential to ensure rosters support workforce sustainability and safe, high-quality care.

articles.title: Holding the Emotion, Carrying the Responsibility: A Qualitative Study of Respiratory Therapists in Saudi Critical Care.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory therapists (RTs) work under considerable pressure in critical-care settings, caring for critically ill patients while maintaining professional composure. Yet little is known about how they manage these emotional demands, particularly when responsibility for patient outcomes may exceed their authority over treatment decisions. This study explored how Saudi RTs build composure, encounter its relational limits, and negotiate responsibility for outcomes beyond their control. METHODS: In this qualitative study, semi-structured interviews were conducted in Arabic with thirteen RTs working in critical-care settings across Saudi Arabia, purposively sampled to vary gender, years of experience, and hospital or region. Data were analysed in Arabic using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis, and selected quotations were translated into English after themes had been developed. RESULTS: Analysis generated the overarching theme, "Holding the Emotion, Carrying the Responsibility", and three interrelated themes. In "You Are the Patient's Mirror" participants described developing composure as a patient-oriented professional practice rather than emotional detachment. In "The Human Side You Can't Overcome" they described how relational proximity, including personal resemblance, prolonged care, and families' grief, could disrupt this composure. In "Did I Do Enough?" they described how staffing pressures, constrained authority, and team dynamics shaped responsibility for care and outcomes beyond their control. CONCLUSION: Professional composure among RTs did not reflect emotional detachment; rather, participants remained emotionally responsive while containing their expression in the service of patient care. Emotional burden intensified when close clinical involvement and perceived responsibility were not matched by equivalent authority over care decisions and outcomes. These findings suggest that supporting RTs requires attention not only to individual emotional regulation, but also to the organisational and interprofessional conditions that shape responsibility, authority, and control in critical care.

articles.title: CT-Assessed Sarcopenia Combined with Laboratory Inflammatory Markers for Outcome Prediction in Critically Ill, Pulmonary, and Geriatric Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia, assessed via computed tomography (CT), is an emerging prognostic tool in critically ill, pulmonary, and geriatric patients. Laboratory inflammatory markers such as C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) are routinely obtained in these populations. Whether CT-assessed sarcopenia combined with laboratory markers offers superior prognostic accuracy over either measure alone remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: To systematically evaluate the prognostic value of CT-assessed sarcopenia, alone or combined with laboratory inflammatory/nutritional markers, for predicting mortality, mechanical ventilation duration, and ICU length of stay in critically ill, pulmonary, and geriatric patients. METHODS: MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to December 2024. Observational studies (prospective or retrospective cohorts, case-control) that reported CT-based sarcopenia assessment alongside at least one laboratory inflammatory marker and at least one clinical outcome were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Random-effects meta-analysis was performed; heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. RESULTS: Twenty-five studies encompassing 12,347 patients were identified. The pooled odds ratio for mortality in sarcopenic versus non-sarcopenic patients was 2.28 (95% CI: 1.83-2.83; I² = 22.1%) across critically ill ICU cohorts. In COVID-19 pulmonary populations, pooled OR for in-hospital mortality with low skeletal muscle mass was 5.84 (95% CI: 1.07-31.83). CT-derived muscle measurements correlated inversely with CRP (r = -0.315), fibrinogen (r = -0.392), D-dimers (r = -0.363), and WBC count (r = -0.287). Combined CT-sarcopenia and inflammatory marker models outperformed conventional scoring systems (APACHE II, SOFA, CURB-65, PSI). CONCLUSIONS: CT-assessed sarcopenia, when integrated with laboratory inflammatory markers, provides a robust, mechanistically grounded, and clinically accessible multimodal prognostic framework across critically ill, pulmonary, and geriatric populations.
articles.ai_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the prognostic value of CT-assessed sarcopenia, alone or combined with laboratory inflammatory markers, for predicting mortality and other outcomes in critically ill, pulmonary, and geriatric patients. The results showed that CT-assessed sarcopenia, when integrated with laboratory inflammatory markers, provides a robust prognostic framework. The pooled odds ratio for mortality in sarcopenic patients was 2.28, and 5.84 in COVID-19 pulmonary populations.
articles.ai_significance: This study provides a clinically accessible multimodal prognostic framework for critically ill, pulmonary, and geriatric populations, which can help clinicians make more informed decisions.

articles.title: Endotracheal tube size selection in critically ill patients: a 4-year single-center experience in Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intubation is a critical aspect of airway management and supportive care for intensive care unit (ICU) patients. Inappropriate size of endotracheal tubes (ETT) affects the patient's airway, it is crucial to choose an appropriate size for each patient. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess current practices of ETT size. SELECTION: for adult ICU patients and to explore factors associated with it. DESIGN AND SETTINGS: Single-center, retrospective cohort study at King Fahad Hospital of the University, Saudi Arabia. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted for adult patients admitted to ICU from January 2020 to January 2024 at King Fahad Hospital of the University. Inclusion criteria included patients aged 18 years or older, underwent intubation and was followed by tracheostomy. Those with missing data, had laryngeal or thyroid masses, had upper airway obstruction by any cause and upper airway surgery were excluded. MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was compliance of ETT size selection with established guidelines. Secondary outcomes included associations between ETT size (mm), patient demographics and intubation indications. RESULTS: A total of 228 ICU patients were analysed [mean (standard deviation) age of 61.8 (19.6) years]. The median internal diameter of the ETT size was 7.5 mm, with neurological causes being the most common indication for intubation. ETT size showed a significant positive correlation with height (rs=.341; P<.001) and weight (rs=0.190; p=0.004), but not with body mass index (rs=.050; P=.456). In multivariable analysis, larger ETT size was significantly associated with male sex (adjusted odds ratio, aOR 2.38, 95% confidence interval, CI 1.12-5.05), pulmonary indication for intubation (aOR 2.31, 95% CI 1.10-4.86), older age (aOR 1.20 per 10 years, 95% CI 1.02-1.42), and height (aOR 1.95 per 10 cm, 95% CI 1.20-3.16), whereas weight was not independently associated after adjustment (aOR 1.04 per 10 kg, 95% CI 0.85-1.26). Overall, 77% of ETT size selection did not comply with height-based guidelines. CONCLUSIONS: No standardized ETT size selection guidelines were followed for adult ICU patients. Male sex, height, older age, and pulmonary indication were independent predictors of larger ETT size, supporting the implementation of more structured, height-informed ETT sizing protocols.
articles.ai_summary: This study reviewed endotracheal tube (ETT) size selection in critically ill patients over 4 years at a Saudi Arabian hospital. The researchers found that ETT size was not consistently chosen according to established guidelines and was associated with patient demographics such as height, sex, and age. They also identified factors that predicted larger ETT size.
articles.ai_significance: This study highlights the need for more structured and evidence-based approaches to ETT size selection in ICU patients, which could improve patient outcomes and reduce complications.

articles.title: Effects of Integration Sedation Interruption With Early Mobility on Patient Outcomes and Prevention of Intensive Care Unit-Acquired Weakness in Critically Ill Ventilated Patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early mobilization and sedation reduction are critical strategies for improving patient outcomes. AIM: This study assessed the effects of integrating daily sedation interruptions with an early progressive mobility strategy on outcomes in critically ill, ventilated patients. STUDY DESIGN: A quasi-experimental research with a control group was conducted on a sample of 60 mechanically ventilated adult patients who met the inclusion criteria. We randomly divided the patients into 30 groups, with each representing the control and study groups. Data were gathered using 4 tools. RESULTS: The intervention group showed significant improvements (P < .001) in Medical Research Council strength scores, progressive mobility milestones, and functional assessment. Moreover, the intervention group showed significant improvements in clinical outcomes (P < .001), including shorter hospital stays, fewer adverse events, improved discharge status, and better weaning outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: The protocol for integrating sedation interruptions with early progressive mobility is associated with improved outcomes of critically ill ventilated patients. Further randomized controlled trial studies are suggested to improve patients' clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Quality Improvement Strategies in Preventing Healthcare-Associated Infections Among Neurosurgical Patients Admitted to Intensive Care Units: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remain a major and largely preventable cause of morbidity, excess mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and escalating healthcare costs in intensive care units (ICUs) worldwide. Neurosurgical patients are particularly vulnerable because of frequent exposure to invasive devices such as external ventricular drains (EVDs), central venous catheters, urinary catheters, and mechanical ventilation, combined with impaired neurological status and prolonged ICU stays. Although quality improvement (QI) strategies have been widely implemented across critical care settings, evidence specific to neurosurgical and neurocritical care populations remains fragmented. OBJECTIVES: To systematically evaluate the effectiveness of QI interventions in reducing HAI incidence among neurosurgical and neurological ICU patients and to assess their impact on secondary outcomes including ICU length of stay, device utilization, and bundle compliance. METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from January 2010 to May 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies for the primary evidence synthesis included randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, and observational cohort studies evaluating structured QI interventions for HAI prevention in neurosurgical or neurological ICU populations, or mixed ICU settings with extractable neurocritical care data. Systematic reviews identified during screening were retained for contextual interpretation and reference screening but were excluded from the primary evidence synthesis to avoid duplication of overlapping primary data. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I, Cochrane RoB 2, and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale according to study design. RESULTS: Seventeen primary studies from 14 countries met eligibility criteria and were included in the primary narrative synthesis. Three systematic reviews were retained for contextual interpretation. Structured QI interventions consistently reduced device-associated infection rates across studies. The strongest evidence was observed for EVD-specific care bundles, with EVD-related infection rates decreasing from 14.35 to 3.21 per 1,000 catheter-days following bundle implementation, and one study reporting 20 consecutive infection-free months after interprofessional bundle adoption. Device-associated infection prevention bundles also demonstrated clinically meaningful reductions, including VAP rates decreasing from 68.2 to 47.4 per 1,000 ventilator-days and CAUTI rates from 24.9 to 13.4 per 1,000 catheter-days following structured educational interventions. CLABSI rates declined substantially following standardized central venous catheter bundle implementation, reaching zero in one study with sustained monitoring. Risk of bias was predominantly low to moderate across included primary studies. CONCLUSIONS: Structured QI interventions, particularly EVD-specific care bundles, device-associated infection prevention protocols, and staff education programs with compliance monitoring, consistently reduce HAI incidence in neurosurgical and neurological ICU settings. Although the evidence base is predominantly non-randomized, findings are directionally consistent across diverse healthcare systems and institutional contexts. Universal adoption of evidence-based infection prevention frameworks in neurocritical care is strongly supported.

articles.title: The Link Between Novel Coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Endothelial Dysfunction in ICU-Admitted COVID-19 Patients: A Key for Hypercoagulability and Thrombosis.
articles.journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
articles.abstract: BackgroundEndothelial dysfunction and platelet activation contribute to the hypercoagulable state observed in severe COVID-19. This study investigated circulating P-selectin and von Willebrand factor (vWF) in ICU-admitted COVID-19 patients and examined their associations with hematological, coagulation, and in-hospital outcomes.Materials and methodsA case-control study was conducted involving 140 participants, including 70 ICU-admitted COVID-19 patients and 70 healthy controls. Complete blood counts (CBC), CBC-derived parameters, coagulation profiles, D-dimer levels, and soluble plasma concentrations of P-selectin and von Willebrand factor (vWF) were measured and correlated with hematological indices in the current study.ResultsCOVID-19 patients had significantly prolonged prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time compared with controls (both p < 0.0001). Plasma P-selectin concentrations were significantly higher in COVID-19 patients than in controls (median 5674.50 [IQR 4778.50-6398.50] vs 3243.50 [2210.50-4332.75] pg/mL, p < 0.0001), whereas vWF concentrations did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.1175). After adjustment for age and sex, COVID-19 status remained independently associated with higher P-selectin concentrations (adjusted ratio 1.620, 95% CI 1.319-1.989, p < 0.0001), whereas the association with vWF remained non-significant (adjusted ratio 1.533, 95% CI 0.896-2.624, p = 0.1179). Neither P-selectin nor vWF was independently associated with in-hospital mortality among COVID-19 patients with definitive outcomes.ConclusionICU-admitted COVID-19 patients exhibited marked elevation of circulating P-selectin that remained significant after adjustment for age and sex, supporting an association between severe COVID-19 and platelet/endothelial activation. In contrast, vWF did not differ significantly between groups after either unadjusted or adjusted analysis. Neither biomarker independently predicted in-hospital mortality in this cohort. These findings support P-selectin as a marker of vascular and platelet activation in severe COVID-19 while highlighting the need for larger, clinically well-characterized cohorts to determine its prognostic utility.

articles.title: Impact of Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE II) Scores on the Occurrence of a Hospital-Acquired Pressure Injury in ICU Patients: A Comparative Analytical Study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pressure injuries represent a significant challenge for patients, healthcare professionals, and health systems. Their incidence serves as an indicator of quality of care in both primary and specialized care settings. AIM: To determine the association between Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE II) scores and the development of hospital-acquired pressure injuries in ICU patients. METHODOLOGY: A retrospective cohort study with comparative analysis was conducted. Critically ill patients admitted to a tertiary care hospital between July 2022 and January 2023 were categorized into two groups based on the presence or absence of pressure injuries. The Braden score was assessed for each patient, and APACHE II scores were stratified into four groups: group 1 (scores 31-40), group 2 (scores 21-30), group 3 (scores 11-20), and group 4 (scores 3-10). RESULTS: Pressure injuries occurred in 46% of patients. Patients with pressure injuries had a mean APACHE II score of 17.70 compared to 15.33 in patients without pressure injuries; however, this difference was not statistically significant. CONCLUSION: APACHE II scores were not significantly associated with pressure injury occurrence in this study population.

articles.title: Trends in Temperature Control after Cardiac Arrest in Cardiac Intensive Care Units: An Analysis from the Critical Care Cardiology Trials Network.
articles.abstract: Temperature control (TC) is recommended for comatose patients after cardiac arrest (CA). In the TTM2 trial, targeted normothermia (≤37.5°C) resulted in similar mortality and functional outcomes as targeted hypothermia (33°C). The Critical Care Cardiology Trials Network (CCCTN) is a multinational registry of cardiac intensive care units (CICU) coordinated by the TIMI Study Group (Boston, MA). Between 2018-2024, consecutive comatose CA admissions were classified as occurring before vs. after publication and initial assimilation of TTM2. We compared temporal trends in TC use, temperature targets, and outcomes between the pre- and post-TTM2 eras, including in subgroups with initial shockable (VT/VF) vs. non-shockable (PEA/asystole) rhythms. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for baseline differences. Among 1,706 comatose CA admissions, 773 occurred in the pre-TTM2 era and 933 in the post-TTM2 era. TC use was similar pre- and post-TTM2 (74% vs. 78%; p=0.06), including in subgroups with shockable (84% vs. 85%; p=0.85) and non-shockable rhythms (64% vs. 68%; p=0.26). Post-TTM2, target temperatures shifted towards normothermia (target temperature ≥36°C: 38% [pre] vs. 71% [post]; p<0.001). Mortality was higher post-TTM2 vs. pre-TTM2 among CA admissions with shockable rhythms (50% vs. 42%; aOR 1.48, 95% CI 1.11-1.99), but not with non-shockable rhythms (76% vs. 75%; aOR 1.03 [0.71-1.49]). Comparing CA admissions with shockable rhythms to non-CA admissions, the difference in proportional increase in mortality between eras was not statistically significant (ROR 1.20 [0.91-1.58]). In a large CICU cohort of comatose CA patients, overall use of TC remained stable over the study period (2018-2024), but clinicians increasingly favored targeted normothermia. In-hospital mortality among patients with initial shockable rhythms was higher in the post-TTM2 era, which may be related to secular changes in CICU patients over time.

articles.title: Coronary artery disease severity in patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a secondary analysis of the INCEPTION trial.
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) can restore circulation in patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Subsequent invasive coronary angiography (ICA) allows the treatment of reversible causes and enables the evaluation of the presence and severity of coronary artery disease, facilitating insights into the cause of refractory arrest. This secondary analysis of the INCEPTION trial, which randomized refractory OHCA patients between ECPR or conventional CPR, included all patients who underwent ICA. Angiograms were reanalyzed following a standardized protocol by two cardiologists, on presence of significant stenoses (>50%), with calculation of the SYNTAX score as a proxy for coronary artery disease severity. Patients were grouped as having "ROSC" or "no-ROSC", irrespective of the original assignment. In addition, patients with "no-ROSC" who had persistent ventricular arrhythmias were compared with those who converted to non-shockable rhythms. We included 73 patients: 29 ROSC and 44 no-ROSC (persistent ventricular arrhythmia, n=10; non-shockable conversion, n=34). No-ROSC patients had more frequent obstructive coronary artery disease (84% versus 66%, p=0.037), were more likely to have at least one acute culprit lesion (52% versus 21%, p=0.009) than ROSC patients, and had a higher SYNTAX score (17 ± 11 versus 10± 9, p=0.002). Lesions were predominantly left-sided. Patients who do not achieve ROSC after refractory OHCA have more complex CAD and present more frequently with obstructive disease and a culprit lesion than patients who achieve ROSC. This seems particularly evident in patients who rapidly convert to a non-shockable rhythm.

articles.title: Prevalence and Patterns of Acute Cerebral Infarctions in Comatose Survivors of Cardiac Arrest.
authors: Critical Care Electroencephalogram Monitoring Research Consortium
articles.abstract: It is well-established that hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI) is the leading cause of death and disability after cardiac arrest. However, there is limited information about concurrent acute cerebral infarctions (ACI) and their association with clinical outcomes in comatose cardiac arrest survivors. This was a retrospective multicenter cohort study of adult patients after cardiac arrest. We included patients who had brain MRIs performed within 7 days of cardiac arrest and excluded patients with a diagnosis of acute traumatic brain injury, intracranial hemorrhage, and acute ischemic stroke on admission. Univariate and multivariable analyses were performed to identify factors associated with ACI and to evaluate the association between ACI and unfavorable outcomes at hospital discharge (i.e., Cerebral Performance Category of 3-5). Of 351 patients included, 106 (30.2%) had ACI on MRI. The most common ACI pattern was multifocal small embolic-appearing (38.7%), followed by punctate (33%), territorial (18.9%), watershed (14.2%), and lacunar (14.2%), with overlapping patterns in 17% of patients with ACI. The patients with ACI were older (64 [54-71] vs 56 [39-66] years). Chronic white matter lesions were associated with ACI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.79 [1.04-3.1], p<0.05). On univariate and multivariable analyses, ACI was not associated with unfavorable outcomes. Older age (aOR 1.04 [1.02-1.07], p<0.001) and presence of HIBI on MRI (aOR 8.41 [3.95-17.88], p<0.001) were associated with unfavorable outcomes on multivariable analysis. ACI was present in nearly a third of patients with cardiac arrest. The most common pattern of ACI was multifocal embolic-appearing, and ACI was associated with chronic white matter lesions. The independent impact of ACI on cardiac arrest survivors' outcomes requires additional investigation in future prospective studies.

articles.title: Psychological outcomes of spouses of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest survivors according to witnessing and cardiopulmonary resuscitation performance: Results from the cross-sectional DANCAS study.
articles.abstract: Spouses often witness out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) and perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), but associations with psychological outcomes remain unclear. The aim was to describe the prevalence of symptoms of anxiety, depression and caregiver strain according to spouses' level of involvement and to investigate associations between involvement and these outcomes. This cross-sectional study used data from spouses participating in the national DANCAS survey. Symptoms of anxiety and depression were assessed using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, and caregiver strain using the Modified Caregiver Strain Index. Associations between involvement and psychological outcomes were investigated using logistic regression models adjusted for sex, age and employment status. Of 461 spouses, 32% (n=148) reported symptoms of anxiety, 10% (n=44) symptoms of depression and 25% (n=115) caregiver strain. The prevalence of symptoms did not differ significantly across the levels of involvement. In adjusted analyses, witnessing OHCA without performing CPR was associated with higher odds of symptoms of depression compared with not witnessing OHCA (OR 3.18 95% CI 1.38-7.35). No statistically significant associations were observed for symptoms of anxiety or caregiver strain. Symptoms of anxiety and caregiver strain were common across all levels of involvement. Witnessing OHCA without performing CPR was associated with higher odds of symptoms of depression, while no other associations were found. These findings suggest that level of involvement alone may be insufficient to identify spouses at risk of psychological distress.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Neurological Outcomes After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Sequential Adjusted Analysis from the JAAM Registry.
articles.abstract: Sex differences in outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remain controversial. We examined sex differences in neurological outcomes after OHCA and explored how the estimated association changed as measured patient, arrest, and treatment characteristics were sequentially included. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from the Japan Association for Acute Medicine OHCA Registry (2014-2022). Adult non-traumatic OHCA patients (≥ 18) were included. The primary outcome was favorable neurological outcome (CPC 1-2) at 1 month, and the secondary outcome was 1-month survival. Sequential logistic regression models adjusted for age, arrest characteristics, bystander interventions, initial shockable rhythm, public-access automated external defibrillator (PAD/AED) use, and advanced treatments. Age-stratified post hoc analyses further evaluated PAD/AED use and initial rhythm. Among 65,346 patients (39,576 men and 25,770 women), women had lower crude 1-month favorable neurological outcomes (2.4% vs. 5.4%; p < 0.01) and 1-month survival (4.5% vs. 8.7%; p < 0.01). The crude odds ratio (OR) for 1-month favorable neurological outcome in women versus men was 0.44 (95% CI, 0.40-0.48), compared with 1.00 (95% CI, 0.89-1.12) in the fully adjusted model. Women aged 18-64 years had better neurological outcomes than men when PAD/AED was used (66.7% vs. 49.0%; p < 0.01) or when the initial rhythm was shockable (37.7% vs. 30.0%; p < 0.01), but these differences diminished with age. Women have poorer crude neurological and survival outcomes after OHCA. However, the association between women and favorable neurological outcomes progressively attenuated with the sequential inclusion of measured factors. The causal contributions of individual factors cannot be determined from this exploratory sequential analysis.

articles.title: Digital twin-based simulation of physiological responses to prone positioning in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
articles.abstract: Digital twin-based simulation, in which a patient-specific counterfactual outcome is constructed from observational data, could enable individualised treatment effect estimation from routinely collected clinical data. Applications in critical care remain scarce, however, and it is unclear how well such methods capture the complex physiological responses to ICU interventions. We adapt an established digital twin framework to simulate multiple short-term physiological effects of prone positioning, an intervention with well-documented effects on oxygenation in mechanically ventilated patients. In this retrospective study using AmsterdamUMCdb, mechanically ventilated patients were separated into a treatment group (first prone positioning event) and control group (no documented proning). Using pre-intervention data, we trained a recurrent neural network-based encoder to learn patient-specific latent representations. For each proned patient, a synthetic twin was constructed as a sparse, weighted mixture of control patients. Treatment effects were estimated as the difference between observed post-proning outcomes and the simulated counterfactual across five signals: PaO2/FiO2 ratio, mechanical power, ventilatory ratio, dynamic compliance, and estimated cardiac output. Simulation fidelity was assessed through placebo testing, and treatment effect heterogeneity was examined by baseline PF ratio. We included 4,935 patients (469 proned, 4,466 never proned). Prone positioning was associated with a significant overall increase in PaO2/FiO2 ratio (ATT: + 51.2 mmHg, 95% CI [41.6, 60.9], p < 0.001), with the largest effect at lower PF ratios (PF < 100 and 100 ≤ PF < 200), and no significant effect at PF ≥ 200. Mechanical power increased (+ 12.6 J/min [11.2, 14.1], p < 0.001) and dynamic compliance decreased (- 26.4 mL/cmH2O [ - 28.9, - 23.8], p < 0.001) across all strata, while ventilatory ratio rose modestly (+ 0.11 [0.04, 0.18], p = 0.002). Estimated cardiac output showed no significant overall effect. Digital twin-based simulation can produce clinically plausible estimates of the multi-outcome physiological effects of prone positioning. The oxygenation findings align with established trial evidence, while the simultaneous characterisation of respiratory and haemodynamic effects illustrates the approach's potential for a more comprehensive understanding of ICU interventions from observational data.

articles.title: A scoping review of large-animal models of oleic acid-induced acute lung injury: a call for standardisation and improved translatability.
articles.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) lacks effective disease-modifying therapies despite decades of preclinical work. Oleic acid-induced acute lung injury (OA-ALI) is one of the oldest and most widely used large-animal models of experimental ALI and reproduces selected early features of human ARDS, yet its implementation, reporting, and reproducibility have never been systematically mapped. We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-compliant scoping review of in vivo large-animal studies using OA to induce ALI. Five databases and two preclinical trial registries were searched from inception to 28 September 2026. Eligible studies were charted for animal characteristics, OA dosing and administration, ventilatory and haemodynamic management, adverse events, and ALI assessment mapped to American Thoracic Society (ATS) domains.
