Reporting completeness of 31 predefined key variables was assessed overall, by species and by period. All eligible studies were considered for the bibliometric analysis (historical cohort), and those published from 2000 onwards in the methodological analysis. Of 3259 records, 546 large-animal OA studies were identified (historical cohort), and 227 studies (3480 animals) published since 2000 were analysed. Pigs accounted for 63% of studies, followed by dogs and sheep; median study duration was 4 h (> 24 h in only 9 studies). Among reporting studies, OA was mostly given via central venous access (80.5%) at a median total dose of 0.1 mL/kg (IQR 0.08-0.12), whereas the vehicle, delivery pattern, dose per bolus and titration strategy varied substantially. Reporting of key methodological variables was frequently incomplete: no study reported all applicable predefined variables, and 186 (81.9%) omitted ≥ 6, although the median proportion of applicable items not reported decreased from 33.3% (2000-2009) to 24.1% (2020-2026). Mortality, adverse events, and vasoactive support during OA administration were reported in only about one in four studies. At study end, ALI was formally assessed in 83.7% of studies, mostly with physiological endpoints rather than histology, barrier, or inflammatory outcomes. Bibliometric analyses showed a long-standing but fragmented literature without dominant reference protocols. Large-animal OA-ALI remains a widely used model of selected early features of ARDS, but incomplete reporting, heterogeneity in key methodological choices, and the absence of widely referenced models in the literature limit reproducibility and translational interpretation. Adoption of standardised reporting practices, broader multidomain ALI assessment aligned with ATS recommendations, and use of the proposed OA-ALI-specific minimal reporting checklist may improve the reproducibility, comparability, and translational value of future studies.

articles.title: Assessment and treatment of pain and sedation in mainland Chinese ICUs: a nationwide web-based survey.
authors: Chinese Analgesia and Sedation Education and Research (CASER) group
articles.abstract: To investigate the current practice and perception of pain, sedation, consciousness, and delirium management in intensive care units (ICUs) in mainland China. The Chinese Analgesia and Sedation Education and Research (CASER) group performed a nationwide online survey. The questionnaire covered respondent demographics, perceived importance of analgesia and sedation, self-reported guideline familiarity, physician-nurse responsibilities, assessment frequency, medications, and real-world analgesia/sedation delivery on the survey day. In total, 4521 valid responses were collected, 2999 from general ICUs and 2926 from physicians. Most respondents regarded pain (88.72%), sedation (89.89%), and consciousness/delirium assessment (85.84%) as important and reported familiarity with relevant guidelines. There was discrepancy in respondent self-reported knowledge of guidelines and their objective performance on test questions. Respondents reported analgesia and sedation were provided routinely at 15.51% and on demand at 70.34%. Physicians dominated treatment decisions. Assessment frequency varied substantially, particularly for consciousness and delirium; 43.37% performed such evaluations only based on clinical status. Opioids were the primary analgesics (87.69%); midazolam (44.57%) and propofol (31.01%) were the leading sedatives. Fewer than half of ICU patients received combined analgesia and sedation on the survey day (48.28%). The perception and practice of pain, sedation, consciousness, and delirium assessment and management among ICU staff in mainland China are heterogeneous and insufficiently standardized. More accurate understanding and rigorous implementation of existing clinical guidelines are urgently needed.

articles.title: Severe leptospirosis in Mayotte (2009-2017): epidemiological, clinical and microbiological characteristics of intensive care unit patients and comparison with other French tropical territories.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract: Leptospirosis is a globally distributed zoonotic disease that may cause severe and life-threatening illness, particularly in tropical regions. The primary objective was to describe severe leptospirosis cases in Mayotte, a French island in the Indian Ocean. Secondary objectives were to characterize the Leptospira strains identified and to compare the findings with data from other French territories. We conducted a retrospective study of adult patients admitted to the ICU of Mayotte Hospital for severe leptospirosis between 2009 and 2017. Leptospirosis was confirmed by a positive PCR targeting the 16S rRNA (rrs) or lipL32 gene in clinical samples, including blood, urine and cerebrospinal fluid. Findings were compared with published data from other French tropical overseas territories and mainland France. During the study period, 55 patients were included, representing 18% of all hospitalized leptospirosis cases. Forty-five patients (82%) were male, with a median age of 44 years (IQR 33-55). Vasopressor support, renal replacement therapy and mechanical ventilation were required in 56%, 56% and 27% of patients, respectively. ICU mortality was 7.3%. Typing was available for 21 isolates and identified predominantly Leptospira borgpetersenii serogroup Mini (n=14), followed by Leptospira interrogans serogroup Pyrogenes (n=4). No L. interrogans serogroup Icterohaemorrhagiae was identified. Severe disease was predominantly associated with L. borgpetersenii serogroup Mini and L. interrogans serogroup Pyrogenes, despite the absence of the serogroup Icterohaemorrhagiae. Despite frequent requirements for organ support, ICU mortality remained low compared with that reported in other French tropical territories and mainland France.

articles.title: Associations of Naples Prognostic Score with Acute Kidney Injury and the Risk of All-Cause Death in Critically Ill Patients with Sepsis: A Retrospective Cohort Study Utilizing MIMIC.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSepsis is a leading cause of death in critically ill patients, and acute kidney injury (AKI) as a common complication further increases mortality. The Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) integrates inflammatory and nutritional markers and shows promise for risk stratification, yet its association with AKI incidence and all-cause death (ACD) in critically ill patients remains poorly characterized. This study evaluates these associations.MethodsWe collected patient data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV), designated AKI as the primary outcome and severe AKI and ACD at 30, 90, and 365 days as secondary outcomes. Multivariate logistic regression (LR) was employed to examine the relationships of NPS with AKI incidence and severity. We constructed multivariate Cox proportional hazards (CPH) models to analyze the relationship of NPS with ACD, and conducted survival analysis utilizing the Kaplan-Meier approach to compare survival outcomes between groups.ResultsThis study included 5680 patients, whose median age was 66.48 (56.47-76.95) years. Among them, 3302 (58.13%) were male. Multivariate LR analysis suggested that each 1-point increase in NPS was associated with higher odds of AKI (odds ratio [OR] 1.194, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.120-1.274, P < .001) and higher odds of severe AKI (OR 1.245, 95% CI 1.181-1.313, P < .001). CPH model analysis suggested that each 1-point increase in NPS was associated with a higher hazard of 30-day mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 1.168, 95% CI 1.089-1.252, P < .001). High-NPS participants had higher odds of AKI, a higher hazard of ACD, and a lower 30-day survival rate.ConclusionIn this MIMIC-IV cohort of critically ill patients with sepsis, higher NPS was associated with higher odds of AKI and severe AKI and a higher hazard of ACD. The incremental prognostic value and clinical utility of this metric can be further validated.

articles.title: Linezolid Use, Platelet Dynamics, and Bleeding Risk in Critically Ill Patients with Advanced Chronic Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract: Linezolid is frequently used in critically ill patients against multidrug-resistant Gram-positive pathogens. In advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD), impaired hepatic clearance may aggravate thrombocytopenia and bleeding, yet data on linezolid in this population remain limited. To evaluate the impact of linezolid therapy on platelet dynamics and bleeding risk in critically ill ACLD patients. Retrospective cohort study (2013-2023) at the ICU, Department of Gastroenterology and Hepatology, Medical University of Vienna, using longitudinal data, multivariate analysis, and propensity score matching (PSM). 246 ICU admissions (223 patients) with ACLD were included, of whom 59 received linezolid. Patients receiving linezolid had lower platelet nadir (36 vs 55.5 G/L, p=0.004), a more pronounced decrease from admission to nadir (57 vs 38.5 G/L, p=0.019), and received more platelet concentrates (40.7% vs. 16%, p <0.001). Severe thrombocytopenia at ICU discharge was more frequent under linezolid (50.8% vs. 33.2%, p=0.015). These differences were no longer significant after PSM. Linezolid was not independently associated with thrombocytopenia at discharge (OR: 2.08 [0.91-4.88], p=0.086) or bleeding events (OR: 1.24 [0.69-2.25], p=0.5). Survival was comparable between groups. Although linezolid was associated with a more pronounced platelet decline and more frequent severe thrombocytopenia, bleeding events were not increased. A clinically relevant effect cannot be excluded given the limited cohort size and wide confidence intervals. Underlying liver disease and critical illness, rather than linezolid, appear to be the main drivers of thrombocytopenia. Prospective studies with therapeutic drug monitoring are warranted to clarify linezolid's hematotoxic effects in ACLD.

articles.title: Reassessing Sleep Scoring in the Critically Ill: Using Hypnodensity to Estimate Inter-Rater Ambiguity.
articles.abstract: Sleep assessment in the critically ill is complicated by atypical electrophysiology and substantial variability in manual scoring. To examine whether probabilistic sleep representations can better capture this ambiguity, we analysed 61 long-duration intensive care unit (ICU) polysomnography recordings scored independently by up to six experts. Inter-rater agreement for categorical sleep staging was low (Cohen's κ: 0.08-0.47), with frequent disagreements across most sleep stages and particularly for REM, which accounted for less than 1% of total sleep. Automated scoring achieved agreement with individual scorers comparable to the highest human-human pairs, despite being trained on non-ICU data. Hypnodensity analysis revealed considerably stronger alignment between manual and automatic scoring than did categorical labels. The median micro-averaged intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) between automatic and manual hypnodensity was 0.72 (IQR: 0.60-0.82), indicating moderate to good agreement. Average cosine similarity (ACS) was higher and less variable across recordings (median 0.80; IQR: 0.74-0.85), reflecting reduced sensitivity to sleep stage distributions. These findings suggest that hypnodensity provides a more robust and potentially informative representation of ICU sleep than discrete staging alone and that automatic hypnodensity can approximate human scoring patterns even under conditions of substantial inter-rater variability. Probabilistic sleep representations may support more reliable characterization of sleep architecture and sleep stage ambiguity in critically ill patients, offering a promising, complementary approach for future ICU sleep research.

articles.title: Flu: Hospital and intensive care admissions up 80% as trusts declare critical incidents.
Outcomes of an Interprofessional Intensive Care In Situ Simulation Program Over a Five-year Period.
articles.journal: Simulation in healthcare : journal of the Society for Simulation in Healthcare
articles.abstract: Translational and in situ simulation activities improve clinical performance, identify latent patient safety threats, and test systems and processes. However, there are few examples of established, sustained translational simulation programs, particularly in intensive care unit (ICU) settings. We collected data on an interprofessional in situ simulation program in a tertiary ICU between February 2021 and December 2025. Educational, quality assurance, feasibility, and sustainability outcomes were assessed. A total of 790 clinicians provided feedback over the 5-year study period. A total of 203 in situ simulation sessions were scheduled, with 168 (82.8%) of these sessions run. The proportion of cancelled sessions decreased steadily from 33.3% in 2021 to 9.1% in 2025 (P = 0.016). Over 99% of respondents felt that in situ simulation training was "very helpful" (86.8%) or "helpful" (13.0%) for their clinical practice. There was no statistically significant difference in participant perceptions between the 7 different scenarios (P = 0.98). There were no reported incidences of participants feeling psychologically unsafe and no episodes of participant refusal. Three new ICU protocols were operationalised, and 5 new cognitive aide, checklist, or algorithm items were actioned. Of tested items, over 94% of respondents recommended their clinical use. Iterative changes were made to protocols, checklist and algorithm items following simulation testing. Over a 5-year period, this program has become embedded in routine clinical operations by demonstrating long-term feasibility and sustainability, high levels of participant satisfaction, and translational impact by focusing on quality assurance initiatives and interprofessional team training.

articles.title: Intensive care for post-surgical nonagenarian and centenarian patients in Australia and New Zealand, 2010-2023.
articles.abstract: Data regarding postoperative intensive care unit admissions for patients older than 90 years are limited. We determined the incidence of intensive care unit admission, in-hospital and long-term mortality, and risk factors for hospital mortality among surgical patients 90 years or older. This registry-based retrospective cohort study used the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Adult Patient Database (2010-2023). A total of 21,195 patients were admitted with a surgical diagnosis, received active treatment, and had known hospital mortality. A sub-cohort of 11,474 patients was used for logistic regression modelling, and 10,459 patients had long-term mortality data. Hospital mortality decreased from 12.6% in 2010 to 8.6% in 2023. The median long-term survival was 31.5 months (95% confidence interval 30.5 to 32.6) for 2018-2023 admissions. Among preoperative factors, male sex (odds ratio 1.58; 95% confidence interval 1.33 to 1.87; P < 0.001) and frailty (odds ratio 1.34 per 1-point increase in Clinical Frailty Scale score, 95% confidence interval 1.25 to 1.43; P < 0.001) correlated with elevated mortality. Elective surgery (odds ratio 0.47, 95% confidence interval 0.38 to 0.58; P < 0.001), planned admissions (odds ratio 0.63, 95% confidence interval 0.52 to 0.77; P < 0.001), interventional cardiology (odds ratio 0.39, 95% confidence interval 0.20 to 0.76; P = 0.006), and orthopaedic procedures (odds ratio 0.77, 95% confidence interval 0.61 to 0.98; P=0.033) correlated with diminished hospital mortality. This binational database study indicated improving mortality outcomes and reasonable long-term survival among nonagenarian and centenarian surgical intensive care unit patients. These findings suggest that clinicians are selecting appropriate surgical candidates, and patient outcomes are improving.

articles.title: Acute Pulmonary Embolism in the ICU: A Twelve-Year Analysis of 195 392 Hospitalizations Across United States Health Systems.
articles.abstract: ImportanceThe intensive care unit (ICU) burden of acute pulmonary embolism (PE) in the United States, and the extent to which social vulnerability shapes outcomes at the critical care level, remain incompletely characterized in the contemporary treatment era.ObjectiveTo evaluate the epidemiology, treatment, and outcomes of acute PE in adults admitted to United States ICUs, with a focus on socioeconomic vulnerability.DesignRetrospective cohort study over 48 calendar quarters (January 2014 to December 2025).SettingUnited States ICUs within the Epic Cosmos electronic health record database.Participants195 392 hospitalizations of 189 663 unique adults admitted to an ICU with a principal billing diagnosis of acute PE.InterventionsNone.Measurements and Main OutcomesThe incidence of ICU hospitalization for acute PE rose from 6.40 to 10.52 per 1000 ICU admissions, an increase of 0.34 per 1000 per year (95% CI 0.31 to 0.37; Poisson rate ratio 1.037 per year). All cause in-hospital mortality was 8.9%; annual mortality declined from 10.5% (2014) to 8.3% (2019), peaked at 9.7% during the pandemic (2021), and settled at 8.5% to 9.0% without returning to the 2019 nadir. The share of hospitalizations with a simplified Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index of 0 was stable at 15.3% to 18.5%, vasopressor use rose from 11.9% to 20.8%, and percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy rose from 2.6% (2016) to 31.2% (2025) of hospitalizations. Mortality rose across Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) quartiles from 8.5% (Quartile 1, least vulnerable) to 10.7% (Quartile 4, most vulnerable); after adjustment for severity, comorbidity, race, rurality, and time, the Quartile 4 odds ratio was 1.24 (95% CI 1.16 to 1.33; c statistic 0.717), robust across four alternative SVI constructions (1.21 to 1.28) and to state level clustering, with an E value of 1.79. Anticoagulation practice transformed, with direct oral anticoagulant use rising from 17.7% to 74.3% and warfarin falling from 60.1% to 4.1%.ConclusionsAcross twelve years, the ICU burden of acute PE grew substantially, in parallel with the adoption of catheter based reperfusion and without growth in the share of lowest risk admissions, and greater socioeconomic vulnerability was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality.

articles.title: Effects of tonicity and composition of intravenous maintenance fluid therapy on sodium and water homeostasis in a porcine model of controlled hemorrhage and resuscitation: a randomized study.
articles.abstract: During perioperative hypovolemic stress, impaired electrolyte-free water excretion may increase the risk of hyponatremia during intravenous maintenance-fluid therapy. Given the clinical relevance of this risk, we compared the effects of three maintenance fluids differing in tonicity and composition on plasma sodium (p-Na) concentrations in a porcine model of controlled hemorrhage and resuscitation. The primary outcome was the change in p-Na from baseline (T1) to study completion (T6). Twenty-four anaesthetized, mechanically ventilated pigs were randomized 1:1:1 to balanced half-isotonic crystalloid (70 mmol/L sodium, 45 mmol/L chloride, 25 mmol/L acetate), balanced isotonic crystalloid (140 mmol/L sodium, 118 mmol/L chloride, 4 mmol/L potassium, 1 mmol/L magnesium, 30 mmol/L acetate), or normal saline (154 mmol/L sodium, 154 mmol/L chloride), each containing 1% glucose and infused at 10 mL/kg/h from sedation (T0) to T6. Hemorrhage began at T2; at resuscitation (T3), pigs received 60% of withdrawn autologous blood and Ringer's acetate equivalent to the remaining 40%. P-Na differed among groups over time (p = 0.001) and was lower with balanced half-isotonic crystalloid than with balanced isotonic crystalloid (p < 0.001) or normal saline (p = 0.006). At T6, 5 of 8 animals receiving balanced half-isotonic crystalloid had developed hyponatremia (p-Na < 135 mmol/L) compared with none receiving balanced isotonic crystalloid and one receiving normal saline. Cumulative fluid balance did not differ among groups; however, sodium and chloride balances increased stepwise from balanced half-isotonic crystalloid to balanced isotonic crystalloid and normal saline, with significant differences between all groups. Hemorrhage caused significant reductions in mean arterial pressure, heart rate, cardiac output, urine flow rate, creatinine clearance, renal blood flow, renal oxygen delivery and consumption, and significantly increased plasma renin and aldosterone concentrations. Lysine-vasopressin concentrations were already elevated at T0. Medullary aquaporin-2 abundance was higher with normal saline than with either balanced solution. In this porcine model of controlled hemorrhage and resuscitation, balanced half-isotonic maintenance fluid therapy lowered p-Na and increased the risk of hyponatremia. Balanced isotonic crystalloid maintained p-Na while avoiding the greater sodium and chloride retention associated with normal saline. These findings support further clinical evaluation of balanced isotonic maintenance fluids during perioperative hypovolemic stress.

articles.title: Opioid administration prior to in-hospital cardiac arrest.
articles.abstract: Opioid administration is common in hospitalised patients. The opioid antagonist naloxone has been proposed as a potential adjunct during cardiopulmonary resuscitation. We aimed to describe opioid exposure within 24 hours before in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) and explore associations with outcomes. Retrospective observational study on all adult (≥18 years) IHCA during 2024 across nine hospitals in southernmost Sweden, registered in the Swedish Registry for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation. Opioid administrations were collected from medical records. Exploratory logistic regressions assessed associations between opioid exposure (any administration and cumulative dose) and return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and 30-day survival, adjusted for age, sex, witnessed IHCA and national early warning score. Opioids were administered within 24 hours preceding IHCA in 108/267 (40%) patients and in 43/267 (16%) patients within the last two hours. Median time from last opioid administration to IHCA was 2.7 hours (IQR 0.5-7.7). Median oral cumulative morphine milligram equivalent dose was 17 mg (IQR 9-30). Naloxone was administered in 6/267 (2%) of IHCA. Opioid administration within 24 hours prior to IHCA was not associated with ROSC (OR 1.03 [95%CI 0.59-1.78, p=0.93]) or 30-day survival (OR 0.98 [95%CI 0.55-1.73], p=0.94). Higher cumulative opioid doses were associated with lower odds of ROSC (OR 0.91 [95%CI 0.83-1.00], p=0.042), but not 30-day survival (OR 0.98 [95%CI 0.90-1.08], p=0.69). Opioid administration within 24 hours preceding IHCA is common, with frequent administrations shortly before cardiac arrest. Further research is warranted investigating a potential role of opioid reversal during IHCA.

articles.title: MRI-Derived Spatial Patterns of Post-Cardiac Arrest Brain Injury Are Associated With Cerebral Oxygenation Dynamics.
articles.abstract: Post-cardiac arrest brain injury (PCABI) varies substantially in severity and anatomical distribution between patients. We evaluated whether anatomically resolved diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI) lesion patterns are associated with cerebral oxygenation following cardiac arrest. We conducted a retrospective study of 24 patients with PCABI who underwent brain MRI and intraparenchymal neuromonitoring. Ischemic lesion burden was quantified as the percentage of tissue with an apparent diffusion coefficient <650×10-6 mm2/s across 164 brain segments. Principal component analysis (PCA) and k-means clustering were used to identify MRI-derived injury patterns for downstream physiological analysis. Brain tissue oxygen tension (PbtO2), intracranial pressure (ICP), and jugular venous oxygen saturation (SjvO2) were analyzed during the first 72 hours after cardiac arrest. Three reproducible MRI-derived injury patterns (i.e., clusters) were identified (n=13, 6, and 5), with progressively greater whole-brain lesion burden from Cluster 1 (10.16% [9.00-11.68]) to Cluster 2 (22.14% [17.83-25.12]) and Cluster 3 (38.40% [30.92-41.45]; p<0.001). Greater whole-brain lesion burden was associated with lower PbtO2 (r=-0.44, p=0.031) and higher SjvO2 (r=0.53, p=0.009), but not ICP (r=0.11, p=0.623). PbtO2 was lower in Cluster 3 than Cluster 1 (16.0±10.6 vs 26.6±9.0 mmHg; p=0.027), whereas SjvO2 was higher in Clusters 2 and 3 than Cluster 1 (both p<0.05). MRI-derived injury patterns differed in global lesion burden, PbtO2, and SjvO2, but not ICP. Greater whole-brain lesion burden was associated with lower PbtO2 and higher SjvO2, whereas no association was observed with ICP. These findings show that the extent and distribution of diffusion-restricted brain injury are linked to distinct cerebral oxygenation profiles after cardiac arrest.

articles.title: Reversed airflow during asynchronous volume controlled mechanical ventilation in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: a physiological observational study.
articles.abstract: Chest compressions during the inspiratory phase of a ventilation can force air out of the lungs, so-called reversed airflow. Human data on this phenomenon during mechanical ventilation are lacking. We aimed to quantify its frequency and magnitude during asynchronous mechanical ventilation in intubated adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients receiving continuous chest compressions. This single-centre descriptive cross-sectional study used prospectively collected data from patients treated by a physician-staffed prehospital team. After tracheal intubation, patients were ventilated with an Oxylog 3000 transport ventilator in volume-controlled mode without positive end-expiratory pressure, during continuous manual chest compressions. Intratracheal pressures recorded via two catheters allowed calculation of airflow and ventilation parameters during the first minute after intubation. Reversed airflow was defined as expiratory airflow during the inspiratory phase of a mechanical breath. Continuous data are reported as median (first-third quartile). Twelve patients were included (median age 68 years [62-75]; 7 [58.3%] male), of whom 5 (41.7%) achieved sustained return of spontaneous circulation. Reversed airflow occurred in 10 (83.3%; 95% CI 55.2-95.3) patients and in 141 of 172 (82.0%; 95% CI 75.6-87.0) analysed ventilations. The median reversed-airflow volume was 61 mL [42-80] per episode. Median ventilation rate was 14 breaths/min [13-16], gross inspiratory tidal volume 324 mL [305-345], minute ventilation 4.8 L/min [3.8-5.9], and peak inspiratory pressure 46 cmH2O [40-52]. Reversed airflow occurred frequently during asynchronous volume-controlled mechanical ventilation with the Oxylog 3000 in intubated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients receiving continuous manual chest compressions. Its physiological and clinical implications require further investigation.

articles.title: Improvement in Peak Oxygen Consumption Following Cardiac Rehabilitation in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest (OHCA) Survivors: A Comparative Study with ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) Patients.
articles.abstract: To investigate the impact of phase II cardiac rehabilitation (CR) on cardiopulmonary fitness in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) survivors and to compare outcomes with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients categorized by Killip classification. This retrospective study was conducted at a tertiary medical center in Taiwan. We included 31 OHCA survivors whose cardiac events occurred between February 1, 2012, and June 30, 2023, and who completed phase II CR with symptom-limited cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) performed before and after CR. For comparison, 78 patients with STEMI were included, comprising 54 with Killip class I-II and 24 with Killip class III-IV. All participants underwent phase II CR, which was scheduled for 36 sessions and consisted of aerobic and resistance training. The primary outcomes were changes in CPET parameters after CR, including peak workload, peak oxygen consumption (V̇O2peak), and percent-predicted V̇O2peak. Paired t tests were used to evaluate within-group changes, and repeated-measures ANOVA was employed to compare between-group differences. OHCA survivors exhibited significant improvements in V̇O2peak (+3.9 mL/kg/min, p < 0.001), peak workload, and percent-predicted V̇O2peak after CR, with a mean improvement of 24.8% in V̇O2peak. These gains were comparable to those seen in STEMI patients across Killip classes. Although OHCA survivors had lower pre-CR V̇O2peak, they demonstrated similar trainability. This study highlights that OHCA survivors can undergo CR and achieve meaningful improvements in cardiopulmonary fitness, comparable to patients with myocardial infarction. These findings support the implementation of structured CR programs in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Association of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Arterial Coupling With Short-Term Prognosis in Patients With Sepsis: A Bedside Echocardiography-Based Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo assess the prognostic value of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion/pulmonary artery systolic pressure (TAPSE/PASP), a noninvasive marker of right ventricular-pulmonary arterial coupling, for 28-day and 90-day mortality in sepsis.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included adults with sepsis who underwent bedside echocardiography within 24 h of ICU admission. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression assessed associations between TAPSE/PASP and mortality. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed 90-day survival.ResultsAmong 360 patients, 107 (29.7%) died within 28 days. TAPSE/PASP was lower in non-survivors than survivors [0.40 (0.33-0.50) versus 0.60 (0.49-0.77) mm/mm Hg; P < 0.001]. After adjustment for age, sex, SOFA score, lactate, septic shock, mechanical ventilation, and NT-proBNP, each 0.1 mm/mm Hg increase in TAPSE/PASP was associated with lower odds of 28-day mortality (OR = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.61-0.93; P = 0.012). TAPSE/PASP alone had an AUC of 0.799 (95% CI: 0.751-0.848), with an optimal cutoff of approximately 0.466 mm/mm Hg. Adding TAPSE/PASP to the clinical model increased the AUC from 0.846 to 0.854 (DeLong P = 0.234); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.842. Higher TAPSE/PASP was associated with a lower 90-day mortality hazard (HR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.71-0.96; P = 0.013). Patients with TAPSE/PASP ≤0.40 mm/mm Hg had lower 90-day survival.ConclusionLower TAPSE/PASP was associated with higher 28-day mortality and a higher 90-day mortality hazard in sepsis. Its addition did not significantly improve clinical-model discrimination. Prospective multicenter validation is needed.

articles.title: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation provides flow, not afterload: reframing left ventricular afterload during peripheral VA ECMO.
Echocardiography in ARDS: beyond imaging, toward bedside decision-making.
Lactate infusion as therapeutic strategy in critically ill patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: RESuscitation of Critically ill patients Using hypErtonic LACtate (RESCUE-LAC) Collaborators
articles.abstract: Administering lactate to critically ill patients or patients undergoing major surgery may improve hemodynamics, reduce intracranial pressure and decrease fluid requirements. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to analyze whether these beneficial effects also translate into mortality reduction. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing lactate infusion against any control in adult patients having critical illness or undergoing major surgery. Primary outcome was mortality at the last reported follow-up. Data on other clinical outcomes (length of stay, survival with good neurological outcome, adverse events), and hemodynamic data (heart rate, blood pressure, cardiac output, fluid balance) were also extracted. A total of ten RCTs with a total of 763 patients were included. All studies investigated hypertonic sodium lactate (HSL), compared against isotonic or hypertonic fluids. Investigated settings included acute cardiovascular care (cardiac and aortic surgery, acute heart failure), severe burn injury and traumatic brain injury. Mortality was similar in all settings but has to be taken as hypothesis generating due to the very low number of trials. We found no difference in other secondary outcomes. Hypertonic sodium lactate did not demonstrate a mortality difference, but administering HSL appeared to be safe, as no adverse events were reported. Overall, our findings have to be considered hypothesis-generating rather than practice changing due to the very small sample size and different populations. International prospective register of systematic reviews, PROSPERO registration no. CRD420251124739.

articles.title: Global variability in ICU sedation practices: Does it matter?
articles.abstract: Sedative and opioid infusions are commonly administered to promote patient comfort and safety, and to facilitate mechanical ventilation of adult patients in the intensive care unit (ICU). Sedation guidelines promote use of the ABCDEF bundle that incorporates an analgesia-first approach, maintains light sedation through protocolization and/or spontaneous awakening trials, avoids benzodiazepines and promotes use of dexmedetomidine (vs. propofol) for patients at high risk for delirium or who are failing spontaneous breathing trials due to agitation. This narrative review identifies substantial variability in the use of the ABCDEF bundle, and the guideline-recommended sedation practices embedded in it, between different ICU populations, ICUs within and across health systems, and between different countries and regions. The application of the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) explains factors influencing this variability including the sedation intervention itself, external influences on the ICU, organization of the ICU, clinician knowledge and experience, and activities needed to sustain change. Strategies to address barriers for implementing evidence-based ICU sedation management and reduce identified global variability are proposed to improve the outcomes of mechanically ventilated adults admitted to the ICU.

articles.title: Metabolomic signatures of augmented renal clearance in traumatic brain injury and aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: A Neuro-Metabolome study.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract: Augmented renal clearance (ARC), defined as a creatinine clearance (CrCl) ≥ 130 mL/min/1.73 m2, occurs commonly in critically ill patients and accelerates elimination of renally cleared drugs, potentially leading to worse outcomes. The underlying mechanisms driving ARC however remain poorly characterized. We aimed to characterize the serum metabolomic signature of ARC in patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI) and aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) to elucidate the underlying pathophysiology and identify candidate biomarkers. In this single-center, cross-sectional analysis of prospectively collected samples, serum samples from the first 50 consecutive eligible patients with TBI or SAH were classified by measured CrCl and analyzed by untargeted chemical isotope labeling LC-MS. Primary findings were defined by fold change and Storey q < 0.25 across 10,503 peak pairs, and associations were re-estimated with age as a continuous covariate. Thirty-two patients (64%) had ARC and were younger than non-ARC patients (median 47 vs. 66 years). In the overall comparison, of 1481 identifiable features, 10 met q < 0.25, including hypoxanthine (higher in ARC). No feature met q < 0.25 in SAH, whereas 52 peak pairs did in TBI, including noradrenaline, metanephrine, and β-hydroxybutyrate. After adjusting for age, twenty annotated metabolites remained significant with less than 20% change in effect size, including, dipeptides, N-acetyl-serine, and homocitrulline. This is the first metabolomic investigation of ARC in neurocritical care. ARC was characterized by reduced circulating levels of nitrogenous solutes, amino acid derivatives and purine metabolites, reflecting enhanced renal clearance within a systemic response to brain injury. These preliminary, diagnosis-stratified findings require validation in larger cohorts to advance biomarker development and targeted therapy.

articles.title: Multivariate and temporal relationships between continuously derived individualized intracranial pressure (iICP) thresholds and multi-modal cerebral physiology in moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract: Current moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) management relies on guideline-based intracranial pressure (ICP) and cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) thresholds to mitigate secondary brain injury. However, these fixed, population-derived targets fail to account for substantial inter- and intra-patient variability in cerebral physiology. Individualized intracranial pressure (iICP) has emerged as a promising personalized physiologic target. Recently, the feasibility of continuous derivation of iICP has been demonstrated. However, the relationship between continuously derived iICP and multimodal cerebral physiology remains unknown. A retrospective exploratory analysis was conducted using high-frequency physiologic data from adult patients with moderate-to-severe TBI enrolled in the Winnipeg Acute TBI database. Continuous iICP estimates were retrospectively derived at 1-minute intervals using a previously described algorithm. Associations between iICP-derived burden and established cerebral physiologic insult burden metrics were evaluated using linear regression analysis. Multivariate physiologic structure was characterized using hierarchical clustering, k-means clustering, and principal component analysis. Temporal relationships were evaluated using cross-correlation, Granger causality, and VARIMA-based impulse response function analyses. A total of 150 patients were included. Compared with conventional guideline-based ICP thresholds, burden above iICP demonstrated stronger associations with cerebrovascular reactivity-based physiologic insult burden. Across clustering and principal component analyses, iICP consistently demonstrated greatest similarity to measures of intracranial dynamics while remaining distinct from both hemodynamic and cerebrovascular reactivity metrics. Temporal analyses revealed limited evidence of reproducible short-term coupling between iICP and individual physiologic parameters. However, impulse response function analyses demonstrated the largest modeled iICP responses following perturbations in MAP and CPP. Continuously derived iICP demonstrated distinct relationships with intracranial dynamics, cerebrovascular reactivity, and cerebral perfusion-related physiology. These findings provide hypothesis-generating physiologic characterization of iICP and support prospective, outcome-linked evaluation of its real-time clinical implementation.

articles.title: Impact of Atrial Fibrillation on the Association Between Shock Index and Trauma Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Trauma remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, with hemorrhagic shock as the most common cause of preventable traumatic death. Shock Index (SI) (heart rate/systolic blood pressure) is a clinical marker of hemodynamic instability associated with an increased risk of massive transfusion, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and mortality. However, SI interpretation may be confounded in patients with atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter ( collectively, AF), whose baseline tachycardia can distort SI values independent of true hemodynamic compromise. This retrospective cohort included adult trauma patients (≥18 y) admitted to a level I trauma center between January 2020 and October 2025. We excluded patients with missing discharge status or vital signs. We determined AF status from admission documentation and prior medical history. Collected variables included age, sex, injury mechanism, Injury Severity Score, and admission SI. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes included hospital and ICU length of stay (LOS). Group comparisons used chi-square and Student's t-tests. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated factors independently associated with mortality; linear regression examined associations between AF, SI, and resource utilization, adjusting for age, sex, Injury Severity Score, mechanism, and SI category. Among 14,553 trauma patients, 1012 (7%) had AF. AF patients were older (median 77 versus 46 y), more often females (48.9% versus 36.2%), and predominantly sustained blunt trauma via ground-level falls (78.1% versus 26.9%; all P < 0.001). AF was not independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio 1.03, 95% confidence interval 0.68-1.57; P = 0.882). SI ≥ 1.30 remained independently associated with mortality in AF patients (adjusted odds ratio 3.73, 95% confidence interval 1.16-11.97; P = 0.027). AF was independently associated with longer hospital LOS (+1.91 d) and ICU LOS (+1.14 d; both P < 0.001). Despite underlying rhythm irregularity, elevated SI remained independently associated with mortality in AF trauma patients. SI can still be used as a diagnostic data point in clinical decision-making for these complex patients.

articles.title: Mineralocorticoid-responsive polyuria and increased urinary sodium excretion associated with voriconazole: a case report.
articles.abstract: Voriconazole (VRCZ) has been associated with renal and adrenal adverse effects, including rare cases of salt-wasting nephropathy. However, the clinical characteristics and underlying mechanisms of VRCZ-associated natriuresis remain incompletely understood.A 48-year-old male with chronic empyema and refractory pneumothorax was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) because of worsening respiratory status. VRCZ therapy was administered from ICU day 1 through day 22. During the third week of ICU admission, his urine output progressively increased, reaching 4,000-6,000 mL/day from ICU day 23 onward. This increase was accompanied by increased urinary sodium excretion. Despite substantial urinary sodium losses and continuous fluid administration, his serum sodium concentration initially remained within the normal range. VRCZ was discontinued on ICU day 23; however, polyuria and increased urinary sodium excretion persisted for several days. On ICU day 23, the active renin concentration was 2.36 pg/mL, and the aldosterone concentration was below 4.0 pg/mL. Fludrocortisone was initiated at 0.05 mg/day on ICU day 26, after which urine output gradually decreased. Fludrocortisone was discontinued on ICU day 43, and polyuria did not recur.This case suggests the presence of a mineralocorticoid-responsive state characterized by marked polyuria and increased urinary sodium excretion during VRCZ therapy. Although a causal relationship between VRCZ exposure and impaired aldosterone production cannot be established, VRCZ may have contributed to reduced mineralocorticoid activity. Clinicians should consider possible mineralocorticoid dysfunction when unexplained polyuria and increased urinary sodium excretion develop during VRCZ therapy, even in the absence of overt hyponatremia.

articles.title: EMPODERA Intervention for Spanish-speaking Latino Caregivers of Critically Ill Oncology Patients: Cultural Adaptation Process.
articles.journal: Journal of pain and symptom management
articles.abstract: Surrogate decision-makers of critically ill patients admitted to intensive care units (ICUs) often experience extreme psychological distress. For Spanish-speaking Latino caregivers, additional socioeconomic and healthcare challenges frequently compound their emotional suffering. The present study aimed to adapt the EMPOWER intervention to address the unique needs of Spanish-speaking Latino caregivers. Mixed-methods, approach to adapt the EMPOWER intervention to EMPODERA, guided by ecological validity and cultural adaptation process models. Spanish-speaking Latino caregivers of ICU patients (n=11), Latino critical care providers (n=7), and mental health providers who treat Latino caregivers (n=5) from one ICU at a comprehensive cancer center in New York City and professional networks across the U.S. and Latin America were recruited. The EMPOWER intervention (Enhancing & Mobilizing the POtential for Wellness & Emotional Resilience) is an ultra-brief intervention originally designed to improve coping and reduce distress in English-speaking surrogates. Analysis of the quantitative and qualitative findings suggest several adaptations including: (1) reduce stigma of assistance for mental health and provide educational materials promoting psychosocial care, (2) offer a resource booklet to address caregivers' social needs, (3) mitigate literacy issues using simple language and visual aids, and (4) include culturally-syntonic metaphors that resonate more effectively with the target audience. Our findings highlighted the significance of making key adaptations of EMPOWER. Feedback suggested the importance of clarifying definitions of concepts, using clear language, and incorporating values to align with Latino cultural values. Key informants also recommended supplementing the intervention with psychoeducational resources to address mental health stigma. Future research is needed to evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of EMPOWER for Latino caregivers.

articles.title: What nurses should not do when managing the PiCCO haemodynamic monitoring system in critically ill adults: A scoping review.
articles.abstract: To map the errors that critical care nurses should avoid when managing the 5 PiCCO system in critically ill adults, trace each error to its supporting sources and classify the type of evidence behind it. Scoping review (Arksey and O'Malley; Levac et al.) reported according to PRISMA-ScR. Records from PubMed (without nursing or age filters, validated against six known sources), Scopus, CINAHL, Cuiden, Dialnet, ENFISPO and SciELO were screened 10 independently by two reviewers; manufacturer documentation was searched, and sources from an earlier search phase were re-assessed. Each item was classified by evidence type. Fifty-eight sources were included: 20 retained from the earlier search phase, 36 from the database searches, one manufacturer document and one nursing article found on a journal website. Thirty-one "Not-to-Do" items were mapped across seven competency domains; 15 configuration and calibration account for 12 items, and two items rest only on indirect evidence. Recalibration should follow clinical need or change in the pulse contour signal rather than a fixed interval. The largest share of the mapped items concerns configuration and calibration, upstream of parameter interpretation; how often these errors occur in practice is unknown. 20.

articles.title: Higher ERAS compliance is associated with shorter hospital stay and lower ICU utilization in a resource-limited healthcare system - a prospective colorectal cohort study.
articles.abstract: ​Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways integrate evidence-based perioperative care to improve recovery after colorectal surgery. Although a compliance threshold of 70-75% has been proposed, outcomes at higher adherence levels remain incompletely characterized, particularly in resource-limited healthcare systems. We aimed to evaluate the achievable compliance and its association with postoperative outcomes in such a setting.This prospective single-center cohort included patients undergoing elective colorectal surgery between 2022 and 2024. Compliance with 20 ERAS elements was assessed in six groups (≤ 75% and 5-percentage-point bands up to 100%). Outcomes included hospital length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU) utilization, morbidity, readmission, and mortality. Unadjusted analyses were supplemented by exploratory multivariable models.Among 338 patients, mean compliance was 89.3%; median LOS was 6 days (interquartile range 5-7). ICU admission occurred in 23.7%, total morbidity in 28.1%, and early morbidity in 16.9%. Higher compliance correlated with shorter LOS (R = - 0.36), lower ICU admission (R = - 0.30), and fewer early complications (R = - 0.19; all p < 0.001). After adjustment, each 5-percentage-point increase in compliance was associated with a 4.8% relative reduction in geometric mean LOS (p = 0.0023) and approximately 5.4 h shorter ICU stay among admitted patients (p = 0.0039). Late complications and readmission showed no statistically significant unadjusted compliance association.High ERAS compliance was achievable in a resource-limited healthcare system. Across the examined compliance groups up to 100%, higher adherence was associated with shorter hospitalization and ICU duration. Morbidity findings were less consistent and did not show uniform additional benefit.

articles.title: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy with delivery at 24-27 weeks' gestation: risk factors and adverse maternal outcomes.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract: Early-onset hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) prior to 34 weeks are associated with significant morbidity and mortality for pregnant patients and their neonates, but HDP with delivery prior to 28 weeks is less well characterized. We sought to identify risk factors and quantify maternal morbidity and mortality for HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks' gestation. This retrospective cohort study used United States births within the Premier Healthcare database between October 2015 and December 2020. Included individuals were 12-55 years old, with birth at 24 weeks' gestation or later. HDP was categorized by gestational age at delivery (24-27, 28-33, 34-36, and ≥37 completed weeks' gestation). We assessed maternal demographic data, clinical characteristics, and adverse pregnancy outcomes, including mortality, severe maternal morbidity (SMM), intensive care unit (ICU) admission and readmission. Multivariable logistic regression estimated associations between candidate risk factors and HDP stratified by gestational age at delivery; results are reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Multivariable logistic regression estimated the association of each gestational-age subgroup of HDP with adverse pregnancy outcomes. Separate models were built using distinct reference groups including 1) no HDP and 2) HDP at or beyond 37 weeks' gestation. Of 4,666,784 births, 546,962 (11.7%) had an HDP. Of those with HDP, 5,797 (1.1%, 0.1% of all births) delivered at 24-27 weeks, 35,237 (6.4%, 0.8% of all births) delivered at 28-33 weeks, and 413,657 (75.6%, 8.9% of all births) delivered after 37 weeks. Risk factors common across gestational age subtypes of HDP included chronic hypertension, chronic kidney disease, pregestational diabetes, pre-existing cardiac disease, body mass index (BMI) ≥40 kg/m2, use of assisted reproductive technology, and age ≥40 years. Risk factors most associated with HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks were chronic hypertension (aOR 11.45, 95%CI 10.85-12.08), chronic kidney disease (aOR 4.88, 95%CI 4.24-5.62), and antiphospholipid antibody syndrome [APLS] (aOR 4.51, 95%CI 3.46-5.87). Multiple pregnancy and pregestational diabetes were most associated with HDP with delivery at 28-33 weeks (aOR 7.48, 95%CI 7.27-7.69 and aOR 3.06, 95%CI 2.95-3.17). BMI ≥40 kg/m2 was most associated with HDP with delivery at ≥37 weeks (aOR 2.33, 95%CI 2.29-2.36). HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks had the highest rate of SMM (616 per 10,000 births [95%CI 556-681] vs 26/10,000 [95%CI 25-26] and 77/10,000 [95%CI 74-80] among those with no HDP and HDP with delivery at ≥37 weeks, respectively). The odds of SMM and ICU admission were highest among those with HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks. Maternal mortality was rare, but occurred most frequently in those with HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks (121 per 100,000 births [95%CI 49-249] vs 5/100,000 [95%CI 4-5] and 7/100,000 [95%CI 5-10] among those with no HDP and HDP with delivery at ≥37 weeks, respectively). HDP with delivery at 24 to 27 weeks' gestation occurred in 0.1% of all pregnancies and was associated with disproportionately high SMM compared to HDP with delivery at ≥37 weeks. Risk factors for HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks may differ from those for HDP with delivery later in gestation, particularly HDP at term.

articles.title: When AI gets CPR wrong: why clinicians must stay in the loop.
When better reporting cannot solve the wrong question: Rethinking the diagnostic role of AKI biomarkers.
A narrative framework for breaking bad news in intensive care: The Shakespearean tragedy approach.
articles.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
articles.abstract: Approximately 20% of patients admitted to UK Intensive Care Units die during admission, frequently following sudden devastating illness in previously well individuals. Families are often psychologically unprepared, and communication failures remain a common source of complaint and moral distress. Formal end-of-life communication training is inconsistently embedded within UK postgraduate medical education. Drawing on narrative medicine, adult learning and narrative transportation theory, and informed by over a decade of faculty experience on the NHS Blood and Transplant National Deceased Donation Simulation Course, we developed a structured ICU-specific framework for breaking bad news: the Shakespearean Tragedy Approach (STA). Free-text feedback from 287 delegates across 22 course deliveries at 7 UK centres (September 2022-March 2026) was analysed using a directed content analysis approach to assess the acceptability of the approach as taught. The STA structures end-of-life conversations into a Prologue, three Acts and an Interval, grounded in Freytag's dramaturgical arc and supported by an ABCDE communication mnemonic, with consideration of organ donation embedded as an integral component of ICU end-of-life care. Directed content analysis identified eight themes. The most prevalent themes were the adoption and intended clinical application of the taught communication techniques (63%) and early specialist nurse integration into EOL conversations (33%). One delegate (<1%) raised concerns regarding protocolisation and early SNOD involvement. The Shakespearean Tragedy Approach provides a theory-informed, narrative-driven framework tailored to the time-pressured and family-centred realities of intensive care, with evidence of acceptability to senior ICU resident doctors.

articles.title: Electrolyte deficiencies in adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit: a narrative review.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract: Electrolyte deficiencies and their treatment are ubiquitous in patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). We sought to conduct a narrative review of hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia, hypophosphatemia, and hypokalemia in critical care. We searched Ovid MEDLINE®, Embase®, Cochrane CENTRAL, and reference lists for information relevant to the physiology, epidemiology, and treatment of electrolyte deficiencies in adults with critical illness. We also looked for information about financial costs and environmental impact of treatment. Electrolyte deficiencies are common in patients admitted to the ICU, with prevalences of 55-88% for hypocalcemia, 27-66% for hypomagnesemia, 15-53% for hypophosphatemia, and 17-50% for hypokalemia. Neuromuscular and cardiovascular symptoms are common to all four deficiencies, and the benefits and harms of routine or protocolized treatment are uncertain. Calcium replacement is potentially fraught, with possible harm in cardiac arrest data, lack of any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating replacement, and difficulties diagnosing deficiency outside of ionized calcium measurement. Prophylactic magnesium administration may prevent postoperative atrial fibrillation in patients undergoing cardiac surgery, but whether protocolized replacement reduces atrial fibrillation or mortality in patients with critical illness without cardiac problems is uncertain. Phosphate replacement may be relevant to ventilator weaning and ICU-acquired weakness, owing to its physiologic role in cellular energy and available clinical data. Potassium replacement has been investigated in large observational studies and an RCT, indicating that higher thresholds are not superior to lower ones. Enteral replacement is associated with lower costs and less environmental impact compared with the intravenous route. Electrolyte deficiencies and their treatment are common in adult patients admitted to the ICU. The impact of particular thresholds and dosing strategies for treatment on patient outcomes, resource use, and the environment remain important areas for future research.

articles.title: High-PEEP ventilation is associated with pulmonary injury, inflammatory changes, and hippocampal cellular alterations after experimental ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) frequently require mechanical ventilation during intensive care. Although experimental evidence suggests that injurious ventilation may amplify neuroinflammation, the effects of different ventilatory strategies on blood-brain barrier (BBB)-related molecular markers and glial responses after AIS remain poorly understood. We hypothesized that increasing levels of positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) would modulate cerebral inflammation after AIS and would be associated with BBB alterations, glial remodeling, and hippocampal injury. Twenty-four male Wistar rats were subjected to focal AIS induced by thermocoagulation of pial vessels. After 24 h, the animals were mechanically ventilated for 2 h as follows: tidal volume, 6 mL/kg; FiO2, 0.25 at different PEEP levels (3 cmH2O, 9 cmH2O, or 11 cmH2O). Arterial blood gases, mean arterial pressure (MAP) and lung mechanics were assessed at baseline and at the end of ventilation. Plasma, cerebrospinal fluid, lungs, and brains were collected for molecular, histologic, and immunohistochemical analyses. MAP did not differ among groups throughout the experiment. PEEP 11 cmH₂O resulted in higher transpulmonary peak and plateau pressures than the lower-PEEP groups and in higher transpulmonary driving pressure, particularly compared with PEEP 3 cmH₂O. Higher PEEP was associated with increased pulmonary inflammation, endothelial injury markers, and alveolar heterogeneity. In plasma, circulating interleukin (IL)-1β (p = 0.014) and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α (p = 0.011) were higher in the PEEP 11 cmH2O group compared with PEEP 3 cmH2O group. In the brain, high PEEP increased cerebral IL-1β and TNF-α, reduced ZO-1 expression, and lowered hippocampal neuronal density. Morphometric analysis further demonstrated astrocytic and microglial remodeling within the hippocampus. MAP did not associate with cerebral biomarkers, while PEEP showed a positive correlation with cerebral TNF-α expression (r = 0.56, p = 0.02). High-PEEP ventilation intensified pulmonary and cerebral inflammatory responses after experimental AIS and was associated with reduced expression of a key BBB junctional protein, glial remodeling, and reduced hippocampal NeuN-positive neuronal density.

articles.title: Out of hospital cardiac arrest following low voltage electrical injury with complete neurological recovery.
articles.abstract: Low voltage electrical injuries are generally associated with minimal or no external burns but may cause severe injury, fatal cardiac arrhythmias and respiratory arrest depending on length of exposure, size of individual, environmental humidity and the cross-sectional area in contact with electrical source. Complete neurological recovery after prolonged resuscitation is uncommon. We report a case of 22 years old male who sustained low voltage electrical injury culminating in out of hospital cardiac arrest. He brought to the emergency department within 10 min after the incident. With initial rhythm of asystole. High quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation started immediately according to advanced cardiac life support guideline; the rhythm converted from asystole to ventricular fibrillation after third cycle of resuscitation requiring three defibrillation attempts. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved at the end of eighth cycle of resuscitation. Subsequently the patient admitted to intensive care unit and post cardiac arrest care were continued which includes mechanical ventilatory support, hemodynamic support, seizure management, fever prevention. The patient showed progressive neurological improvement and discharged home after three days of stay in intensive care unit with complete neurological recovery. This case shows the critical importance of immediate transport to the hospital, early high-quality CPR and comprehensive post cardiac arrest care for patient survival.

articles.title: Association Between Initial Mechanical Power and 28-Day Mortality in Invasively Ventilated Patients: a Retrospective Cohort Study in a Mixed Latin American ICU.
articles.abstract: Background and AimsMechanical power integrates multiple ventilatory variables into a single measure of energy transferred to the respiratory system and has been associated with mortality in critically ill patients. However, evidence from Latin America remains scarce, and no previous large cohort from the region has directly compared mechanical power with driving pressure. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between initial mechanical power and 28-day mortality, and to compare its prognostic performance with driving pressure in a mixed intensive care unit in Latin America.Patients and MethodsA retrospective cohort study included adult patients who required invasive mechanical ventilation for at least 24 h between January and December 2024 in a tertiary care teaching hospital. Mechanical power was calculated from first-24-h ventilatory parameters obtained during controlled ventilation. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Discriminative performance was assessed with ROC analysis, survival with Kaplan-Meier curves, and independent associations with Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, APACHE II, and SOFA scores.ResultsA total of 496 patients were included; 28-day mortality was 28.4%. Mechanical power was significantly higher in non-survivors than in survivors (18.84 [13.21-23.53] vs 13.93 [10.73-18.06] J/min; P < .001). Discriminative performance was moderate (AUC 0.67; 95% CI 0.62-0.73) and higher than that of driving pressure (AUC 0.61; DeLong P = .025). Patients with mechanical power ≥17 J/min had lower survival (Log-rank P < .001). In the joint Cox model, mechanical power remained independently associated with mortality (HR 1.03; 95% CI 1.02-1.05), whereas driving pressure did not.ConclusionsInitial mechanical power was independently associated with 28-day mortality and provided modest incremental prognostic information compared with driving pressure in this Latin American cohort. These findings are exploratory and require external validation in larger multicenter studies.

articles.title: Telehealth to Support Coordinated Spontaneous Awakening and Breathing Trials in Invasive Ventilation: The TEACH Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Coordinated spontaneous awakening trials and spontaneous breathing trials (C-SAT/SBT) improve outcomes for patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation, but implementation remains inadequate. To evaluate whether a telehealth intervention added to a standard audit and feedback implementation of C-SAT/SBT increases adherence and improves outcomes compared with standard audit and feedback implementation alone (control). A cluster randomized type 2 hybrid effectiveness-implementation clinical trial was conducted in 12 Intermountain Health hospitals in Utah and Idaho. Patients aged 16 years or older who were intubated and mechanically ventilated in the intensive care unit were enrolled from December 1, 2022, until July 31, 2025, with last follow-up on January 23, 2026. Telehealth hospitals received real-time oversight from telecritical care nurses and respiratory therapists for adherence to C-SAT/SBT and a standard audit and feedback implementation. Control hospitals received only standard audit and feedback. Co-primary outcome measures were adherence to C-SAT/SBT and ventilator-free days to day 28. C-SAT/SBT was defined as any day that the SAT and SBT were separately adherent, and the SAT followed the SBT within 2 hours or both occurred before noon, or the patient was extubated. Change in adherence from baseline was compared between groups using a mixed-effects logistic model with prespecified 1-sided significance testing. Change in ventilator-free days was compared using a mixed-effects proportional odds model. There were 4544 patients at telehealth hospitals, 6438 patients at control hospitals, and 1789 preimplementation common baseline patients (median [IQR] age, 62 [47-71] years; 4826 [37.8%] female). The baseline C-SAT/SBT adherence rate of 43.9% increased to 90.3% at telehealth intervention hospitals and to 77.6% at control hospitals (odds ratio for change in telehealth vs change in control, 2.87; 1-sided 95% lower confidence limit, 2.44; P < .001; absolute difference, 11.4%; 95% CI, 8.8%-14.3%). Median (IQR) ventilator-free days from a common baseline of 24 (0-26) increased to 25 (10-27) at telehealth intervention hospitals and 25 (1-27) at control hospitals (odds ratio for change in telehealth vs change in control, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.01-1.45, P = .04; absolute difference, 1.02 days; 95% CI, 0.05-1.96 days). Among adults intubated and mechanically ventilated in the intensive care unit, adding real-time telehealth support for C-SAT/SBT improved adherence and increased ventilator-free days more than a standard audit and feedback implementation alone. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05141396.

articles.title: Comparing Heart Rate Variability Upon Admission to Intensive Care Unit Between Moderate-Severe Traumatic Brain Injury and Orthopedic Controls: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is associated with autonomic dysfunction measurable through heart rate variability (HRV). Although reduced HRV during prolonged monitoring has been associated with poor outcomes following TBI, comparisons with other forms of traumatic injury remain limited. We conducted an exploratory prospective cohort study of adults with moderate-severe TBI (msTBI) and isolated severe orthopedic trauma controls enrolled at a single institution from 2020 to 2024. Continuous cardiac telemetry was collected during the first 15 minutes of intensive care unit (ICU) admission. HRV metrics included standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN), root-mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), percentage of successive normal-to-normal intervals differing by >50 ms (pNN50), and low-frequency to high-frequency power ratio (LF/HF). Clinical outcomes including pneumonia, sepsis, infection, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and acute kidney injury were assessed during the first week of hospitalization. Among 94 patients (51 msTBI; 43 orthopedic controls), time-domain HRV measures were significantly reduced in the majority of msTBI patients compared with published normative values. In adjusted analyses, SDNN was similar across groups (mean difference: 27.0, 95% CI: -3.8 to 57.9, P=0.086). RMSSD, pNN50, and LF/HF were also similar. Within the msTBI cohort, HRV metrics were not associated with first-week clinical outcomes or hospital mortality. In this exploratory study, early HRV abnormalities following trauma may reflect autonomic impairment, but measurements immediately upon ICU admission may not capture evolving msTBI-specific dysfunction. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to draw definitive conclusions regarding clinically meaningful autonomic changes and associations with msTBI outcomes.

articles.title: Association of Early Autonomic Dysfunction with Cerebral and Systemic Hemodynamics in Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract: Autonomic dysfunction is prevalent after severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI) and associated with poor outcomes. Heart rate variability (HRV) reflects the dynamic balance between sympathetic and parasympathetic autonomic activity and can be readily examined using bedside cardiac waveforms. The relationship between autonomic dysfunction and cerebral perfusion is underexplored. We aimed to characterize the relationship between early autonomic dysfunction and cerebral and systemic hemodynamics after sTBI. We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients enrolled in the BOOST-3 clinical trial with available cardiac and intracranial pressure (ICP) waveform data. Time-varying standard deviation of normal-normal intervals (SDNN) at 5-min resolution over the first 24 h postinjury was calculated. Cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) was calculated from dynamic ICP and mean arterial blood pressure (MAP) measurements. The association between time-varying SDNN, cerebral hemodynamics, and systemic hemodynamics was examined with moving correlation analysis and time-lagged linear mixed-effects models. Among 341 patients, the mean (SD) age was 41.8 (17.0) years, and 273 (80.1%) patients were male. Median (IQR) initial Glasgow Coma Scale score was 6 (4-7). On moving correlation analysis, lower SDNN correlated with lower CPP (peak r = 0.52 at 119 h postinjury, p < 0.001) over the first 5 days postinjury. In time-lagged models, lower SDNN was associated with lower MAP (peak standardized β = 0.019, p < 0.001) and lower CPP (peak standardized β = 0.025, p < 0.001) intermittently over 12 lag hours. Early autonomic dysfunction after sTBI is associated with intermittently lower MAP and lower CPP in the subsequent 12 h. These results link early postinjury autonomic activity to altered hemodynamics and support further investigation of HRV in this population.

articles.title: Clozapine Intoxication: What Can We Learn from Case Reports? A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Clozapine remains the gold standard for treatment resistant schizophrenia; however, the complex pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties makes clozapine susceptible to interactions and thus increase the risk of intoxications. By reviewing published case reports on acute clozapine intoxications, we aimed to identify clinical scenarios, risk factors and trajectory outcomes, to recommend potentially preventable measures. We systematically searched PubMed and Embase and included all published articles describing cases with acute intoxication in adults (18-64 years) by using the ICD-10 definition of acute intoxication. Furthermore, a description of increases in clozapine dose or plasma levels should be evident (or suspected) for inclusion. Case reports were categorized exclusively in one of the following groups: 'drug-drug interactions', 'intentional overdose', 'infection/inflammation', 'smoking cessation', 'unintentional overdose' and 'other'. Eighty-seven studies were included, resulting in 100 case reports. The largest group was intentional overdose with 35 cases (35.0%), followed by infection/inflammation 22 (22.0%), drug-drug interactions 18 (18.0%), other 13 (13.0%), smoking cessation 8 (8.0%) and lastly unintentional overdose 4 (4.0%). Overall, 34 cases (34.0%) required intensive care while 35 (35.0%) required medical hospitalization (non-intensive care). Two cases had a fatal outcome. Maximum survived clozapine plasma level was 9476 ng/mL and the highest survived ingested dose was 12.5 g. The most common intoxication symptoms were sedation, confusion and tachycardia. The major finding of this review is that clozapine-induced intoxications can be life-threatening, illustrated by 2 fatal cases and 34 cases (34.0%) receiving treatment in an intensive care unit. This points out that clozapine intoxications should be taken seriously, and preventable measures should be taken whenever possible.

articles.title: Zinc supplementation in adults with sepsis and septic shock: a double-blind randomized trial.
articles.abstract: Sepsis and septic shock remain major causes of morbidity and mortality in intensive care units (ICUs). Zinc deficiency is common in critically ill patients and may contribute to immune dysregulation, inflammation, and organ dysfunction. However, evidence regarding zinc supplementation in sepsis remains limited. This study aims to evaluate the clinical effects of early oral zinc supplementation in adults with sepsis or septic shock and low serum zinc concentrations. In this prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial, 60 adults with Sepsis-3 sepsis or septic shock and low serum zinc concentrations were randomized (1:1) to receive oral zinc sulfate (50 mg elemental zinc daily) or matching placebo until ICU discharge or death. The primary outcome was total hospital length of stay (LOS). Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, ICU LOS, vasopressor duration, acute kidney injury, need for renal replacement therapy, duration of invasive mechanical ventilation, inflammatory biomarkers, and serial Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores. Analyses were performed on an intention-to-treat basis, including competing-risk analyses accounting for in-hospital death. Overall mortality was 23.3% in the zinc group and 36.7% in the placebo group (risk ratio 0.64; 95% CI 0.29-1.42; p = 0.260). Total hospital LOS was shorter with zinc supplementation (median [IQR] 9.0 [7.75-12.5] vs 14.0 [10.0-16.25] days; p = 0.006), including among patients with septic shock (10.0 [8.0-11.5] vs 15.0 [11.0-20.0] days; p = 0.004). ICU LOS did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.304). Competing-risk analyses accounting for in-hospital death and baseline prognostic factors did not demonstrate an independent association between zinc supplementation and earlier discharge alive. No consistent treatment-related improvements were observed in mortality, organ dysfunction, inflammatory biomarkers, or other secondary outcomes. Early oral zinc supplementation in adults with sepsis or septic shock and low serum zinc concentrations was associated with shorter unadjusted hospital LOS; however, this association was not confirmed in adjusted competing-risk analyses. Zinc supplementation did not significantly improve mortality or other major clinical outcomes. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger multicenter randomized trials. Trial registration: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT), IRCT20210519051348N2, prospectively registered on February 3, 2025.

articles.title: Intravenous dapagliflozin did not induce ketogenesis or improve cardiac and skeletal muscle function in resuscitated murine sepsis.
articles.abstract: Randomized controlled trials have shown benefits of temporary caloric restriction in acute critical illness, attributed partially to activated ketogenesis. Ketone-ester administration has been associated with improved hemodynamics in cardiogenic-shock and heart-failure patients, and with improved skeletal muscle function in septic mice. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors improve chronic heart failure outcomes, possibly partially through enhanced ketogenesis. We hypothesized that intravenous dapagliflozin activates ketogenesis and improves cardiac and skeletal muscle function in murine sepsis, particularly during intermittent fasting. First, in a dose-finding study, 12 healthy catheterized mice were randomized to placebo or dapagliflozin 1 or 10 mg/kg/day for 5 days. Second, 59 septic mice were randomized to placebo or dapagliflozin 10 mg/kg/day for 3 or 5 days. Sepsis was induced by cecal ligation and puncture; mice received fluids, antibiotics, analgesics, and (from day 1) continuous parenteral nutrition (PN). Third, we randomized 18 septic mice to placebo or dapagliflozin 10 mg/kg/day for 3 days during intermittent fasting, induced by withholding PN for 9 h/day. We performed echocardiography before sacrifice on day 3; extensor digitorum longus muscle force was assessed ex vivo on day 5. Untreated mice served as healthy reference (n = 30). Glucosuria, blood glucose, plasma 3-hydroxybutyrate (3HB), and myocardial metabolic gene expression were assessed. We studied Spearman correlation between plasma 3HB and echocardiographic markers. In healthy catheterized mice, both dapagliflozin doses induced glucosuria (405 [296-500] and 500 [390-500] versus 60 [47-98] mg/dL; P = 0.010 and P = 0.028) without hypoglycemia. Dapagliflozin induced glucosuria in septic mice (day 5: 376 [244-600] versus 0 [0-0] mg/dL; P < 0.001) without affecting survival. With continuous PN, dapagliflozin did not increase 3HB, nor improve cardiac or skeletal muscle function. During intermittent fasting, it lowered blood glucose (53 [41-56] versus 70 [61-78] mg/dL; P = 0.027) without increasing 3HB or improving cardiac function. Myocardial mitochondrial oxidation genes were generally suppressed by sepsis without consistent dapagliflozin effects. 3HB correlated positively with ejection fraction, stroke volume and cardiac output. Dapagliflozin provoked glucosuria, but did not induce ketogenesis, nor improve cardiac or skeletal muscle function in septic mice, regardless of nutritional strategy. Future research should assess alternative strategies that enhance ketone availability.

articles.title: Adverse perinatal outcomes associated with increasing birthweight among U.S. births complicated by diabetes.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract: Macrosomia is increasing in prevalence globally and is more common among pregnancies complicated by diabetes. There are limited data regarding the risks with increasing degrees of birthweight above 4,000 grams among births complicated by diabetes. We sought to evaluate the association between increasing birthweight above 4,000 grams and adverse outcomes among births complicated by diabetes, stratified by diabetes type (preexisting and gestational diabetes). This was a retrospective cohort study of singleton, non-anomalous, U.S. live births to persons with diabetes between 37- and 42-weeks' gestation from years 2012 to 2021 utilizing data from the National Center for Health Statistics. Births of infants weighing at least 3000 grams were included and stratified into four increasing weight categories: 4,000-4,499 grams, 4,500-4,999 grams and ≥5,000 grams with 3,000-3,999 grams serving as the reference group. Maternal outcomes included mode of delivery, obstetric anal sphincter injuries, gestational hypertension, eclampsia, admission to the intensive care unit (ICU), and need for blood transfusion. Neonatal outcomes included Apgar score <7 at 5 minutes, neonatal ICU admission, assisted ventilation, seizures, and infant death. Chi-squared and multivariable Poisson regression analyses were performed for statistical comparisons and presented as adjusted incidence risk ratios (aRR).
