Adverse events, mechanical ventilation duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay did not differ significantly between groups. In this single-center trial, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine was associated with lower postoperative hs-cTnT and CK-MB concentrations, better subjective preoperative sleep quality, and a lower observed incidence of postoperative delirium. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trials to determine whether the biomarker reductions translate into clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefits. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500111431.

articles.title: Mechanical insufflation-exsufflation for clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of respiratory therapy : CJRT = Revue canadienne de la therapie respiratoire : RCTR
articles.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of mechanical insufflation-exsufflation (MI-E) compared with usual care in mechanically ventilated critically ill adults. # Methods We searched Embase, MEDLINE via PubMed, CINAHL, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to April 2026 that compared MI-E with usual care in mechanically ventilated adults. The primary outcome was duration of mechanical ventilation. Secondary outcomes included the amount of aspirated airway secretions, respiratory system compliance, airway resistance, length of ICU stay, and mortality. Meta-analysis was performed when at least two studies provided clinically and methodologically comparable data. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. # Results Six RCTs involving 492 participants were included. For the primary outcome of mechanical ventilation duration, only one RCT contributed to the effect estimate (MD, -2.67 days; 95% CI, -6.91 to 1.57; very-low-certainty evidence). MI-E increased the amount of aspirated airway secretions compared with usual care (MD, 1.47 g; 95% CI, 0.74 to 2.19; very-low-certainty evidence). No statistically significant differences were observed in respiratory system compliance or airway resistance. ICU length of stay also showed no difference (2 RCTs; MD, -1.75 days; 95% CI, -4.61 to 1.10; very-low-certainty evidence). Mortality was evaluated by one RCT (risk ratio, 1.56; 95% CI, 0.44 to 5.50; very-low-certainty evidence). # Conclusions The effects of MI-E on clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients remain uncertain because the available evidence is of low to very low certainty. MI-E may improve airway secretion clearance; however, evidence regarding mechanical ventilation duration, ICU length of stay, and mortality remains very uncertain. Further high-quality randomized controlled trials are required.

articles.title: Global trends and emerging frontiers in neutrophil extracellular trap-related sepsis research: a bibliometric analysis.
articles.abstract: Sepsis remains a major challenge in critical care medicine, and NETs have emerged as important regulators linking inflammation, immunity, coagulation, and tissue injury. However, the global development trajectory and research frontiers of NET-related sepsis studies remain unclear. Publications related to NET-related sepsis research from 2004 to September 19, 2026, were independently retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus databases. After database-specific screening, 263 WoSCC records and 499 Scopus records were retained for separate analyses using VOSviewer and CiteSpace to evaluate publication trends, collaboration networks, knowledge structures, thematic evolution, and emerging research attention. The WoSCC and Scopus analytical datasets contained 263 and 499 records, respectively. WoSCC analysis showed that China had the highest publication output, whereas the United States had the highest citation impact and collaboration strength among the listed countries. Cleaned author-keyword analysis highlighted sepsis, neutrophil extracellular traps, NETosis, inflammation, neutrophil, platelet, acute lung injury, and septic shock. Cross-database comparison showed a high correlation in complete-year publication trends (Spearman's ρ = 0.986) and partial overlap in high-frequency author keywords. Independent database analyses indicate sustained growth and a progressively interconnected knowledge structure in NET-related sepsis research. The results describe publication, collaboration, citation, and thematic attention patterns; they do not establish biomarker performance or therapeutic efficacy. Future studies may benefit from standardized NET measurement and reporting, multicenter validation of NET-related biomarkers and predictive models, and appropriately designed clinical investigations.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of sivelestat in sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome: an updated meta-analysis based on disease severity and treatment strategy subgroups.
articles.abstract: Sivelestat sodium hydrate is a selective neutrophil elastase inhibitor that attenuates neutrophil-mediated alveolar-capillary injury and is used in some East Asian countries for acute lung injury/ARDS. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of sivelestat in sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and explored whether disease severity, baseline mortality risk, and treatment background modify the mortality effect. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and ClinicalTrials.gov from database inception to August 27, 2026. Eligible studies were adult studies of sepsis-induced ARDS comparing a sivelestat-containing regimen with an otherwise comparable regimen without sivelestat. COVID-19-only cohorts, non-septic ARDS, mixed-etiology studies without a separable sepsis subgroup, and comparisons in which both groups received sivelestat were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included P/F ratio, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, organ-function scores, inflammatory markers, and adverse events. Mortality was pooled as odds ratios (ORs) using a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood; Hartung-Knapp intervals were used for the primary and study-design analyses. This review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO. Fourteen studies were eligible for qualitative synthesis, and 10 studies (943 patients) provided extractable 2 × 2 mortality data. Deaths occurred in 73/431 patients receiving sivelestat and 125/512 controls. Sivelestat was associated with lower mortality (OR=0.55, 95% CI 0.36-0.84; I2 = 0%). The signal persisted in randomized trials (OR=0.37, 95% CI 0.16-0.86; I2 = 0%). Study-level point estimates appeared more favorable in cohorts with baseline P/F < 100 mmHg and control mortality >30%; however, interaction tests were not statistically significant and severity analyses were ecological. Leave-one-out analyses were stable. Egger testing did not detect significant small-study asymmetry (P = 0.197), although power was limited. Baseline-stratified treatment effects by IL-6, PCT, CRP, or neutrophil elastase were unavailable for quantitative effect-modification analyses. In an updated and etiologically strict evidence synthesis, sivelestat was associated with lower mortality in sepsis-induced ARDS, including in randomized trials. Severe hypoxemia and high baseline risk remain plausible enrichment factors, but current aggregate evidence is insufficient to support a validated phenotype-guided prescribing rule. Co-intervention reporting was sparse, and residual confounding by prone positioning, sedation, neuromuscular blockade, and steroid background cannot be excluded. PROSPERO CRD420261541158.

articles.title: Ventilator care bundles in adult ICUs: a systematic review and meta-analysis of ventilator-associated pneumonia risk and incidence density.
articles.abstract: Ventilator care bundles are used to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but differences in outcome denominators and study design complicate interpretation. We examined patient-level VAP risk and ventilator-time incidence density separately. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Web of Science were searched from inception on 11 August 2026. Eligible bundles contained at least three clinical practices for adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation in ICUs. Nonconcurrent before-after comparisons were pooled separately for VAP risk ratios (RRs) and incidence rate ratios (IRRs). Comparisons with unclear timing, randomized results, and segmented interrupted time-series results were presented separately. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood and Knapp-Hartung intervals, with modified Knapp-Hartung sensitivity analyses. ROBINS-I and GRADE assessed bias and certainty. Twenty-three non-randomized study families contributed to the primary meta-analyses; 22 contributed VAP data. Bundle implementation was associated with lower VAP risk (14 studies; n = 5,905; RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.51-0.76; I2 = 9.0%; prediction interval 0.47-0.82). The pooled incidence rate ratio was 0.55 (12 studies; 95% CI 0.41-0.73; I2 = 79.9%), but the prediction interval included the null (0.25-1.22). ICU length of stay (3 studies; MD -2.53 days, 95% CI -7.59 to 2.53) and mechanical ventilation duration (2 studies; MD -3.64 days, 95% CI -13.96 to 6.69) remained uncertain. All pooled estimates were at serious risk of bias. Certainty was low for VAP risk and very low for the other pooled outcomes. Nonconcurrent comparisons associated bundle implementation with lower reported VAP risk, with low certainty. Incidence-density associations varied across settings, and evidence for ICU length of stay and ventilation duration was very uncertain. Evaluations with independent concurrent controls, stable surveillance, and adherence monitoring are needed. PROSPERO (CRD420261484358).

articles.title: Effects of enteral nutrition strategies on clinical outcomes in critically ill patients with shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Shock is a life-threatening clinical emergency that demands a sound treatment strategy. Nutritional support is among the key adjuvant therapies, but its application in shock remains controversial. This study explores how early enteral nutrition (EEN) affects the outcome of critically ill patients admitted with shock. This meta-analysis searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) over a period from the inception of each database to October 31, 2025. Critically ill patients admitted with shock were included as the study cohort. The primary outcomes were 28-day mortality and 90-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included ICU mortality, ICU length of stay (LOS-ICU), in-hospital mortality, hospital length of stay (LOS-H), ventilator-free days (VFD), nosocomial infection/reinfection, and adverse complications. Thirteen trials were included in this study. For the primary outcomes, EEN was not associated with 28-day mortality [relative risk (RR) = 1.03, 95% CI: 0.93-1.14] and 90-day mortality (RR = 1.04, 95% CI: 0.95-1.14). For secondary outcomes, EEN decreased LOS-ICU [standardized mean difference (SMD) = -0.28, 95% confidence interval (CI): -0.53 to -0.03] and LOS-H (SMD = -0.41, 95% CI: -0.61 to -0.21), without affecting VFD, nosocomial infection or reinfection, and Adverse reactions or complications. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested that the benefits of EEN varied by nutritional regimen. The high initial protein group was linked to lower LOS-ICU (SMD = -0.94, 95% CI: -1.59 to -0.30). The high initial calorie group was associated with shorter LOS-H (SMD = -0.12, 95% CI: -0.20 to -0.04), whereas the low initial calorie group reduced the adverse reactions or complications (RR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.25 to 0.77). In critically ill patients with shock, EEN with high initial caloric or protein supply may reduce hospital stay, whereas low initial caloric early enteral nutrition is associated with fewer adverse reactions. Given post-hoc subgroup limitations and marked population heterogeneity, findings should be interpreted cautiously. Additional high-quality trials are needed to develop individualized nutritional strategies for these patients.Systematic Review Registration: identifier CRD420261282657.

articles.title: Perioperative intravenous dexamethasone on postoperative delirium and delayed neurocognitive recovery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders include postoperative delirium (POD), delayed neurocognitive recovery (dNCR), and postoperative neurocognitive disorder. Although neuroinflammation may contribute to these conditions, randomised trials of perioperative dexamethasone have reported inconsistent findings. We updated the evidence on intravenous dexamethasone for POD and dNCR, as well as recovery and safety outcomes. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Ovid MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library through September 4, 2026. Randomised trials comparing perioperative intravenous dexamethasone with placebo or usual care in adults undergoing surgery were eligible. The co-primary outcomes were POD and trial-defined postoperative cognitive decline mapped to the dNCR time window according to the 2018 nomenclature framework. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed for the co-primary outcomes using RoB 2 and GRADE. Eight reports representing seven independent trials were included. Four independent trials involving 1,069 unique participants contributed to the POD analysis (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.37-1.03; I2 = 51%). Four independent trials comprising six comparisons and 1,533 unique participants contributed to the dNCR synthesis (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.65-1.41; I2 = 64%). Certainty of evidence was very low for both co-primary outcomes. Exploratory estimates suggested shorter time to extubation and hospital and intensive care unit stays, based on two small cardiac-surgery trials with substantial methodological limitations. Infection and hyperglycaemia estimates were imprecise, whereas continuous glucose measures indicated greater perioperative glucose exposure with dexamethasone. A possible reduction in POD remains uncertain, while no clear effect was identified for dNCR. Certainty was very low for both outcomes. Recovery findings remain exploratory and are influenced by a trial with substantial post-randomisation losses and high risk of bias for POD. These findings should be considered alongside increased perioperative glucose concentrations. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261381836, PROSPERO CRD420261381836.

articles.title: Non-pharmacological interventions for dyspnea during invasive mechanical ventilation in critical-care and prolonged-ventilation settings: a systematic review and evidence map.
articles.abstract: Dyspnea is common and distressing in adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU) and prolonged-ventilation services. Non-pharmacological interventions might relieve it without additional sedative or opioid exposure, but the trial evidence has not been mapped. An initial search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science to 31 July 2025, supplemented by citation tracing, was followed by a reproducible search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and CINAHL Complete executed on 31 July 2026 (cut-off 30 June 2026); a PubMed re-run on 12 October 2026 identified no further eligible study. Randomized and comparative within-patient studies in invasively ventilated adults were eligible, without language restriction. Interventions were mapped as clinician-delivered non-pharmacological interventions (stratum A) or ventilator titration (stratum B). The primary outcome was patient-reported dyspnea on a visual analogue, numeric rating, or Borg scale during invasive ventilation. Parallel-group trials were assessed for trustworthiness with INSPECT-SR, and results were synthesized by effect direction following the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guideline. Thirty-five studies (37 reports) were included: 10 in stratum A and 25 in stratum B. Randomized between-arm evidence without serious trustworthiness concerns came from two small trials: acupressure reduced dyspnea compared with massage in 52 patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease receiving prolonged ventilation ( P = 0.009 ), and an exhalation-port comparison in 20 tracheostomy-ventilated patients, reported as a congress abstract, showed no clear difference. A single-session music trial ( n = 136 ) had serious INSPECT-SR concerns and was reported as a sensitivity result only. Sensory interventions (music, facial airflow, nasal high flow) reduced dyspnea in at least one randomized contrast in each of three crossover studies of 17-37 participants, and clinician-directed ventilator adjustment reduced dyspnea in all four before-after studies. Certainty for every outcome was very low. Randomized evidence on non-pharmacological relief of dyspnea during invasive ventilation is limited to two small trials. Acupressure, sensory interventions, and individualized ventilator adjustment warrant adequately powered randomized trials; no clinical recommendation is supported. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251116624, identifier PROSPERO CRD420251116624.

articles.title: H-shaped sponge positioner prevents pressure injuries during prolonged prone ventilation in acute respiratory distress syndrome: a single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: In patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome, prolonged prone position ventilation is frequently employed to enhance oxygenation but often results in pressure injuries. To protect patients from such injuries, a new H-shaped sponge locator was designed in the study. In this single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial, 60 patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome requiring extended prone position ventilation (≥ 12 hours per session) were recruited from the General Intensive Care Unit at Xiangtan Central Hospital, Hunan Province, China, between May 2023 and May 2024. Participants were randomly allocated to either the intervention group, which received prone positioning with the assistance of the H-shaped sponge positioner, or the control group, which used conventional soft pillows for support. The primary outcomes included the number of anatomical sites affected by pressure injuries and injury severity, classified according to the revised 2016 National Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel/the European Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel staging criteria. Secondary outcomes included mean airway pressure, oxygenation index (PaO2/FiO2), intravesical pressure, and the frequency of support device adjustments. Data from 29 patients in each group were analyzed. Significant group × time interactions were observed for both the number of pressure injury sites and overall incidence. Although pressure injuries increased progressively across all sessions in both groups, patients in the intervention group consistently had fewer injury sites. There were no significant group × time interactions for mean airway pressure or intravesical pressure. However, both measures increased over time in all patients, with significantly lower values in the intervention group. Oxygenation index improved over time, with no statistically significant differences between groups. The intervention group required markedly fewer support device adjustments. In patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome receiving extended prone position ventilation, the H-shaped sponge positioner significantly outperformed standard soft pillow support in preventing pressure injuries. This cost-efficient device not only minimized the number and severity of pressure ulcers but also reduced mean airway and intra-abdominal pressures and decreased the frequency of nursing interventions. Given its ease of use and affordability, the H-shaped positioner holds substantial promise for clinical application, particularly in resource-constrained settings, and warrants further evaluation in broader implementation studies. This trial was registred at National Health Security Information Platform (Medical Research Registration and Information System, https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn, Registration No. MR-43-23-039592) on March 30, 2023.

articles.title: Consent for intensive care research involving adults who lack decision-making capacity: A jurisdictional analysis of Australia's fragmented framework.
articles.journal: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
articles.abstract: Critically ill adults frequently cannot consent to research because of sedation, delirium, shock or mechanical ventilation, yet safe intensive care depends on evidence generated in this population; several treatments once regarded as standard care proved harmful when finally tested in randomised trials. The ethical framework for enrolling adults who lack decision-making capacity is national-the National Health and Medical Research Council National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research (2025), in effect since 23 June 2026-but legal authority for substitute consent is conferred by eight state and territory statutes that differ in terminology, in decision-maker hierarchies, in whether they address research at all, and whether they permit enrolment in an emergency. Mapping four representative study archetypes across all eight jurisdictions shows that the lawful basis for enrolling the same patient shifts with study design as much as with geography; differing statutory definitions, tribunal involvement and the transition to the 2025 National Statement produce material and avoidable inconsistency. Contemporary Australian intensive care trials show that practice has converged on the National Statement while the underlying legislation has not; the resulting inconsistency risks inequity, underrepresentation of critically ill patients, and bias in the evidence generated. We set out principles for reform (Box 1): nationally consistent framing of substitute consent for research-common terminology and legal principles, an explicit emergency-research pathway in every jurisdiction, and consistent interpretation within each jurisdiction-developed with consumers and with the clinicians and clinical research nurses who obtain consent, and taken forward with formal endorsement from the relevant professional bodies.

articles.title: Variation in capability, organisational structure, and treatment processes for critically ill adults with moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury in Australia and New Zealand.
articles.journal: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
articles.abstract: To characterise between-centre variation in capability, organisational structure, and treatment processes for adults with moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury (msTBI) admitted to intensive care (ICU) in Australia and New Zealand (ANZ). Cross-sectional questionnaire supplemented by linked Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society CORE Critical Care Resources Registry descriptors. ANZ ICUs treating adults with msTBI, October-December 2025. Variation in organisational structure and capability, ICU treatment processes, neuroprognostication, withholding or withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy, and fulfilment of selected Australian TBI Quality Indicator Set elements. Heterogeneity was assessed using the index of qualitative variation (IQV) for nominal items and Leik's dispersion for ordinal items; values <0.3 were considered low, 0.3-0.7 moderate, and >0.7 substantial. Moderate or substantial heterogeneity was observed in 39 of 74 measured items (53%). Substantial heterogeneity included neurocritical care subspecialty expertise (IQV 1.00), perceived devastating traumatic brain injury management (IQV 0.99), cerebrospinal fluid drainage timing (IQV 0.93), withholding or withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy decision-making processes (IQV 0.86), arterial transducer zero level for cerebral perfusion pressure calculation (IQV 0.82), haemoglobin targets (Leik's dispersion 0.81), and post-ICU follow-up interval (IQV 0.81). Low heterogeneity in several advanced neuromonitoring and neuroprognostication modalities reflected consistent non-use or unavailability. Fulfilment of the six measured Australian TBI Quality Indicator Set indicators ranged from 2/6 to 5/6 across centres. Among ANZ ICUs providing care for adults with msTBI, moderate or substantial variation was evident in over half of measured organisational and clinical aspects of care. These findings identify targets for research and quality improvement and highlight centre variation as a potential modifier of patient outcomes.

articles.title: Use of osilodrostat in life-threatening ectopic Cushing syndrome secondary to neuroendocrine tumor.
articles.abstract: Ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) syndrome is a rare, severe form of endogenous Cushing syndrome requiring rapid cortisol reduction; experience with osilodrostat in critically ill patients remains limited. A 41-year-old woman with a prior supraglottic neuroendocrine tumor (NET) presented with rapidly progressive proximal weakness, severe hypokalemia, hypertension, and delirium. Adrenocorticotropic hormone-dependent hypercortisolism was confirmed, with a 12 × 10 × 14-cm abdominal mass showing somatostatin receptor uptake as the probable ectopic source. She required intensive care, intubation, and intravenous etomidate, but developed vasoplegic shock and multiorgan failure despite cortisol reduction. Etomidate was replaced by oral osilodrostat, which rapidly achieved stable serum cortisol over 4 weeks. Open left hepatectomy confirmed a well-differentiated ACTH-positive NET, with postoperative biochemical remission and marked neurological recovery. This case highlights osilodrostat as an effective, safe, and less labor-intensive alternative to parenteral steroidogenesis inhibition in severe ectopic Cushing syndrome, enabling stabilization before definitive surgery.

articles.title: Beyond survival in critical illness: patient-centred outcomes, the survival-morbidity paradox and caregiver burden: a comprehensive review.
articles.abstract: Advances in critical care have reduced intensive care unit (ICU) mortality, but improved survival has not consistently translated into meaningful long-term recovery. This "survival-morbidity paradox" highlights the need to consider patient-centred outcomes beyond survival. This narrative review used a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE from database inception to 20 March 2026, supplemented by reference-list screening. Relevant original studies, systematic reviews, and narrative reviews were selected and synthesised thematically. Post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) encompasses persistent physical, cognitive, and psychological impairments following critical illness. ICU-acquired weakness may lead to prolonged disability and loss of independence, while cognitive deficits associated with delirium and neuroinflammation may persist for years. Anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder can further compromise quality of life. The burden also extends to families and caregivers through post-intensive care syndrome-family (PICS-F), encompassing psychological, social, and financial challenges. Patient-centred outcomes include functional status, quality of life, independence, and societal reintegration. Early rehabilitation, ICU follow-up clinics, family-centred care, psychological support, and digital health strategies offer potential approaches to improving recovery, although evidence of benefit varies. The survival-morbidity paradox calls for a broader definition of success in critical care. Integrating multidimensional, longitudinal outcomes and patient- and family-centred support into clinical care and research may help bridge the gap between survival and meaningful recovery.

articles.title: The value of low-resolution intracranial pressure burden analysis in traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract: In traumatic brain injury (TBI) patients requiring invasive intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring, we evaluated the utility of ICP burden calculation with low-resolution data in predicting mortality and 6-month functional outcome. An observational study was performed on 213 patients with moderate or severe TBI and an ICP intraparenchymal catheter, admitted to a trauma center from 2012 to July 2025. ICP burden ≥ 15 mmHg was calculated with the methods of pressure-time dose and percentage of monitoring time with an ICP ≥ 15 mmHg. ICP burden was compared across clinical groups (age, sex, neurosurgical intervention), and its association with outcomes was explored, adjusting by confounders. The utility of adding ICP burden to prognosis predicted by the established IMPACT model was evaluated. Median time of invasive ICP monitoring was 5 days. In the whole cohort, a higher ICP burden was associated with higher ICU mortality. High ICP burden was associated with worse 6-month functional outcome in patients who did not need a neurosurgical intervention or only external ventricular drainage. Among these patients, a model combining IMPACT and ICP burden showed a trend toward improved prediction of worse outcomes. A linear relationship between high ICP burden and worse outcomes was found with an ICP burden ≥ 30 mmHg*h per day above 15 mmHg. ICP burden above 15 mmHg extracted from ICU records may help in adjusting patient prognostic, even from a low-resolution data source, using methods such as pressure-time dose or the proportion of time above this threshold.

articles.title: Effect of fascial plane blocks providing postoperative analgesia on mechanical ventilation duration in the ıntensive care unit and early oxygenation after cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract: The primary objective of this study was to examine whether a combined pecto-intercostal fascial plane block (PIFB) and serratus anterior plane block (SAPB) influences the duration of mechanical ventilation in patients who underwent open cardiac surgery via median sternotomy with cardiopulmonary bypass. Secondary objectives included evaluating the effects of this analgesic approach on early postoperative oxygenation parameters, pain intensity scores, and overall opioid consumption. This retrospective observational study enrolled 206 adult patients who underwent open cardiac surgery through median sternotomy between January and July 2025. Participants were allocated into two groups based on the postoperative analgesic strategy employed: the Block group (G1, N.=107), which received combined PIFB and SAPB, and the Control group (G0, N.=99), which was managed with conventional multimodal analgesia. To minimize selection bias, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied using seven clinical covariates. Mechanical ventilation duration was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves, Cox proportional hazards regression, and the restricted mean survival time (RMST) method. Patients in the Block group demonstrated a significantly shorter median duration of mechanical ventilation compared to controls (300 vs. 420 min; RMST difference: -65.8 min; 95% CI: -94.2 to -41.6; P<0.001). The incidence of prolonged intubation, defined as mechanical ventilation exceeding 480 minutes, was markedly lower in the Block group (G1=6.5% vs. G0=20.2%; Firth OR: 0.29; 95% CI: 0.11-0.75; P=0.011). Postoperative pain scores were significantly reduced across all assessment time points in the Block group (Benjamini-Hochberg corrected q<0.001), and total opioid requirements declined by approximately 28% (IRR: 0.719; P<0.001). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected with respect to the PaO<inf>2</inf>/FiO<inf>2</inf> ratio or the length of intensive care unit stay. CONCLUSİONS: The combined application of PIFB and SAPB was associated with a shorter duration of mechanical ventilation and lower opioid consumption following cardiac surgery. Incorporating fascial plane blocks into multimodal analgesia protocols may confer meaningful clinical benefits, particularly in patients considered to be at elevated perioperative risk.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine-associated bradycardia in perioperative and critical care settings: a cross-database pharmacovigilance study using FAERS and JADER.
articles.abstract: Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is a highly selective α2-adrenoceptor agonist widely used for sedation in perioperative and critical care settings. Although bradycardia is a recognised adverse effect, its temporal reporting patterns and associated clinical characteristics remain incompletely characterised. This study investigated DEX-associated bradycardia using two independent spontaneous reporting systems. We conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER) database from 2004Q1 to 2025Q3. Reports suggestive of perioperative or critical care use were identified using predefined proxy indicators. Disproportionality analyses were performed to detect cardiovascular safety signals. Time to onset (TTO) patterns were evaluated using Weibull modelling, and factors associated with bradycardia reporting were examined using multivariable case-non-case logistic regression. Sensitivity analyses assessed the consistency of the findings. Among 2505 DEX reports, 717 involved bradycardia-associated events (FAERS, n = 327; JADER, n = 390). Bradycardia showed prominent disproportionality signals in both databases. Among 198 reports with valid TTO data, the median onset time was 0 days in both databases, with similar Weibull shape parameters (FAERS, β = 0.849; JADER, β = 0.847), suggesting early clustering of reported events. Pre-existing cardiovascular disease showed the strongest adjusted association with bradycardia reporting (OR 4.88, 95% CI 3.92-6.09), followed by concomitant opioid use (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.37-2.22) and β-adrenoceptor blocker exposure (OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.08-3.13). These associations were generally consistent across sensitivity analyses. DEX-associated bradycardia showed consistent reporting signals across FAERS and JADER, with reported onset times frequently concentrated near treatment initiation. Cardiovascular disease and concomitant opioid or β-adrenoceptor blocker exposure were associated with higher odds of bradycardia reporting. Although spontaneous reporting data cannot establish causality or quantify incidence, these findings provide complementary post-marketing evidence supporting careful cardiovascular assessment and haemodynamic monitoring during DEX administration.

articles.title: Machine learning for early identification of delirium in ICU patients with acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Delirium is common in critically ill patients and is associated with worse outcomes, but its risk factors among adults with acute kidney injury (AKI) in the intensive care unit (ICU) are not fully described. We aimed to develop and validate a simple machine learning model to predict delirium during ICU stay in adult AKI patients and to identify the most important clinical predictors. We retrospectively included ICU patients aged 18 years or older with a diagnosis of AKI. The cohort was randomly split 70:30 into a training set and a validation set. Patients were labeled as having delirium or non-delirium based on events occurring during the ICU stay. In the training set, the Boruta algorithm was used to identify confirmed predictors, which were then fed into 9 supervised machine learning classifiers. Model performance was assessed in the validation set using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were calculated to interpret feature importance. Among the validation cohort, CatBoost showed the best discrimination with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.742 (95% confidence interval = 0.676-0.809). SHAP analysis of the final model identified diabetes, pneumonia, chloride, red blood cell, and prothrombin time as the most influential predictors of delirium. A CatBoost model built on Boruta-confirmed clinical variables showed moderate discrimination for ICU delirium in adults with AKI. The most influential predictors identified by SHAP - diabetes, pneumonia, chloride, red blood cell count, and prothrombin time - may help clinicians recognize high-risk patients and prioritize preventive measures. External validation is needed before wider clinical use.

articles.title: Non-linear association between enteral nutrition initiation time and sepsis-associated delirium: A retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-III database.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated delirium (SAD) is a common and critical complication in sepsis patients. Early enteral nutrition is recommended for sepsis patients, yet the relationship between enteral nutrition (EN) initiation time and SAD incidence remains unclear. This study aimed to explore this relationship. The Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III database was queried to identify sepsis patients who had received EN during their intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Multivariable logistic regression explored the relationship between EN initiation time and SAD incidence. Restricted cubic spline depicted the correlation shape. Subgroup and interaction analyses evaluated the robustness. Exploratory decomposition analysis was used to decompose this association. 2431 patients were enrolled. Multivariable logistic regression showed that EN initiation time was associated with SAD incidence (Tertile 2: odds ratio = 1.363, 95% confidence interval: 1.004-1.857, P = .048; Tertile 3: odds ratio = 1.452, 95% confidence interval: 1.06-1.994, P = .021). The trend test was significant (P for trend = .023). Restricted cubic spline demonstrated a nonlinear relationship between EN initiation time and SAD incidence (P-overall = 0.014, P for nonlinear = 0.01). No interactions were detected between EN initiation time and any subgroup. Exploratory decomposition analysis indicated that the duration of vasopressor use (P = .014), hospital (P = .024)/ICU (P = .034) length of stay, and mean levels of platelet count (P = .02) and mean anion gap (P < .001) during the first 3 days of ICU admission statistically accounted for a portion of the observed association between EN initiation time and SAD incidence. Earlier EN initiation showed a nonlinear association with lower SAD incidence. This relationship was partially accounted for by differences in duration of vasopressor use, hospital/ICU length of stay, platelet, and anion gap. Due to the observational nature of this study, these findings are exploratory and do not establish causation. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether this association is causal and to establish the optimal timing of enteral nutrition initiation.

articles.title: Delirium prevalence and practices across intensive care units in Singapore: a point prevalence survey.
authors: for SICM NICER (Society of Intensive Care Medicine Singapore National Investigators for Clinical Epidemiology and Research)
articles.abstract: Delirium is characterised by a disturbance in attention and awareness, alongside an acute change in cognition that develops over a short period and fluctuates in severity. It is associated with critical illness. This study aimed to determine the point prevalence of delirium in Singapore's intensive care units (ICUs) and assess the adherence of local delirium management practices and evidence-based international guidelines. A point prevalence survey was conducted on World Delirium Awareness Day, 13 March 2024. Local ICU leads completed questionnaires, and data on delirium prevalence and management practices were collected and compared with international guidelines. Responses were received from 12 adult and two paediatric ICU leads, representing 66% of adult and 100% of paediatric ICUs in Singapore's public health institutions. Of 143 ICU patients, 92 (81.4%) were assessed for delirium, with 32 (34.8%) screening positive. Adult ICUs generally adhered to PADIS recommendations, including limiting benzodiazepine use, routinely assessing for delirium, and implementing protocols for pain management and sedation. However, holistic non-pharmacological care was lacking. Paediatric ICUs showed strong adherence to PANDEM guidelines, although deficiencies remained in delirium assessment and noise reduction practices. The most frequently reported barriers to improving management strategies were manpower shortages, time constraints and educational gaps. Overall, local practices aligned well with international guidelines, but gaps remained in non-pharmacological interventions, resources, time and education. Addressing these gaps through quality improvement initiatives may enhance delirium management in ICUs.

articles.title: Long-Term Cognitive Function Following Haloperidol Vs. Placebo Treatment in ICU Patients With Delirium.
articles.abstract: To investigate the effects of haloperidol vs. placebo on long-term cognitive function in formerly critically ill patients with ICU delirium, 1 year after randomization in the Agents Intervening against Delirium in the ICU (AID-ICU) randomized clinical trial. Pre-planned 1-year follow-up of the AID-ICU trial conducted from June 2019 to April 2023. Three university-affiliated ICUs in Denmark. Adult ICU patients previously enrolled in the AID-ICU trial. Patients in the AID-ICU were randomized to either haloperidol or placebo (0.9% saline) when treated for delirium in the ICU. The primary outcome was global cognitive function at 1 year, assessed using Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychologic Status (RBANS) Global Index Score Secondary outcomes including domain-specific RBANS scores and executive function, measured by the Trail Making Test A and B. Analyses used the intention-to-treat population. Non-survivors were assigned the lowest possible score on each outcome, reflecting death as a competing outcome. Missing data among survivors were handled using multiple imputations. Of the 632 randomized patients, 624 were included. Cognitive outcome data were available for 134 of 343 surviving patients: 67 in the haloperidol group and 67 in the placebo group. Median global cognitive scores were 40 (interquartile range [IQR]: 40-75) in the haloperidol group and 40 (IQR: 40-72) in the placebo group (mean difference: 2; 95% CI, -3 to 7; p = 0.48). No significant differences were observed in secondary outcomes. Given the high proportion of missing data, best-worst and worst-best sensitivity analyses were performed, yielding estimates in opposite directions. In this 1-year follow-up of the AID-ICU treatment with haloperidol for delirium in the ICU was not associated with improved long-term cognitive function compared with placebo. However, given the extent of missing outcome data and the divergent results of our sensitivity analyses, this estimate should be interpreted as imprecise rather than conclusive; clinically relevant effects of pharmacologic delirium treatment on cognition cannot be excluded, and future adequately powered studies with more complete follow-up are warranted.

articles.title: Prevalence and Characteristics of Coma in Latin American Critical Care Units: The COMA LATAM Study.
authors: and members of the Coma in Latin America (COMA LATAM) group, on behalf of the Latin American Brain Injury Consortium (LABIC) and the Curing Coma Campaign
Colombia and Costa Rica and Cuba and Dominican Republic and Ecuador and El Salvador and Guatemala and Honduras and Mexico and Panama and Paraguay and Peru and Puerto Rico and Uruguay and Venezuela
articles.abstract: To determine the point prevalence of coma across Latin American critical care units, characterize its etiology, and explore short-term outcomes. Multinational, cross-sectional point prevalence study with exploratory 14-day follow-up assessment. Three hundred ninety-two hospitals across 19 Latin American countries, including ICUs, intermediate care units, neurocritical care units, cardiovascular ICUs, and trauma ICUs. Adult patients (≥ 18 yr) meeting the Coma Epidemiology, Evaluation, and Therapy care survey (COME-TOGETHER) criteria on May 28, 2024. Patients under deep sedation or pharmacological coma induction were excluded unless the coma state preceded pharmacological intervention. None (observational study). Among 8305 critically ill patients, 1145 met coma criteria (point prevalence 13.8%), with country-specific rates ranging from 5.1% to 36.8%. Individual patient data were available for 729 patients (63.7%). Traumatic brain injury was the leading individual cause (24.8%), followed by hypoxic-anoxic brain injury (14.6%) and intracerebral hemorrhage (13.5%). When categorized by pathophysiology, vascular causes predominated (48.6%), followed by traumatic brain injury (24.8%) and other causes (26.6%). Age-stratified analysis revealed trauma predominantly affecting younger patients, while cerebrovascular causes predominated in older groups. Among patients with 14-day follow-up data (29% of cohort), mortality was 29.2%, with 67.7% of survivors recovering from coma. Only the Charlson Comorbidity Index was independently associated with implementation of life-sustaining therapy limitations (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.15-1.30; p < 0.001). Coma affects nearly one in seven ICU beds across Latin America, with substantial country variation and distinct age-dependent etiology patterns. The significant burden highlights the need for targeted prevention strategies and specialized neurocritical care resources throughout the region.

articles.title: Analysis of outcome predictors in traumatic brain injury patients requiring intensive care management reveals an independent role of dynamic measures.
articles.abstract: Research in traumatic brain injury (TBI) mediation and outcome have developed many methods of assessing patient state and response. While several outcome calculators for TBI have been suggested, these calculators do not include all collected variables in the management of these patients; with a paucity of studies on how these hundreds of variables contribute statistically to long-term outcome. Thus, this work endeavors to assess the statistical relationships between commonly collected variables at admission, and during the first 24 h of critical care, with overall patient outcome. From a retrospective dataset of 1,266 TBI patients requiring intensive care, unique patient variables (including demographic, injury pattern, pathophysiological, treatment and biochemical/imaging biomarkers) were explored. Intra-variable and variable reduction analysis were completed with importance assessed through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method. From all of this we developed predictive models to assess the 6-12-month Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) using general linear and XGBoost models. Of the 321 variables assessed, a final 36 variables were found to be the important and non-redundant, that included common variables (Glasgow coma scale (GCS), age, heart rate and blood pressure at scene of accident) and individualized measures (S100B level and long pressure reactivity). Survival based on these non-redundant variables resulted in an accuracy of 88.8% 0.723 AUC (0.65-0.795) vs the IMPACT LAB 80.9% 0.608 AUC (0.54-0.677). Notable combining the IMPACT LAB model with the non-redundant variables found an accuracy of 90.3% 0.765 AUC (0.693-0.838) and an improvement of the Nagelkerke R2 value from 0.317 to 0.499. These results found that overall general linear and XGBoost models behave similarly with an increase in non-IMPACT LAB variables performing better in XGBoost models. Broad categories of patient states like survival and favorable outcome can be determined by basic patient variables, however more dynamic measures of individualized response improve the predictive capacity for patient outcomes. Thus, to better understand patient state and more effectively monitor patient outcomes, dynamic and individualized patient physiology needs further evaluation.

articles.title: Propranolol administration following traumatic brain injury induces distinct neuroinflammatory gene expression profiles.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major cause of morbidity and is frequently followed by prolonged intensive care stays with sustained physiologic stress. Beta-blockade has been investigated as an adjunct therapy for TBI given its potential to reduce sympathetic hyperactivation. The molecular mechanisms underlying neuroinflammatory signaling remain incompletely defined. We hypothesized that propranolol (BB) administration following TBI would modify neuroinflammatory transcriptional responses consistent with attenuation of maladaptive inflammatory signaling. Male Sprague-Dawley rats (n=6-8/group) were divided into 6 groups: (1) TBI7d (controlled cortical impact) followed by 7 days of daily handling, (2) TBI7d with daily propranolol administration (TBI BB7d), (3) TBI with chronic restraint stress for 7 days (TBI CRS7d), (4) TBI CRS7d with daily propranolol administration (TBI CRS BB7d), (5) CRS7d (n=7) who underwent daily stress exposure for 7 days; and (6) CRS BB7d (n=7) underwent daily stress exposure with propranolol injections for 7 days. RNA was extracted from the injured frontal lobe and analyzed using the NanoString Neuroinflammation panel. Differential gene expression was analyzed using ROSALIND. Significant differentially expressed genes (sDEGs) were defined as fold change ≥1.5 or ≤-1.5 with p<0.05. Functional pathway analysis was performed using Qiagen Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Compared with TBI alone, TBI BB7d demonstrated 83 sDEGs, including genes associated with neuronal signaling, neurotransmitter regulation, and epigenetic modulation. Pathway analysis identified significant involvement of the IL8 signaling and FXR/RXR. In the TBI CRS7d model, propranolol treatment yielded 21 sDEGs. These genes were enriched in pathways related to cellular stress responses and inflammatory regulation. Propranolol downregulated IL6, IL8, and neuroinflammation signaling pathways. Propranolol administration following TBI, with and without stress, resulted in distinct neuroinflammatory transcriptional profiles. Propranolol was associated with alterations in multiple pathways involved in stress response, immune regulation, and neurorecovery. These findings suggest beta-blockade may modulate stress-related neuroinflammatory signaling following TBI.

articles.title: Religion and Religiosity in End-of-Life Decisions in Neurocritical Care.
articles.abstract: End-of-life decisions are shaped by diverse biographical, social, and cultural factors. Few studies have systematically examined the impact of religion on end-of-life decisions, and even less data are available on religiosity (i.e., strength of religious faith). The Religion and religiosity in End-of-life deCisiOns in neuroCritIcaL carE (RECONCILE) study aimed to investigate whether religiosity, rather than religion, plays a decisive role in shaping end-of-life decisions. Prospective observational study. The study was conducted between 2021 and 2024 at two neuro-ICUs at Charité-Universitätsmedizin Berlin. We prospectively studied patients with acute brain injury and poor neurologic prognosis defined by the absence of regaining decision-making capacity or sufficient autonomy. A total of 100 patients were included. None. Relatives were consulted to ascertain the patients' presumed wishes regarding the continuation or withdrawal of life-sustaining intensive care. The 10-item Santa Clara Strength of Religious Faith questionnaire was applied to measure the patient´s religiosity on a scale between 10 and 40 points. We applied the t-test for independent variables to evaluate the influence of religiosity on end-of-life decisions. To adjust for possible confounders like age, sex, nationality, and religion, we calculated a logistic regression as well as an analysis of variance calculation. In patients in whom intensive care was continued, the median score was significantly higher compared with patients in whom intensive care was withdrawn (28.1 ± 9.0 vs. 20.5 ± 8.3; p < 0.001; Cohens d = 0.875). This finding was reproduced in each denominational group. Religion, age, and sex showed no significant association with the end-of-life decision behavior. Germans chose withdrawal of therapy significantly more often than non-Germans (p = 0.01) but also showed significantly lower religiosity scores (21.9 vs. 27.9; p = 0.003). The RECONCILE study demonstrates that religiosity looks more important in influencing end-of-life decisions than religion. Higher levels of religiosity were associated with a preference for more aggressive treatment, even when neurologic prognosis is poor.

articles.title: Opioid-Sparing Pain Control in Lung Transplantation: A Single-Center Experience with Intraoperative Intercostal Nerve Cryoablation.
articles.abstract: Postoperative pain following lung transplantation is substantial and contributes to opioid exposure, delirium risk, and prolonged recovery. We evaluated the impact of intraoperative intercostal nerve cryoablation on postoperative opioid use, delirium incidence, and early clinical outcomes. We conducted a single-center retrospective matched cohort study of adult lung transplant recipients. Patients who underwent intraoperative intercostal nerve cryoablation (intervention) were compared with a historical matched cohort of recipients who did not undergo cryoablation (control). The primary outcome was cumulative opioid use, measured in oral morphine milligram equivalents (MME), during the first 14 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included delirium incidence, ventilator days, intensive care unit and hospital lengths of stay, and early postoperative complications. The study included 19 patients in the cryoablation group and 38 matched controls. Cryoablation was associated with a reduction in cumulative opioid use through postoperative day 14 (428 MME vs. 603 MME, p=0.681). Rates of postoperative delirium were slightly lower in the intervention group (58% vs. 66%, p=0.571). Cryoablation was not associated with increased complications. There were trends toward shorter median ventilator duration and total hospital length of stay in the intervention group, although results were not statistically significant. Intraoperative intercostal nerve cryoablation is a feasible and safe adjunct in lung transplantation and is associated with reduced early postoperative opioid use. These findings support further prospective evaluation of cryoablation as an opioid-sparing strategy in lung transplant recipients.

articles.title: Comparative epidemiology and outcomes of gram-negative and non-gram-negative External Ventricular Drain (EVD)-related infections: a 10-year single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract: External ventricular drainage (EVD) is a device used in neurosurgical intensive care to monitor intracranial pressure and treat acute hydrocephalus. Ventriculostomy related infections (VRI) remain the major complications, with reported rates of 8 to 11 cases per 1000 EVD days. Most VRI cases are caused by skin commensal bacteria but Gram-negative bacilli (GNB) infections may carry a worse prognosis. We conducted a single-center, retrospective, observational study in a neurosurgical ICU, from January 2014 to December 2023. All patients who developed VRI were included. A composite endpoint of poor clinical outcome was defined a priori and included cerebral abscess or antibiotic treatment failure. Among the study period, 1868 patients had an EVD, and we included 71 patients who developed a VRI (2.05 / 1000 EVD days; mean age 50 ± 14 years), with a mortality rate in ICU of 10% (n = 7). The most frequent pathogens were methicillin-sensitive coagulase-negative Staphylococci (n = 26, 38%) and GNB (n = 24, 35%). Between GNB and non-GNB VRI, there was a significant difference between groups regarding the primary endpoint (p = 0.040), no significant difference for the occurrence of cerebral abscess (p = 0.262) but there was more antibiotic treatment failure in the GNB group (p = 0.015). Patients with GNB-related VRI had higher SAPS II scores (47 vs. 33, p < 0.001), longer durations of mechanical ventilation (34 days vs 20, p < 0.005), longer ICU stays (48 days vs. 28, p < 0.001). In our study, the incidence of VRI was 2.05 cases per 1000 EVD days. GNB related VRI accounted for 34% of cases. Significant differences in poor clinical outcomes were observed between GNB-related VRI and other VRI types. A higher rate of treatment failure, a higher initial severity score and a longer duration of mechanical ventilation and ICU hospitalization were observed in the GNB-VRI group.

articles.title: The role of intensive-care-unit fluid balance in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: A single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract: While liberal fluid use is common to prevent vasospasm-related hypoperfusion in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH), excess fluids can cause cerebral edema, impair microcirculation, and worsen outcomes. This study explores the role of fluid balancing in the ICU and its potential as a predictor of aSAH outcomes. The cumulative intensive care unit (ICU) fluid balance was evaluated in all consecutive aneurysmal aSAH cases treated between 01/2003 and 08/2024 (n = 1318). Primary endpoints included delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI)-related infarction, in-hospital mortality, and unfavorable 6-month outcomes (modified Rankin Scale >3). Multivariable models were adjusted for treated vasospasm and baseline characteristics; sensitivity analyses addressed ICU length of stay, treatment era, early death and residual confounding. Cumulative ICU fluid balance ranged from -12.5 L to + 80.5 L. Each 5-L increase was associated with DCI-related infarction (aOR:1.47, 95%-CI:1.30-1.67) and unfavorable 6-month outcome (aOR:1.82, 95%-CI:1.58-2.11); the latter remained robust after adjustment for ICU-length-of-stay (aOR:1.97, 95%-CI:1.70-2.31). In-hospital mortality was associated with mean daily fluid balance (aOR:3.19 per L/day, 95%-CI:2.44-4.23) and with cumulative balance only after accounting for ICU stay. A data-derived cut-off of + 3.8 L corresponded to the cohort median and was unstable. Higher cumulative ICU fluid balance was dose-dependently associated with complications and, most robustly, with poor functional outcome after aSAH. Because fluid balance partly reflects treatment and complication duration, it should be regarded as a marker of a complicated course that may also contribute to harm. Prospective studies are needed to clarify causality.

articles.title: Association of vitamin therapy with acute encephalopathy with febrile convulsive status epilepticus and neurological outcomes.
articles.abstract: Acute encephalopathy with febrile convulsive status epilepticus (AEFCSE) has a poor prognosis, but no definitive treatment. We aimed to evaluate whether early combination vitamin therapy (VT) (vitamin B1, B6, and l-carnitine) could prevent AEFCSE onset and improve neurological outcomes of pediatric febrile status epilepticus (FSE). The present, single-center, retrospective observational study enrolled patients admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit during 2017-2019 and 2022-2024 with FSE lasting ≥30 min. The patients were categorized into a VT group, who received vitamins within 72 h of the initial seizure onset, and a non-VT group. The primary outcome was the AEFCSE incidence. The secondary outcome was AEFCSE-related, poor neurological prognosis as defined by the Pediatric Cerebral Performance Category score. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on propensity scores was used to adjust for confounding factors. Of 109 included patients with FSE, 40 (37%) and 69 (63%) were in the VT and the non-VT group, respectively. AEFCSE occurred in eight (20%) and 11 (16%) patients in the respective group. After adjustment, VT was associated with lower but non-significant odds of AEFCSE (odds ratio [OR]: 0.60; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.21-1.73). AEFCSE-related, poor neurological outcomes occurred in five (13%) and eight (12%) patients in the respective group. After adjustment, the odds were lower but non-significant (OR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.16-1.90). Early combination VT demonstrated an exploratory association with lower AEFCSE incidence and improved neurological outcomes in children with FSE albeit the findings were inconclusive.

articles.title: Association Between Therapeutic Intervention Intensity and Postoperative Delirium Following Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Surgery.
articles.abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to investigate the association between therapeutic intervention intensity in the intensive care unit (ICU) and postoperative delirium in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. It also examined factors associated with therapeutic intervention intensity. Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted in the Cardiovascular Surgery Intensive Care Unit of XXX City Hospital between February 2025 and February 2026. The study included 100 consecutive adult patients who underwent isolated on-pump CABG surgery. Data were collected using a Personal Information Form, the Therapeutic Intervention Scoring System (TISS-28), and the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU). Both TISS-28 and CAM-ICU were administered once at the 48th postoperative hour, with TISS-28 assessing interventions performed during the preceding 24 h. Descriptive statistics, group comparisons, correlation analyses, and binary logistic regression were performed. Regression analysis examined the association between TISS-28 scores and postoperative delirium after adjustment for age and sex. Firth's penalized logistic regression was additionally performed as a sensitivity analysis. Results: The mean TISS-28 score was 40.96 ± 3.68. Postoperative delirium was detected at the 48th postoperative hour in 9.0% of patients. Patients with delirium had significantly higher TISS-28 scores than those without delirium (47.44 ± 7.95 vs. 40.32 ± 2.16, p = 0.028). Female patients had significantly higher TISS-28 scores than male patients (p = 0.013). TISS-28 scores showed a weak negative correlation with age and a weak positive correlation with the number of children (p < 0.05). Higher TISS-28 scores were associated with delirium after adjustment for age and sex (OR = 2.20, 95% CI: 1.33-3.64, p = 0.002). This association was also observed in the Firth sensitivity analysis (OR = 1.86, 95% CI: 1.31-3.19, p < 0.001). Conclusions: Greater therapeutic intervention intensity was associated with delirium detected at the 48th postoperative hour after adjustment for age and sex in patients undergoing CABG surgery. However, the small number of delirium events, single-time-point assessment, and potential residual confounding limit causal and predictive interpretations. Larger prospective studies with repeated delirium assessments are needed to clarify this association.

articles.title: Charted times of bedside pain assessments are slot labels: prevalence across hospitals, consequences for estimating analgesic onset, and when hourly charting is an adequate approximation.
articles.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
articles.abstract: Temporal and causal analyses of electronic health records (EHRs) treat the charted time of an observation as the time it was made. We quantified how often bedside pain and sedation assessments are charted to a time slot, how this affects estimates of analgesic onset, and when hourly charting is an adequate approximation. We used intensive care unit (ICU) data from one academic center (MIMIC-IV) and 78 hospitals (eICU-CRD). Slot labeling was identified from charted minutes and from the delay between charted and entry times. In MIMIC-IV, opioid administration times served as anchors, and faster onset of intravenous (IV) than oral opioids as a pharmacologic benchmark. We compared onset estimated from charted times with onset from exactly timed records, bounded true assessment times under alternative charting mechanisms, and used simulation to relate bias to the ratio of slot width to response time constant (Δ /k ). In MIMIC-IV, 68% of pain and 76% of sedation scores were charted on the hour and entered a median of 41-44 minutes later. Of the first reassessments after a dose, 32-34% of on-hour records carried a time before the dose, against 12-14% of off-hour records. Across eICU hospitals, the on-hour share ranged from 15% to 92% (10th-90th percentile). By charted time, oral opioids appeared nearly as fast as IV (pain change at 15-30 minutes, - 1.76 vs - 2.11 points); exactly timed records showed - 0.80 vs - 2.00. Slower oral onset held under every charting mechanism compatible with the data, but its magnitude was not identified (ratio of time constants 1.2-11.6). In simulation, analysis by charted time was adequate up to Δ /k ≈ 2 when rounding was to the nearest slot, but only up to Δ /k ≈ 0.1 when rounding had a direction. Charted times of bedside assessments are often slot labels, and charting practice is hospital-specific. For ICU analgesic onset, neither condition for an adequate approximation can be assumed, and EHR data alone cannot recover the size of the effect.

articles.title: Critically ill trauma in Portugal: a multicenter intensive care cohort study of frailty, organ dysfunction, and outcomes.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Multicenter data on critically ill trauma patients admitted to Portuguese intensive care units (ICUs) are lacking. We aimed to characterize their epidemiology, injury profile, organ dysfunction trajectories and outcomes, and to evaluate the prognostic performance of severity and frailty measures. Multicenter retrospective cohort study within the National Intensive Care Registry (RNMI) of adults (≥ 18 years) admitted to an ICU as a direct consequence of trauma (1 October-31 December 2024) in 32 of 50 voluntarily participating Portuguese ICUs; not nationally representative. SAPS II, ISS, TRISS, the Clinical Frailty Scale, daily SOFA scores, organ support, quality of life and mortality were collected. Prognostic performance was assessed by ROC analysis, multivariable logistic regression, calibration, and mixed-effects modelling of serial SOFA. 457 patients were included; median age 61 years (IQR 45-74), 72.0% male. Falls were the leading injury mechanism (46.9%). Traumatic brain injury (32.9%) and thoracic trauma (21.4%) predominated. Observed ICU and hospital mortality were 11.0% and 15.3%, respectively. SOFA scores were consistently higher in non-survivors from day one. SAPS II showed the highest discrimination for hospital mortality (AUC 0.874, 95% CI 0.825-0.924), followed by TRISS (0.758) and the Clinical Frailty Scale (0.702). SAPS II, day-1 SOFA, and frailty were independently associated with hospital mortality. SAPS II over-predicted mortality (observed/expected 0.64), whereas TRISS showed a non-significant tendency to under-predict it (1.32, 95% CI 0.99-1.72). In this multicenter cohort from 32 voluntarily participating ICUs, patients were older, with frequent falls, neurotrauma and thoracic injury, and moderate mortality. Organ dysfunction trajectories and frailty were associated with hospital mortality, but incremental predictive value was not assessed; both merit inclusion in future trauma registry frameworks.

articles.title: From evidence to bedside: A decade of critical care pharmacotherapy and implications for ICU training.
articles.abstract: Pharmacotherapy management is integral to the care of critically ill patients, yet decisions are frequently made in dynamic and uncertain conditions. Over the last decade, a series of large trials and shifts in understanding have reshaped how therapies are selected and applied in the intensive care unit (ICU), often challenging long-standing practices and refining established treatment strategies. This review examines influential studies and paradigm shifts across four major areas of ICU pharmacotherapy: respiratory failure and acute respiratory distress syndrome, infectious disease and antimicrobial therapy, hemodynamic management in sepsis and septic shock, and sedation and delirium. We highlight how emerging evidence led to pharmacotherapeutic evolution within each domain and identify common patterns across these domains supporting a movement toward individualized, context-dependent care and more deliberate use of pharmacologic therapies. For trainees, the last decade provides important lessons regarding application of pharmacotherapy in the ICU, including the need to integrate evidence interpretation with clinical judgement.

articles.title: Does gabapentin affect the incidence of postoperative delirium in a dose dependent pattern?
articles.abstract: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway for Colorectal Surgery (CRS) emphasizes opioid-sparing analgesia to reduce ileus and length of stay (LOS). Our hospital adopted gabapentin as part of postoperative analgesia for CRS. We evaluated the association between perioperative gabapentin use and postoperative delirium (POD). We retrospectively analyzed 1,165 encounters of patients ≥65 years undergoing elective CRS between 04/2015-06/2023. Encounters requiring critical care, LOS>3 months, or readmissions were excluded. Delirium was identified using chart review, ICD codes and/or new antipsychotic use. Multivariate logistic regression compared delirium rates among three groups: No Gabapentin (NG), low dose (LG) and high dose (HG). Models adjusted for age, race, ethnicity, gender, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), etc. Subgroup analyses investigated delirium by age, gender, CCI. 1,027 individuals were studied: 20.5% NG, 70.8% LG, and 8.7% HG. NG Individuals were older (75.5±7.2) than LG (74.2±6.7) or HG (72.7±6.6), while CCI (6.6±3.8) was similar across groups. The NG group had more patients with dementia (NG 14.2% vs LG 9.5%, p=0.05 vs HG 11.2%). A higher incidence of POD was noted in NG (34.6%) when compared with LG (25.3%, 1.74(1.22-2.47), adj. p=0.002) as well as HG (23.6%, p=0.06). Prior gabapentin exposure did not significantly impact the incidence of postoperative delirium (OR 1.33 (0.86-2.05)) when the cohort was compared based on prior gabapentin exposure. The use of low dose gabapentin postoperatively is associated with lower incidence of delirium compared to absence of gabapentin. However, the absence of gabapentin in our study is a reflection of baseline vulnerability for delirium. Prior exposure to gabapentin had no influence on incident POD. Future prospective trials are required to address the factors to be considered when determining the optimal dosing of gabapentin in older surgical adults.

articles.title: Contemporary Sedation Practices in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Analgesia and sedation are essential components of intensive care, but general recommendations are largely derived from heterogeneous critically ill populations rather than cardiac patients, who present distinct pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and hemodynamic considerations. This narrative review aims to summarize the interactions between commonly used sedative and analgesic agents, including opioids, benzodiazepines, propofol, etomidate, ketamine, and dexmedetomidine, and the pathophysiological alterations seen in specific cardiac conditions. For each drug class, cardiovascular effects, clinical trade-offs, and disease-specific suitability are outlined. Moreover, alongside pharmacological considerations, practical management of pain and sedation monitoring and nonpharmacological adjuncts are also discussed, with data extrapolated from general intensive care unit populations to compensate for the scarcity of cardiac-specific studies. The review aims to offer a practical overview of contemporary sedation practices in the cardiac intensive care unit, highlighting the importance of tailoring drug choice to the patient's cardiac phenotype and hemodynamic profile, while considering the potential need for mechanical circulatory support, alongside a careful titration of the selected agent and multimodal analgesia when feasible. Additionally, the lack of randomized trials in the cardiac intensive care unit highlights how optimal pharmacological regimens and comprehensive pain and agitation management protocols in the cardiac population represent areas warranting further dedicated research.

articles.title: ICU delirium: From key drivers to targeted prevention.
Handling of the Non-Assessable Verbal Glasgow Coma Scale and Computed Illness Severity in Critically Ill Adults with Acute Brain Injury: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) contributes to illness-severity scores. The verbal component cannot be observed in intubated patients; the MIMIC Code Repository sets "No Response-ETT" rows to a total of 15.ObjectiveTo quantify non-assessable verbal GCS examinations and describe how their handling changes computed severity, the analyzed population and mortality-model performance.Materials and MethodsRetrospective MIMIC-IV cohort (Boston, 2008 to 2022) of adults with acute brain injury (first intensive care unit stay per hospitalization); a "No Response-ETT" verbal entry was non-assessable. Five GCS derivation strategies were compared; four used the lowest eye-plus-motor examination of the first 24 h. The eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD; United States, 2014 to 2015) supported replication.ResultsOf 14,230 stays, 45.2% had a non-assessable verbal examination; 47.5% of ventilated stays had none assessable in the first 24 h. A non-assessable lowest examination was associated with mechanical ventilation (adjusted odds ratio, 32.8; 95% CI, 27.8 to 38.6). The official first-day GCS was 15 in 44.7% of 14 215 stays; 94.1% of default-rule totals of 15 were incompatible with the eye-plus-motor sum charted at that examination. With one mortality-model specification refitted per GCS derivation on the same stays, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.749 (95% CI, 0.739 to 0.760) with the official first-day GCS and 0.820 (0.812 to 0.828) with an eye-and-motor (Brennan) estimate. Complete-case analysis excluded 5509 of 14 192 stays and 72.8% of deaths. In eICU-CRD, stays with an unscored GCS component had higher mortality (16.6% vs 9.2%), but totals of 12 or more were no more frequent after the first documented ventilation entry (17.3%) than before (19.5%).ConclusionIn this cohort, how a non-assessable verbal GCS was handled changed computed severity and the analyzed population. Studies and benchmarks that use GCS-based severity should report the handling rule.

articles.title: Long-term Electroclinical Outcomes After Herpes Simplex Virus Encephalitis: A Single-Center Case Series.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveHerpes simplex virus encephalitis (HSVE) remains an important cause of severe sporadic encephalitis. Electrographic seizures and status epilepticus may be underrecognized during the acute phase, and their relationship with long-term outcome is incompletely defined. We aimed to describe acute EEG abnormalities and long-term seizure and cognitive outcomes in adults with HSVE.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed adults hospitalized with HSVE in the neurology ward or neurological intensive care unit between 2013 and 2022. Demographic and clinical characteristics, MRI findings, routine or continuous video-EEG findings, antiseizure treatments, and long-term outcomes were obtained from electronic health records and the EEG archive.ResultsNine patients (7 men; age range: 30-77 years) were included. Altered mental status was the most frequent presenting feature, and 3 patients had clinical seizures at presentation. MRI abnormalities were bilateral in 4 patients. EEG showed lateralized periodic discharges in 5 patients, electrographic status epilepticus in 4, and electrographic seizures not meeting status criteria in 1. Median follow-up was 8 years (range: 4-13 years). No patient with available follow-up reported recurrent clinical seizures after discharge. Mood and/or cognitive complaints were present in 6 of 8 patients with evaluable long-term clinical data.ConclusionIn this neurologically selected HSVE cohort, electrographic seizures and status epilepticus were frequent despite clinical seizures being documented in only one-third of patients at presentation. Long-term clinical seizure control was favorable under continued antiseizure treatment, whereas cognitive and mood complaints remained common. Larger studies using systematic continuous EEG and standardized neuropsychological assessment are needed.

articles.title: Cipepofol Versus Propofol Across Adult Anaesthesia and Sedation: A Comprehensive Clinical Review of Pharmacology, Clinical Efficacy, Recovery, and Safety.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Following FDA approval of cipepofol for adult surgical induction in May 2026, its comparative evidence requires interpretation within the approved indication and other studied settings. This comprehensive clinical review examines pharmacology, efficacy, cardiorespiratory effects, injection pain, recovery, and safety. Materials and Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to 16 July 2026. Adult randomised comparisons were considered, with second-author assistance in sorting and verification. This structured narrative review was not a formal systematic review; no meta-analysis, formal risk-of-bias assessment, or GRADE assessment was undertaken. Results: The source set comprised 85 randomised comparative study reports: 41 in general anaesthesia, 40 in procedural or adjunct sedation, and four in ICU sedation. A single participant total is not presented because enrolment, eligible-arm, and analysed populations were not consistently defined. Pivotal trials demonstrated high protocol success, and directly reported comparisons showed less injection pain with cipepofol. Haemodynamic and respiratory findings varied by regimen, population, endpoint definition, and rescue practice. Recovery findings were mixed. Neurocognitive benefit, organ protection, mortality reduction, and rare-harm superiority were not established. Conclusions: Cipepofol is an effective hypnotic under the adult protocols evaluated. Following approval, clinical interpretation should distinguish surgical induction from maintenance, procedural sedation, and ICU applications. Potential tolerability advantages do not establish overall safety superiority or justify reduced monitoring.

articles.title: Language Concordance in Critical Care: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Language barriers are associated with differences in care delivery processes and outcomes in critical care settings, with differences despite language assistance services.
