A retrospective, single-center, observational study was conducted over three years (January 2021 to December 2023) in the Neuro-intensive care unit of Nepal Mediciti Hospital. Patients were categorized based on their primary diagnosis. Data from 820 patients were analyzed using descriptive statistics for demographics, diagnoses, duration of intensive care unit stay, mechanical ventilation, and outcomes (survival, mortality, survival, mortality, and leave against medical advice withdrawal of treatment). Data were extracted using the National Intensive Care Unit Registry maintained by NICRF (Nepal Intensive Care Research Foundation). A total of 820 cases were analyzed. Males constituted 65.9% of admissions. The most preponderant patient population was aged ≥ 61 years, with cerebrovascular diseases (47.2%), being the leading diagnosis, followed by trauma (19.8%). Mechanical ventilation was required in 32.8% of cases. Overall ICU survival was 71.3%, with 28.7% mortality. Older age, lower admission Glasgow Coma Scale, vascular diagnosis, and mechanical ventilation were independent predictors of ICU mortality. Cerebrovascular diseases and trauma are the primary drivers of Neuro-intensive care unit admissions. Prioritizing stroke prevention and trauma reduction programs may reduce mortality in neurocritical care.

articles.title: Temporal trends in renal replacement therapy use in adults with acute kidney injury: A severity-stratified multicentre observational study.
articles.journal: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
articles.abstract: Observational analyses of renal replacement therapy (RRT) use in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with acute kidney injury (AKI) are limited by the circularity between Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) AKI staging and RRT exposure. Retrospective cohort study of adults who developed AKI in 12 Queensland ICUs, Australia, from January 2015 to December 2021, with severity staged by KDIGO criteria with the RRT criterion removed. The primary outcome was the RRT utilisation proportion; secondary outcomes were the interval from ICU admission to RRT, biochemical values and cumulative fluid balance at initiation, and mortality. Trends were examined by unadjusted quasi-binomial regression and by mixed-effects logistic regression with a site random intercept, adjusted for demographics, illness severity, comorbidities, and organ support. Of 89 186 ICU admissions, 31 980 with AKI were included; 3475 (10.9%) received RRT. Unadjusted RRT utilisation did not change overall (odds ratio [OR] per year 1.001; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.982 to 1.019) and decreased in Stage 3 AKI (0.954; 0.926 to 0.983). After case-mix adjustment, utilisation increased (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) per year 1.041; 1.019 to 1.064; p < 0.001), including in stage 1 (1.061; 1.014 to 1.111; p = 0.011) and stage 2 (1.073; 1.031 to 1.118; p < 0.001) AKI, although stage 1 was significant in only nine of 13 sensitivity analyses. The interval to RRT shortened by 1.2 h per year (p = 0.001) and preinitiation fluid balance fell by 73 mL per year (p = 0.028). Biochemical values at initiation and mortality were stable. The trend was not consistent across sites (p < 0.001 for a site-specific slope). Adjusted RRT utilisation increased at the patient level overall and in stage 2 AKI, with a less consistent increase in stage 1 AKI; however, the trend was heterogeneous across sites. This highlights the importance of case-mix adjustment and of prospective indication-level data in future observational studies.

articles.title: Low-intensity versus medium-intensity continuous renal replacement therapy for critically ill patients (LIMIT) trial: Protocol summary and statistical analysis plan of a randomised clinical trial.
articles.journal: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
articles.abstract: Severe acute kidney injury in critically ill patients may require continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), yet mortality remains high. A standard CRRT intensity is 20-25 mL/kg/hr, because higher doses have not improved outcomes. Excessive treatment may cause harm by removing antibiotics and other essential substances and potentially impairing renal recovery. Observational data suggest that lower-intensity CRRT may be effective, warranting a clinical trial to compare low-versus standard-intensity therapy. The objective of this study was to describe the prespecified protocol and the statistical analysis plan of the low-intensity versus medium-intensity continuous renal replacement therapy for critically Ill patients (LIMIT) trial. The LIMIT trial is an investigator-initiated, multicentre, open-label, randomised clinical trial, with a target sample size of 400 participants. The trial compares low-intensity CRRT (12 mL/kg/hr) and medium-intensity CRRT (25 mL/kg/hr) in adult patients with acute kidney injury requiring CRRT in the participating intensive care units. The primary outcome is a hierarchical composite of survival and time to successful liberation from RRT through day 28 from randomisation, analysed using a win-ratio. Secondary outcomes include intensive care unit mortality, hospital mortality, dialysis dependence at hospital discharge among survivors, vasopressor-free days at day 28, and ventilator-free days at day 28. The LIMIT trial will evaluate the effect of low-intensity CRRT on mortality and time to successful liberation from RRT compared with medium-intensity CRRT in adults with acute kidney injury. Its findings may also inform future research on broader patient-centred and societal implications of CRRT intensity.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence and continuous renal replacement therapy.
articles.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is an important intervention in the treatment of acute kidney injury (AKI) in intensive care, and its application scope continues to expand alongside technological advancements and an increasing patient population. However, in current clinical practice, several factors, including individual patient differences, dynamic treatment needs, and the rational allocation of medical resources, pose challenges to CRRT implementation. The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) offers new approaches to address some of these challenges, and its applications in developing decision-support models, refining workflows, and supporting patient communication and education may contribute to more precise and efficient CRRT management. In this article, we discuss the current evidence and potential applications of AI in CRRT, as well as the challenges and strategies for clinical implementation, aiming to provide a reference for future research and clinical translation of AI-assisted CRRT.

articles.title: Relationship between selected microRNAs, pentraxin 3 and uromodulin in pathophysiology of septic acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication of sepsis and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients. Combined assessment of serum pentraxin 3 (PTX3), uromodulin (UMOD), and circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) may improve understanding of the pathophysiology of septic AKI. In this study, 81 critically ill adults with sepsis were stratified into AKI and non-AKI groups, and 90 healthy volunteers served as controls. Blood samples were collected on days 1 and 4 after the diagnosis of sepsis. PTX3 and UMOD concentrations were measured by ELISA, and miRNA expression was assessed by RT-qPCR. Seven miRNAs were validated, and their target genes associations were analyzed using TargetScanHuman8.0. PTX3 and UMOD distinguished healthy controls from septic patients, whereas only PTX3 differentiated patients with AKI from non-AKI. Baseline PTX3 and procalcitonin were independently associated with AKI on days 1 and 4. In AKI group, four analyzed miRNAs showed significant intercorrelations on day 1; however, these weakened by day 4 with changes in renal function and sepsis. Selected miRNAs were interpreted in the context of predicted target genes and pathways related to NF-κB signaling, renal cell apoptosis, and autophagy/mitophagy, rather than as direct causal regulators demonstrated in this study. PTX3, UMOD, and selected miRNAs provide complementary information on septic AKI and support a multifactorial concept of its pathophysiology.The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT06498336) on May 2, 2024 to March 31, 2026.

articles.title: Comparison of acute kidney injury after robot-assisted versus laparoscopic partial nephrectomy in high-risk patients: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Whether robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) compared with laparoscopic partial nephrectomy (LPN) in patients with limited renal reserve remains uncertain. We compared early AKI and six-month renal outcomes between approaches in high-risk patients. This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients with solitary kidney, documented CKD, or preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 who underwent laparoscopic or robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy between October 2015 and December 2023. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) adjusted for measured baseline differences. The primary outcome was creatinine-defined AKI within 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included AKI stage, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, length of stay, non-AKI complications, and 6-month renal function postoperatively. Sensitivity analyses restricted the cohort to 2021-2023 or applied overlap weighting. Among 227 patients, 76 underwent robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy and 151 underwent laparoscopic partial nephrectomy. After IPTW, 24-hour AKI occurred in 32.4% versus 26.9% (odds ratio [OR] 1.30, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.68-2.49; p = 0.425). AKI stage (common OR 1.27, 95% CI 0.70-2.31; p = 0.435) and ICU admission (20.0% vs 18.1%; p = 0.740) were similar. Operative duration was longer with RAPN (median difference 20.9 min; p < 0.001), whereas clamp time and blood loss were comparable. Postoperative length of stay was 4 versus 5 days (p = 0.058). Six-month eGFR was lower after RAPN (45.9 vs 51.0 mL/min/1.73 m2; median difference -5.1, 95% CI -9.5 to -0.7; p = 0.022), but percentage eGFR decline did not differ (p = 0.299). A > 20% decline occurred in 19.3% versus 9.3% (OR 2.33, 95% CI 1.00-5.45; p = 0.050). The primary AKI finding was consistent in sensitivity analyses. In high-risk patients, robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy was not associated with a lower incidence or severity of 24-hour postoperative creatinine-defined AKI compared with LPN. Six-month renal findings were exploratory and warrant confirmation.

articles.title: Association Between Urinary pH and Vancomycin-Associated Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract: Vancomycin (VCM) is an antibiotic widely used to treat Gram-positive bacterial infections but commonly causes severe acute kidney injury (AKI). Because VCM contains an amino group with a pKa of 7.2 and has an isoelectric point of 7.2, its ionization state may depend on urinary pH, potentially influencing susceptibility to VCM-associated AKI (VCM-AKI). This study aimed to clarify the relationship between urinary pH and VCM-AKI. This study analysed patients whose urinary pH was measured during intravenous VCM treatment at Chiba University Hospital between April 2013 and December 2024. The onset of VCM-AKI was determined using a modified KDIGO 2012 criteria. A multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with VCM-AKI. The number of analysed patients without and with AKI were 437 and 50, respectively. The multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that intensive care unit admission, loop diuretics use, serum VCM trough concentration and urinary pH (odds ratio, 0.69; 95% confidence interval, 0.48-0.98; p = 0.04) were significantly associated with VCM-AKI. The findings of this retrospective study suggest that urinary pH is significantly associated with VCM-AKI in hospitalized patients. Further prospective studies are needed to validate this association.

articles.title: Phosphate-containing versus phosphate-free replacement solution in critically ill patients requiring continuous renal replacement therapy: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Hypophosphatemia is a common electrolyte disturbance in critically ill patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of phosphate-containing versus phosphate-free replacement solutions in preventing CRRT-associated hypophosphatemia. In this multicenter randomized controlled trial, 90 patients requiring CRRT were randomly assigned to receive phosphate-containing or phosphate-free replacement solutions. The primary outcome was the incidence of hypophosphatemia during the first 48 h of CRRT. Prespecified secondary outcomes included phosphate supplementation, hyperphosphatemia, glucose-related safety outcomes, insulin requirements, and exploratory assessments of serum creatinine and SOFA score. A total of 90 patients were randomized (45 per group), with comparable baseline characteristics, including age, SOFA score, sepsis, CKD, and serum phosphate levels. Patients receiving phosphate-containing replacement solutions had a significantly lower incidence of hypophosphatemia than those receiving phosphate-free solutions (15.6% vs. 68.9%; adjusted OR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.01-0.18). The phosphate-containing group also required less phosphate supplementation. Hypoglycemia was more frequent in the phosphate-containing group than in the phosphate-free group (8.9% vs. 0%; p = 0.042). No significant between-group differences were observed in serum creatinine or SOFA score. Phosphate-containing replacement solutions reduced hypophosphatemia and phosphate supplementation requirements during the first 48 h of CRRT. Given the observed transient hypoglycemia and hyperphosphatemia, particularly in patients with preexisting hyperphosphatemia, careful monitoring of serum phosphate and glucose is warranted. Larger multicenter trials with longer follow-up are needed to determine whether these biochemical benefits translate into clinically meaningful patient outcomes.

articles.title: Association Between Daily Fluid Balance Trajectories and Dynamic Organ Failure Resolution (SOFA-2) in Sepsis: A Latent Class Growth Analysis of 16 262 Patients.
articles.abstract: BackgroundFluid management in sepsis has transitioned toward restrictive de-resuscitation during the intensive care unit (ICU) ebb phase (Days 3-7). The clinical heterogeneity of longitudinal fluid trajectories, their interaction with active therapeutic de-resuscitation, and their prognostic association with dynamic organ recovery evaluated under the 2025 SOFA-2 criteria require clarification in large multicenter databases.ObjectiveTo identify latent phenotypes of daily net fluid balance during the de-resuscitation phase and examine their independent associations with dynamic organ failure resolution and 28-day mortality after accounting for active de-resuscitation interventions.MethodsWe performed a retrospective observational cohort study of 16 262 adult septic patients from the MIMIC-IV v3.1 database who survived at least 72 h in the ICU. Daily net fluid balances (ml/kg/day) from Day 3 to Day 7 were modeled using group-based trajectory modeling without prior outcome stratification. Active de-resuscitation interventions, including cumulative intravenous loop diuretic dosing and renal replacement therapy (RRT), were extracted. Multivariable logistic regression and sensitivity analyses evaluated independent associations with 28-day mortality and longitudinal SOFA-2 trajectories.ResultsThree distinct trajectory phenotypes were identified: Class 1 (Rapid Recovery, 85.4%, n = 13 892), Class 2 (Late Response, 8.3%, n = 1354), and Class 3 (Persistent Failure, 6.3%, n = 1016). Class 1 maintained a steady, low net balance and experienced the lowest 28-day mortality (20.8%). Class 2 exhibited sustained high fluid retention until Day 5 before a delayed downward inflection, whereas Class 3 showed relentless fluid accumulation. Daily SOFA-2 scores resolved rapidly in Class 1 (decreasing from 4.24 on Day 3 to 1.18 by Day 7), whereas recovery was stalled in Class 2 (1.71 by Day 7) and persistently blunted in Class 3 (2.17 by Day 7). In multivariable logistic regression fully adjusted for baseline illness severity, loop diuretic exposure, and RRT, both Class 2 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.30, 95% CI 1.14-1.49; P < .001) and Class 3 (aOR 1.27, 95% CI 1.09-1.48; P = .002) were independently associated with increased 28-day mortality compared with Class 1. These associations remained consistent across sensitivity analyses restricted to non-RRT patients and loop diuretic users.ConclusionDiscrete longitudinal fluid balance phenotypes identify clinically distinct sub-populations during the de-resuscitation window of sepsis. Rather than proving direct causality, these trajectories serve as clinical markers of underlying endothelial integrity, intrinsic excretory capacity, and physiological responsiveness to de-resuscitation.

articles.title: Machine learning for early identification of delirium in ICU patients with acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Delirium is common in critically ill patients and is associated with worse outcomes, but its risk factors among adults with acute kidney injury (AKI) in the intensive care unit (ICU) are not fully described. We aimed to develop and validate a simple machine learning model to predict delirium during ICU stay in adult AKI patients and to identify the most important clinical predictors. We retrospectively included ICU patients aged 18 years or older with a diagnosis of AKI. The cohort was randomly split 70:30 into a training set and a validation set. Patients were labeled as having delirium or non-delirium based on events occurring during the ICU stay. In the training set, the Boruta algorithm was used to identify confirmed predictors, which were then fed into 9 supervised machine learning classifiers. Model performance was assessed in the validation set using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were calculated to interpret feature importance. Among the validation cohort, CatBoost showed the best discrimination with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.742 (95% confidence interval = 0.676-0.809). SHAP analysis of the final model identified diabetes, pneumonia, chloride, red blood cell, and prothrombin time as the most influential predictors of delirium. A CatBoost model built on Boruta-confirmed clinical variables showed moderate discrimination for ICU delirium in adults with AKI. The most influential predictors identified by SHAP - diabetes, pneumonia, chloride, red blood cell count, and prothrombin time - may help clinicians recognize high-risk patients and prioritize preventive measures. External validation is needed before wider clinical use.

articles.title: Earlier Application of Methylene Blue in Vasoplegic, Adrenergic Vasopressor-Resistant Patients is Associated with Better Clinical Outcomes. A Retrospective Analysis of 464 Patients.
articles.abstract: Severe shock hails a dismal prognosis for patients in intensive care units. Vasoplegic patients, refractory to adrenergic catecholamines face an increased risk for in-hospital mortality. However, the optimal timing for Methylene Blue (MB) in these vasopressor-resistant patients, remains unclear. This was a retrospective, single-center study conducted in the intensive care unit (ICU) of a tertiary medical center. 464 patients were included, 183 (39%) admitted to the general ICU and 281 (61%) to the cardiothoracic ICU. All patients developed vasoplegia and were treated with MB after a median time of 11.2 hours from admission. In the aggregated cohort, earlier MB administration was associated with lower ICU mortality (30% vs. 52%, p < 0.001), lower in-hospital mortality (41% vs. 59%, p < 0.001), lower 1-year mortality (46% vs. 62%, p < 0.001), and reduced need for continuous Veno venous hemofiltration (33% vs. 53%, p < 0.001). In survival analyses of the whole cohort, earlier MB administration was associated with reduced in-hospital mortality in univariate analysis (HR = 0.64; 95% CI 0.47-0.86, p = 0.003) and remained significant after multivariable adjustment (HR = 0.69; 95% CI 0.51-0.94, p = 0.018). ICU-specific analyses attenuated the association. In this retrospective, single-center cohort, earlier administration of MB was associated with improved clinical outcomes among ICU patients treated for vasoplegia, including lower mortality and reduced need for renal replacement therapy. Prospective studies are warranted to determine whether earlier MB administration should be incorporated into treatment protocols for adrenergic vasopressor-resistant vasoplegia.

articles.title: Applied pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic principles: A case-based approach.
articles.abstract: Knowledge of pharmacology is essential when caring for critically ill patients. Critical illness introduces several pharmacokinetic changes that affect the disposition of drugs in the body. Additionally, the presence of organ failures, common in this population, as well as the addition of extracorporeal devices can affect drug concentrations and lead to therapeutic failure or drug accumulation and toxicity. All phases of pharmacokinetics (absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination) can be affected. These derangements, that are dynamic throughout the course of critical illness, lead to profound pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic alterations, rendering models derived from healthy populations unreliable and making titration to objective pharmacodynamic targets and frequent reassessment, essential for achieving therapeutic success while minimizing toxicity and adverse effects. Recent innovations in technology, including artificial intelligence, present promising opportunities to guide drug dosing and predict adverse reactions based on patient characteristics. This review uses a patient case to demonstrate the importance of understanding these principles of pharmacology to optimize patient outcomes while minimizing the risk of harm from medications.

articles.title: ICU Mortality Associated With Clinically Important Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Multistate Analysis.
articles.abstract: Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding may increase mortality and time to discharge from the ICU. Conventional analyses ignore timing and treat bleeding as a binary event. We evaluated the association between time-dependent clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding and ICU mortality. A multicenter cohort study using data from an international stress ulcer prophylaxis trial. A total of 4821 invasively ventilated adult participants. None. A multistate model was specified with two transient ICU states (bleed-free and post-bleed) and four absorbing states (ICU discharge or death, each with or without bleeding). The Aalen-Johansen method was used to estimate transition and state occupancy probabilities and to describe risks of different clinical courses. Follow-up was censored at 90 days. We fit two Cox models for time to death in the ICU regressing on time-dependent bleeding history while adjusting for age, sex, baseline Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score, admission category (medical/surgical/trauma), vasopressor/inotrope use and renal replacement therapy on study day 1 and randomized allocation of pantoprazole or placebo; a second model also adjusted for time-dependent covariates of advanced life support (invasive mechanical ventilation, vasopressor/inotrope use, and renal replacement therapy). Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding developed in 104 patients (2.2%) in the ICU. Median ICU length of stay for those who experienced bleeding was 19 days (interquartile range [IQR], 11-30 d) vs. 9 days (IQR, 5-15 d) for those who did not. Accounting for immortal time bias, the time-dependent indicator of clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding was associated with increased ICU mortality (hazard ratio, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.13-2.15). At any time, patients who experienced bleeding had approximately 1.6 times the hazard of ICU mortality compared with those without a history of bleeding. Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding as a time-dependent event is associated with an increased risk of ICU mortality.

articles.title: Therapeutic plasma exchange and continuous renal replacement therapy for severe dengue with multiorgan failure: a case report and focused review.
authors: Medauar Reis de Andrade Moreira F
articles.abstract: Severe dengue can progress to acute liver failure, haemolysis, encephalopathy, shock, and multiorgan dysfunction, but the role of therapeutic plasma exchange in treatment remains uncertain. We report a 17-year-old adolescent with NS1-positive dengue managed with continuous renal replacement therapy, therapeutic plasma exchange, and comprehensive intensive care, and provide a focused narrative review of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue. The patient developed abrupt massive intravascular haemolysis, profound anaemia, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, encephalopathy requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, oliguric acute kidney injury, shock, and acute liver failure. She also met five of eight HLH-2004 criteria for secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Continuous renal replacement therapy was initiated before three therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, beginning with an exchange of 1·5 estimated plasma volumes using fresh frozen plasma. Haemodynamic, hepatic, renal, and coagulation parameters subsequently improved. Secondary infection and haemothorax requiring video-assisted thoracoscopic drainage complicated recovery; she was discharged 38 days after admission. Published evidence on the use of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue consists mainly of case reports, small series, and observational cohorts. Therapeutic plasma exchange can be considered an adjunctive rescue therapy in selected refractory cases, particularly acute liver failure or thrombotic microangiopathy phenotypes, but its independent benefit, optimal timing, prescription, and target population remain undefined.

articles.title: A Machine Learning-Based Early Warning System for Renal Replacement Therapy in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract: Renal replacement therapy (RRT) is a life-saving intervention for acute kidney injury in the intensive care unit (ICU). The decision to initiate RRT remains highly complex and subjective. Accurate and timely predictions for the need of RRT initiation are crucial components of personalized care. Using time series patient data (vital signs, laboratory findings, medications, ventilator settings, intake/output, risk scores), we aimed to develop machine learning (ML) models for predicting future initiation of RRT. Using data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-III, MIMIC-IV, and Electronic ICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU), we trained and internally validated models using dataset-specific training, validation, and test splits. We externally validated model performance using held-out eICU hospitals excluded from model development and a temporally distinct cohort of ICU patients admitted during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic period (2020-2022). Models were developed for: (1) screening patients for prediction of the need for RRT after their first 12 hours in the ICU; and (2) real-time dynamic prediction of the likelihood of documented RRT initiation within the next 24 hours. Here, we summarize the results of the ML model aimed at screening patients for early prediction of RRT. In internal validation, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.90 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.886-0.906) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.53 (95% CI, 0.496-0.564) in MIMIC-III. Results were similar in MIMIC-IV and eICU. External validation on ICU patients admitted during the coronavirus disease (COVID) period yielded an AUROC of 0.90 (95% CI, 0.894-0.913) and an AUPRC of 0.57 (95% CI, 0.534-0.602). Additional hospital-level external validation across eight individual eICU hospitals showed AUROCs ranging from 0.86 to 0.91 and AUPRCs ranging from 0.35 to 0.52. Accuracy ranged from 0.78 to 0.84 across validation experiments. By accurately identifying patients at high risk for RRT initiation, the early prediction ML model could serve as a triage tool to prompt closer nephrology evaluation or optimization of fluid and hemodynamic management before overt renal failure develops.

articles.title: A Deep Learning-Based Prediction Model for Mortality in Severe COVID-19 Patients Requiring Intensive Care Unit Admission: A Multicenter Registry Analysis.
articles.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been associated with substantial global mortality. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-based models have shown promise for mortality prediction, evidence focused specifically on critically ill patients remains limited. In addition, meaningful clinical implementation requires models that rely on a minimal set of readily available variables to enable rapid risk stratification. This study aimed to develop a deep learning-based model for predicting mortality in critically ill COVID-19 patients requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission, with an emphasis on efficiency and clinical applicability. This retrospective multicenter study included 900 critically ill patients with COVID-19 admitted to ICUs across 22 centers in Korea between January 1, 2020, and August 31, 2021. A deep learning-based tabular model was constructed, and systematic feature reduction strategies were applied to optimize predictive performance while enhancing practicality. Of the 900 patients, 365 (40.6%) survived and 535 (59.4%) died. Compared with survivors, non-survivors were older, demonstrated more severe clinical and chest X-ray (CXR) findings, had lower respiratory rate-oxygenation (ROX) indices, and required vasopressors and continuous renal replacement therapy more frequently (all P < 0.05). The initial model incorporating 66 variables achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.8500. Following stepwise feature selection, the model was reduced to seven key variables (age, C-reactive protein, lactate dehydrogenase, pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, CXR infiltration, CXR consolidation, and ROX index), resulting in a simplified model with an AUC of 0.8247. A deep learning-based AI model was developed to support clinical decision-making in critically ill patients with COVID-19, offering an efficient and clinically practical approach to mortality risk assessment.

articles.title: Monitoring of Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (VExUS) During Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy in the ICU: the MAVERIC pilot study.
articles.abstract: Venous congestion is increasingly recognised as a key determinant of organ dysfunction during acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Although the Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) score is a promising bedside marker of systemic venous congestion, its dynamic evolution during CRRT remains unknown. We aimed to describe serial changes in VExUS during CRRT and explore their association with ultrafiltration intensity and fluid balance. MAVERIC was a prospective single-centre observational pilot study including adults undergoing CRRT for acute kidney injury. VExUS was assessed before CRRT initiation and after 24 and 48 hours. The primary objective was to describe temporal changes in VExUS using an alluvial plot. Patients were classified into three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution. Associations with net ultrafiltration (NUF) and cumulative fluid balance were explored. Forty-seven patients were included. Overall, VExUS grades decreased significantly during the first 48 hours of CRRT (p =  0.0048). Three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution were identified: persistently low congestion (45%, n = 21), resolving congestion (32%, n = 15), and persistent or worsening congestion (23%, n = 11). Patients with resolving congestion had the highest NUF rates (1.35 [0.85-1.66] mL/kg/h) and the most negative cumulative fluid balance (-36.7 [-74.6 to -21.1] mL/kg), with significant differences across groups (p =  0.003 and p <  0.001, respectively). Patients with persistent or worsening congestion had lower NUF rates. Serial VExUS assessment provides dynamic information on systemic venous congestion during CRRT. Three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution were associated with differences in net ultrafiltration and fluid balance. Serial VExUS monitoring may help identify patients with persistent or worsening congestion, raising the hypothesis that it could inform reassessment of decongestion strategies. Whether integrating serial VExUS assessment into individualised decongestive strategies improves renal outcomes should be evaluated in prospective interventional studies.

articles.title: Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy During ECMO: More than Connecting Two Circuits.
articles.abstract: Background: Combining extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) raises questions concerning vascular access, circuit pressures, anticoagulation, and kidney recovery. We describe a single-center experience and frame the findings within the contemporary literature. Methods: Adults receiving concomitant ECMO and CRRT between January 2023 and June 2026 were retrospectively studied. Circuit performance, anticoagulation strategy, in-hospital mortality and kidney outcomes after intensive care unit discharge were described. Results: Twenty-six patients received CRRT during ECMO; 16 were managed with an integrated configuration and 10 with a dedicated dialysis catheter. Regional citrate anticoagulation was used in 49 of 72 CRRT circuits (68.1%). Overall mortality rate was 17/26 (65.4%). Among 72 CRRT circuits delivered during ECMO support, only three (4.2%) were interrupted because of technical failure. All 11 patients who survived to ECMO discontinuation continued to require CRRT; median observed post-ECMO CRRT duration was 17 days. At 90 days after ICU discharge, five of eight survivors with available kidney function follow-up had recovered to baseline and three had new-onset CKD; none of the nine survivors remained KRT-dependent. Conclusions: The combined use of ECMO and CRRT represents an evolving frontier of multiorgan support in a high-mortality population, in whom improving management and outcomes remains a major unmet need. This complex support requires technical expertise, an understanding of circuit interactions, and awareness of patient-specific clinical challenges and anticipated trajectories to enable individualized management. Nephrological care should therefore extend beyond circuit integration and the acute phase, encompassing kidney support and subsequent renal recovery.

articles.title: Outcomes of heart transplantation with or without pre-transplant mechanical circulatory support: a single-center cohort study in Korea.
articles.abstract: Heart transplantation is considered the definitive treatment for patients with end-stage heart failure (HF). Many patients with end-stage HF progress to cardiogenic shock or severe low cardiac output states while on the waiting list and require mechanical circulatory support (MCS) as a bridge to transplantation. The primary endpoint of this study was to assess overall survival after heart transplantation according to pre-transplant MCS use. The secondary outcomes included postoperative complications, intensive care utilization, and perioperative transfusion requirements. This retrospective single-center study included recipients of heart transplantation. A total of 100 consecutive patients were categorized into three groups according to pre-transplant MCS use (ECMO, LVAD, and non-MCS groups). Follow-up was censored on February 28, 2026. The mortality was significantly higher and the overall survival was significantly lower in the ECMO group than in the non-MCS group. Overall survival significantly differed among the three groups (log-rank P = 0.001), driven mainly by worse survival in the ECMO group than in the non-MCS group, whereas survival did not significantly differ between the ECMO and LVAD groups. The ECMO group showed a significantly worse survival than the non-MCS group, whereas survival did not significantly differ between the ECMO and LVAD groups, which was likely attributed to the small sample size of the LVAD group. Postoperative continuous renal replacement therapy and other markers of organ dysfunction were more frequent in the ECMO group and likely reflected the greater severity of illness in these patients rather than the independent risk factors.

articles.title: Predictive model for acute kidney injury in critical patients with pulmonary embolism based on machine learning: A multicenter clinical study.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is recognized as an acute, critical cardiovascular condition, and acute kidney injury (AKI) is frequently observed as a complication in this clinical context. Currently, no predictive tools are available to accurately assess AKI risk in critical patients with PE. A predictive model was developed in this study to estimate AKI risk in critical PE. Data obtained from Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV were utilized for the development of training and internal validation sets, while data derived from Emergency Intensive Care Unit Collaborative Research Database were employed for external validation. Eight machine learning models were developed through least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariate logistic analysis, and a web-based calculator was subsequently deployed. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration curve assessment, and decision curve analysis to determine discrimination, calibration accuracy, and clinical utility. Feature importance within the optimal performing models was quantified through Shapley Additive eXplanation analysis. Incremental predictive value relative to the pulmonary embolism severity index score was evaluated via net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement. A total of 2187 and 2183 patients diagnosed with critical PE were enrolled by 2 centers. In the training set, 1725 (78.88%) patients had AKI, whereas 1185 (54.28%) patients had AKI in the validation set. Hypertension, heart failure, pneumonia, sepsis, ventilation, respiratory rate, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, partial pressure of oxygen, lactate, and Oxford Acute Severity of Illness Score were ultimately identified as risk factors for AKI in critical PE. The extreme gradient boosting model demonstrated the most stable discrimination, calibration, and clinical benefit across training (area under curve [AUC] = 0.825), internal validation (AUC = 0.771), and external validation (AUC = 0.757) sets. Shapley Additive eXplanation analysis of the optimal model revealed that Oxford Acute Severity of Illness Score, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and partial pressure of oxygen contributed substantially to AKI risk. Relative to the pulmonary embolism severity index model, the proposed model exhibited superior performance in predicting AKI. A machine learning prediction model that integrates clinical indicators with disease activity scores was constructed and externally validated to estimate the risk of AKI in critical PE. A web-based calculator was subsequently developed to enable clinicians to identify high-risk cohorts and furnish evidence-based guidance for early intervention and individualized management.

articles.title: Transportable early renal recovery phenotypes and 30-day major adverse kidney events after sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: A MIMIC-IV discovery and eICU-CRD external-validation cohort study.
articles.abstract: Early renal recovery after sepsis-associated acute kidney injury is heterogeneous. We aimed to derive clinically interpretable early recovery phenotypes, assess their transportability through fixed-centroid external assignment, and examine associations with 30-day major adverse kidney events (MAKE30). This retrospective discovery and external-validation cohort study used Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV and eICU-CRD. Eligible patients were adults with a first intensive care unit stay and Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes -compatible acute kidney injury within 7 days of sepsis onset. K-means clustering integrated five renal, fluid, and hemodynamic domains across twelve 6-hour intervals after acute kidney injury onset. Stability was assessed by repeated 80% patient subsampling. eICU CRD patients were assigned to fixed MIMIC-derived centroids without reclustering. Modified Poisson models estimated adjusted risk ratios (RRs). Of 9725 Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV patients with known MAKE30 status, 2529 (26.0%) experienced MAKE30. Four phenotypes were identified in 7965 patients: low-burden rapid-recovery, preserved-diuresis intermediate-risk, oliguric kidney-failure, and shock-vasopressor. The four-cluster solution had a median adjusted Rand index of 0.939 (empirical 2.5th-97.5th percentiles, 0.892-0.990). Relative to the low-burden phenotype, adjusted MAKE30 RRs were 1.74 (95% confidence interval , 1.58-1.90), 3.80 (3.47-4.16), and 3.68 (3.34-4.06). In eICU-CRD, 4708 of 8771 patients (53.7%) could be assigned; corresponding RRs were 2.82 (2.45-3.23), 4.78 (4.00-5.72), and 4.99 (4.32-5.76). Unassigned patients had higher MAKE30 rates than assigned patients (41.1% vs 25.2%). MAKE30 associations persisted in landmark and distance-restricted analyses. Early renal recovery trajectories identified four reproducible clinical phenotypes associated with MAKE30. Fixed-centroid assignment reproduced the direction of these associations in eICU-CRD patients with sufficient trajectory data. Selective assignment and the observational design limit generalizability and preclude conclusions about phenotype-guided treatment.

articles.title: Distinct associations of age, frailty, and comorbidity with AKI occurrence, mortality, and kidney function recovery in older ICU patients: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in critically ill older adults, but the associations of chronological age and baseline vulnerability to kidney outcomes remain uncertain. We examined associations of age, frailty, and comorbidity with AKI occurrence, in-hospital mortality, and kidney function recovery. This retrospective cohort included adults aged ≥60 years admitted to six intensive care units at a Brazilian university hospital from 2023 to 2025. AKI followed KDIGO creatinine criteria; frailty was measured by the modified frailty index (MFI) and comorbidity by the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI). Modified Poisson (AKI occurrence), time-dependent Cox (mortality), and Fine-Gray (kidney function recovery, with death as a competing event) models were used. Among 2387 patients, illness severity and chronic kidney disease prevalence increased with age. AKI developed in 1396 patients (58.5%), rising from 56.2% (60-69 years) to 63.3% (≥80 years); age, MFI (adjusted risk ratio 1.030 per point), and CCI (1.028 per point) were each associated with AKI occurrence. AKI (hazard ratio 3.135, 95% CI 2.585-3.801) and age (1.039 per year) were associated with in-hospital death, whereas MFI and CCI were not after adjustment for acute illness. Of 927 survivors with AKI, 50.2% recovered by discharge. Age was not independently associated with recovery, whereas greater MFI and CCI were associated with lower recovery. Age, frailty, and comorbidity captured distinct dimensions of risk: AKI and age were associated with in-hospital mortality, whereas baseline vulnerability, more than age, was associated with kidney function recovery, supporting frailty and comorbidity assessment in ICU risk stratification.

articles.title: The Impact of Early Changes in Albumin Levels on Long-Term Kidney and Mortality Outcomes in Patients With Acute Kidney Injury Undergoing Continuous Kidney Replacement Therapy.
authors: LINking health medical records, biospecimens, and biosignals in Korean patients with Acute kidney injury consortium (LINKA) investigators
articles.abstract: To investigate the association between early changes in the levels of serum albumin during continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) and long-term dialysis dependence and mortality in patients with acute kidney injury who survived for 90 days or more days after CKRT initiation. A multicenter retrospective cohort study. Eight university-affiliated tertiary hospitals in South Korea participating in the LINking health medical records, biospecimens, and biosignals in Korean patients with Acute kidney injury consortium cohort. The study involved 1087 adult patients with acute kidney injury who survived for 90 or more days after CKRT initiation between January 2017 and June 2022. None. Based on albumin levels at CKRT initiation and on day 7, patients were categorized into the persistent, resolved, new-onset, and no hypoalbuminemia groups. A composite of progression to end-stage kidney disease and all-cause mortality within 365 days was the primary outcome. The composite outcome occurred in 33.4% (363/1087) of the patients. The adjusted odds ratio (aOR) for the primary outcome was significantly higher in all groups when compared with the no hypoalbuminemia group (persistent: aOR, 2.64; 95% CI, 1.73-4.04; p < 0.001; resolved: aOR, 2.27; 95% CI, 1.38-3.75; p < 0.001; new-onset: aOR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.06-2.68; p = 0.028). No hypoalbuminemia group was associated with the most favorable prognosis, whereas persistent hypoalbuminemia was associated with the worst outcomes. During CKRT, early albumin level changes are associated with long-term kidney failure and mortality risk. Persistent hypoalbuminemia predicts the worst outcomes. Even in patients without baseline hypoalbuminemia, early decline in albumin is associated with worse prognosis.

articles.title: Improving the delivered dose achievement rate in continuous renal replacement therapy: a quality improvement project.
Proteomics, Metabolomics, and Transcriptomics in Cardiac Surgery: A Narrative Review.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
articles.abstract: The objectives of this study were to examine how proteomics, metabolomics, and transcriptomics have changed the understanding of major complications of cardiac surgery, and to consider how these findings might inform future cardiothoracic anesthesia and perioperative critical care research. Across ischemia-reperfusion injury, cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB)-induced systemic inflammation and coagulopathy, postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF), cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI), delirium, and acute respiratory distress syndrome, omics studies indicate that these clinically similar syndromes are molecularly heterogeneous. Transcriptomics describes CPB-induced inflammation as an organized gene regulatory program; proteomics resolves network-level stress, complement, and tubular injury responses; and metabolomics captures rapid, phenotype-dependent shifts in substrate use, including the succinate-hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha axis linking ischemia to inflammation. Several signals-preoperative lipid-transport and redox proteins in patients with POAF, intraoperative proteomic shifts preceding delirium, and tubular metabolic reprogramming in patients with CSA-AKI-appear before conventional clinical criteria are met. The current contribution of omics is conceptual rather than clinical. Several molecular signals precede conventional clinical criteria, but earlier detection has so far not been shown to be actionable: there has been no randomized trial to test whether acting on an omics-derived signal alters outcome after cardiac surgery. Most evidence is derived from small, single-center, exploratory cohorts with limited independent replication, and no current guideline incorporates omics-based phenotyping. The near-term value lies in trial design-selection of higher-risk patients, matching interventions to plausible mechanisms, and sampling early enough to detect modifiable injury-rather than routine bedside use. Prospective serial sampling, standardized multicenter biobanks, and externally validated clinical-omics models are required before molecular phenotyping can guide perioperative care.

articles.title: Association of medication burden and potential drug-drug interactions with acute kidney injury among critically ill patients receiving anticancer therapy at a tertiary care centre.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: BackgroundCritically ill patients with cancer are exposed to many drugs, including anticancer agents, antimicrobials and supportive medications, which increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and potential drug-drug interactions (pDDIs). The contribution of medication burden and pDDIs to acute kidney injury (AKI) in this population is not well characterised.ObjectiveTo assess the association of medication burden and pDDIs with AKI among critically ill patients receiving anticancer therapy.MethodsThis retrospective observational study was conducted in the intensive care units (ICUs) of a tertiary care centre from August 2025 to September 2026. Adults with malignancy who received anticancer therapy within 30 days before or during ICU stay were included. AKI was defined and staged by KDIGO criteria. Medication burden (total drugs and nephrotoxic drugs) and pDDIs (screened using a standard interaction database) were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of AKI.ResultsOf 210 patients, 86 (41.0%) developed AKI. Patients with AKI had a higher median number of drugs (11 vs 8, p < 0.001) and pDDIs (6 vs 3, p < 0.001). Independent predictors of AKI were ≥10 distinct drugs (aOR 2.62; 95% CI 1.32-5.18), at least one nephrotoxicity-related pDDI (aOR 2.87; 95% CI 1.43-5.76), APACHE II score (aOR 1.09 per point), pre-existing CKD, sepsis, and cisplatin exposure. In-hospital mortality was higher with AKI (39.5% vs 21.8%, p = 0.007).ConclusionHigh medication burden and nephrotoxicity-related pDDIs were independently associated with AKI in critically ill cancer patients. Routine pharmacist-led medication review and renal-focused interaction screening may help reduce preventable kidney injury.

articles.title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Patients With Pulmonary Hemorrhage.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Severe pulmonary hemorrhage may lead to refractory hypoxemia and/or hemodynamic collapse and cause high mortality. However, the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in this patient population is rare. The aim of this study is to better define and understand this patient population by exploring the baseline characteristics, complications, and outcomes of patients who receive ECMO support due to pulmonary hemorrhage, based on data extracted from the extracorporeal life support organization (ELSO) registry. Between 2003 and 2023, 96 patients received ECMO due to pulmonary hemorrhage. Complications occurred in 54% of the patients, mainly acute kidney injury (AKI) with need for renal replacement therapy (RRT; 28%) and bleeding (pulmonary, gastrointestinal) (15%). Respiratory infections occurred in 37.1% of the patients. The most common diagnostic/therapeutic procedures were computed tomography scans in 9%, bronchoscopy in 41%, surgery in 8%, and apheresis in 6% of the patients. Interventional radiology procedures were performed in only 2% of the patients. Interpretation of these data should be performed cautiously, as underreporting is a known limitation of the ELSO Registry. Forty-seven patients (49%) were weaned from ECMO, and 46 (48%) survived until discharge. Survival and complication rates are comparable to the overall ECMO cohort in the ELSO Registry, which makes ECMO a feasible strategy in this patient population.

articles.title: The efficacy and safety of micronutrient complementation in adults during the acute phase of critical illness: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract: Critically ill patients often experience metabolic imbalances and potentially low micronutrient blood levels that worsen oxidative stress and impair immune function. Despite guideline recommendations, micronutrient complementation is inconsistently applied due to accessibility issues and the lack of validated assessment tools during acute critical illness. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the impact of early intravenous micronutrient complementation on clinical outcomes in ICU patients using real-world electronic medical record data. Adult ICU patients at National Taiwan University Hsinchu Branch from July 2024 to November 2025 who received parenteral nutrition (PN) for at least 24 hours were included. Patients were divided into a treatment group receiving micronutrients within 72 hours of ICU admission and a control group without complementation. Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and infectious complications after day 6 of PN; secondary outcomes included ICU/hospital length of stay, inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers, organ support needs, and refeeding syndrome incidence. Among 462 patients analyzed, 213 received early micronutrient therapy. Baseline characteristics such as age (control 65.3±16.6 vs treatment 67.7±13.8 years), BMI (control 28.70±8.95 vs treatment 23.74±4.91 kg/m2), admission categories (control MICU 10.2%, SICU 43.7% vs treatment MICU 9.3%, SICU 36.8%), APACHE II score (control 16.8±8.5 vs treatment 17.3±8.1), and TISS score (control 20.5±7.5 vs treatment 19.6±6.2) were largely comparable. Thetreatment group significantly reduced infectious complications, with logistic regression confirming protective effects (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.20-0.49, p<0.001). Secondary outcomes showed no differences in LOS, vasopressor use, oxygen therapy, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) requirement, PN duration, or refeeding syndrome. The treatment group exhibited delayed enteral nutrition (EN) initiation (control 8.9 ± 8.9 days vs treatment 11.0 ± 10.7 days; p=0.02) but demonstrated significant improvements in inflammatory and metabolic parameters. The linear regression model were performed and demonstrated significantly reductions in C-reactive protein (CRP)(B = -10.91 mg/dL, 95% CI -13.16 to -8.65, p<0.001), serum lactate levels (B = -1.49 mmol/L, 95% CI -2.58 to -0.40, p=0.007), and time to lactate normalization (B = -0.90 days, 95% CI -1.64 to -0.16, p=0.017). In subgroup analysis, a total of 213 patients were included, of whom 138 received standard micronutrient complementation, and 75 received micronutrients with additional zinc complementation, which demonstrated further benefits. For instance, the group receiving additional Zn reduced infectious complications (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.21-0.85, p=0.02), shorter ICU LOD (B = -3.97 days, 95% CI-7.64 to -0.30, p=0.03), and faster lactate clearance (B = -1.17 days, 95% CI -1.87 to -0.47, p=0.09). These results support early comprehensive micronutrient complementation to enhance immune and metabolic recovery in critically ill patients and highlight the need for prospective biomarker-guided studies.

articles.title: Timing of Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy, Cumulative Fluid Balance, and 90-Day Major Adverse Kidney Events in Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: We examined associations of continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) timing and cumulative fluid balance with major adverse kidney events at 90 days (MAKE-90) and CRRT liberation in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-centre cohort included 148 adults receiving CRRT. Exposures were early (≤24 h; n = 65) versus delayed (>24 h; n = 83) initiation after intensive care unit admission and cumulative fluid balance through 72 h after CRRT initiation. Analyses included multivariable logistic regression, competing-risk models, restricted cubic splines, and sensitivity analyses. Results: MAKE-90 occurred in 61.3% of evaluable early-CRRT patients and 75.9% of delayed-CRRT patients (unadjusted odds ratio 1.99, 95% confidence interval 0.97-4.08; p = 0.058). Delayed initiation was not associated with MAKE-90 after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio 1.01, 0.42-2.39). Each additional litre of fluid balance was associated with higher odds of MAKE-90 (1.34, 1.10-1.62; p = 0.003), a lower subdistribution hazard of liberation (0.86, 0.78-0.94), and a higher subdistribution hazard of death before liberation (1.23, 1.07-1.40). There was no evidence of non-linearity in the fluid-balance association (p = 0.912). Conclusions: Greater cumulative fluid accumulation was associated with adverse kidney outcomes and reduced CRRT liberation. These observational findings support prospective evaluation of individualised fluid management but do not establish a causal benefit from earlier CRRT or fluid removal.

articles.title: Association between pre-stroke anemia and risk of acute kidney injury following ischemic stroke: A multi-institutional retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Although anemia is an established risk factor for acute kidney injury (AKI), its specific impact on post-stroke AKI remains inadequately explored. This study aimed to investigate the association between pre-stroke anemia and the risk of developing AKI after acute ischemic stroke. This retrospective study, using the TriNetX research network database, identified adult patients who experienced their 1st recorded ischemic stroke between January 2010 and December 2023. Patients were categorized based on hemoglobin levels within 3 months pre-stroke: anemia (hemoglobin ≥8.0 and <12.0 g/dL) versus control (hemoglobin ≥12.0 g/dL). After 1:1 propensity score matching, we analyzed the outcomes at 1-year follow-up. The primary endpoint was the development of AKI during the follow-up period. Secondary endpoints comprised all-cause mortality, pneumonia, and intensive care unit admission. After propensity score matching, 61,896 patients were included in each cohort. Patients with pre-stroke anemia had a significantly higher 1-year risk of AKI (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.83-1.96), mortality (HR: 1.86, 95% CI: 1.80-1.93), pneumonia (HR: 1.76, 95% CI: 1.69-1.84), and intensive care unit admission (HR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.55-1.65) compared to controls (all P < .001). A graded association was observed between increasing anemia severity and adverse outcomes. The findings remained robust across sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Pre-stroke anemia is associated with an increased risk of post-stroke AKI and other adverse outcomes. However, given the observational nature of this study, future prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings and elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Recovery after more than one month of dialysis in legionella-associated acute kidney injury: a case evaluated with gallium-67 scintigraphy and renal biopsy.
articles.abstract: Distinguishing tubulointerstitial nephritis (TIN) from acute tubular necrosis (ATN) is clinically important in Legionella-associated acute kidney injury (AKI), because TIN may respond to corticosteroid therapy whereas ATN does not. However, kidney biopsy is often not feasible in critically ill patients, and noninvasive approaches to guide treatment decisions are needed. We report a 73-year-old man with severe Legionella pneumonia complicated by dialysis-dependent AKI persisting for more than one month despite resolution of the infection and discontinuation of all antibiotics by Day 9. Markedly elevated urinary beta2-microglobulin (118,539 μg/L at Day 28) and diffuse intense bilateral renal uptake on gallium-67 scintigraphy (grade 5, clearly exceeding liver and vertebral body uptake) on Day 31 supported ongoing renal inflammation in the setting of prolonged tubular injury. A diagnostic trial of prednisolone (0.5 mg/kg/day) was initiated; from approximately 1 week later, urine output increased, serum creatinine declined, and hemodialysis was successfully discontinued on Day 43. Renal function returned to pre-illness baseline by Day 57 (serum creatinine 0.75 mg/dL). Kidney biopsy performed after clinical stabilization showed acute tubular injury with chronic tubulointerstitial changes and a focal, reactive T-cell infiltrate; prior or partially treated TIN could not be excluded. This case shows that renal recovery remains possible in Legionella-associated AKI even after more than 1 month of dialysis dependence, and suggests that gallium-67 scintigraphy, interpreted alongside serial urinary tubular injury markers, may provide ancillary evidence of ongoing renal inflammation when biopsy is not immediately feasible.

articles.title: Association Between Succinylated Gelatin Exposure and Acute Kidney Injury in Critically Ill Trauma Patients: A Retrospective Five-Year Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Early fluid resuscitation is a cornerstone of trauma care, but the relationship between resuscitation strategies and acute kidney injury (AKI) remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate whether administration of 4% succinylated gelatin is associated with the development of AKI in critically ill trauma patients during the first seven days of intensive care unit (ICU) treatment. Methods: We conducted an observational retrospective single-center cohort study including 215 adult trauma patients admitted to the ICU at a tertiary care center between 2015 and 2020. Gelatin exposure, kidney function, and clinical outcomes were assessed from the pre-ICU phase through the first ICU week. The primary outcome was the development of AKI, at stage ≥ 2 of the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) staging. We used mixed-effects models, competing-risk analyses, correlation analyses and exploratory unsupervised clustering to explore associations between gelatin use and renal outcomes. Results: AKI occurred in 17% of patients and was associated with older age, higher Simplified Acute Physiology Score 3 (SAPS3), pre-existing comorbidities, and early signs of hemodynamic and metabolic compromise. Gelatin doses of ≥10 mL/kg/day were not associated with a consistent rise in serum creatinine or progression of AKI over time. Multivariable regression models revealed no independent association between gelatin and worsening AKI. Instead, KDIGO stage worsening was primarily associated with AKI present at ICU admission and with crystalloid volume. Clustering analysis identified a high-risk phenotype with increased gelatin exposure, but this cluster also showed pronounced shock and inflammation, suggesting confounding by indication. In a competing-risk analysis, gelatin was not associated with new-onset AKI, whereas higher gelatin doses were associated with a lower rate of ICU discharge. Conclusions: In this retrospective cohort of critically ill trauma patients, succinylated gelatin administration showed no statistically significant association with KDIGO-defined AKI progression across unadjusted and adjusted models. Gelatin doses of ≥10 mL/kg/day were more frequently administered in patients with greater hemodynamic instability, suggesting that gelatin use primarily reflected underlying illness severity rather than acting as a direct nephrotoxic agent. These findings provide no evidence of an independent nephrotoxic effect of gelatin when used as part of balanced trauma resuscitation strategies.

articles.title: Early enteral versus continued intravenous trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in critically ill adults: a comparative effectiveness study.
articles.abstract: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole is the preferred treatment for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP) and exhibits excellent enteral bioavailability. Critically ill patients are nevertheless frequently maintained on intravenous therapy despite limited supporting clinical outcome data. We compared outcomes associated with early enteral therapy versus continued intravenous trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole in critically ill adults with PCP. We performed a multicentre retrospective cohort study of adults with proven or probable PCP requiring intensive care from 2018 to 2025. A 48 h landmark design was used to minimize immortal time bias. Patients were classified by trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole route at 48 h as early enteral or continued intravenous therapy. The primary outcome was 30 day mortality. Secondary outcomes included 90 day mortality, new renal replacement therapy and average daily fluid balance through Day 5. Inverse probability weighting with doubly robust regression was used. Among 254 patients, 153 (60.2%) received early enteral therapy and 101 (39.8%) remained on intravenous therapy. Early enteral therapy was associated with lower adjusted 30 day mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.49; 95% CI, 0.27-0.89), an adjusted risk difference of -14.1% (95% CI, -25.6% to -2.5%). Early enteral therapy was also associated with lower 90 day mortality (aOR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.25-0.88). Renal replacement therapy and average daily fluid balance did not differ significantly. Early enteral trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole in critically ill adults with PCP was not associated with worse clinical outcomes. Although residual confounding cannot be excluded, prolonged intravenous therapy may be unnecessary when enteral administration is feasible. Prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: Sodium bicarbonate therapy for metabolic acidosis in critically ill patients: a Bayesian systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the effects of sodium bicarbonate therapy on mortality and renal outcomes in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis. We performed a systematic review and Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intravenous sodium bicarbonate with placebo or usual care in adult intensive care unit patients with metabolic acidosis. MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL were searched from inception to December 2025, with an updated search on 2 April 2026. The primary outcome was short-term all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT) initiation, 90-day mortality, RRT-free days, vasopressor-free days, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay and adverse events. Four RCTs including 1544 patients were analysed. Sodium bicarbonate did not show a clear short-term mortality benefit (RR 0.94, 95% CrI 0.73-1.22), with a posterior probability of benefit of 72.1%. For RRT initiation, sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower risk (RR 0.74, 95% CrI 0.59-0.98), with a posterior probability of benefit of 97.2%. Effects on other outcomes were small or imprecise, and no consistent safety signal was identified. Current randomised evidence does not demonstrate a clear survival benefit from sodium bicarbonate therapy in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis, but suggests a high probability of reducing RRT initiation. Further trials should define the patients most likely to benefit. PROSPERO registration: CRD420251246519.

articles.title: V-V ECMO for refractory near-fatal asthma: A 12-year single-centre observational study of clinical outcomes and psychological impact.
articles.abstract: To review the clinical data of adult patients receiving veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) for near-fatal asthma at a single UK respiratory ECMO centre, including morbidity and mortality follow up. Retrospective single-centre case series (2013-2025). A specialized UK respiratory ECMO centre. 79 adult patients with near-fatal asthma refractory to maximal conventional critical care management including mechanical ventilation. Veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. 79 patients (median age 35 years, 53% female and 47% male) were included. Pre-ECMO physiological derangement was profound (median pH 7.05, PaCO2 14.7 kPa). Median ECMO duration was 3 days (IQR 2-4). Survival to ICU discharge and 6-month survival was 98.7%. Complications occurred in 27.8% of patients, most frequently acute kidney injury requiring renal replacement therapy (10.1%). At 6-month follow-up, clinically significant anxiety and depression were present in 27.9% and 20.9% of survivors, respectively, while 37.2% screened positive for post-traumatic stress symptoms. Veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) represents an effective rescue therapy for patients with refractory near-fatal asthma, demonstrating excellent short- and long-term survival outcomes when applied in carefully selected cases. The incidence of complications remains acceptable and manageable within this context. The prevalence of anxiety and depression in this cohort appears to be lower than that reported in a published systematic review of the broader ECMO population; however, rates of post-traumatic stress symptoms are comparatively higher.

articles.title: The right drug in the wrong biological state? Alkaline phosphatase and cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury.
Ibuprofen Use and Acute Kidney Injury Among Adults Admitted to the Hospital.
articles.abstract: Although nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are the most effective nonopioid analgesics for acute pain, they may be underused in the inpatient setting due to uncertainty regarding the risk of acute kidney injury (AKI). Whether inpatient exposure to NSAIDs, such as ibuprofen, substantially increases AKI risk and how ibuprofen-associated AKI varies across patient subgroups remain unknown. To determine whether ibuprofen use is associated with AKI in hospitalized patients and whether the finding varies across AKI risk factor subgroups. A retrospective active-comparator cohort study of hospitalized patients (aged ≥18 years) without end-stage kidney disease or contraindications to NSAID treatment admitted from January 1, 2004, to June 30, 2017, in a large academic health system including 3 hospitals in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with follow-up until 48 hours after treatment end, hospital discharge, or 14 days elapsed, whichever occurred first. Analyses were conducted from March 2023 through August 2026. At least 24 hours of treatment with ibuprofen or oxycodone for acute pain. The primary outcome was AKI, defined by changes in serum creatinine and incident kidney replacement therapy (KRT). Balancing weights were used to adjust for baseline covariates and weighted Poisson regression used to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% CIs. This study included 78 656 patients (median age, 59 [IQR, 47-69] years; 38 092 females [48%]) treated with ibuprofen (n = 6313) or oxycodone (n = 72 343). There were 4799 AKI events (79% stage 1) during 270 472 days of follow-up (17.7 events per 1000 days). After adjustment for baseline differences, patients treated with ibuprofen had a higher rate of any AKI (IRR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.09-1.38), severe AKI (IRR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.08-1.72), and KRT (IRR, 3.29; 95% CI, 1.35-8.03). IRRs were greater in postoperative (IRR, 1.70 [95% CI, 1.28-2.27] vs 1.12 [95% CI, 0.98-1.28]) and critically ill (IRR, 1.65 [95% CI, 1.29-2.11] vs 1.16 [95% CI, 1.02-1.33]) patients. In patients at low risk (those non-critically ill, nonpostoperative, aged <60 years without kidney dysfunction; ibuprofen, n = 2966; oxycodone, n = 20 440), ibuprofen was not associated with higher AKI risk (IRR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.75-1.18). This study in an inpatient cohort found that ibuprofen was associated with higher rates of AKI and KRT, but this excess risk was concentrated in patients at high risk. Patients at low risk may be able to receive ibuprofen safely yet were often prescribed oxycodone.

articles.title: Modified Hybrid Repair with Open Reconstruction of Infrarenal Aortoiliac Segment for Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms Without Custom Distal Landing Zone: A Single-Center Case Series.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Inadequate distal landing zones can limit hybrid repair of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA). We evaluated a modified strategy combining prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction, retrograde visceral and renal revascularization, and thoracic stent-graft exclusion. Methods: This retrospective single-center case series included all nine consecutive patients with inadequate native distal landing zones who underwent single-stage modified hybrid repair in 2025. Open aneurysm excision and aortoiliac reconstruction provided the distal sealing segment and inflow for visceral and renal bypasses. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included postoperative length of hospital stay, 30-day major complication rate, 30-day paraplegia rate, 1-year reintervention rate, 30-day readmission rate, and technical success rate. Results: Five patients had Crawford extent II aneurysms and four had extent III aneurysms. Technical success was achieved in all nine patients. Median operative time, estimated blood loss, and intensive care unit stay were 724 min, 2500 mL, and 8 days, respectively. Thirty-day all-cause mortality was 0% (0/9). No spinal cord ischemia or mesenteric ischemia occurred within 30 days. Acute kidney injury occurred in six patients (66.7%), including one who received continuous renal replacement therapy. One patient required early covered stent-graft repair of a right iliac anastomotic leak. At a median follow-up of 9 months (IQR, 6-12), all reconstructed visceral and renal bypasses were patent, no new endoleak was detected, and all patients were alive. No additional reintervention was required. Conclusions: Modified hybrid repair with prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction was technically feasible in selected TAAA patients with inadequate distal sealing anatomy. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to evaluate durability and refine indications.

articles.title: From Biomarkers to Bedside: Guiding Therapeutic Strategies in Refractory Septic Shock of Abdominal Origin.
articles.abstract: Septic shock of abdominal origin remains one of the most challenging conditions in critical care, with a substantial proportion of patients progressing to a refractory state despite adequate source control and standard resuscitative measures. Molecular biomarkers are established tools for early diagnosis and prognostic stratification and have been proposed as candidate tools for individualizing therapeutic decisions. This narrative review examines the evidence on biomarkers relevant to abdominal sepsis-associated septic shock-including procalcitonin, presepsin, lactate, interleukin-6 and gut-derived markers of intestinal barrier dysfunction-and examines how far they may inform the timing of source control, vasopressor escalation and the use of adjunctive therapies. Every marker is classified as diagnostic, prognostic, treatment-monitoring or predictive (treatment-selection), since a marker associated with outcome is not thereby a marker that predicts benefit from an intervention. We report turnaround time and availability for each assay, and the effect of acute kidney injury and kidney replacement therapy on its interpretation. The review offers a practical, evidence-informed framework and identifies the gaps that warrant investigation. No biomarker-guided strategy in this population has been prospectively validated; biomarkers remain adjuncts to clinical, radiological and surgical assessment and must never delay source control.

articles.title: Clinical Impact of Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Among Patients With HIV/AIDS and Disseminated Histoplasmosis in a Hyperendemic Region of Northeastern Brazil.
articles.abstract: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome that may occur in people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA), often triggered by opportunistic infections such as disseminated histoplasmosis (DH). The substantial overlap in clinical and laboratory features between HLH and DH complicates timely diagnosis. To describe HLH among PLWHA with DH and compare clinical, laboratory and outcome characteristics between patients with and without HLH. A retrospective observational study was conducted at São José Hospital of Infectious Diseases, Fortaleza, Brazil, between March 2023 and June 2024. Hospitalised PLWHA with DH were evaluated for HLH based on the presence of ≥ 3 HLH-2004 criteria and an H-Score ≥ 169. Baseline clinical, laboratory and outcome parameters were compared between patients with and without HLH. Among 61 patients diagnosed with DH, 11 (18.0%) met the study criteria for HLH. Patients with HLH were more likely to present with hepatomegaly (p = 0.036), haemoptysis (p = 0.030) and lower platelet counts (p = 0.029). In-hospital mortality was significantly higher among patients with HLH (54.5% versus 18.0%; p = 0.019). These patients more frequently required renal replacement therapy (p = 0.028) and intensive care unit admission (p = 0.048). Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing demonstrated significantly reduced in-hospital survival among patients with HLH (p = 0.015). HLH represents a severe complication in PLWHA with DH and is associated with increased mortality and greater need for intensive care. Early recognition and use of adjunctive diagnostic tools may facilitate timely management and improve clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Extensive Stray-Dog Mauling as Major Contaminated Crush Trauma Causing Severe Rhabdomyolysis, Acute Kidney Injury, and Overt Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation: Recovery Without Renal Replacement Therapy.
articles.abstract: An adolescent male developed severe rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury, overt disseminated intravascular coagulation, and respiratory fluid overload after extensive stray-dog mauling. The course reflected overlapping traumatic, inflammatory, and infectious mechanisms. He recovered without renal replacement therapy through source control, individualized antimicrobials, conservative renal support, and timely transition to de-resuscitation.

articles.title: Cefepime Dose Individualization in Early Sepsis: A Pragmatic Feasibility Trial Protocol.
authors: Beta-Lactam Optimization and Outcomes Management (BLOOM) Study Group
articles.abstract: Cefepime is a core antibiotic in sepsis treatment, yet standard dosing yields 10- to 30-fold exposure variability in critical illness.
