VAP occurred in 100/5,918 ventilator-days (16.9 per 1,000) vs. 77/4,106 (18.8 per 1,000) (No CHX vs. CHX). The adjusted Poisson incidence rate ratio was 1.08 (95% CI 0.84-1.38; p = 0.56). 28-day mortality was 28.7% vs. 26.4% (no CHX vs. CHX) (adjusted OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65-1.15; p = 0.33). ICU length of stay was longer in the CHX arm (adjusted mean difference + 0.89 days, 95% CI + 0.19 to + 1.58; p = 0.013). BOAS and CPOT scores did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, adding 0.12% chlorhexidine to a standardized oral-care bundle did not reduce VAP incidence density or 28-day mortality and was associated with a modest increase in ICU length of stay. Routine CHX use provided no clear incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Regisrty- India (CTRI) identifier [CTRI/2024/02/062201], registered [01 February 2024].

articles.title: Bacterial epidemiology and attributable mortality of Ventilator-associated pneumonia before and after COVID-19 pandemic (2018-2021).
articles.abstract: BackgroundVentilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in mechanically ventilated patients. The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly modified VAP epidemiology and microbial ecology.MethodsWe conducted a prospective multicenter cohort study within the REA-REZO network (≈20% of French ICU beds), 1 January 2018-31 December 2021. All adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation were included. VAP was defined according to ECDC criteria. Primary endpoints were VAP incidence density (per 1000 ventilation-days) and 30-day attributable mortality. Secondary endpoints included resistance patterns and pre-pandemic versus pandemic trends.ResultsAmong 98,047 patients, 12,251 patients developed VAP, with an incidence of 18.9/1000 ventilation-days. Peak incidence occurred at day 10 (29/1000 ventilation-days). Thirty-day attributable mortality was 4.9% [95% CI 3.7;6.2], rising to 7.2% [6.0;8.5] at 60 days. Gram-negative bacteria accounted for 78.0% of isolates, predominantly Enterobacterales (46%) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (20%). Third-generation cephalosporin resistance reached 27% in Enterobacterales and 25% in P. aeruginosa. The COVID-19 patients had a higher VAP rate (19.5% vs 9.7%, p<0.001) and mortality (36.9% vs 31.0%, p<0.001).ConclusionsVAP remains highly prevalent in French ICUs with substantial attributable mortality. The COVID-19 pandemic nearly doubled VAP incidence and worsened resistance profiles. Intensified prevention bundles during the first 10 days of ventilation and reinforced antimicrobial stewardship are critical.

articles.title: Immunological signatures of sepsis in abdominal solid organ transplant recipients: A multilayer and multicentric prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection. Patients with prior abdominal solid organ transplantation (SOT) are highly susceptible to infection due to chronic immunosuppression, yet exhibit improved survival once sepsis occurs. The underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We conducted a post hoc analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort of septic patients (SepsisDataNet.NRW; n = 538). Clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Immune profiling included serum cytokines, flow cytometric immunophenotyping, plasma proteomics, and intracellular signaling using proximity ligation assays (PLA) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). To reduce clinical confounding, complementary exploratory analyses were performed in a non-septic kidney transplant cohort (e:KID). SOT patients demonstrated improved 30-day survival compared with non-SOT patients (84% vs. 66%; adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.95). Cytokine analysis revealed lower IL-6 and TNF-α levels alongside higher IL-18 concentrations, indicating an altered inflammatory profile. Flow cytometry showed reductions in adaptive immune cells but relatively preserved innate immune function, reflected by higher monocytic HLA-DR expression. Proteomics identified enrichment of innate immune, complement, and lipid metabolic response networks. PLA-based cellular analyses revealed increased GLUT1 expression and enhanced TFAM/TFB2M interaction in SOT patients, indicating a distinct immunometabolic marker profile. In e:KID patients paired serum metabolomics demonstrated higher glucose and lower lactate concentrations 12 months after transplantation, accompanied by broader alterations in lipid and branched-chain amino acid profiles. In patients with sepsis, abdominal SOT is associated with significant better survival than in non-SOT patients. Septic abdominal SOT patients display a distinct immune phenotype characterized by attenuated systemic inflammation, relative preservation of selected innate immune readouts, and alterations in immunometabolic markers.

articles.title: Quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly reveals a non-linear association with 30-day mortality in sepsis: a proof-of-concept pilot study.
articles.abstract: Direct, cell-resolved quantification of NLRP3 inflammasome activation in clinical patients has not been feasible. Previous studies have relied on indirect surrogates such as downstream cytokines, which are influenced by inflammasome-independent pathways and systemic clearance kinetics, potentially explaining the inconsistent prognostic findings reported in the literature. We applied a proximity ligation assay (PLA) to directly visualise NLRP3-caspase-1 complex formation in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of septic patients, providing a cell-specific, in situ readout of inflammasome assembly at the single-cell level. In this prospective, multicentre proof-of-concept pilot study, 78 patients fulfilling Sepsis-3 criteria were enrolled across three university hospitals. The PLA was validated in THP-1-derived macrophages against established readouts of canonical inflammasome activation prior to clinical application. Patients were stratified into low (n = 28), intermediate (n = 23), and high (n = 27) NLRP3 inflammasome activity groups. Median age was 64 years (IQR: 56-78), 63% were male, and median Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score was 8 (IQR: 4-12). Baseline characteristics, disease severity scores, and routine inflammatory biomarkers did not differ across activity groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed a non-linear pattern of 30-day survival, with the most favourable outcomes in the intermediate activity group. Both low and high activity were associated with increased mortality (log-rank p = 0.003). In adjusted Cox regression, low inflammasome activity (HR 7.88, 95% CI 1.79-34.65; p = 0.006) and high inflammasome activity (HR 4.35, 95% CI 1.01-19.88; p = 0.048) remained associated with 30-day mortality. Modelling PLA activity as a continuous variable using restricted cubic splines confirmed a significant non-linear association with 30-day mortality, independent of the tertile-based categorisation (p for non-linearity = 0.015). This proof-of-concept pilot study demonstrates that direct in situ quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly is feasible in septic patients and reveals a non-linear association with 30-day survival. These findings indicate that PLA-based profiling captures immune heterogeneity beyond routine inflammatory biomarkers. Larger independent cohorts are needed to validate these findings before clinical application or patient stratification can be considered.

articles.title: Candida Septic Shock: If Every Hour Matters, Who Requires Empiric Therapy?
Adjunctive therapeutic plasma exchange as rescue therapy in septic shock due to streptococcal infection: a multicentric retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Septic shock due to streptococcal infection (SRSS) carries a high mortality and is in part driven by toxin-mediated inflammation. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) may modulate the septic host responses by removing injurious mediators while replenishing protective plasma factors, but data specific to SRSS is lacking. We performed a retrospective, multicenter, cohort study of adults with SRSS between 2012-2024. Patients from three tertiary care ECMO centers in Germany and Switzerland were included requiring (i) streptococcal spp. detected in blood or primary focus and (ii) septic shock according to sepsis-3 definition. Adjunctive TPE with fresh frozen plasma at the intensivists` discretion was compared with standard of care (SOC). The primary outcome was 90-day-hospital mortality. Key exploratory outcomes included 24-h kinetics of vasoactive-inotropic score(VIS) and lactate, as well as SRSS-related complications. Results were validated in a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort. Of 149 patients, 31 (20.8%) received TPE and 118 (79.2%) SOC. TPE patients were more severely ill at baseline: SOFA 14 (IQR 13.5-15) vs 11 (IQR 8-14) (p<0.001); lactate 6.4 vs 2.8 mmol/L (p<0.001); Vasoactive-Inotropic-Score (VIS) 70.7 vs 23.3 (p<0.001); more frequent invasive ventilation (87% vs 65%), VV-ECMO (36% vs 19%), and renal replacement therapy (96.8% vs 52.5%). Overall, 90-day hospital mortality was 27.5% (TPE 29.0%, SOC 27.1%). Following SOFA-score adjustment, TPE was associated with lower mortality risk (aHR 0.67 [95% CI 0.5-0.9]; p=0.009). This was validated in the PSM cohort, with an aHR for TPE of 0.44 (95% CI 0.3-0.8); p=0.002. Mixed-effects modeling demonstrated a significant VIS reduction only with TPE (fixed effect 24-h change, p=0.027) and improved lactate decrease versus SOC. In SRSS, adjunctive TPE was associated with rapid hemodynamic stabilization and improved lactate kinetics. Exploratory adjusted survival analyses support prospective evaluation of TPE in SRSS.

articles.title: Molecular Subtypes in Acute Respiratory Illness and Sepsis.
articles.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Sepsis and acute respiratory illness are clinical syndromes that encompass profound biological heterogeneity. The resulting heterogeneity of treatment effect is now widely understood as the explanation to why immunomodulatory trials in critical care have not me their study endpoints, thereby misclassifying effective therapies as futile while concealing harm in biologically ineligible subgroups. High-dimensional molecular profiling offers a route to resolve this heterogeneity into tractable subgroups or subtypes. Here we review molecular subtypes across adult and paediatric sepsis, pneumonia, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), spanning transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic platforms. Blood transcriptomic frameworks derived independently in multiple countries, and subsequently harmonized by international consensus efforts, converge on recurring immune archetypes: a myeloid inflammatory state dominated by neutrophil activation; a mixed myeloid and lymphoid dysregulated state carrying the highest mortality; and a relatively immunocompetent state with preserved lymphocyte function and the most favourable clinical trajectory. Plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling recapitulate this architecture at orthogonal molecular layers, arguing that these archetypes are platform-independent rather than artefacts of any single technology. Cross-syndrome convergence is asymmetric, which plausibly reflects the methodological differences between top-down latent class analysis in ARDS and bottom-up unsupervised clustering in sepsis. Secondary analyses of randomized controlled trials consistently show subtype-dependent responses to treatment strategies, with a coherent directionality with potential benefit in hyperinflammatory states, and harm in immunosuppressed or adaptive immune-prevalent states. Subtype membership is not static; trajectory, not baseline assignment, most strongly encodes prognosis. Realising precision critical care now requires prospective, subtype-stratified trials of which none has yet been completed.

articles.title: Serial bedside retinal optical coherence tomography angiography in sepsis associated circulatory dysfunction.
Beyond avoiding failure: the proactive and beneficial role of appropriate antimicrobial therapy in the ICU.
Can Platelet Indices Predict Gram-Positive Bacterial Infections in ICU Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundUntil now, blood culture remains the gold standard for diagnosis of bloodstream infections (BSI). We investigated the diagnostic accuracy of complete blood count (CBC), particularly platelet indices, as a less expensive and more rapid alternative for the diagnosis of BSI, which allows for early proper antibiotic administration.MethodsA total of 169 patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) from July 2023 to July 2025 who had suspected BSI and were tested via blood culture (BC). Patients were classified into a BSI group (n = 143) and a non-BSI group (n = 26). The BSI group was further classified into three subgroups as Gram negative bacteremia (n = 87), Gram positive bacteremia (n = 46) and candidemia (n = 10). Demographic parameters and hematological parameters were recorded and compared between the groups. To evaluate sensitivity and specificity, we constructed receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.ResultsPatients with positive blood culture had significantly higher PCT, CRP, Neutrophil, PDW, MPV, MPV/PLT, PDW/PLT, and lower PWR, MPV/PCT, PDW/PCT & PLT/PCT compared to patients with negative blood culture. PLT/PCT, PCT, MPV/PCT, CRP, PDW & PDW/PCT have the highest AUCs (AUCs were 0.73, 0.71, 0.70, 0.69, 0.69 & 0.68, respectively). RDW, MPV/PLT, and PDW/PLT significantly increase, and platelet count significantly decreases among patients with Gram-positive compared to patients with Gram-negative bacterial infection. RDW, platelet, MPV/PLT & PDW/PLT have the highest AUC and accuracy in diagnosis of Gram-positive bacteria (AUC were 0.64, 0.62, 0.62 & 0.62, respectively).ConclusionThe RDW, platelet count, MPV/PLT, and PDW/PLT demonstrated the greatest accuracy in predicting Gram-positive bacterial infections.

articles.title: Brachial-to-Radial Pressure Gradient in Critically Ill Patients Treated With Vasoactive Agents: A Prospective Observational Study.
authors: Polish Perioperative and Critical Care Research Group (PERI-CRIT)
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To determine the incidence of a significant noninvasive brachial-to-radial arterial pressure gradient (NIBR-APG) and its clinical associations in critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents. DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, observational study. SETTING: Thirteen ICUs in Poland. PATIENTS: Adult ICU patients with radial arterial catheters receiving vasoactive agents hospitalized between April 2025 and July 2025. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Invasive radial mean arterial pressure (MAP) and noninvasive brachial MAP were measured twice and averaged. A NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg was predefined as clinically significant. Baseline characteristics, hemodynamic variables, and outcomes were recorded. Among 303 patients, 49.5% were surgical admissions and 33.3% had septic shock. The median NIBR-APG was 4.5 mm Hg (interquartile range, 0.0-10.0 mm Hg). Fifty-six patients (18.4%) exhibited a NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg. Compared with patients without a significant gradient, these patients received higher norepinephrine-equivalent doses (0.23 vs. 0.10 µg/kg/min), had higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (11 vs. 10), prolonged capillary refill time (3.0 vs. 2.5 s), and higher lactate concentrations (2.7 vs. 1.3 mmol/L). In multivariable analysis, only vasoactive drug dose was independently associated with NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg (odds ratio, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.12-2.52). ICU mortality was higher in patients with significant gradients (48.0% vs. 30.1%). CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one in five critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents demonstrated a clinically significant NIBR-APG. The presence of this gradient was independently associated with higher vasoactive drug requirements and was accompanied by greater illness severity and higher ICU mortality.

articles.title: Scientific Output in Septic Shock According to Country Income and Gender: A Meta-Epidemiological Study.
articles.abstract: We aimed to assess trends in septic shock publications by country income and author gender. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for articles indexed with "septic shock" between January 2014 and December 2024. All peer-reviewed publication types were eligible. Conference abstracts and non-peer-reviewed material were excluded. Bibliographic data, first and last author affiliations, country income level (World Bank classification: low- and middle-income countries [LMICs] and high-income countries [HICs]), and journal prestige (SCImago Journal Rank [SJR]) were extracted. Author gender was inferred using the NamSor application programming interface (API). Of 10,352 eligible publications, LMIC-affiliated first authors increased over time (+2.13% per year; 95% CI, +1.66 to +2.61; p < 0.001) from 18% in 2014 to 37% in 2024. Women represented 35.6% of first authors and 25.0% of last authors (with around 20% of authors not classifiable by the NamSor API), with higher proportions in LMICs than HICs (p < 0.001) for both first authors (44.5% vs. 32.5%) and last authors (35.2% vs. 21.5%). Gender concordance was more frequent, with female first authors more often paired with female last authors than male first authors (31.7% vs. 21.1%). Cross-income collaborations, especially involving LMIC last authors, remained rare. Articles led by men in HICs were more often published in higher-SJR journals compared with those led by women (p < 0.001), whereas no gender differences were observed among LMIC-affiliated authors. Despite encouraging growth in LMIC contributions and female representation, major inequities persist. Strengthening equitable collaborations and supporting underrepresented groups would broaden participation and enhance the global applicability in critical care research.

articles.title: Role of Mitochondrial Impairment in Sepsis-Induced Platelet Activation.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced mitochondrial impairment has been described in different organs, in both animal models and humans. Excessive radical oxygen species (ROS) could be involved in this phenomenon. As a result, antioxidants have been proposed as a potential therapeutic strategy, although results remain controversial. Platelet hyperactivation is considered a central pathogenic mechanism in the development of sepsis-induced organ damage. In this study, we aimed to determine whether mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to platelet hyperactivation during sepsis. We also evaluated the effect of ROS scavenging using the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoTEMPO. Laboratory investigation. University Hospital. Patients with sepsis/septic shock (n = 3/7), nonseptic burn patients (n = 10), and healthy control subjects (n = 10). Platelet mitochondria and isolated platelets from healthy donors were treated in vitro with plasma from patients with sepsis/septic shock and healthy subjects, before and after preincubation with MitoTEMPO. We measured platelet oxygen consumption rates in isolated human platelets using the Seahorse Extracellular Flux Analyzer. Platelet mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activity was measured in mitochondria-enriched fractions by spectrophotometry. Platelet aggregation in platelet-rich plasma was analyzed using light-transmission aggregometry, and leukocyte-platelet adhesion in whole blood by flow cytometry.We found that incubating platelets with septic plasma significantly reduced basal, maximal, and adenosine triphosphate-linked oxygen consumption rate. Incubation of platelet mitochondria with septic plasma also reduced platelet Complex I activity, compared with healthy plasma or plasma from nonseptic burn patients. This decrease was associated with an increase in Epinephrine-induced platelet activation. Preincubating platelets with the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO significantly reversed these effects. Our results show that the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO prevents mitochondrial dysfunction and enhances platelet activation induced by septic plasma in human platelets in vitro. This may help in designing new therapeutic approaches to prevent sepsis-induced organ damage mediated by mitochondrial dysfunction and platelet hyperactivation.

articles.title: Delay From Hypotension Onset to Appropriate Antifungal Therapy Initiation Is the Critical Determinant of Outcome in Candida Septic Shock.
authors: and the Cooperative Antimicrobial Therapy of Septic Shock (CATSS) Database Research Group
articles.abstract: To determine the effect of delays in initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy from the initial onset of persistent hypotension to the outcome of Candida septic shock. Retrospective cohort study. A total of 32 academic and community hospitals in Canada, the United States, and Saudi Arabia (July 1989 to June 2018). A total of 850 adult patients with culture-positive Candida septic shock. None. Out of 850 patients with Candida septic shock, 69.2% patients (589) received appropriate antifungal therapy after the onset of persistent hypotension. A strong relationship was observed between the delay in initiation of pathogen-appropriate antifungal (PAA) therapy and hospital survival. The adjusted odds ratio of death was 1.045 per hour of delay (95% CI, 1.035-1.056; p < 0.0001). The survival rate was 86% when an appropriate antifungal for the isolated pathogen was administered within 2 hours of the initial documentation of persistent hypotension. Thereafter, hospital survival decreased an average of 5.0% per hour for each hour of delay to 10-12 hours of delay. In a multivariate analysis, which included the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score and epidemiologic/therapeutic variables, the time to initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy emerged as the single strongest predictor of outcome. Sensitivity analysis further demonstrated that the adverse effects of delayed antifungal treatment were consistent across various subgroups, including different types of infections, pathogens, and antifungal drug classes. Median time to appropriate antifungal therapy was 32.3 hours (interquartile range, 11.2-66.0 hr), with only 16.9% receiving therapy within 6 hours of hypotension onset. Administration of PAAs within the first hours of documented hypotension significantly improved hospital survival. Less than 20% of patients received appropriate antifungals within 6 hours of documented hypotension.

articles.title: Pancreatic stone protein versus conventional biomarkers for prognostic discrimination in sepsis: a meta-analysis of paired AUC comparisons.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic stone protein (PSP) has been proposed as a prognostic biomarker in sepsis, but its comparative performance versus C-reactive protein (CRP) and procalcitonin (PCT) remains uncertain. We performed a meta-analysis of direct within-study paired AUC comparisons between PSP and CRP and/or PCT in critically ill adults with sepsis, septic shock, or acute infection-related conditions in whom sepsis development or clinically relevant adverse outcomes were prospectively evaluated. Differences in AUC (ΔAUC) were pooled using random-effects models. The principal conservative analysis included one comparison per independent cohort and comparator. Seven studies comprising 803 unique participants contributed 21 paired comparisons. In the principal conservative analysis, PSP showed a higher prognostic AUC than CRP, with a pooled ΔAUC of 0.179 (95% CI 0.095-0.262; p < 0.001), although between-cohort heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 81.65%). Compared with PCT, the pooled ΔAUC was 0.153 (95% CI 0.114-0.193; p < 0.001), with no observed heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%). The mortality-only sensitivity analysis showed a similar pooled effect for PSP versus CRP (ΔAUC 0.17, 95% CI 0.08-0.26), with substantial heterogeneity persisting, and for PSP versus PCT (ΔAUC 0.153, 95% CI 0.114-0.193), with no observed heterogeneity. Exclusion of the clinically distinct intra-abdominal infection cohort (Michailides et al.) likewise did not materially change the PSP-versus CRP estimate (ΔAUC 0.166, 95% CI 0.077-0.256). The direction and approximate magnitude of the pooled effects were also preserved across alternative assumptions for the within-study correlation. Available comparative evidence suggests that PSP may have greater prognostic discrimination than CRP and PCT. The findings were broadly maintained across sensitivity analyses, but the limited number of independent cohorts and substantial heterogeneity in the CRP comparison warrant caution. Further prospective studies are required to confirm these findings and establish their clinical relevance. This systematic review was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420261340301).

articles.title: Vasopressors Combination Therapy (Norepinephrine Plus Vasopressin Receptor Agonists) Improve Septic Shock Outcome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundStudies showed different results of vasopressors combination therapy in septic shock patients. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the outcomes of combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists in adult septic shock.MethodsCochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and PubMed databases were searched up to September 27, 2026, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists versus norepinephrine alone in septic shock patients. Two reviewers independently extracted data on mortality, ICU length of stay, renal replacement therapy (RRT) and adverse events. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) was applied to assess random error.ResultsTwenty-one RCTs involving 3873 septic shock patients were included. The results showed that the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists was associated with lower mortality at the longest complete follow-up compared with norepinephrine alone (RR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.83 to 0.99, P = .02), but with an increased risk of digital ischemia (RR = 2.21, 95% CI 1.15 to 4.27, P = .02). Subgroup analysis indicated that the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists may provide survival benefits for more severe septic shock patients (RR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.00, P = .04). Moreover, compared with norepinephrine alone, the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin showed a trend towards reducing the longest follow-up mortality (RR = 0.89, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.00, P = .05). TSA indicated lack of firm evidence for a beneficial effect.ConclusionsIn adults with septic shock, the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists may reduce mortality at the longest complete follow-up compared with norepinephrine alone (low quality of evidence), but may increase risk of digital ischemia (low quality of evidence). This benefit mainly appeared in more severe septic shock patients. Moreover, norepinephrine plus vasopressin may confer a survival advantage.

articles.title: Early adequate empiric antifungal therapy and 28-day mortality in ICU patients with candidemia: a pooled patient-level analysis of EUROBACT-1 and EUROBACT-2 cohorts.
articles.abstract: The optimal timing of empiric antifungal therapy in patients with suspected candidemia remains uncertain. In practice, many antifungal treatments initiated empirically are eventually found to be unnecessary, exposing patients to potential toxicity, selection of non-albicans Candida species, emergence of resistance, and additional costs. The objective of the study was to evaluate whether adequate empiric antifungal therapy initiated within 2 days after blood culture draw was associated with 28-day mortality. We performed a pooled secondary analysis of two prospective worldwide observational cohorts (EUROBACT-1 and EUROBACT-2) including adult patients with Candida bloodstream infection. The exposure was defined as receipt of adequate antifungal therapy within 2 days after blood culture draw. Propensity scores for receiving early adequate antifungal therapy were estimated using prespecified covariates, and inverse probability of treatment weights were applied in a weighted Cox proportional hazards model to assess the association with 28-day mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted according to study cohort, Candida species, and presence of hypotension at the time of bloodstream infection. As a sensitivity analysis, a frailty Cox proportional hazards model including a random center effect was performed. The final study population included 272 patients with candidemia from 158 centers, including 81 from EUROBACT-1 and 191 from EUROBACT-2. One hundred and ten patients received early adequate antifungal therapy and 162 did not. Overall, 38.6% of patients (105/272) died within 28 days, including 40.9% (45/110) in the early adequate therapy group and 37.0% (60/162) in the non-early adequate therapy group. In the weighted Cox model, early adequate antifungal therapy was not significantly associated with 28-day mortality (HR 1.23, 95% CI 0.82-1.83, p = 0.314). Results were consistent across subgroup analyses according to study cohort, Candida species, the presence of hypotension at the time of bloodstream infection, as well as in the frailty Cox sensitivity analysis. Early adequate antifungal therapy was not independently associated with improved 28-day survival in ICU patients with candidemia. These findings support a more targeted approach to early empirical antifungal treatment and underscore the need to identify patient subgroups most likely to benefit from immediate therapy.

articles.title: Toward very early vasopressin use in septic shock: observational data accumulate but trial evidence still lacking.
Fluid Therapy in Mechanically Ventilated Critically Ill Adult Patients.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Fluid therapy is ubiquitous in the intensive care unit (ICU) but carries risks, especially in mechanically ventilated patients. Contemporary global practice across dose, indication, and type is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To characterize ICU fluid practices in mechanically ventilated adults. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: International prospective observational cohort study between April 2024 and July 2025, across 206 ICUs in 41 countries on 6 continents. Consecutive adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation within 3 days of ICU admission and ventilated 24 hours or more. Exclusion criteria were age younger than 16 years and transfer under mechanical ventilation from another ICU. EXPOSURES: Fluid volume, indication, and type after intubation. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Key measures included (1) total infused volume and daily fluid balance over 7 days after intubation; (2) the indication for fluid therapy over the first 3 days after intubation; (3) the proportion of total administered fluid volume attributable to each fluid type over the first 3 days after intubation. RESULTS: Among 2454 patients analyzed (median age, 63 years [IQR, 49-73 years]; 63.6% [1560] male), median daily fluid input peaked on day 1 at 3.0 L (IQR, 2.2-4.0 L) and declined to 2.6 L (IQR, 1.8-3.5 L) through day 6. Daily fluid balance (median, 0.9 L; IQR, 0.1-1.9 L on day 1) decreased to less than 0.3 L (IQR, -0.5 to 1.2 L) by day 3 and remained near-neutral through day 6. Maintenance and replacement fluids (to meet daily requirements and to correct ongoing losses; 31.9%) and creep fluids (to deliver medications and maintain catheter patency; 30.9%) were the primary indications, whereas resuscitation (to restore circulating blood volume; 16.0%) accounted for a smaller proportion. Isotonic balanced crystalloids (48.9%) and isotonic saline (0.9% sodium chloride) (27.0%) were common; colloids were rare (1.3%). Substantial between-site variation persisted after adjustment for case-mix. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this prospective international cohort study, fluid therapy varied widely among mechanically ventilated critically ill patients, with maintenance and creep fluids-rather than resuscitation fluids-accounting for most total volume.

articles.title: Long-Lasting Mental Disorders in Caregivers of ICU Sepsis Survivors and Their Association With Patients' Post-Intensive Care Syndrome: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
authors: Investigating Long-term Outcomes of ICU patients with Sepsis or Septic shock (ILOSS) Study Group
articles.abstract: To investigate the prevalence of long-term mental disorders in caregivers of ICU sepsis survivors and examine associations with post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) in patients. Prospective observational study. Twenty-one mixed ICUs. Caregivers (the next of kin) of the patients diagnosed with sepsis between November 2020 and April 2022. None. Caregivers and patients were assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months after hospital discharge by telephone and mail. The primary outcome was caregiver mental disorders (mental post-intensive care syndrome-family [PICS-F]). Mixed-effects logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate the association between caregiver PICS-F and patient PICS. Ninety-four caregiver-patient dyads were analyzed. Caregivers were a median of 67 years old (55-79 yr old), 31 (33.0%) were male, and 41 (43.6%) were spouses. Patients were a median of 74 years old (69-82 yr old), and 54 (57.4%) were male. The prevalence of mental PICS-F did not decrease from 3 to 12 months (43% vs. 42%, respectively), whereas the presence of PICS symptoms in patients decreased from 82% to 62%. In mixed-effects logistic regression, the presence of PICS symptoms in patients was significantly associated with PICS-F (adjusted odds ratio, 3.00; 95% CI, 1.54-5.88; p < 0.01). Among the individual patient PICS domains, only mental PICS was significantly associated with PICS-F (3.71; 2.03-6.77; p < 0.01), whereas physical and cognitive impairments in patients were not. The prevalence of mental PICS-F in caregivers of ICU sepsis survivors was frequent and long-lasting over the first year after hospital discharge. Since it was most strongly associated with patients' mental disorders rather than physical or cognitive impairments, the mental PICS domain in patients may be an important indicator of PICS-F and should be considered in future studies.

articles.title: Escalating Vasopressor Intensity and the Goals-of-Care Documentation Gap in Septic Shock: Relevance to the Proposed Refractory Shock Threshold.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe 2026 joint SCCM/ESICM Delphi consensus identified vasopressor intensity as a defining feature of refractory septic shock, yet its relationship to real-world goals-of-care documentation remains unclear.ObjectivesWe assessed the association between escalating vasopressor intensity and documented surrogate goals-of-care markers among septic shock decedents.MethodsRetrospective cohort study of adult septic shock decedents in MIMIC-IV (2008-2022) requiring vasopressors ≥6 h and surviving ≥24 h after initiation. Vasopressor intensity was quantified by peak norepinephrine equivalent (NEE) dose during ICU stay and stratified as: 0.01-0.50 (stratum 1), >0.50-0.99 (stratum 2), and ≥1.00 µg/kg/min (stratum 3). The primary outcome was death without documented surrogate goals-of-care markers, defined as having neither a documented do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order nor documented palliative care involvement.ResultsThe final cohort included 2458 patients: stratum 1 (n = 1033), stratum 2 (n = 909), and stratum 3 (n = 516). Death without documented goals-of-care markers increased across strata (23.8%, 28.3%, 31.2%; p-for-trend=0.001). After multivariable adjustment, stratum 3 patients remained more likely than stratum 1 to die without documented goals-of-care markers (aOR 1.32; 95% CI 1.02-1.69; p = 0.03). Palliative care documentation declined progressively with increasing vasopressor intensity (59.2%, 52.0%, 46.9%; p-for-trend<0.001), accompanied by lower rates of integrated DNR/palliative care documentation (47.0%, 40.0%, 36.4%; p-for-trend<0.001). Patients exceeding the Delphi-proposed refractory shock threshold (NEE >0.50 µg/kg/min) were more likely to die without documented goals-of-care markers than those below the threshold (29.3% vs 23.8%; p = 0.002).ConclusionHigher vasopressor intensity was paradoxically associated with a greater likelihood of death without documented goals-of-care markers and with lower palliative care documentation. These findings suggest a disconnect between escalating physiologic severity and documentation of surrogate goals-of-care markers in refractory septic shock and warrant further evaluation.

articles.title: The impact of intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiac surgery for infective endocarditis.
articles.abstract: Postoperative sepsis and/or systemic inflammatory response syndrome caused by infective endocarditis (IE) can lead to significant postoperative mortality. Intraoperative hemoadsorption therapy has shown promising results in the treatment of sepsis and dysregulated inflammatory response during cardiac surgery. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of intraoperative hemoadsorption in high-risk patients with IE undergoing cardiac surgery. A total of 176 high-risk patients with IE were enrolled from 10/2020 to 10/2024. Patients with intraoperative hemoadsorption (HA group, n = 93) were compared to patients without hemoadsorption (control, n = 83). The primary endpoint was a composite of 30-day mortality, incidence of vasoplegic syndrome within the first 24 h and 7 days postoperatively, and intensive care (ICU) stay, analyzed using an unmatched hierarchical win-ratio method. There were no differences in baseline characteristics between the groups. The mean hemoadsorption time was 106 ± 61 min in the HA group. Vasoplegic syndrome was more frequent in the control group (49.4% vs. 24.7%, p < 0.001). Importantly, 30-day mortality was also significantly lower with intraoperative hemoadsorption (7.5% vs. 20.5%, p = 0.003). The mean ICU stay was shorter in the HA group (7.8 ± 4.6 vs. 11.5 ± 4.2 days, p < 0.001). The analysis met the primary endpoint in favor of patients receiving intraoperative hemoadsorption (win ratio 3.83; 95% CI 2.55, 5.74; p < 0.001). In high-risk cardiac surgery patients with IE, the intraoperative use of hemoadsorption was associated with a significantly lower incidence of postoperative vasoplegic syndrome and lower overall 30-day mortality. These findings should be interpreted in the context of the study's methodological limitations and confirmed in future randomized controlled trials. This study was approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB00012919) of the French Society of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery (CERCSFCTCV20251021).

articles.title: Bioactive adrenomedullin dynamics and microcirculatory changes in a porcine model of hemorrhagic shock.
articles.abstract: Hemorrhagic shock is a leading cause of preventable trauma death, marked by impaired oxygen delivery and endothelial dysfunction. Bioactive adrenomedullin (bio-ADM) regulates endothelial barrier integrity, but its dynamics during hemorrhagic shock and resuscitation remain unclear. This secondary analysis of a porcine hemorrhagic shock model investigated bio-ADM and its association with macro- and microcirculatory parameters during resuscitation. All animals received crystalloid infusion (10 mL/kg/h) from anesthesia induction onward. Shock was induced by blood withdrawal to maintain MAP at 40 ± 5 mmHg for 60 min (T5), before randomization to control (n = 7), fluid (n = 6), or noradrenaline (n = 7) groups, with intervention groups titrated to MAP targets of 65 then 90 mmHg (60 min each). Macrocirculation was assessed via vital signs and pulse contour analysis; microcirculation via hyperspectral imaging (tissue oxygenation, hemoglobin, water index). Fluid resuscitation improved macrohemodynamics and microcirculatory oxygenation versus control and noradrenaline, which failed to sustain perfusion and impaired microcirculatory oxygenation. Bio-ADM increased after shock induction (p < 0.001), peaking at T9 (120 min of therapy). At T5, levels were comparable among control (16.8 [13.6-18.9] pg/ml), fluid (15.65 [15.43-16.55] pg/ml), and noradrenaline (14.3 [7.85-18.95] pg/ml). Thereafter, bio-ADM continued to rise in control (19.7 [17.4-32.6] pg/ml) and noradrenaline (21.2 [14.4-33.45] pg/ml), while stabilizing in the fluid group (12.05 [10.65-15.18] pg/ml); accordingly, the T5-T9 increase was smaller in the fluid group than in control (p = 0.022) or noradrenaline (p = 0.003). The fluid group received ~3-fold more fluid by T9. Higher bio-ADM correlated with lower MAP, higher lactate, and lower ScvO₂, but not oxygen delivery (DO₂); a higher tissue water index correlated with a smaller rise. Bio-ADM increased during hemorrhagic shock, extending previous observations from cardiogenic and septic shock, and represents a comparatively non-specific marker of endothelial and microcirculatory stress rather than specific to any single shock etiology. Effective resuscitation was associated with stabilization, rather than a clear decrease, of bio-ADM levels, though this coincided with higher fluid administration, and dilution cannot be excluded. Whether bio-ADM offers therapeutic utility to guide resuscitation remains unclear, warranting further prospective evaluation in animal and human studies.

articles.title: The effect of preload on Doppler systolic time in a large emergency department cohort with suspected sepsis.
articles.abstract: Change in the corrected flow time of the common carotid artery (ccFTΔ) during a preload challenge (PC) is a surrogate for stroke volume change (SVΔ) to infer preload responsiveness (PR). This is a retrospective cohort study comprising patients with suspected sepsis in a large, publicly funded, academic emergency department; no patient health information is linked to the Doppler assessments. Carotid Doppler spectrograms from a wireless, wearable critical care Doppler ultrasound system are analyzed for ccFTΔ during a PC (either infusion of 300 mL of crystalloid over 3 min or a Trendelenburg maneuver). The primary objectives of this study are to describe the proportion of PR patients by previously described ccFTΔ thresholds (i.e., both 4 and 7 ms ccFTΔ ), describe time-to-peak (TTP) ccFTΔ, and evaluate the ability of baseline ccFT to detect ccFTΔ during PC, using both the equations of Wodey and Bazett. Comparisons of related outcomes were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm procedure, baseline ccFT discrimination was quantified using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and TTP was estimated using patient-level bootstrap resampling. Threshold-agnostic ccFTΔ trajectories were additionally explored using unsupervised k-means clustering of patient-level temporal responses for both correction equations. A PC was attempted in 4367 patients and an adequate ccFTΔ was collected from 4,128 patients (95%). In total, 982,937 Doppler cardiac cycles are included. The median ccFTΔ was 7.3 milliseconds (ms). 51.9% of patients had a ccFTΔ ≥ 7 ms, while 68.6% had a ccFTΔ ≥ 4 ms by the equation of Wodey. For Bazett, these fractions were 61.2% and 73.5%, respectively. For patients identified as PR based upon either a 4 ms or 7 ms ccFTΔ threshold, the time-to-peak ccFTΔ was 27.5 s for both equations. Baseline absolute ccFT did not discriminate PR from PUR patients under both correction formulae (AUROC 0.56-0.57). To our knowledge this is the largest reported dataset of ED patients with suspected sepsis receiving PR assessments by Doppler ultrasound, comprising nearly 1 million Doppler cardiac cycles obtained from over 4100 ED patients. Both 7 ms and 4 ms ccFTΔ thresholds described clinically-accepted rates of PR. The TTP was roughly 30 s into PC and baseline ccFT did not accurately detect ccFTΔ during PC. Finally, a hypothesis-generating analysis identified four distinct ccFTΔ trajectories during PC which may represent unique preload response patterns during PR testing.

articles.title: The impact of ventilation mode on systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction in a porcine model of abdominal sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome.
articles.abstract: Sepsis commonly causes acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and immune hyperactivation may be a causal link. Ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) is common in ARDS, and VILI may potentiate organ dysfunction in severe sepsis. We used a porcine model of abdominal sepsis-associated ARDS to test whether ventilation strategy could impact systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction. Female Yorkshire pigs (6-8 months) underwent ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury of the small bowel and fecal clot implantation or sham laparotomy. The abdominal sepsis animals were ventilated with a volume-controlled (VC) mode using the ARDS-Net low tidal volume (LVt) method to set and adjust the mode, and applied at two time points. Late LVt, was applied once PaO2/FiO2 was ≤300, and Early LVt was applied immediately following injury. The third lung protective group used the airway pressure release ventilation (APRV) mode set and adjusted with the time-controlled adaptive ventilation (TCAV) method, also applied immediately after injury. Animals were supported for 48 h using standardized resuscitation protocols and euthanized. Physiologic variables, clinical lab data, lung histology, and plasma proteome were assessed. Sham animals showed no evidence of sepsis or ARDS, whereas all experimental animals developed septic shock, requiring fluid resuscitation and vasopressors. Both LVt groups developed ARDS as measured by PaO2/FiO2 ratio by the study end (Late LVt: 129.9±16.0; Early LVt: 205.2±24.2), while the Early APRV group did not (429.4±59.4). The Sham and experimental groups all had similar proteomes at baseline. The proteomes diverged over time and ended in three distinct groups: Sham, Late LVt/Early LVt, and Early APRV. The most significantly differentially expressed proteins distinguishing the groups were involved in the immune and inflammatory response, with APRV having the lowest inflammatory signature. In a porcine model of abdominal septic shock we found that animals ventilated with a higher mean airway pressure strategy (APRV) had decreased plasma proteomic signatures of inflammation compared to those ventilated with a conventional low tidal volume strategy. Our findings are hypothesis generating and not directly translatable to the clinical setting. Future studies should focus on further elucidating a link between VILI and its effect on systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction.

articles.title: Effect of vasopressin and its analogues on microcirculatory perfusion: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Arginine vasopressin (AVP) is a non-adrenergic vasopressor increasingly used in the management of shock. While it restores arterial pressure, its effects on the microcirculation remain uncertain, with potential for reduced regional perfusion and tissue oxygenation. The aim of this systematic review is to evaluate the effects of intravenous AVP and its analogues on microcirculatory perfusion across different haemodynamic conditions and vascular beds. A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Web of Science was conducted. Animal and human publications evaluating the effects of intravenous AVP or analogues on microcirculatory perfusion assessed with in vivo microcirculatory imaging or flowmetry techniques were included. Publications were grouped by haemodynamic condition and vascular bed. Of 1693 records, 39 publications (31 animal, 7 human, 1 combined) were included, comprising 43 study-units and 152 individual measurements. Overall perfusion was decreased in 33%, unchanged in 48%, and increased in 19% of measurements, compared with baseline, saline, or other vasopressors. By haemodynamic condition, perfusion was decreased/unchanged/increased (n=study-units; % of measurements) in physiological conditions (n = 14: 57/38/4), vasodilatory or septic shock (n = 23: 24/55/21; versus baseline, fluid resuscitation or noradrenaline), haemorrhagic shock (n = 3: 17/17/67; versus baseline, saline or noradrenaline), cardiac dysfunction or arrest (n = 2: 0/67/33; versus adrenaline or noradrenaline) and cirrhosis-related portal hypertension (n = 1: 0/0/100). Across vascular beds: gastrointestinal tract (n = 18: 30/42/27), kidney (n = 9: medulla 77/23/0, cortex 27/64/9), sublingual bed (n = 7: 19/68/13), cerebral cortex (n = 2: 0/67/33), cutaneous bed (n = 6: 42/42/17), and conjunctiva (n = 1, 100/0/0). AVP and its analogues reduced microcirculatory perfusion most consistently under physiological conditions, whereas effects in vasodilatory or septic shock were more heterogeneous. Across vascular beds, the highest proportion of measurements showing reduced perfusion was in the renal medulla. These results highlight the divergent effects of vasopressin across vascular beds and clinical conditions.

articles.title: ESICM LIVES 2026.
Antibiotic Stewardship in Nonoperative Facial Trauma: Necessary or Not?
articles.abstract: Closed facial fractures are common and often treated nonoperatively. Routine systemic antibiotic prophylaxis is controversial because infection rates are low and antibiotics can cause harm. We assessed whether prophylactic antibiotics reduce infectious complications in closed, nonoperative facial fractures. A systematic review was conducted of adults with closed, nonoperative facial fractures (emergency department, inpatient, intensive care unit). PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through September 19, 2025. Studies compared systemic prophylaxis versus none and/or ≤24 hours versus >24 hours. Seven US studies comprising 3274 patients met the inclusion criteria. Across studies, fracture-related infection rates were low and were not reduced by prophylactic antibiotics. In the largest prospective multicenter cohort, Mian et al reported a 30-day facial fracture-associated infection rate of 1.0%, with no significant benefit for ≤24 hours or >24 hours of prophylaxis compared with none (adjusted odds ratio 1.24-1.32). Orbital and zygomatic cohorts reported no infectious complications regardless of prophylaxis strategy. In sinus-involving and intensive care unit cohorts, fracture-site infection and sinusitis were rare; most infectious events were pneumonia or ventilator-associated pneumonia rather than facial fracture-specific infections. Longer antibiotic exposure was associated with isolated cases of Clostridioides difficile colitis. Available evidence does not support routine systemic prophylaxis for uncomplicated closed, nonoperative facial fractures. The strongest inference applies to patients without another indication for antibiotics. Current data do not identify fracture-specific subgroups in whom prophylaxis improves outcomes; accordingly, management should emphasize local care, return precautions, and structured follow-up.

articles.title: State-of-the-art review: ß-blockade in critical illness.
articles.abstract: Critical illness is characterised by activation of the sympathetic nervous system which plays an important adaptive role in maintaining cardiovascular stability and organ perfusion. However, excessive sustained adrenergic stimulation may become maladaptive, contributing to tachyarrhythmias, myocardial injury, immune dysregulation, metabolic derangements, and organ dysfunction. This state-of-the-art review evaluates the role of ß-blocker therapy as a potential strategy to modulate or counteract the adrenergic response in critically ill patients. Current data suggest that their use remains highly context-dependent and controversial. There are established benefits in selected scenarios, including acute myocardial infarction, tachyarrhythmias, hypertensive emergencies, thyroid storm, and prevention of variceal bleeds. In contrast, evidence is limited or conflicting in septic shock, traumatic brain injury, acute heart failure, burns and other critical care syndromes. Concerns include impairment of compensatory cardiovascular responses, reduction of cardiac output, hypotension, and compromised organ perfusion. Furthermore, the safety and efficacy of ß-blockade appear to depend on the type and dose of ß-blocker, patient phenotype, timing of initiation, hemodynamic reserve, and whether therapy represents continuation of chronic treatment, withdrawal and re-initiation, or de novo initiation during acute illness. This review highlights major gaps in knowledge, including the absence of reliable indicators to identify patients most likely to benefit, uncertainty regarding optimal treatment targets and monitoring strategies, and limited randomised evidence in heterogeneous ICU populations. A phenotype-driven, physiology-guided approach that accounts for hemodynamic status, sympathetic spectrum and timing of ß-blocker therapy is likely required to optimise outcomes.

articles.title: Distinct weaning phenotypes in patients unsuccessful in weaning from invasive mechanical ventilation: a secondary analysis of the WEAN SAFE cohort.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterise the trajectories and outcomes of patients who enter the weaning process but fail to wean from invasive mechanical ventilation (MV). METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the WorldwidE AssessmeNt of Separation of pAtients From ventilatory assistancE (WEAN SAFE) cohort, we examined weaning duration and intensity, decisions to withdraw or withhold life-sustaining therapy (WLST), and clinical outcomes in patients not weaning from invasive ventilation. The primary outcome was ICU mortality. RESULTS: Of the 5664 patients in the study population, 1270 (22.4%) never underwent a separation attempt (SA), while 4394 (77.6%) had at least one SA; of these, 664 (15.1%) eventually failed weaning from invasive MV at day 90, while 3730 (65.9%) successfully weaned. Failed-Wean patients had the longest duration of invasive ventilation and longest ICU stay of all groups. Compared with Successful-Wean, Failed-Wean patients underwent more separation attempts, but fewer attempted extubations and more reintubations and tracheostomies. ICU mortality was 78% in Failed-Wean compared with 2% in Successful-Wean. Three clinically distinct Failed-Wean phenotypes were identified, distinguished by separation attempt count and WLST timing: Phenotype A (single SA + WLST), Phenotype B (single SA, no WLST), and Phenotype C (> 1 SA). A failed-first SA was strongly associated with WLST decisions. In this cohort, a WLST decision was associated with a higher hazard of ICU mortality and shorter median time to ICU death. CONCLUSIONS: Three weaning failure phenotypes were identified with distinct clinical profiles, weaning trajectories, and outcomes. A strong relationship exists between failed first separation attempts, WLST decision, and the risk of death, which deserves further investigation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03255109.

articles.title: [A preliminary study on the protective effect of dapagliflozin on multi-organ function in the early stage of sepsis].
articles.abstract: Objective: This preliminarily study aims to evaluate the short-term efficacy and safety of dapagliflozin on multi-organ functions in patients with sepsis. Methods: This single-center, prospective, randomized controlled clinical trial enrolled 136 patients with sepsis to the Intensive Care Unit of Northern Jiangsu People's Hospital between April and December 2025. The patients were randomly assigned to the intervention group and the control group. Both groups received standardized treatment for sepsis, and the intervention group was also administered with dapagliflozin at a dose of 10 mg for 5 days. Changes in the sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) scores after the intervention served as the primary outcome. The secondary outcomes included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), renal function indicators, and clinical prognosis. Results: There were no statistically significant differences in the baseline data and changes in SOFA scores before and after treatment between the two groups (50 patients per group, P>0.05). On the 5th day of treatment, the median LVEF was significantly higher in the intervention group [60.0% (55.0%, 62.5%)] than in the control group [55.0% (49.0%, 58.0%), P<0.001]. The 28-day all-cause mortality rate in the intervention group [26% (13/50)] was lower than in the control group [36% (18/50)], but the variance did not reach statistical significance (P=0.387). The incidences of adverse events were comparable between both groups. The intervention group showed higher distribution of urine ketone body grades (Z=-2.1, P=0.040), but ketoacidosis was not observed. Conclusions: The short-term treatment of sepsis patients with dapagliflozin did not significantly reduce the SOFA scores, but improved LVEF and showed a trend of reducing all-cause mortality at 28 days. The short-term treatment was safe.

articles.title: Integrating Hemodynamic Indices Into the Definition of Refractory Septic Shock: Is There a Role for Catecholamine Refractoriness and Assistance Guide Based on Cardiogenic Shock Hemodynamics (CRASH) Index?
New Criteria for Refractory Septic Shock: Relying on Treatment to Define a Disease.
Analysis of the etiology of infection and antimicrobial resistance in chronic critically ill patients: a longitudinal study.
articles.journal: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)
articles.abstract: Hospital acquired infections and sepsis play an important role both as a triggering factor for chronic critically illness [CCI] and as a common complication of this syndrome. The aim of this study is to describe the clinical progression of sepsis episodes in CCI patients in the intensive care unit [ICU] of a Brazilian public hospital. A retrospective longitudinal study was conducted in a general ICU, from July 2022 to June 2023. The convenience sample consisted of 779 patients. Demographic, clinical, and microbiological data were analyzed. The incidence of CCI was 20.9% (n=166). Septic shock on the first day of hospitalization occurred in 60.2%, and the hospital mortality rate was 50%. A total of 362 episodes of infection were recorded. Ventilator-associated pneumonia [VAP], urinary tract infection (UTI), and bloodstream infection (BSI) were the most prevalent infections (40%, 20.7%, and 19.6%, respectively). Bacteria of the ESKAPE group - (Enterococcus spp., Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterobacter spp.) accounted for 57% of all positive samples, showing high bacterial resistance, with a predominance of resistance to carbapenems in Gram-negative bacilli. The incidence of CCI at the research institution was high. Factors such as SAPS3 score, multiple infections, and diagnosis of shock or sepsis were predictors of in-hospital mortality. VAP was the most prevalent site of the recorded infection episodes. Multidrug-resistant bacteria from the ESKAPE group were identified from admission, and formal temporal analysis demonstrated a statistically significant increase in antimicrobial resistance over the course of hospitalization, particularly when the main Gram-negative pathogens were analyzed together.

articles.title: Procalcitonin-guided antibiotic therapy in ICU patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis with GRADE and trial sequential analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)
articles.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of PCT-guided antibiotic therapy compared with standard care in adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients with sepsis or septic shock. PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and Web of Science were searched from database inception to January 2026 to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing PCT-guided antibiotic strategies with standard care in adult ICU patients with suspected or confirmed bacterial infections. The primary clinical outcome was all-cause mortality at the longest available follow-up, whereas the key antimicrobial stewardship outcome was duration of antibiotic therapy. Secondary outcomes included infection relapse, new infection or superinfection, antimicrobial-free days, clinical cure, and length of ICU or hospital stay. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using intention-to-treat data. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) and the GRADE framework were applied to assess the conclusiveness and certainty of the evidence. Sixteen RCTs involving 7,966 patients were included. PCT-guided therapy did not reduce all-cause mortality compared with standard care (RR = 0.99, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.06; p = 0.72), with trial sequential analysis indicating insufficient evidence to draw a definitive conclusion. In contrast, PCT-guided strategies significantly reduced antibiotic duration (MD = -1.51 days, 95% CI -2.24 to -0.78), with trial sequential analysis confirming a conclusive benefit. Procalcitonin guidance was associated with an increase in antimicrobial-free days without higher rates of new infection, superinfection, or clinical failure. Additionally, no significant differences were observed in ICU or hospital length of stay. In adult ICU patients with sepsis or septic shock, RCT-guided antibiotic strategies were associated with reduced antibiotic exposure and increased antibiotic-free days, without a detectable improvement in survival. These findings support the use of procalcitonin as an adjunctive antimicrobial stewardship tool, provided that it is integrated with clinical assessment, microbiological data, and sound clinical judgment.

articles.title: Association between urine pH on ICU day 1 and 90-day mortality in sepsis: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)
articles.abstract: Urine pH is an easily obtainable bedside indicator of urinary acidification; however, its prognostic value in sepsis remains unclear. We investigated the association between urine pH measured on intensive care unit (ICU) Day 1 and 90-day mortality in patients with sepsis. This single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted at Shiga University of Medical Science Hospital between August 2011 and April 2023. Adult ICU patients with sepsis who had urine pH measured on ICU Day 1 were included. Urine pH was assessed using dipstick colorimetry, and the earliest value within 12 h of ICU admission was analyzed. The primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality. Associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Among 468 patients (median age 72 years; 61.8% male), the 90-day mortality rate was 25.6%. Spline analysis showed no evidence of nonlinearity (P=0.331). Each 0.5-unit increase in Day-1 urine pH was associated with lower 90-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.572; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.422-0.776; P<0.001). Mortality was 30.2% in patients with urine pH ≤6.0 and 11.4% in those with urine pH >6.0; higher urine pH remained associated with lower mortality risk after adjustment (adjusted HR 0.279; 95% CI 0.147-0.529; P<0.001). Urine pH on ICU Days 2 or 3 was not significantly associated with mortality. Lower urine pH on ICU Day 1 was independently associated with increased 90-day mortality in sepsis, suggesting that urine pH may complement early risk stratification in critically ill patients.

articles.title: Direct hospital costs and cost drivers in Greek intensive care units: a micro-costing analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)
articles.abstract: Intensive Care Units (ICUs), though comprising a small proportion of total hospital beds, represent a disproportionately high share of healthcare expenditure. Accurate cost assessment is vital for optimizing resource allocation, particularly in resource-limited settings like Greece. To estimate the direct hospital cost of ICU hospitalization in adult patients using a micro-costing approach and to identify clinical and organizational factors driving these costs. A prospective surveillance study was conducted over two years in four multidisciplinary adult ICUs in the Attica region. Detailed patient-level data on demographics, clinical status, interventions, and resource use were collected daily. Direct ICU costs, both fixed and variable, were calculated from the hospital perspective using a bottom-up micro-costing approach. Multivariable linear regression was used to identify independent predictors of ICU costs. The analysis included 500 patients, representing 12,689 patient-days. The total hospitalization cost was €6.33 million. The median cost per ICU admission was €7,756.8, with variable costs comprising 72.5% of total expenditures. Antibiotics accounted for nearly 50% of variable costs. Significant independent cost drivers included blood transfusion (additional €2,063), prolonged ICU stay (each day added ~€264), ventilator-associated events (+€2,374), central line-associated bloodstream infections (+€1,877), surgical site infections (+€6,609), and patient-to-nurse ratios >2 (+€5,000). ICU costs are shaped not only by patient severity and interventions but also by modifiable structural factors such as infection rates and staffing ratios. Investments in infection prevention, evidence-based transfusion practices, and adequate nurse staffing could yield substantial cost savings while improving patient outcomes in Greek ICUs. These insights provide critical, evidence-informed guidance for strengthening critical care in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Effect of furosemide deresuscitation on fluid distribution and bioelectrical impedance analysis parameters in septic patients: a secondary analysis of a double-blind, randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a leading cause of mortality globally, accounting for 11 million deaths annually, particularly in ICU patients. Fluid therapy is critical in sepsis management, yet aggressive resuscitation often leads to fluid overload, worsening outcomes. Bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) is a noninvasive method for monitoring body fluid distribution, providing insights into fluid imbalances associated with sepsis mortality. This study evaluates the impact of furosemide-induced fluid deresuscitation on fluid distribution and clinical outcomes in patients with sepsis. A secondary analysis of a double-blind, randomized controlled trial was conducted in forty sepsis patients with cumulative fluid balance >1,500 mL and urine output <0.8 mL/kg/hour. Patients were randomised to the intervention (furosemide infusion) and control (placebo) groups. BIA was used to assess total body water (TBW), extra-cellular water (ECW), intracellular water (ICW), and related parameters at baseline and after 48 hours. Outcomes included changes in fluid distribution, ICU length of stay, RRT use, and 28-day mortality. At baseline, no significant differences were observed in demographic or clinical characteristics between the groups. All BIA parameters showed no significant differences, except for the ECW/ICW ratio and ICW levels. After 48 hours, the intervention group exhibited a significant reduction in ECW/ICW ratio (P = 0.005) and ICW levels (P = 0.004), while the control group showed increases in ICW and TBW. Mortality rates were higher in the control group (36.8% vs 25.0%), though not statistically significant (P = 0.423). Severe hypoalbuminemia was more frequent in the control group, potentially contributing to fluid imbalance. While furosemide-induced deresuscitation may influence fluid redistribution, its effect on clinical outcomes remains inconclusive.

articles.title: Duration of antibiotic therapy in sepsis and severe infections in critically ill patients.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Antibiotic treatment duration in critically ill patients has undergone major reevaluation. Historically concerns for short therapy included a lower cure rate and emergence of resistance, whereas prolonged courses raised risks of microbiome disruption, superinfection, Clostridioides difficile colitis, and resistance. Defining optimal duration of therapy in sepsis and severe infections remains challenging due to heterogeneity in host immunity, pathogen virulence, infection site and source control. Mechanistic insights from microbiology and PK/PD highlight how bacterial inoculum, biofilms, mutant selection windows and altered drug distribution in critical illness influence bacterial clearance and resistance selection. Experimental models and PK-optimized dosing strategies underscore the potential to shorten therapy by accelerating pathogen eradication. Across a range of serious infections, randomized trials consistently show that short course therapy (<7 days) is noninferior to longer courses, including bacteremia, intra-abdominal infections and ventilator-associated pneumonia. Biomarker guided strategies-particularly procalcitonin-based algorithms-might further individualize duration of therapy and safely reduce exposure. Uncertainty remains for S. aureus bacteremia, infections caused by non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli, difficult to treat multidrug-resistant organisms, invasive candidiasis and immunocompromised patients. Robust evidence supports markedly reduced duration of therapy for uncomplicated bloodstream infections after effective source control, intra-abdominal infections and ventilator-associated pneumonia. Infections involving retained prosthetic material or devices often require prolonged therapy or long-term suppressive regimens. Future research must include adequately powered trials across diverse populations, and evaluate rapid diagnostics, host-response profiling, and individualized response-guided strategies. Optimizing antibiotic duration in critically ill patients ultimately requires integrating mechanistic understanding, individual clinical evolution, and stewardship principles to balance potential efficacy and potential harm.

articles.title: Fluid-intolerance signals as bedside safety limits during early septic shock resuscitation: a multicenter randomized trial.
articles.abstract: Fluid resuscitation in early septic shock has a narrow therapeutic index. Signals of fluid intolerance are frequently present during early resuscitation, yet current resuscitation strategies do not incorporate them to guide when to limit fluid administration. We evaluated whether integrating fluid-intolerance signals as safety limits could reduce fluid-induced harm without compromising hypoperfusion resolution. In this multicenter, open-label randomized trial in three Chilean ICUs, mechanically ventilated adults with septic shock, persistent hypoperfusion, fluid responsiveness, and at least one high-risk criterion for fluid-induced harm were randomized 1:1 to a fluid-intolerance-limited resuscitation strategy or standard care during a 6-hour protocol window. In the intervention arm, before each bolus, fluid-intolerance signals (lung ultrasound score, VExUS, E/lateral e', and central venous pressure) were graded as traffic-light: green received a 500-mL bolus, yellow 250 mL, and red no further fluid. Standard care delivered 500-mL boluses while hypoperfusion and fluid responsiveness persisted. The primary outcome was the change in PaO2:FiO2 from baseline to 6 h (ΔPaO2:FiO2). Recruitment was discontinued before the planned sample size was reached because continued enrollment was no longer feasible. Among 113 screened patients, 36 of a planned 62 were randomized, and 35 were analyzed (18 standard care, 17 intervention). The intervention group received a lower protocol bolus volume during the 6-hour intervention window than the standard-care group (250 [125-500] vs. 650 [500-1500] mL; between-group difference, - 500 mL [95% CI, - 750 to - 250]). Cumulative fluid exposure from pre-randomization through the end of the protocol window was similar between groups (3375 [2375-3875] vs. 3750 [1875-4851] mL; between-group difference, - 150 mL [95% CI, - 1470 to 1250]). The primary outcome favored the intervention: median ΔPaO2:FiO2 was 40.5 [24.0-58.5] versus - 37.9 [-69.2 to -12.5]; p < 0.001 (between-group median difference + 78.3 points; 95% CI 50.5 to 110.0), and 0-6-hour changes in lactate and capillary refill time did not differ. Because the trial was stopped early, the effect of a fluid-intolerance-limited resuscitation strategy on oxygenation remains uncertain. A larger trial would be needed to determine whether this strategy improves oxygenation. Such a trial appears feasible. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT06568744, registered August 21, 2024.

articles.title: Dosing of anti-infective drugs in patients undergoing therapeutic plasma exchange - considerations for practical application: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) is used in a wide range of indications and patient populations. The current guidelines of the American Society for Apheresis on the use of therapeutic apheresis in clinical practice list 166 graded indications for TPE. Many indications are related to the treatment of critically ill patients. Indeed, two multicenter trials are currently investigating the role of TPE in the treatment of early septic shock. MAIN BODY: During TPE, usually 1.0-1.5 times the calculated plasma volume is exchanged using albumin solution or fresh frozen plasma as replacement fluid, although considerable deviations from this recommended exchange volume have been reported. Depending on the TPE modality (membrane-based or centrifugal), the duration of the procedure ranges between 90 and 140 min. TPE removes not only unwanted substances such as inflammatory mediators or pathological antibodies but may also remove drugs that are essential for the treatment of the underlying disease. Furthermore, changes in plasma protein concentrations due to TPE may affect the volume of distribution (Vd) and the concentrations of protein-bound drugs. The objective of the current narrative review is to introduce general principles of TPE-associated drug removal as well as the current literature on the dosing of anti-infectives in patients undergoing TPE. CONCLUSION: Pharmacokinetic characteristics, including volume of distribution, plasma protein binding, endogenous clearance, and redistribution kinetics, have been demonstrated to influence the susceptibility of a drug to TPE-associated removal. TPE may substantially affect plasma levels of drugs with low volume of distribution and high protein binding, including aminoglycosides and glycopeptides. Further studies are needed because direct evidence on the pharmacokinetics of anti-infective drugs undergoing TPE in sepsis remains limited. Specific timing or dosing strategies are therefore not supported by sufficient evidence and should be individualized according to drug-specific pharmacokinetics, TPE characteristics, and clinical situation.

articles.title: Beyond macrocirculatory targets: a multimodal framework for microcirculatory and organ perfusion monitoring in sepsis.
articles.abstract: Microcirculatory dysfunction may persist despite restoration of conventional macrocirculatory targets in sepsis, reflecting loss of hemodynamic coherence. This review synthesizes current microcirculatory monitoring approaches according to the physiological information they provide and examines how complementary modalities may be integrated to characterize persistent or regional tissue hypoperfusion. A narrative review of PubMed-indexed literature was conducted, with emphasis on bedside peripheral perfusion assessment, tissue oxygenation and superficial perfusion imaging, direct microvascular visualization, and organ- or tissue-specific monitoring. Recent studies were prioritized together with landmark methodological and validation studies. Available techniques interrogate distinct but overlapping components of the circulation. Bedside peripheral measures provide rapid information on skin reperfusion and vascular tone; spectroscopic and optical techniques characterize tissue oxygenation, reactivity, and spatial perfusion heterogeneity; direct microvascular imaging enables assessment of microvascular density and flow; and organ-specific approaches provide information on renal, cerebral, or retinal perfusion and oxygenation. Discordance between these domains may persist despite improvement in blood pressure or cardiac output, supporting serial multimodal rather than single-variable interpretation. However, substantial heterogeneity in acquisition protocols, measurement sites, devices, analytical methods, and proposed thresholds limits comparability and clinical implementation. Microcirculatory monitoring should currently be viewed as a complementary framework for identifying persistent or heterogeneous tissue hypoperfusion beyond conventional macrocirculatory targets. Its integration into individualized resuscitation remains promising but requires standardized methodology, external validation, and prospective interventional evidence before any single modality or multimodal strategy can be adopted as a validated resuscitation endpoint.

articles.title: The NLRP3 inflammasome in physiological and dysfunctional host response in human sepsis and critical illness: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The NLRP3 inflammasome is a cytosolic multiprotein complex that serves as a key regulator of innate immunity by reacting to pathogen- and damage-associated signals and orchestrating downstream inflammatory responses. Inflammasome activation induces caspase-1-dependent maturation of interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-18 and gasdermin D, which results in pyroptotic cell death. MAIN TEXT: While tightly controlled inflammasome activation is essential for effective host defence and pathogen clearance, accumulating evidence implicates its dysregulation as a central driver of host response imbalance in critical illness. In conditions such as sepsis and acute respiratory distress syndrome, excessive activation contributes to hyperinflammation, endothelial dysfunction, immunothrombosis, and multi-organ failure. Conversely, insufficient or exhausted inflammasome responses may impair microbial clearance and predispose to secondary infections. These observations underscore the context-dependent and temporally dynamic role of inflammasome signalling as being either protective or pathogenic. Emerging therapeutic strategies aim to restore immune homeostasis through targeted modulation of inflammasome pathways, including IL-1 blockade (e.g., anakinra) and inhibition of upstream signalling components. However, clinical translation remains challenging, requiring improved patient stratification, biomarker-guided approaches, and a deeper understanding of disease heterogeneity.
