The random-effects or bivariate model was used to calculate the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. Overall, machine learning models show moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis, with a combined AUC of 0.82 for the training set (46 studies, 15 models) and 0.79 for the validation set (50 studies, 25 models). Logistic regression is the most widely evaluated model, demonstrating stable performance (validation AUC = 0.81). Integrated methods, including random forest and XGBoost, performed equally well, with AUCs between 0.81 and 0.83 in both groups. Although LightGBM and DL-CMT achieved the highest AUCs in the training and validation sets, respectively, both estimates were based on a single study. Among the complications, the evidence for sepsis-associated encephalopathy (AUC = 0.81, 3 studies) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (AUC = 0.80, 4 studies) is the most conclusive and best demonstrated. Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury showed moderate and stable performance (validation AUC = 0.79, 4 studies). Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy showed significant attenuation from training to validation (AUC 0.84 vs 0.78, all from a single study), and random forest performed well in training (AUC = 0.98) but was not widely reported. Septic shock reached the highest AUC (0.95), but this was based on a single study. The predictive utility of sepsis-associated delirium is limited (AUC = 0.67, 1 study), and sepsis-induced myocardial injury is moderate (AUC = 0.77, 1 study).For long-term mortality, evidence is extremely lacking. Only SAE (AUC 0.88 during training and 0.86 during validation) and SCRS (combined AUC 0.76) provided single study estimates, ruling out reliable conclusions. In this meta-analysis, machine learning models showed moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis. Among complications, SAE and SIC had the strongest evidence and best performance, whereas SAD showed limited utility. Evidence for long-term mortality was extremely scarce. These findings support the potential role of machine learning in early prognostic risk stratification, yet they also highlight the urgent need for rigorous external validation and higher-quality studies, particularly for under-investigated complications.

articles.title: Global trends and emerging frontiers in neutrophil extracellular trap-related sepsis research: a bibliometric analysis.
articles.abstract: Sepsis remains a major challenge in critical care medicine, and NETs have emerged as important regulators linking inflammation, immunity, coagulation, and tissue injury. However, the global development trajectory and research frontiers of NET-related sepsis studies remain unclear. Publications related to NET-related sepsis research from 2004 to September 19, 2026, were independently retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus databases. After database-specific screening, 263 WoSCC records and 499 Scopus records were retained for separate analyses using VOSviewer and CiteSpace to evaluate publication trends, collaboration networks, knowledge structures, thematic evolution, and emerging research attention. The WoSCC and Scopus analytical datasets contained 263 and 499 records, respectively. WoSCC analysis showed that China had the highest publication output, whereas the United States had the highest citation impact and collaboration strength among the listed countries. Cleaned author-keyword analysis highlighted sepsis, neutrophil extracellular traps, NETosis, inflammation, neutrophil, platelet, acute lung injury, and septic shock. Cross-database comparison showed a high correlation in complete-year publication trends (Spearman's ρ = 0.986) and partial overlap in high-frequency author keywords. Independent database analyses indicate sustained growth and a progressively interconnected knowledge structure in NET-related sepsis research. The results describe publication, collaboration, citation, and thematic attention patterns; they do not establish biomarker performance or therapeutic efficacy. Future studies may benefit from standardized NET measurement and reporting, multicenter validation of NET-related biomarkers and predictive models, and appropriately designed clinical investigations.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of sivelestat in sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome: an updated meta-analysis based on disease severity and treatment strategy subgroups.
articles.abstract: Sivelestat sodium hydrate is a selective neutrophil elastase inhibitor that attenuates neutrophil-mediated alveolar-capillary injury and is used in some East Asian countries for acute lung injury/ARDS. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of sivelestat in sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and explored whether disease severity, baseline mortality risk, and treatment background modify the mortality effect. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and ClinicalTrials.gov from database inception to August 27, 2026. Eligible studies were adult studies of sepsis-induced ARDS comparing a sivelestat-containing regimen with an otherwise comparable regimen without sivelestat. COVID-19-only cohorts, non-septic ARDS, mixed-etiology studies without a separable sepsis subgroup, and comparisons in which both groups received sivelestat were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included P/F ratio, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, organ-function scores, inflammatory markers, and adverse events. Mortality was pooled as odds ratios (ORs) using a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood; Hartung-Knapp intervals were used for the primary and study-design analyses. This review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO. Fourteen studies were eligible for qualitative synthesis, and 10 studies (943 patients) provided extractable 2 × 2 mortality data. Deaths occurred in 73/431 patients receiving sivelestat and 125/512 controls. Sivelestat was associated with lower mortality (OR=0.55, 95% CI 0.36-0.84; I2 = 0%). The signal persisted in randomized trials (OR=0.37, 95% CI 0.16-0.86; I2 = 0%). Study-level point estimates appeared more favorable in cohorts with baseline P/F < 100 mmHg and control mortality >30%; however, interaction tests were not statistically significant and severity analyses were ecological. Leave-one-out analyses were stable. Egger testing did not detect significant small-study asymmetry (P = 0.197), although power was limited. Baseline-stratified treatment effects by IL-6, PCT, CRP, or neutrophil elastase were unavailable for quantitative effect-modification analyses. In an updated and etiologically strict evidence synthesis, sivelestat was associated with lower mortality in sepsis-induced ARDS, including in randomized trials. Severe hypoxemia and high baseline risk remain plausible enrichment factors, but current aggregate evidence is insufficient to support a validated phenotype-guided prescribing rule. Co-intervention reporting was sparse, and residual confounding by prone positioning, sedation, neuromuscular blockade, and steroid background cannot be excluded. PROSPERO CRD420261541158.

articles.title: Ventilator care bundles in adult ICUs: a systematic review and meta-analysis of ventilator-associated pneumonia risk and incidence density.
articles.abstract: Ventilator care bundles are used to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but differences in outcome denominators and study design complicate interpretation. We examined patient-level VAP risk and ventilator-time incidence density separately. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Web of Science were searched from inception on 11 August 2026. Eligible bundles contained at least three clinical practices for adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation in ICUs. Nonconcurrent before-after comparisons were pooled separately for VAP risk ratios (RRs) and incidence rate ratios (IRRs). Comparisons with unclear timing, randomized results, and segmented interrupted time-series results were presented separately. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood and Knapp-Hartung intervals, with modified Knapp-Hartung sensitivity analyses. ROBINS-I and GRADE assessed bias and certainty. Twenty-three non-randomized study families contributed to the primary meta-analyses; 22 contributed VAP data. Bundle implementation was associated with lower VAP risk (14 studies; n = 5,905; RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.51-0.76; I2 = 9.0%; prediction interval 0.47-0.82). The pooled incidence rate ratio was 0.55 (12 studies; 95% CI 0.41-0.73; I2 = 79.9%), but the prediction interval included the null (0.25-1.22). ICU length of stay (3 studies; MD -2.53 days, 95% CI -7.59 to 2.53) and mechanical ventilation duration (2 studies; MD -3.64 days, 95% CI -13.96 to 6.69) remained uncertain. All pooled estimates were at serious risk of bias. Certainty was low for VAP risk and very low for the other pooled outcomes. Nonconcurrent comparisons associated bundle implementation with lower reported VAP risk, with low certainty. Incidence-density associations varied across settings, and evidence for ICU length of stay and ventilation duration was very uncertain. Evaluations with independent concurrent controls, stable surveillance, and adherence monitoring are needed. PROSPERO (CRD420261484358).

articles.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence Education on Nursing Decision-Making in Intensive Care Units (ICUs): Systematic Review Study.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transitioned from a theoretical concept into an active collaborator within intensive care units (ICUs). While predictive algorithms, smart alarms, and hemodynamic metrics offer immense potential to improve patient safety, their clinical efficacy is fundamentally dependent on the competency and literacy of the nursing workforce. This review article evaluates current literature on AI educational interventions for critical care nurses and analyzes their direct impact on clinical decision-making speed. A comprehensive literature review was conducted to synthesize contemporary research (2021-2026) focusing on clinical AI applications and nursing educational approaches. A targeted literature tracking process was conducted across major academic databases, including PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL, and Google Scholar. A total of 34 peer-reviewed articles, including primary studies, scoping overviews, and theoretical frameworks, were selected and analyzed using a thematic synthesis approach to map out current educational strategies and their operational impacts. The literature demonstrates that AI education for nurses is primarily driven by three strategic modalities: curriculum-based learning, simulation-based training, and interprofessional workshops. Effective educational interventions significantly reduce cognitive overload by mitigating alarm fatigue and sharpening situational awareness. Furthermore, structured training optimizes time-to-decision and enhances clinical accuracy during high-stakes events like sepsis progression and acute hemodynamic collapse. Integrating AI literacy into nursing education transforms frontline clinicians from passive technology users into informed, autonomous decision-makers. To overcome current systemic barriers such as the "explainability gap" and the lack of standardized curricula, educational institutions must establish uniform, ethically grounded competency frameworks.

articles.title: Resuscitation of the Trauma Patient.
articles.journal: Emergency medicine clinics of North America
articles.abstract: This article provides a practical overview of modern trauma resuscitation for emergency clinicians. It emphasizes early recognition of shock, timely hemorrhage control, and activation of massive transfusion protocols. Guidance is provided on fluid resuscitation, permissive hypotension, airway management, and treatment of agitation in critically ill trauma patients. Personalized management of trauma-induced coagulopathy using viscoelastic testing, along with monitoring biomarkers such as lactate and base deficit, is highlighted. The importance of effective team coordination, leadership, and rapid decision-making to improve outcomes in high-acuity trauma care is emphasized.

articles.title: Effects of Iloprost on Nitric Oxide Biomarkers in Patients With Septic Shock and Severe Endotheliopathy.
articles.abstract: Septic shock is characterized by profound endothelial dysfunction, which may involve changes in the prostacyclin and nitric oxide (NO) pathways and contribute to immune dysregulation, coagulopathy, and vascular instability. Iloprost has shown potential to modulate NO biomarkers in non-septic conditions. We investigated whether treatment with the prostacyclin analog iloprost affected plasma concentrations of the NO biomarkers ADMA, SDMA, arginine, and homoarginine in patients with septic shock and severe endotheliopathy. This preplanned sub-study of the randomized, blinded COMBAT-SHINE trial enrolled 274 adult ICU patients with septic shock and severe endotheliopathy (defined as soluble thrombomodulin (sTM) > 10 ng/mL) who had consented to the use of data. Five participants from the full trial population withdrew consent. Participants were allocated to a 72-h infusion of iloprost (1 ng/kg/min) versus placebo. Plasma concentrations of ADMA, SDMA, arginine, and homoarginine were measured at 0, 24, 48, and 72 h. Changes in biomarker concentrations were assessed using linear mixed models, with predefined subgroup analyses. All results were considered exploratory. In explorative analyses, iloprost treatment, compared with placebo, did not statistically significantly change plasma concentrations of ADMA and SDMA (estimated difference in means -4% (95% CI: -13%, 6%; p = 0.4) and-2% (95% CI: -14%, 10%; p = 0.7), respectively), or plasma concentrations of arginine and homoarginine (estimated difference in means 9% (95% CI: -6%, 27%; p = 0.2) and 17% (95% CI: -3%, 42%; p = 0.10), respectively). None of the NO biomarkers changes over time (0-24 h, 24-48 h, or 48-72 h) differed between the iloprost and placebo groups (all p > 0.3). Findings were consistent across predefined subgroups. In this sub-study of a randomized clinical trial of adults in the ICU with septic shock and severe endotheliopathy, infusion of iloprost 1 ng/kg/min for 72 h did not affect plasma concentrations of the NO biomarkers ADMA, SDMA, arginine, and homoarginine. This substudy of a larger trial of iloprost versus placebo for sepsis outcomes (COMBAT-SHINE trial) examined specifically nitric oxide markers in a septic shock and epithelial injury cohort. Iloprost treatment at the tested dose did not appear to affect markers of nitric oxide measured as ADMA, SDMA, arginine or homoarginine levels.

articles.title: Intensive Care Unit Management of the Hemodynamically Significant Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.abstract: Acute pulmonary embolism remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with prognosis determined by right ventricular (RV) adaptation to the abrupt rise in pulmonary vascular resistance. Although most cases can be managed outside the intensive care unit, patients with RV failure, hemodynamic instability, or cardiac arrest require advanced monitoring and intervention. Management in this setting emphasizes rapid diagnosis and risk stratification, timely initiation of reperfusion therapies, and carefully tailored hemodynamic and respiratory support. Optimal outcomes rely on multidisciplinary collaboration, early escalation of care, and individualized, evidence-based decision-making.
articles.ai_summary: This article reviews ICU management of hemodynamically significant pulmonary embolism. It highlights that patients with right‑ventricular failure, hemodynamic instability, or cardiac arrest require advanced monitoring and intervention. Key points include rapid diagnosis, risk stratification, timely reperfusion, and tailored hemodynamic and respiratory support.
articles.ai_significance: Understanding these ICU strategies is important because pulmonary embolism can rapidly worsen right‑ventricular function and cause death. Applying a structured approach may improve outcomes in critically ill patients.

articles.title: Prospective Observational Study Assessing Patient Characteristics, Management and Early Outcomes of Major Trauma Patients With Prehospital Shock. A preliminary report of the Sydney COAST study.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in trauma resuscitation, significant gaps remain in understanding how early physiological and biochemical derangements influence clinical outcomes. The Sydney 'Clinical Outcomes following Acute Shock in Trauma' (COAST) registry was developed by clinicians containing both prehospital and in-hospital data, allowing for the identification of risk factors that influence early mortality for major trauma patients with shock. This study reports the formation of the registry and the patient cohort enrolled over its first 12 months. A multi-centre, prospective registry of shocked adult trauma patients treated by prehospital medical teams and transported directly to a Sydney-based major trauma centre. Shock was defined as either (1) systolic blood pressure less than 100 mmHg, (2) shock index greater than one, (3) blood transfusion or (4) administration of inotropes. Descriptive statistics were used to report outcomes including injuries, pathology, transfusions, immediate intervention, mortality and length of stay. Two hundred fifty seven patients were enrolled. The predominant shock criteria for inclusion was hypotension (90% of cases), whilst 53% received prehospital blood transfusion. Interventional haemorrhage control was required in 31% of cases, whilst 74% received in-hospital transfusion. Injury severity was high (median injury severity score of 27). Four-hour mortality was 4.7% (9% at 24-h and 21% at 30-days). Consistent with recent observational studies, the Sydney COAST registry captured a cohort of critically ill trauma patients, not all of whom may have had haemorrhage. This will serve as an important dataset, allowing clinicians to better understand factors driving traumatic shock whilst exploring avenues for improving care in these cases.

articles.title: The path towards precision transfusion medicine in critical care: focus on patient physiology, not only on study populations.
Massive Transfusion-Associated Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome After Liver Transplantation: A Case Report and Retrospective Estimate of the Sodium Load.
articles.abstract: A 67-year-old woman with acute-on-chronic liver failure and profound preoperative hyponatraemia (central-laboratory serum sodium 116 mmol/L preoperatively; 120.3 mmol/L on the first intraoperative blood gas) underwent emergency living-donor liver transplantation complicated by an estimated blood loss of 6200 mL. Resuscitation comprised 20 units of packed red blood cells (PRBC), 12 units of fresh frozen plasma (FFP), 34 units of cryoprecipitate, three units of apheresis platelets, approximately 7.7 L of crystalloid and albumin, 60 mL of 7% sodium bicarbonate and 70 mEq of potassium chloride, with no hypertonic saline. Serum sodium measured on the operating-room blood gas analyser rose from 120.3 to 132.5 mmol/L over 7 h (+12.2 mmol/L), and by 18 mmol/L between the preoperative central-laboratory value and arrival in the intensive care unit, exceeding the 8-10 mmol/L per 24 h limit recommended by the European Renal Best Practice guideline. She developed dysarthria and dysphagia after extubation on postoperative day (POD) 6 and severe tetraparesis with decreased consciousness on POD 7. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) on POD 7 (rapid protocol) reported no pontine lesion, whereas MRI on POD 19 showed T2 hyperintensity in the central pons and both thalami, consistent with osmotic demyelination syndrome with extrapontine involvement. A simple pooled Adrogué-Madias calculation, with its assumptions stated, estimated the sodium contributed by the infused products at roughly +10 to +17 mmol/L, the same order of magnitude as the observed rise. This case illustrates that blood products, isotonic crystalloids and sodium bicarbonate together can deliver a substantial sodium load during massive transfusion, that the load can be estimated approximately, and that an early MRI without a reported pontine lesion does not exclude osmotic demyelination.

articles.title: Therapeutic plasma exchange and continuous renal replacement therapy for severe dengue with multiorgan failure: a case report and focused review.
authors: Medauar Reis de Andrade Moreira F
articles.abstract: Severe dengue can progress to acute liver failure, haemolysis, encephalopathy, shock, and multiorgan dysfunction, but the role of therapeutic plasma exchange in treatment remains uncertain. We report a 17-year-old adolescent with NS1-positive dengue managed with continuous renal replacement therapy, therapeutic plasma exchange, and comprehensive intensive care, and provide a focused narrative review of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue. The patient developed abrupt massive intravascular haemolysis, profound anaemia, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, encephalopathy requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, oliguric acute kidney injury, shock, and acute liver failure. She also met five of eight HLH-2004 criteria for secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Continuous renal replacement therapy was initiated before three therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, beginning with an exchange of 1·5 estimated plasma volumes using fresh frozen plasma. Haemodynamic, hepatic, renal, and coagulation parameters subsequently improved. Secondary infection and haemothorax requiring video-assisted thoracoscopic drainage complicated recovery; she was discharged 38 days after admission. Published evidence on the use of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue consists mainly of case reports, small series, and observational cohorts. Therapeutic plasma exchange can be considered an adjunctive rescue therapy in selected refractory cases, particularly acute liver failure or thrombotic microangiopathy phenotypes, but its independent benefit, optimal timing, prescription, and target population remain undefined.

articles.title: Predictors of high perioperative blood transfusion during isolated CABG using minimally invasive extracorporeal circulation.
articles.journal: The International journal of artificial organs
articles.abstract: The concept of minimally invasive extracorporeal circulation (MiECC) was conceived as a strategy to reduce the effects of hemodilution, inflammation, and blood transfusions during CABG surgery. Despite these technological advancements, perioperative blood transfusion is still common practice. In this research, we sought to determine transfusion needs, the independent factors predicting high transfusion burden, and its clinical effect at an early stage after surgery. In this retrospective study performed at a single center, 144 patients were studied for CABG using MiECC from January 2019 to December 2025. The subjects were divided into a group requiring low transfusion (<3 units of packed red blood cells (RBC); n = 88) and a group requiring high transfusion (⩾3 units of RBC; n = 56). Characteristics were compared between the two groups. Predictors of increased need for transfusion were found using multivariable logistic regression analysis. In total, 109 patients (75.7%) received red blood cell transfusions, of which 56 patients (38.9%) required at least three units. Patients in the high-transfusion group were older, with lower preoperative hemoglobin levels, poor renal function, and presence of chronic kidney disease. Moreover, they also had higher skin-to-skin operative duration. High transfusion was associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, increased duration of ICU stay and hospitalization, frequency of re-exploration due to bleeding, and increased in-hospital mortality. Lower preoperative hemoglobin was found to be the most significant independent factor for large transfusion requirements (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.54-0.82; p < 0.001). Despite the use of MiECC, perioperative blood transfusion remains common practice. Perioperative anemia, defined by low hemoglobin concentration, was identified as the strongest independent factor for significant transfusion requirement, while chronic kidney disease is another high-risk population. The findings provide support for better management of anemia before surgery and for a broader use of patient blood management programs to reduce transfusion rate and improve perioperative outcomes.

articles.title: Risk factors associated with the development of a catheter-related thrombosis in patients with critical illness: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract: We sought to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis with the primary objective to identify prognostic factors associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Our secondary objective was to report the incidence of this entity. We searched, MEDLINE® and Embase® from inception through 4 May 2024 for all studies in patients with critical illness that reported catheter-related thrombosis, with an updated search performed on 23 October 2025. We included English-language studies that described prognostic factors for developing a catheter-related thrombosis or reported the incidence of this complication in the critical care setting. Two authors performed citation screening and data extraction. We pooled adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) separately for prognostic factors using a random-effects model and inverse variance weighting. Risk of bias for individual studies was evaluated using the Quality in Prognosis Studies tool. We assessed certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations approach. We included 32 studies involving 11,943 patients. Identified prognostic variables with a moderate- or high-certainty association for developing a catheter-related thrombosis include increasing age (aOR per 10-yr increase, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06 to 1.27; three studies; 1,594 patients; high certainty), trauma-related admission (aOR, 1.48; 95% CI, 0.93 to 2.34; three studies; 3,089 patients; high certainty), surgical-related admission (aOR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.77 to 3.52; three studies; 2,208 patients; aHR, 1.35; 95% CI, 0.60 to 3.02; two studies; 297 patients; high certainty), internal jugular insertion site as compared with other insertion sites (aOR, 3.76; 95% CI, 2.82 to 5.01; four studies; 4,681 patients; high certainty), single/double-lumen as compared with more lumens (aOR, 1.61; 95% CI, 0.82 to 3.13; three studies; 1,594 patients; moderate certainty), and peripheral insertion site (aOR, 2.30; 95% CI, 0.74 to 7.08; two studies; 264 patients; moderate certainty). The median incidence of catheter-related thrombosis was 13.3% [interquartile range, 3.7%-31.3%]. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we found that increasing age, surgical type admissions, large catheters, and factors potentially related with catheter duration were associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Furthermore, we identified significant variation in the reported rates of catheter-related thrombosis, with an average rate of approximately 1 in every 8 patients. When these identified risk factors are present, clinicians may consider more aggressive thromboprophylaxis regimens to better tailor prevention strategies to individual patient risk profiles. Open Science Framework ( https://osf.io/5zvg2) ; first submitted 15 June 2024.

articles.title: Successful management of arrow‑rebound‑induced transcervical penetrating trauma with major vascular and pharyngolaryngeal injuries: A case report.
articles.abstract: Penetrating neck injury involving major vessels is highly lethal. Long-trajectory transcervical penetration caused by rebounding arrows is exceptionally rare in civilians, posing significant diagnostic and management challenges. A man in his early 50s presented to the emergency department approximately 2 hours after an arrow, rebounding from a nearby training target, penetrated his neck (entering above the left mandible, exiting on the right). He was conscious with minimal external bleeding but copious oropharyngeal secretions. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed the arrow traversing the hyoid bone and oropharynx, abutting the right common carotid artery (CCA) and compressing the right internal jugular vein (IJV). Open neck injury; combined right CCA and IJV injury; hemorrhagic shock; pharyngolaryngeal trauma without aerodigestive perforation; and pulmonary infection with consolidation. Initial stabilization included arrow shaft shortening by firefighters. Emergency exploration under general anesthesia involved tracheotomy, cervical exploration, primary repair of the right IJV and CCA, and foreign body removal. Postoperative management in the intensive care unit included damage-control resuscitation (transfusion of 7.0 U packed red blood cells, 1100 mL plasma, and 10.5 U cryoprecipitate), antimicrobial therapy (cefuroxime, guided by cultures showing Staphylococcus epidermidis), early individualized anticoagulation (enoxaparin transitioned to rivaroxaban), and systematic correction of coagulopathy and electrolyte disturbances. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 12 with healed wounds. Follow-up at 1, 3, 6.5 months, 1, 2, and nearly 3 years showed intact neurological function. Imaging confirmed stable right IJV occlusion. Anticoagulation was discontinued at 1 month without subsequent bleeding or thromboembolism. Although long-term imaging was limited to a 6.5-month non-contrast computed tomography, the patient remained asymptomatic without signs of venous hypertension or neurological deficits throughout the follow-up period. High-quality preoperative computed tomography angiography with 3D reconstruction is critical for defining the relationship between the foreign body and vital structures. In selected patients, early individualized anticoagulation after excluding active bleeding may mitigate venous thrombosis. Systematic intensive care unit management of coagulopathy, electrolytes, and pulmonary complications is pivotal for survival.

articles.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review of In-Hospital and Post-Discharge Outcomes.
articles.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis determines the incidence of new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) in critically ill patients, risks of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism, anticoagulation therapy, and the proportion diagnosed with AF post-discharge. A search of registered databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL) was performed from inception to April 20, 2026. Eligible studies included critically ill patients (≥ 18 yr old) who developed NOAF during admission to general ICUs or high-dependency units. NOAF was defined as AF in patients without prior history of AF. Data were independently extracted from full-text versions of included studies by nonblinded reviewers. A Bayesian meta-analysis was conducted on 54 studies (367,896 patients) with a random-effects model using R (Version 4.3.3). Pooled incidence of NOAF in critically ill patients was 10.6% (95% credible interval [CrI], 8.6-12.9%). Absolute risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism was 7.1% (95% CrI, 4.5-11.0%), changing to 6.9% (95% CrI, 4.2-11.6%) after age and sex adjustment. Evidence from six studies reports that critically ill patients with NOAF had 1.94 times (95% CrI, 1.23-3.29) higher relative risk of systemic thromboembolism post-discharge than patients without NOAF, rising to 2.01 (95% CrI, 1.54-2.80) with adjustment. Absolute and relative risk are evaluated with follow-up durations ranging from 1.5 months to 5 years, with variable anticoagulation exposure. Anticoagulation rates were low: 32.9% in-hospital (95% CrI, 14.6-57.9%) and 35.9% post-discharge (95% CrI, 19.7-55.9%). On follow-up, 23.9% (95% CrI, 13.9-38.5%) of critically ill patients with NOAF were subsequently diagnosed with AF. Our review suggests that NOAF during critical illness is associated with significantly increased risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism and subsequent AF diagnosis. However, rates of anticoagulation initiation remain low, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification and targeted strategies post-discharge.

articles.title: Global Prevalence of Obstetric Causes of Critical Illness in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: To determine the prevalence, risks, and outcomes of obstetric causes of critically ill pregnant women admitted to the ICU. We searched the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Ovid, and ScienceDirect databases up to May 15, 2026. We included studies reporting primary data on critically ill pregnant and postpartum women (up to 48 d post-delivery) admitted to an ICU, with relevant obstetric risk factors and maternal outcomes. Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The pooled prevalence was estimated using a random-effects model with 95% CIs. Of the 3,735 total records, 50 studies met the eligibility criteria, encompassing 7,756,232 women receiving obstetric care in tertiary hospitals across 20 countries, with 49,299 ICU admissions. Globally, 1.0% (95% CI, 0.8-1.3%) of pregnant and postpartum women experience critical illness and require admission to an ICU. The frequency varies according to the country's income levels, with the highest in low-income countries (4.1%) and the lowest in high-income countries (0.5%). Notably, 72.3% of ICU admissions were attributed to known obstetric causes, primarily obstetric hemorrhage (23.3%) and hypertension in pregnancy (26.9%). Nearly 33.3% of ICU patients required either respiratory or transfusion support, and the maternal mortality rate among ICU-admitted obstetric women was 8.5%. Nearly one in 100 pregnancies require admission to intensive care due to critical illness, and nearly three-quarters of these admissions were due to direct obstetric causes, with high maternal morbidity and mortality. Obstetric hemorrhage and hypertensive disorders account for the majority of ICU admissions. Strengthening obstetric care in resource-limited settings through the expansion and optimization of intensive care services is essential for improving maternal and neonatal outcomes and reducing preventable morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Outcomes with Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis versus Mechanical Thrombectomy for Patients with Intermediate/High Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Meta-Analysis of 24,090 Patients.
articles.abstract: Randomized trials comparing the outcomes with catheter-directed medical thrombolysis (CDT) versus mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for patients with intermediate/high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) are limited. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE. Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and the length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Summary estimates were analyzed using a random effects model. A total of 18 studies (24,090 intermediate/high risk patients) were eligible for the analysis. CDT was associated with longer length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay (mean difference: 1.01 days, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-1.15) compared with MT. While there was no statistical difference between the two groups regarding the risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.01, p = 0.068) and major bleeding (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.74-1.55, p = 0.705). Similarly, the incidence of other clinical outcomes; all-cause readmission, PE-related readmission, blood transfusion rates, length of hospital stay, cardiac arrest, and stroke, were similar between the two groups. Among patients with intermediate/high risk PE treated with catheter-based therapies, there was no difference regarding the clinical outcomes between CDT and MT, but CDT was associated with a longer ICU stay. Larger, well designed randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Association of Early Palliative Care with End-of-Life Care Quality and Nonbeneficial Treatments in Taiwan: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.
articles.abstract: Early palliative care has been associated with reduced aggressive care near the end of life (EOL), particularly among patients with cancer. However, evidence regarding the association between early palliative care and potentially nonbeneficial treatments near the EOL remains limited, particularly among patients with noncancer terminal illnesses and in real-world clinical practice. To examine the association between early palliative care, EOL care quality indicators, and nonbeneficial treatments among terminally ill cancer and noncancer patients under a universal health insurance system. This retrospective population-based study used Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database to identify adults who received palliative care within one year before death in 2019. Early palliative care was defined as initiation of any palliative care service more than 90 days before death. Outcomes included indicators of EOL care quality and nonbeneficial treatments within the last 30 days of life. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models were used to adjust for demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and terminal diagnoses. Among 46,343 decedents, 17.2% received early palliative care. Early palliative care was associated with lower odds of aggressive EOL care, including more than one emergency department visit, more than one hospitalization, a hospital stay exceeding 14 days, intensive care unit admission, in-hospital death, use of an endotracheal tube, ventilator support, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Early palliative care was also associated with reduced use of nonbeneficial treatments, including blood transfusion and tube feeding or intravenous nutrition. In a nationwide cohort, early palliative care was associated with improved EOL care quality and reduced use of nonbeneficial treatments among terminally ill patients. These findings underscore the clinical importance of earlier palliative care involvement in supporting patient-centered decision making near the EOL and reducing potentially nonbeneficial interventions.

articles.title: Sepsis in Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy: A Six-Year Nationwide Analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Healthcare Resource Utilization in Hospitalizations for Hematologic Malignancies.
articles.abstract: Patients receiving chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy are at increased risk for infection and sepsis due to malignancy-related immune dysfunction, lymphodepleting chemotherapy, and immunosuppression used to treat CAR T-cell toxicities; however, nationally representative estimates of sepsis burden and economic impact remain limited. This study uses nationally representative U.S. data to evaluate patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, and healthcare utilization associated with sepsis among hospitalizations involving CAR T-cell therapy. Adult hospitalizations for acute lymphoblastic leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, or multiple myeloma in which CAR T-cell therapy was administered between 2017 and 2022 were identified from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) and stratified by sepsis status. After excluding records with missing covariates, survey-weighted analyses were performed to generate nationally representative estimates. Multivariable regression models were used to evaluate differences in mortality and secondary outcomes, with statistical significance defined as a two-sided p value < 0.05. Among 10,450 weighted CAR T-cell therapy hospitalizations, 645 (6.2%) were complicated by sepsis. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in hospitalizations with sepsis (28.7% vs 1.1%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 33.96; 95% confidence interval [CI] 18.67-61.75). Sepsis was independently associated with higher odds of acute kidney injury (aOR 4.31), respiratory failure (aOR 11.85), acute hepatic failure (aOR 44.42), and septic shock (aOR 411.05), along with greater use of renal replacement therapy, mechanical ventilation, and vasopressors. Thrombohemorrhagic events were more frequent among hospitalizations with sepsis, including disseminated intravascular coagulation (aOR 9.30), acute venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.95), acute coronary syndrome (aOR 27.63), acute ischemic stroke (aOR 7.53), gastrointestinal hemorrhage (aOR 6.47), and intracranial hemorrhage (aOR 4.84), as well as increased need for cryoprecipitate and fresh frozen plasma transfusion (aOR 2.70). Sepsis was also associated with longer hospital stay (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR] 1.96) and higher hospitalization charges (adjusted charge ratio [aCR] 1.22). Sepsis was documented in approximately 6% of CAR T-cell hospitalizations and was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, organ dysfunction, critical-care utilization, longer hospitalization, and higher hospitalization charges. These findings highlight the substantial clinical and healthcare burden associated with sepsis in this population.

articles.title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain. This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated. A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099). In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

articles.title: Viscoelastic haemostatic assay-guided transfusion versus conventional coagulation testing in critically ill non-cardiac adults with active bleeding or clinically significant coagulopathy: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
When the Filter Becomes the Source: POCUS Detection of Inferior Vena Cava Filter Thrombosis Extending Into the Right Atrium.
articles.abstract: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters are used to prevent pulmonary embolism in patients with venous thromboembolism when anticoagulation is contraindicated. Although uncommon, filter thrombosis can result in thrombus propagation and potentially life-threatening embolic complications. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) provides a rapid bedside assessment of the heart, lungs, and may facilitate the prompt recognition of unexpected thromboembolic complications. A 43-year-old man with hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage was admitted to the intensive care unit requiring mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. Six days after admission, he developed sudden severe hypoxemia, tachycardia, and hypotension requiring reinitiation of norepinephrine. POCUS demonstrated bilateral anterior A-lines, left femoral and popliteal deep vein thrombosis, and preserved right ventricular (RV) function without echocardiographic evidence of RV strain. Catheter-based pulmonary angiography confirmed subocclusive thrombosis involving segmental branches of the right middle and lower lobes, which was treated with mechanical thromboaspiration, followed by IVC filter placement because anticoagulation was initially contraindicated. Four days later, he developed a new episode of acute hypoxemia despite remaining hemodynamically stable. Repeat POCUS demonstrated a large mobile thrombus in transit within the right atrium. Subcostal longitudinal imaging of the IVC demonstrated a large elongated thrombus attached to the IVC filter, with a freely mobile portion extending into the right atrium. Urgent mechanical thrombectomy and IVC filter replacement were performed. The new filter was positioned approximately 2 cm below the confluence of the hepatic veins with the inferior vena cava. Approximately 24 h later, follow-up POCUS showed no evidence of new thrombus formation. More than 2 weeks after admission, following a follow-up brain CT showing no significant progression of the intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation with enoxaparin was initiated and progressively increased to a full therapeutic dose. This case highlights the value of POCUS for the prompt bedside recognition of an established and potentially life-threatening complication of IVC filter placement. Systematic bedside cardiac and venous ultrasound may identify thrombus propagation into the right atrium even in the absence of RV dilation or echocardiographic evidence of RV strain, facilitating timely endovascular intervention.

articles.title: Association between inpatient aspirin exposure and 28-day mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis-induced coagulopathy: A cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the association between inpatient aspirin exposure and 28-day mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC). We conducted a retrospective cohort study extracting data from the MIMIC-IV v3.1 database (2008-2022). Adult critically ill patients with SIC in the intensive care unit (ICU) were included. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Secondary outcomes encompassed mortality (e.g., in-hospital, ICU, 60-day, 90-day, and 1-year) and duration of ICU-free, ventilation-free, or vasopressor-free days within 28 days of admission to the ICU. Multivariable Cox regression, propensity score matching (PSM), inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), overlap weighting (OW), pairwise algorithmic weighting (PA), and doubly robust estimation were employed to control confounders. Robustness of findings was assessed through subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Among 9095 critically ill patients with SIC, 3207 (35.3%) received aspirin during ICU hospitalization. After 1:1 propensity score matching (2069 pairs), inpatient aspirin exposure was independently associated with significantly lower 28-day mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.85; P < .001). This association remained consistent across multiple analytical methods including IPTW (HR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.70-0.84; P < .001), OW (HR 0.72; 95% CI: 0.61-0.84; P < .001), PA (HR 0.73; 95% CI: 0.61-0.84; P < .001), and doubly robust estimation (HR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.61-0.94; P < .001). Inpatient aspirin exposure was also associated with more favorable secondary clinical outcomes (all P < .001). In critically ill patients with SIC, inpatient aspirin exposure was independently associated with lower 28-day mortality and more favorable clinical outcomes. These findings should be interpreted as an association rather than evidence of a causal therapeutic effect. Prospective randomized studies are warranted to validate these findings.

articles.title: Early platelet count trajectories and short- and long-term mortality in patients with sepsis: a group-based trajectory modeling study based on the MIMIC-IV database.
articles.abstract: Platelet abnormalities are common in sepsis; most studies evaluate single measurements. We characterized early platelet count trajectories during the first 48 h after intensive care unit (ICU) admission and evaluated associations with short- and long-term mortality. Adult Sepsis-3 patients were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. Group-based trajectory modeling was applied to platelet counts at 12-48 h after ICU admission. Associations with mortality were examined using Kaplan-Meier, multivariable Cox and logistic models, with propensity-matched, multiple-imputation and reclassification analyses and the 48-h landmark analysis as primary; sepsis-induced coagulopathy was scored using International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) criteria. Among 5,046 ICU stays (4,775 patients), four trajectories were identified: persistently low (n = 1,153; 22.8%), moderate with mild decline (n = 1,847; 36.6%), high with moderate decline (n = 1,516; 30.0%) and very high with marked decline (n = 530; 10.5%). In the primary landmark analysis (n=4,930), adjusted 28-day mortality hazard ratios versus the moderate-with-mild-decline group were 1.66 (95% CI 1.40-1.97), 1.33 (1.12-1.57) and 1.34 (1.07-1.69), consistent at 90 days, 1 year and in whole-cohort and matched analyses. Sepsis-induced coagulopathy affected 82.6% of persistently low patients; trajectory and coagulopathy remained jointly associated with mortality. Trajectory membership improved reclassification over clinical variables (continuous NRI 0.193, 95% CI 0.160-0.281). Early platelet trajectories identify four sepsis patient groups with distinct mortality risk. The persistently low association was most robust; the high-but-declining association was attenuated in five-group analyses. Trajectories add information beyond single measurements.

articles.title: Prevention of stress-related gastrointestinal bleeding in critically ill adults.
articles.abstract: The occurrence of clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) is low. This summary highlights publications pertaining to risk factors for UGIB, pharmacologic stress ulcer prophylaxis (SUP), and the role of enteral nutrition. Critically ill adults requiring mechanical ventilation or those with multiple trauma, severe neurologic illness, extensive thermal injury, or shock should receive SUP only in the presence of circulatory support, coagulopathy, thrombocytopenia, liver disease, acute kidney injury, or anticoagulants or platelet inhibitors. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) reduce the occurrence of clinically important UGIB compared to histamine-2 receptor antagonists (H2RAs) but may be associated with unexplained mortality, especially when patients are more severely ill. SUP should be discontinued when risk factors subside or the patient is no longer critically ill. The concomitant administration of enteral nutrition and SUP may predispose patients to pneumonia. Discontinuing SUP when enteral nutrition is tolerated is reasonable. SUP is inappropriately ubiquitous across critically ill populations. Understanding risks associated with UGIB should enhance the appropriate initiation and discontinuation of SUP. Further exploration of SUP outcomes relative to severity of illness is warranted to ensure SUP is effective and well tolerated.

articles.title: Renal Decline Before Heart Transplantation in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Recipients: United Network for Organ Sharing Analysis.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Although baseline renal impairment and post-heart transplantation (HT) dialysis are established clinical predictors, the prognostic impact of pre-HT renal decline in patients bridged with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed patients from the United Network for Organ Sharing registry who underwent HT following LVAD support between 2009 and 2024. Renal decline was defined as a greater than or equal to 40% reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from listing to HT. Among 10,454 patients, 624 (6.0%) experienced pre-HT renal decline. Patients with renal decline had longer waitlist durations (median 297 vs. 197 days; p < 0.001), lower eGFR at HT (42.0 vs. 70.6 ml/min/1.73 m2; p < 0.001), and higher rates of post-HT dialysis (23.7 vs. 12.8%; p < 0.001). Independent predictors of renal decline included longer waitlist time and perioperative blood transfusions, whereas HeartMate 3 LVAD use was protective. Renal decline was independently associated with an increased risk of post-HT dialysis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.64) and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 1.16), with post-HT dialysis strongly predicting mortality (aHR: 3.48). Renal deterioration is a significant predictor of post-HT dialysis and mortality in LVAD-bridged patients. Incorporating renal trajectory into risk stratification may enhance candidate selection and promote perioperative renal protection strategies.

articles.title: Practice variation in mechanical circulatory support: a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of Japanese interventional cardiologists in the CVIT Kyushu-Okinawa chapter.
articles.abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) practice for cardiogenic shock may vary with institutional resources and operator experience, but data from Japanese interventional cardiologists are limited. We conducted an anonymous cross-sectional survey of 720 members of 83 Japanese Association of Cardiovascular Intervention and Therapeutics (CVIT)-certified or affiliated training hospitals in the CVIT Kyushu-Okinawa Chapter (September-October 2025); 536 returned questionnaires (74.4%), and consent was confirmed for 385 (53.5%). The primary analysis included 276 respondents who had performed intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), or Impella CP insertion within 12 months: 163 at Impella-capable and 113 at non-Impella-capable hospitals. Documented MCS and extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation protocols were more frequently reported by respondents from Impella-capable hospitals (46% vs. 6% and 39% vs. 13%, respectively), as was collaboration with emergency and critical care physicians; no statistically significant difference was detected in perceived need for collaboration. MCS selection varied between groups. At Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) shock stage C, IABP (44%) and Impella CP (48%) were selected with similar frequency among respondents in Impella-capable hospitals, whereas IABP was selected by 79% in non-Impella-capable hospitals. At stage E, ECPELLA (79%) and VA-ECMO plus IABP (84%) predominated, respectively. Among respondents with device-specific operator experience within 12 months, vascular access and anticoagulation practices varied between groups. Procedural anxiety was lower with higher CVIT qualification; however, 19% of board-certified members reported anxiety about Impella CP insertion and 45% about emergency intubation. These findings identify MCS practice variation across several domains warranting further evaluation.

articles.title: [Sepsis-induced coagulopathy].
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) represents a frequent and prognostically highly relevant complication of sepsis, characterized by a dysregulated interaction between inflammation, endothelial activation and coagulation. Pathophysiologically, the excessive host immune response to pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMP) and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMP), activation of the complement cascade, formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NET) and disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx collectively promote a prothrombotic and antifibrinolytic microenvironment, resulting in microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Approximately 20-25% of critically ill patients with sepsis fulfil the diagnostic criteria for SIC. Current diagnostic approaches rely on scoring systems such as the International Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (ISTH)-SIC, ISTH overt-disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and Japanese Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (JSTH)-DIC scores; however, their clinical utility remains limited as they predominantly collate hemorrhagic parameters even though sepsis is typically characterized by a thrombotically dominated phenotype. Viscoelastic point-of-care assays enable dynamic bedside assessment of coagulation and fibrinolysis, including the frequently occurring hypofibrinolysis or fibrinolytic shutdown, which is associated with an unfavorable outcome; however, for this specific purpose, these methods have not yet been sufficiently validated or established as a diagnostic standard. Data and recommendations on specific therapeutic options are limited. A consistent pharmacological thromboprophylaxis remains the cornerstone in patients with sepsis, with low-molecular weight heparins demonstrating advantages over unfractionated heparin regarding venous thromboembolic complications. Coagulation modulating treatment, such as antithrombin, recombinant thrombomodulin or activated protein C, have thus far failed to demonstrate consistent survival benefits in large randomized clinical trials. Experimental approaches targeting NET formation, complement activation or fibrinolytic modulation appear mechanistically promising but require further clinical validation. Overall, SIC necessitates an individualized, pathophysiology-driven diagnostic and therapeutic approach integrating inflammatory, endothelial, thrombotic and fibrinolytic alterations.

articles.title: Investigating Fibrinolysis Resistance in Sepsis Using High-Multiplex Plasma Proteomics: A Statistical Analysis Plan.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy is characterised by consumptive coagulation abnormalities and resistance to fibrinolysis, which is increasingly recognised as a driver of microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction and mortality. The molecular determinants of the fibrinolysis-resistant phenotype remain incompletely defined. To present a pre-specified statistical analysis plan for a plasma proteomic investigation of fibrinolysis resistance in 89 samples collected serially from 32 critically ill patients with sepsis, using the Olink Explore HT platform (approximately 5400 proteins). The plan is designed to characterise protein associations with a validated bedside measure of fibrinolysis resistance, the ratio of tissue plasminogen activator-induced lysis time to fibrin clot amplitude (TPA-LT/FIBA10). The associations will be examined across the fibrinolysis resistance severity continuum and between three ordinal severity grades, and over time within individual patients. The analytic framework combines five complementary approaches: (i) limit-of-detection-based data filtering, (ii) continuous-variable modelling of protein abundance against TPA-LT/FIBA10 using limma-trend regression, (iii) categorical comparison across severity grades using empirical Bayes moderated statistics, (iv) linear mixed-effects modelling of longitudinal intra-patient trajectories and (v) pathway-level enrichment analysis to translate statistical associations into mechanistic hypotheses. A semi-supervised pathway clustering analysis will describe how proteins change by fibrinolysis resistance in eight a priori defined domains. This multi-model design is intended to define genuine biological signals in a high-dimensional dataset while remaining transparent about the exploratory nature of several components. The statistical reasoning behind each method is discussed alongside anticipated limitations. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06680180.

articles.title: Extensive Stray-Dog Mauling as Major Contaminated Crush Trauma Causing Severe Rhabdomyolysis, Acute Kidney Injury, and Overt Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation: Recovery Without Renal Replacement Therapy.
articles.abstract: An adolescent male developed severe rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury, overt disseminated intravascular coagulation, and respiratory fluid overload after extensive stray-dog mauling. The course reflected overlapping traumatic, inflammatory, and infectious mechanisms. He recovered without renal replacement therapy through source control, individualized antimicrobials, conservative renal support, and timely transition to de-resuscitation.

articles.title: Home-based transfusions in hospice patients with hematologic malignancies: a pilot study.
articles.abstract: Hospice care (HC) for patients with hematologic malignancies (HM) is underutilized due to concerns about cessation of blood transfusions. Home-based transfusion (HBT) programs have proven to be safe, but little research exists for HM patients in HC. We hypothesized that HBT protocol could be safely implemented to reduce symptoms burden, lengthen life expectancy and improve quality of life in HC. In a non-randomized pilot study between 8/2020 and 7/2023, adult transfusion-dependent HM patients were offered weekly transfusion of one unit of packed red blood cells (PRBC) and/or one unit of platelets based on symptoms criteria, not lab values. Exclusion criteria included prior transfusion reactions, extended blood typing, or residence outside 50 miles from the transfusion center. Hospice agencies provided management and support, while Our Blood Institute (OBI) provided palliative HBT. Symptom scores and complete blood counts (CBC) were collected weekly, and EORTC QLQ-C30 quality of life (QOL) questionnaire was completed before and after transfusions. The primary feasibility and safety outcomes were recruitment, ability to administer indicated transfusions, and transfusion reactions. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04454723) on 6/30/2020. We enrolled 21 patients (mean age in years = 67.1 (standard deviation (SD) = 14.4); 100% enrollment, one withdrew consent). Participants received an average of 3.4 units (SD = 3.4) of platelets or PRBCs. No transfusion reactions reported. Mean cost was $571 per week (SD = $939). The EORTC Composite Score least squares-mean difference (post-pre- transfusion) increased 0.18 (SE = 1.88) (p-value = 0.92) but not significantly. Median hospice duration was 11 days, IQR = 8-40 days, 95% CI: 9-33 days. All patients died at home, with no hospitalizations or intensive care unit (ICU) admissions. HBT, in the setting of hospice represents a feasible and safe option for further study to avoid costly hospitalizations and ICU admissions, with limited cost. This trial demonstrates proof of concept for an economical, patient-centered HBT protocol in HM patients receiving HC. P30CA225520, TSET.

articles.title: Anesthetic management of right radical nephrectomy and inferior vena cava thrombectomy for giant renal cell carcinoma: a case report.
articles.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
articles.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with tumor thrombus extension into the inferior vena cava (IVC) represents a major surgical and anesthetic challenge because of the high risk of massive hemorrhage, hemodynamic instability, and intraoperative tumor embolism. We report the case of a 55-year-old man presenting with a large right renal mass measuring 14 × 14 × 13 cm, with a tumor thrombus extending from the right renal vein into the infrahepatic IVC. The patient underwent right radical nephrectomy with caval thrombectomy under general anesthesia and invasive hemodynamic monitoring. Anesthetic management focused on anticipating major blood loss, preventing thromboembolic complications related to thrombus manipulation, ensuring adequate blood product availability, and maintaining perioperative hemodynamic optimization. Intraoperative blood loss was estimated at 3500 mL, which necessitated transfusion of four units of packed red blood cells and four units of fresh frozen plasma. The intraoperative course was favorable, with satisfactory hemodynamic stability throughout the procedure, and the patient was subsequently transferred to the intensive care unit for postoperative monitoring. This case highlights the importance of meticulous multidisciplinary planning and perioperative anesthetic management in patients with locally advanced RCC and an IVC tumor thrombus to minimize potentially fatal hemorrhagic and thromboembolic complications. In summary, this report demonstrates the anesthesiologist's critical role in mitigating the severe hemodynamic and hemorrhagic risks of radical nephrectomy with IVC thrombectomy through meticulous, multidisciplinary perioperative planning. Specifically, this case emphasizes three key clinical messages: (1) early multidisciplinary planning is mandatory for complex urologic oncology; (2) continuous invasive hemodynamic monitoring combined with early vasopressor support is crucial to manage abrupt preload reductions during IVC clamping; and (3) proactive transfusion preparedness via a standardized massive transfusion protocol prevents coagulopathy during massive hemorrhage.

articles.title: An Unusual Presentation of Postoperative Shock: A Case Report of Acute Hypercapnic Acidosis.
articles.abstract: Acute hypercapnic acidosis has the potential to precipitate shock; however, it often goes unrecognized by healthcare professionals. A 33-year-old woman with suspected left plasma cell mastitis underwent resection of a left breast sinus tract under general anesthesia. Intraoperative blood loss was approximately 1000 mL, and the left chest was compressed with gauze bandaging. She had delayed recovery from anesthesia and was transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU). Initial blood pressure was 90/62 mmHg with largely normal arterial blood gas (ABG) results. Despite transfusion and antibiotics, her blood pressure decreased to 70/51 mmHg, accompanied by lethargy and cool, clammy skin, requiring norepinephrine. Repeat ABG showed pH 7.011, PaCO2 107 mmHg, PaO2 110 mmHg (FiO2 40%), base excess -3.0 mmol/L, and normal lactate. Bedside ultrasonography excluded hypovolemic, cardiogenic, obstructive, and septic shock. Low tidal volume (180-220 mL) was noted, and bedside fiberoptic bronchoscopy was unremarkable. Based on these findings, shock due to acute hypercapnic acidosis secondary to excessively tight chest bandaging was diagnosed. The bandage was promptly removed and reapplied with appropriate pressure. Acute hypercapnic acidosis-related shock is uncommon; timely identification and correction of hypoventilation can rapidly reverse shock and improve prognosis. In postoperative patients at risk for hypoventilation who exhibit progressive hypotension or shock, acute hypercapnic acidosis should be considered once other prevalent forms of shock have been excluded. Early and repeated ABG and prompt evaluation of ventilation status are crucial.

articles.title: Catastrophic in-stent thrombosis with antiphospholipid syndrome: a case report.
articles.abstract: In-stent thrombosis despite morphologically optimal stents remains a diagnostic challenge. Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a rare cause that drives thrombosis via tissue factor-mediated coagulation-a pathway not addressed by dual antiplatelet therapy. A 51-year-old male with cardiovascular risk factors underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention for anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Ten days later, he developed refractory ventricular fibrillation requiring extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and intra-aortic balloon pump support. Emergency angiography confirmed complete in-stent thrombosis; intravascular ultrasound excluded a mechanical cause. The intensive care course revealed a triad of red flags: unexplained in-stent thrombosis, recurrent extracorporeal circuit clotting despite stepwise heparin escalation, and arterial and venous thrombosis on full anticoagulation. This prompted antiphospholipid antibody testing, which showed persistent moderate-to-high titre anti-cardiolipin IgM-a profile within the 'controversial' zone of the 2023 ACR/EULAR classification criteria. The patient was managed as APS with intensified triple therapy, later transitioning from heparin to a vitamin K antagonist, and was discharged on Day 27 with no events at 3-month follow-up. Antiphospholipid syndrome should be considered in unexplained in-stent thrombosis even when laboratory criteria are not strictly met. The triad of unexplained in-stent thrombosis, anticoagulation refractory circuit clotting, and incident venous thrombosis is a clinically actionable pattern warranting empiric APS-directed management.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Nafamostat Mesilate Injection in Patients Receiving Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: The objective of the study was to assess the efficacy and safety of nafamostat mesilate injection in patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Dichotomous and continuous outcomes were analyzed using fixed-effect or random-effects models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) or mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Eight studies involving 1,189 patients were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with no anticoagulation, nafamostat mesilate injection was associated with lower mortality (OR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.44-0.76; p < 0.001) and longer filter lifespan (MD, 7.00; 95% CI, 1.50-12.50; p = 0.01). These estimates were derived predominantly from nonrandomized studies and should be interpreted with caution. However, no significant difference was found between nafamostat mesilate injection and no anticoagulation in bleeding complications (OR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.51-2.34; p = 0.82), total duration of CRRT (MD, 4.46; 95% CI, -0.13-9.04; p = 0.06), the proportion of patients requiring transfusion (OR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.54-1.03; p = 0.07), and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (MD, -0.24; 95% CI, -3.85-3.37; p = 0.90) in patients receiving CRRT. The available evidence suggests that nafamostat mesilate injection may be associated with lower mortality and longer filter lifespan compared with no anticoagulation in patients receiving CRRT. However, no clear difference was observed in bleeding complications, total duration of CRRT, the proportion of patients requiring transfusion, or ICU length of stay. These findings are limited by the predominance of nonrandomized designs, small numbers of studies, and substantial heterogeneity. Additional adequately powered randomized studies are needed before clinical benefit can be considered established.

articles.title: Tracheostomy-related bleeding and stomal complications: a literature review.
articles.abstract: Tracheostomy is one of the most commonly performed procedures in critically ill patients, with bleeding representing the most frequent early complication. Stomal bleeding and granulation tissue formation create ongoing management challenges that can complicate patient care. Other complications include stomal infection, subcutaneous emphysema, focal airway stenosis, and tracheoinnominate fistula (TIF), which differ in clinical severity and management. Current management relies on reactive measures, yet no standardized approach exists for preventing or managing persistent minor bleeding around the tracheostomy site. This study aims to review the incidence, pathophysiology, risk factors, and current management of tracheostomy-related bleeding and stomal complications, with emphasis on identifying gaps in prevention and treatment strategies. We conducted targeted literature searches using PubMed/MEDLINE for English-language human studies published between January 1, 2000 and September 17, 2026 involving adults aged 19 years or older. Search terms included "tracheostomy", "tracheotomy", "bleeding", "hemorrhage", "granulation tissue", "tracheoinnominate fistula", "stomal infection", "cellulitis", "abscess", "decannulation", "dislodgement", "subcutaneous emphysema", "tracheal stenosis", "ECMO", "transplantation", "immunosuppression", "tranexamic acid", "epinephrine", and "cautery". We extracted data on incidence rates, management approaches, and clinical outcomes. Bleeding is the most common early complication of tracheostomy procedures, occurring in 0.6-5.0% of cases overall, with rates reaching 5.7% for major or minor bleeding and up to 40% in high-risk populations such as patients on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Stomal infections, airway complications, and early accidental decannulation is also important to consider in tracheostomy patients. Subcutaneous emphysema was primarily associated with early mechanical complications, whereas focal airway stenosis represented a later consequence of granulation. Management of minor superficial bleeding generally consisted of direct pressure, packing, correction of reversible coagulopathy, and selected topical or cautery-based interventions. TIF remained distinct from these complications because even limited or transient bleeding may precede catastrophic hemorrhage, necessitating urgent recognition and escalation when a vascular source is suspected. Tracheostomy-related bleeding and stomal oozing represent common complications with limited preventive options. Current management is reactive, relying on manual pressure application, packing materials, and procedural interventions. Particular attention should be made to distinguish minor superficial bleeding from sentinel or life-threatening hemorrhage. Novel approaches could potentially reduce bleeding complications, minimize granulation tissue formation, and improve patient comfort during the critical early post-tracheostomy period.

articles.title: Bibliometric analysis of key biomarkers in sepsis-induced coagulopathy (2006-2025).
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy is life-threatening in critically ill patients. Thrombin-antithrombin complex and thrombomodulin are key biomarkers, but no 20-year bibliometric analysis exists. We searched PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection (2006-2025) and analyzed 577 articles using CiteSpace and VOSviewer. Publications peaked in 2016 to 2018 and then declined. Japan, the United States, and China were the most productive; the United States had the highest citations. Hotspots focused on sepsis-induced coagulopathy, endothelial injury, and intensive care unit anticoagulation. Thrombin-antithrombin complex/thrombomodulin research is globally established, led by the United States. Future work should enhance international collaboration and develop multi-biomarker models.

articles.title: SEPSIS-INDUCED COAGULOPATHY ATTENUATES THE PROGNOSTIC VALUE OF THE HEMOGLOBIN-ALBUMIN-LYMPHOCYTE-PLATELET (HALP) SCORE IN SEPSIS.
articles.abstract: The hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score predicts outcomes in sepsis, but its platelet denominator is also a core component of sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC), and may distort its prognostic meaning. We examined whether SIC modifies HALP's association with 28-day mortality. We analyzed 6,218 adults meeting Sepsis-3 criteria in MIMIC-IV. HALP was calculated from first ICU measurements; SIC was defined by the 2017 ISTH criteria (score ≥4). Analyses included multivariable regression, interaction testing, propensity-score methods, and platelet-independent coagulopathy definitions, and evaluation of modified HALP (m-HALP; platelets in the numerator). Twenty-eight-day mortality was 25.6%; SIC incidence was 26.1%. HALP showed a J-shaped association with mortality (P for nonlinearity <0.001). The lowest quartile independently predicted death (adjusted OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.20-1.70; HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.10-1.39). This association persisted in non-SIC patients (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.28-1.79) but was attenuated and non-significant in SIC patients (OR 1.14, 95% CI 0.82-1.60; interaction P=0.006). Albumin carried HALP's discrimination in non-SIC patients, whereas platelets dominated in SIC (OR 0.51 per SD, P=0.001). When coagulopathy was redefined without platelets, the modification was no longer significant (P=0.295), indicating it partly reflects the shared platelet component. m-HALP was inversely associated with mortality in both strata (interaction P=0.691). Results were robust to weighting, 90-day mortality, and alternative Cox models. HALP is an independent prognostic marker mainly in septic patients without coagulopathy; once SIC develops, thrombocytopenia both raises mortality risk and arithmetically inflates HALP. Coagulation status should be assessed before HALP-based risk stratification; m-HALP may offer a platelet-consistent alternative.

articles.title: Acute Pain Management in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract: This review summarizes current approaches to pain assessment and pharmacologic therapy in the intensive care unit (ICU) and evaluates the expanding role of regional anesthesia (RA). Contemporary ICU analgesia emphasizes systematic pain assessment and multimodal therapy while avoiding unnecessary deep sedation. RA provides targeted, opioid-sparing analgesia for localized pain but is limited by coagulopathy, infection, altered anatomy, and practical considerations. Fascial-plane blocks may provide useful alternatives in selected patients. Thoracic epidural and paravertebral techniques remain options for selected patients but may cause hypotension and clinically significant bleeding. Ultrasound-guided techniques, including erector spinae, serratus anterior, parasternal, rectus sheath, and transversus abdominis plane blocks, expand analgesic options. Continuous catheter techniques may extend analgesia when prolonged pain is anticipated. However, evidence in heterogeneous ICU populations remains limited, and much of the current evidence is derived from perioperative or trauma populations rather than general medical ICU cohorts. Further ICU-specific comparative trials are needed to define patient selection and clinically meaningful outcomes.

articles.title: Venous Thromboembolism in Acute Necrotizing Pancreatitis Is Associated With Worse Outcomes, With Subtype-Specific Patterns: A Nationwide Analysis, 2016-2022.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) complicates acute necrotizing pancreatitis (ANP), but outcomes across extra-splanchnic deep vein thrombosis (DVT), portal vein thrombosis (PVT), and splenic vein thrombosis (SVT) remain poorly defined. We evaluated national trends and in-hospital outcomes in ANP with versus without VTE and across VTE subtypes.
