METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study across 12 French neuro-ICUs including all adult patients admitted alive after OHCA-aSAH between 2014 and 2024. Demographics, cardiac arrest characteristics, aSAH severity, ICU management, and 6-month neurological outcomes (modified Rankin Scale, mRS) were collected. Firth penalized logistic regression was applied to explore predictors of favorable outcome. RESULTS: Among 15,907 SAH admissions, 164 patients had OHCA-aSAH. Median age was 54 [43-62] years; 47.5% were male. Only 8 patients (4.9%) achieved favorable outcome (mRS ≤ 3) while 156 (95.1%) had poor outcome (mRS ≥ 4), including 154 deaths (mRS 6). Low-flow duration tended to be shorter, epinephrine use lower, and pupillary abnormalities less frequent among survivors, although no independent statistical association could be confirmed. All patients receiving pre-hospital antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy (n = 14, 8.7%) had poor outcome. External ventricular drainage, ICP monitoring, and endovascular aneurysm treatment were more frequent, and ICU and hospital length of stay were longer, in survivors. One hundred and eight patients (65.8%) progressed to brain death within 1 [1-2] day. Penalized regression did not identify independent predictors of good outcome, though pupillary abnormalities and epinephrine use were associated with progression toward brain death. CONCLUSIONS: OHCA-aSAH carries a dismal prognosis, with < 5% achieving favorable neurological recovery. Selected patients may benefit from aggressive neurocritical care, and the high rate of brain death emphasizes the importance of organ donation pathways.

articles.title: Patient blood management in general intensive care patients.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Critically ill and high-risk perioperative patients requiring intensive care are often multimorbid and depend on rapid, highly specialized management. While most comorbidities are difficult to modify in the acute setting, anemia, particularly iron-defi ciency anemia, represents a potentially modifiable risk factor. Clinicians are also often confronted with complex alterations in hemostasis that require rapid assessment and targeted therapeutic interventions, including the optimal use of blood products. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence on Patient Blood Management strategies, including anemia management, the use of small-volume tubes, and the appropriate use of blood products in intensive care unit patients. RESULTS: Intravenous iron supplementation can safely raise hemoglobin to a clinically meaningful degree. Erythropoietin therapy may also raise hemoglobin, but its use should remain selective given uncertain thromboembolic risk. Small-volume blood collection tubes and closed blood-conservation systems should be routinely used to reduce iatrogenic anemia. Current evidence supports restrictive red blood cell transfusion strategies in most clinical settings, particularly in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding. Similarly, a restrictive platelet transfusion strategy is supported by current evidence. Prophylactic platelet transfusion should be reserved for high-risk hematologic malignancies. In other critically ill patients with severe thrombocytopenia, a therapeutic (bleeding-driven) approach is preferred. Finally, current evidence does not support prophylactic fresh frozen plasma transfusion in non-bleeding patients. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, these findings support the implementation of Patient Blood Management strategies that optimize blood health and promote safer, more individualized care in critically ill patients.
articles.ai_summary: This study reviewed current evidence on Patient Blood Management strategies in ICU patients, finding that intravenous iron supplementation and small-volume blood collection tubes can safely reduce anemia, and that restrictive blood transfusion strategies are generally supported.
articles.ai_significance: These findings are significant for ICU clinicians as they provide evidence-based guidance on optimizing blood health and reducing unnecessary blood transfusions, which can improve patient safety and outcomes.

articles.title: Red Cell Transfusion in Critically Ill and Noncritically Ill Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction and Anemia-A Subanalysis of the Myocardial Ischemia and Transfusion (MINT) Trial.
authors: Myocardial Ischemia and Transfusion (MINT) Trial Investigators
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Anemia is common in critically ill patients. In prior trials, a restrictive transfusion strategy was at least as effective as, and possibly superior to, a liberal strategy in critically ill adult patients. However, the Transfusion Requirements in Critical Care (TRICC) trial suggested that a restrictive strategy might be harmful in critically ill patients with ischemic heart disease. Our objective was to compare outcomes for restrictive and liberal transfusion strategies in critically ill and noncritically ill patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and anemia. DESIGN: Subgroup analysis of a parallel, two-arm randomized, controlled trial. SETTING: One hundred forty-four sites in the United States, Canada, France, Brazil, New Zealand, and Australia. PATIENTS: Adult patients with AMI and anemia enrolled in the Myocardial Ischemia and Transfusion (MINT) trial. Patients being treated in an ICU at randomization were considered critically ill. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned to a restrictive (transfuse when hemoglobin < 7-8 g/dL) or liberal (transfuse when hemoglobin < 10 g/dL) transfusion strategy. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We determined the effect of transfusion strategy on death and the composite of death/myocardial infarction (MI) at 30 days among critically ill and noncritically ill patients. Of 3504 patients enrolled in MINT, 1679 (47.9%) were critically ill. At 30 days, death (11.9% vs. 6.5%) and death/MI (18.9% vs. 12.7%) occurred more frequently in critically ill patients compared with noncritically ill patients. A restrictive, compared with a liberal, transfusion strategy resulted in a nonsignificant increase in the risk of death by 9% (risk ratio [RR], 1.09; 95% CI, 0.77-1.54) and death/MI by 9% (RR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.85-1.38) in noncritically ill patients and a nonsignificant increase in the risk of death by 24% (RR, 1.24; 95% CI, 0.95-1.61; interaction p = 0.55) and death/MI by 21% (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.99-1.47; interaction p = 0.52) in critically ill patients. CONCLUSIONS: There is no evidence that the overall MINT trial results, which generally favor a liberal transfusion strategy in AMI patients, apply differently to noncritically ill and critically ill patients.
articles.ai_summary: This study analyzed the effect of blood transfusion strategies in patients with acute myocardial infarction and anemia. It found that a restrictive transfusion strategy did not significantly reduce mortality in either critically ill or noncritically ill patients compared to a liberal strategy.
articles.ai_significance: Understanding the optimal blood transfusion strategy for critically ill patients with acute myocardial infarction and anemia is crucial for improving patient outcomes in the ICU.

articles.title: Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling characterizes tryptophan metabolic disturbance associated with mortality in ICU-admitted SFTS patients.
articles.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus, is associated with high mortality among intensive care unit (ICU) patients; however, the integrated proteomic-metabolomic mechanisms underlying fatal outcomes remain poorly characterized. This prospective cohort study enrolled 68 patients with SFTS, who were admitted to the ICU and classified them as survivors (n = 33) or non-survivors (n = 35) according to their 28-day clinical outcomes. Untargeted metabolomic profiling using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry and quantitative proteomic profiling using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry were performed on plasma samples collected at ICU admission. Multivariable analysis, pathway enrichment analysis, correlation analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were used to identify potential prognostic biomarkers and characterize molecular associations. Non-survivors exhibited more severe multi-organ injury and systemic inflammation. Metabolomic profiling revealed marked disruption of tryptophan metabolism: L-tryptophan levels were decreased, whereas kynurenine and its downstream metabolites (kynurenic acid [KA], 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid [3-HAA], xanthurenic acid [XA], and 5-hydroxyindolepyruvate [5-HIP]) were increased, suggesting activation of the kynurenine pathway. The four core tryptophan metabolites yielded a combined area under the curve (AUC) of 0.934 for predicting 28-day mortality and were correlated with indicators of renal function and coagulation. Proteomic profiling identified 200 differentially expressed proteins: proteins upregulated in survivors were enriched in the proteasome pathway, whereas those upregulated in non-survivors were enriched in the IL-17 pathway and other inflammatory and immune pathways. Integrated analysis revealed that the four tryptophan metabolites were associated with 20 differentially expressed proteins, six of which showed robust associations within outcome subgroups. Collectively, tryptophan metabolic disturbances coupled with inflammatory proteomic features may characterize fatal severe SFTS, and the identified metabolite-protein signatures may serve as promising prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in critically ill patients.

articles.title: Machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with venous thromboembolism and acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI. In this retrospective study, data from 585 ICU patients with VTE and AKI were analyzed. Patients were divided into a training cohort (n = 409) and a validation cohort (n = 176). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with standardization was applied for feature selection. Five machine learning models-logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis (DCA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and feature importance were performed for the optimal model. The performance of the best machine learning model was compared with conventional ICU severity scores (APSIII, LODs, and OASIS). The standardized LASSO regression identified ten optimal predictors: creatinine (cr), age, tumor/cancer, body mass index (BMI), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), urine output, D-dimer (D_D), Charlson comorbidity index, anticoagulant use, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance with a validation AUC of 0.882 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.832-0.924], followed by RF (AUC = 0.878), LightGBM (AUC = 0.870), LR (AUC = 0.838), and SVM (AUC = 0.662). The 5-fold cross-validation AUC for XGBoost was 0.901 ± 0.042, with minimal overfitting (CV-test difference = -0.019). Decision curve analysis demonstrated favorable clinical net benefit of the XGBoost model across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis and feature importance consistently identified urine output, age, LDL, BMI, and D-dimer as the top contributors. Compared with conventional ICU severity scores, the XGBoost model significantly outperformed APSIII (AUC = 0.661), LODs (AUC = 0.652), and OASIS (AUC = 0.647). The logistic regression-based nomogram achieved a C-index of 0.838, providing a user-friendly bedside tool for clinicians. The machine learning-based XGBoost model, incorporating ten readily available clinical variables, demonstrated excellent predictive performance for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with VTE and AKI. This model offers a practical and interpretable tool for early risk stratification and may guide proactive nutritional and therapeutic interventions in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio and short-term mortality in critically ill patients with respiratory diseases: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: To systematically evaluate the association between the HbA1c-adjusted stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) and short-term mortality in patients with severe respiratory diseases and characterize its linear and nonlinear dose-response relationships. PubMed, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang, VIP, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database were searched for observational studies evaluating SHR and short-term mortality, including in-hospital, intensive care unit (ICU), 28-day, or 30-day mortality. Odds ratios (ORs) and hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled separately using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses, linear dose-response analyses, restricted cubic spline analyses, and exploratory analyses of low and high SHR were performed. Eleven studies were included. Four studies contributed to the OR-based primary meta-analysis. Short-term mortality tended to be higher in the highest SHR category than in the study-specific reference category, but the association was not statistically significant (OR = 2.72, 95% CI: 0.74-9.93, P = 0.091; I 2 = 86.4%). Three studies contributed to the HR-based primary meta-analysis, which showed a significant association between higher SHR and increased short-term mortality risk (HR = 1.87, 95% CI: 1.71-2.05, P = 0.001; I 2 = 0%). In HR studies, each 0.1-unit increase in SHR was associated with an approximately 5% increase in short-term mortality risk (HR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.08, P = 0.023). OR studies showed a similar direction of association but did not reach statistical significance. Restricted cubic spline analyses found no clear evidence of nonlinearity. Exploratory analyses suggested higher risks at both low and high SHR levels, but the estimates were imprecise. Current evidence suggests that higher SHR is associated with increased short-term mortality risk in patients with severe respiratory diseases. HR-based evidence was more consistent and supported a positive linear dose-response relationship. OR-based findings pointed in the same direction but showed substantial heterogeneity and did not reach statistical significance. The available evidence is insufficient to confirm a clear nonlinear pattern. Given the limited number of studies and wide confidence intervals, the apparent increase in risk at both low and high SHR levels should be interpreted as exploratory and does not yet support a stable U-shaped or J-shaped dose-response pattern. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261418259, PROSPERO CRD420261418259.

articles.title: Early clinical experience with a novel automated fecal management system for fecal incontinence in high-risk oncology and intensive care unit patients: a retrospective analysis and structured narrative literature review.
articles.abstract: Fecal incontinence (FI) is prevalent in critically ill oncology patients, frequently compounded by chemotherapy-induced diarrhea (CID) and severe thrombocytopenia. Conventional indwelling balloon catheters (IBCs), the standard approach to FI management in the ICU, generate intraluminal radial pressures that frequently exceed mucosal capillary perfusion thresholds and are formally contraindicated by manufacturers in patients with platelet counts below 50 x 109/L. This retrospective analysis and structured narrative literature review evaluates the safety, fecal containment efficacy, and nursing workload impact of a novel pressure-free automated stool management (ASM) system in high-risk oncology ICU patients. A retrospective analysis was conducted at a major academic comprehensive cancer center in the United States during 2025. Outcome data from 190 unique adult oncology ICU patients, including two structured evaluation cohorts of 20 patients each, followed by broader institutional implementation (n=150), were compiled from standardized nursing quality improvement product evaluation forms completed throughout each patient's device-use period. A prospectively designated thrombocytopenic subgroup (n=47; platelet counts <50 x 109/L at device deployment) was analyzed separately. A structured narrative literature review was conducted across PubMed, MEDLINE, and CINAHL (final search: February 2026). Across 190 unique device placements, zero device-related adverse events were observed (adverse event rate 0%; 95% CI upper bound 1.6%, rule of three). In the thrombocytopenic subgroup (n=47), zero device-related adverse events were observed (95% CI upper bound 6.4%). No device-related mucosal bleeding, perforation, ulceration, necrosis, or device malfunction requiring intervention was documented. The device achieved 100% successful fecal diversion, with no major leakage event (defined as stool output requiring linen replacement) recorded. The per-assessment leakage rate was 1.7% (11 positive assessments out of 646 total), all representing minor peripheral moisture requiring only topical hygiene management with no linen change. Daily nursing time with ASM was 6.8 minutes per patient per day; contextual comparison with published estimates of 120 minutes per patient per day (IBC protocol) and 174 minutes per patient per day (absorbent pad management) from Vargo et al. yields estimated differences of 94% and 96%, respectively, subject to methodological differences between datasets. Retrospective chart review identified no chemotherapy delays or ICU length of stay prolongation attributable to device-related complications. This early institutional experience with a novel pressure-free ASM across 190 unique oncology ICU placements, including 47 in patients with severe thrombocytopenia, was not associated with any observed device-related adverse event. These findings represent hypothesis-generating preliminary data and do not establish superiority over conventional devices. The clinical need for safe fecal management alternatives in thrombocytopenic oncology patients is substantive; these data provide rationale for appropriately powered prospective comparative trials.

articles.title: Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation in adult patients admitted to an intensive care unit.
articles.abstract: Most existing recommendations for atrial fibrillation are derived from cardiology settings. However, atrial fibrillation is also highly prevalent among patients admitted to intensive care units and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Therefore, its management in this specific context warrants dedicated guidance. To address this need, The French Intensive Care Society has developed formalized expert recommendations using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) methodology. Twenty-four questions addressing the management of atrial fibrillation were evaluated in adult patients admitted to intensive care units. Of these, twenty-one focused specifically on new-onset atrial fibrillation, one addressed pre-existing atrial fibrillation, and two were applicable to both conditions. The assessment encompassed the role of transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography, the management of potentially reversible triggers (optimization of fluid status, magnesium supplementation, serum potassium targets, and screening for thyroid dysfunction…), strategies for mitigating hemodynamic risk (indications and modalities for rhythm and rate control), and the management of thrombotic risk (indications, regimens, and duration of therapeutic anticoagulation). Eighteen recommendations were formulated, all of which achieved strong agreement among the expert panel. Only two recommendations were supported by a low level of evidence (GRADE 2+), whereas the remaining sixteen relied on evidence that could not be classified within the GRADE framework and were therefore issued as expert opinions. For six additional aspects of atrial fibrillation management, the experts concluded that the available evidence was insufficient to support the formulation of a reliable recommendation.

articles.title: Tranexamic acid use and progression to clinically important bleeding in critically ill patients with non-clinically important non-variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used to reduce bleeding in perioperative and hemorrhagic conditions, but its role in upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) remains controversial. This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated whether TXA use was associated with reduced progression to clinically important gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) in critically ill patients with non-clinically important non-variceal UGIB. Adult ICU patients who developed non-clinically important non-variceal UGIB between 2018 and 2022 were included. Among them, 154 patients receiving TXA within 24 h after bleeding onset (mean duration 1.71 ± 1.42 days; mean total dose 2.12 ± 2.36 g) were compared with 1,660 patients who received neither TXA nor other hemostatic agents. After propensity score matching, 154 matched pairs were analyzed. Progression to clinically important GIB did not differ significantly between the TXA and non- TXA groups before matching (5.8% vs. 5.7%; P=0.951, 95% CI: 0.450-1.707) or after matching (5.8% vs. 7.8%; P=0.664, 95% CI: 0.562-3.164); Exploratory univariate conditional logistic regression analysis showed that TXA use was not associated with this outcome (OR 1.333, 95% CI 0.562-3.164; P=0.514). In the matched cohort, TXA was not associated with significant differences in endoscopy requirement, transfusion requirement, hospital length of stay, in-hospital mortality, or thrombotic complications. Inverse probability of treatment weighting analysis yielded consistent results for the primary outcome (5.1% vs. 5.8%; P=0.418, 95% CI: 0.840-1.522). In critically ill patients with non-clinically important non-variceal UGIB, TXA use was not associated with a statistically detectable reduction in progression to clinically important GIB or improvements in major clinical outcomes. Routine empirical use of TXA in this population should be approached with caution.

articles.title: Longitudinal sepsis-induced coagulopathy score trajectories and mortality in relation to early prophylactic heparin: a multicentre cohort study.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) evolves dynamically, and a single-timepoint score may not capture its longitudinal course. This study characterised SIC score trajectories, evaluated their associations with mortality, and conducted exploratory analyses of early prophylactic unfractionated heparin exposure. SIC score trajectories were characterised using a latent class mixed model. Trajectory-class prediction models were developed from baseline features within the first 24 hours of ICU admission using five algorithms. Heparin analysis used a 48-hour landmark design; weighted Fine-Gray models and cumulative incidence functions estimated 28-day post-landmark in-hospital mortality. The study enrolled 20,168 patients from MIMIC-IV and 5,829 from eICU-CRD. Three SIC trajectories were identified-Persistently High, Rising-then-Falling, and Resolving-comprising 31.9%, 10.6%, and 57.5% of patients in MIMIC-IV and 49.1%, 7.2%, and 43.7% in eICU-CRD. Relative to the Resolving trajectory, adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios (sHR) for mortality were 1.65 (95% CI 1.52-1.78) and 1.33 (1.18-1.49) for Persistently High and Rising-then-Falling in MIMIC-IV, and 1.73 (1.51-1.99) and 1.67 (1.33-2.11) in eICU-CRD. Prophylactic heparin was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard of 28-day post-landmark mortality in MIMIC-IV (sHR=0.908, 95% CI 0.839-0.983, P = 0.018); in an exploratory interaction analysis, the point estimate was more pronounced at higher predicted probabilities of the Persistently High trajectory, but this pattern was not replicated in eICU-CRD (sHR 0.877, 95% CI 0.744-1.034, P = 0.118). SIC score trajectories stratify septic patients into three trajectory classes-Persistently High, Rising-then-Falling, and Resolving-each showing a graded association with 28-day mortality. Early prophylactic unfractionated heparin showed an exploratory association with lower post-landmark mortality in MIMIC-IV that was not independently replicated in eICU-CRD. Although these findings do not support treatment recommendations or trajectory-based anticoagulation decisions, they provide a basis for formulating hypotheses for future prospective studies.

articles.title: Early systemic heparin exposure is associated with lower mortality, reduced disseminated intravascular coagulation, and fewer thrombotic complications in septic shock.
articles.abstract: Septic shock is characterized by thrombo-inflammatory dysregulation and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), contributing to organ failure and mortality. The clinical impact of heparin in septic shock remains uncertain. This study evaluated the association between early systemic heparin exposure and clinical outcomes. A retrospective multicenter cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX federated electronic health record network. Adult patients with septic shock receiving early systemic heparin exposure were compared with patients without heparin exposure. Propensity score matching balanced demographics, comorbidities, infection characteristics, organ dysfunction markers, and severity-related variables. Outcomes included mortality, DIC, thrombotic complications, renal outcomes, hematologic complications, and bleeding-related events. Clinical outcomes were assessed over a predefined 30-day follow-up period using risk-based and time-to-event analyses. A total of 105,472 patients per cohort were included. Early systemic heparin exposure was associated with lower mortality (15.3% vs. 20.8%; p < 0.001) and lower rates of DIC (p < 0.001). Thrombotic complications, including ischemic stroke, acute myocardial infarction, overall thrombotic events, and arterial or venous thrombosis, occurred less frequently among heparin-exposed patients (all p < 0.001). In contrast, heparin exposure was associated with higher rates of acute kidney injury, renal replacement therapy, thrombocytopenia, major bleeding, and transfusion requirement (all p < 0.01). Kaplan-Meier analyses were consistent with risk-based analyses. Early systemic heparin exposure was associated with lower mortality, reduced DIC, and fewer thrombotic complications, but increased rates of renal dysfunction and bleeding-related adverse events. These findings highlight a clinically relevant trade-off between potential benefit and harm. Prospective randomized studies are needed to define optimal patient selection and treatment timing.

articles.title: Beyond renal support: biological modulation across pathophysiological domains during continuous renal replacement therapy - a randomized pilot study.
articles.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is the preferred extracorporeal renal support modality for haemodynamically unstable critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (AKI). Although regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) is primarily used to maintain circuit patency, its biological effects may extend beyond anticoagulation itself. We hypothesized that different anticoagulation strategies are associated with distinct biological modulation across complementary pathophysiological domains during CRRT. We conducted a prospective randomized pilot trial comparing RCA with systemic unfractionated heparin in critically ill adults with AKI requiring CRRT (1:1 allocation). Serial blood samples were obtained before CRRT initiation, at 1 hour and at 24 hours, with paired pre- and post-filter sampling at 1 and 24 hours. Biomarkers represented redox homeostasis (glutathione -GSH, GSSG- and their ratio), neutrophil activation (myeloperoxidase -MPO-), cellular injury (cell-free DNA -cfDNA-) and systemic inflammation (C-reactive protein -CRP-). Healthy reference participants established physiological reference values. Longitudinal analyses used linear mixed-effects models with fixed effects for time, anticoagulation strategy and their interaction. This trial was registered in the European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT No. 2016-004361-12) and at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06646328). Twenty patients were randomized equally to RCA or systemic heparin; baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Among six biomarkers spanning four pathophysiological domains, only MPO showed a significant systemic time × anticoagulation interaction (P = .008); although baseline-adjusted sensitivity analyses did not confirm a significant between-group difference. GSH and cfDNA changed significantly over time irrespective of anticoagulation strategy (both P = .016), while the GSSG/GSH ratio approached a treatment-level difference (P = .067). Across the extracorporeal circuit, CRP increased significantly post-filter at both timepoints, MPO increased at 1h, and GSH showed an anticoagulation-dependent pre-to-post change at 1h. No significant differences were observed in secondary clinical outcomes. These pilot findings suggest that different anticoagulation strategies during CRRT may show domain-specific, rather than uniform, biological modulation, most evident within the neutrophil activation domain, with additional evidence of biomarker-specific kinetics across the extracorporeal circuit. These exploratory results are compatible with the concept that extracorporeal therapies may influence distinct domains differently, a hypothesis warranting confirmation in adequately powered, prospectively designed studies before implications for precision extracorporeal therapy can be drawn.

articles.title: Plasma exchange and double plasma molecular adsorption system combined with continuous renal replacement therapy for hepatitis B-related liver failure complicated by stage 3 acute kidney injury: a case report.
articles.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver failure can progress rapidly to neurological and renal dysfunction. In this setting, declining aminotransferase levels may be misleading if hepatic synthetic function and extrahepatic organ function continue to deteriorate. A 27-year-old woman presented with severe fatigue, dark urine, and jaundice. Laboratory testing showed marked hepatocellular injury, coagulopathy, HBV infection markers, and an HBV DNA level of 3.57 × 10⁶ copies/mL. During hospitalization, serum aminotransferase levels declined substantially; however, bilirubin and coagulation abnormalities worsened, serum creatinine increased from 96 μmol/L on day 1 to 825 μmol/L on day 4, and the patient developed hypersomnia and impaired consciousness. The renal deterioration met criteria for stage 3 acute kidney injury. Following multidisciplinary assessment, plasma exchange combined with a double plasma molecular adsorption system was used for liver-directed extracorporeal support, while continuous renal replacement therapy was initiated primarily for severe acute kidney injury and metabolic support. Consciousness, coagulation, liver function, and renal function subsequently improved. The patient left the intensive care unit on day 7, was discharged on day 24, and maintained normal liver and kidney function during follow-up. This case highlights that declining aminotransferase levels do not necessarily indicate clinical recovery in rapidly progressive HBV-related liver failure. Serial assessment of hepatic synthetic function, neurological status, and renal function identified continued multiorgan deterioration and guided timely, indication-based extracorporeal support. The clinical value of this case lies in the decision-making process for coordinated liver and renal support rather than in the novelty of the individual treatment modalities.

articles.title: Pretreatment body mass index as a prognostic factor for clinical course and survival in primary surgically treated oral squamous cell carcinoma - a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: In oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), body mass index (BMI) is an available but imperfect marker of nutritional reserve. Evidence on pretreatment BMI in surgery-based European OSCC cohorts remains limited, especially regarding perioperative outcomes. This study evaluated associations of pretreatment BMI with overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and perioperative outcomes after curative-intent R0 resection. This retrospective single-center cohort included adult patients with previously untreated primary OSCC, available pretreatment BMI, and curative-intent R0 surgery between 2014 and 2023. BMI was assessed continuously and by World Health Organization (WHO) categories. OS and RFS were analyzed using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, pathological T category, nodal status, microvascular free-flap reconstruction, and diabetes mellitus. Perioperative outcomes included red blood cell (RBC) transfusion, RBC units transfused, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) placement, and intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay. A total of 274 patients with available pretreatment BMI were included; 116 deaths occurred. Five-year OS ranged from 31.4% in patients classified as underweight to 82.0% in patients with obesity. Higher BMI was associated with lower mortality (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99; p = 0.013), and obesity was associated with improved OS compared with normal weight (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.26-0.96; p = 0.037). BMI was not significantly associated with RFS after adjustment (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.97, 95% CI 0.93-1.00; p = 0.080). Higher BMI was associated with fewer perioperative RBC transfusions (any transfusion: OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.98; p = 0.012; number of units: OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.95; p = 0.001). BMI was not independently associated with PEG placement or hospital length of stay; ICU findings depended on BMI modeling. Higher pretreatment BMI was associated with better OS and lower perioperative RBC transfusion requirements, whereas associations with RFS and most other perioperative outcomes were not significant after adjustment. Given the retrospective design and limitations of BMI as a body-composition marker, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Pretreatment BMI may help identify low-BMI patients warranting early supportive-care assessment.

articles.title: The effect of vitamin C supplementation additive to the priming solution on postoperative bleeding in coronary artery bypass grafting: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Patients undergoing cardiac surgery often experience bleeding during and after the procedure. Antioxidants such as Vitamin C (VC) are used to manage postoperative bleeding and inflammation after cardiac surgery. A total of 110 patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) were enrolled. Patients were randomly assigned into two groups of 55 participants each. In the intervention group, 25 mg/kg of VC was added to the CPB priming solution. In the control group, 25 mg/kg of normal saline was added instead. Nurse recorded the amount of chest tube drainage on intensive care unit (ICU) entry, and 2, 4, 6, 12, and 24 hours. They also documented the amount of blood product transfusion required during surgery and in the ICU. The amount of chest tube drainage in the control group was higher than the intervention group, but this difference was not statistically significant between the two groups (P > 0.05). The amount transfused blood in the operating room and in the ICU in the intervention group was 1.64±0.79 and 2.14±1.17 ml, respectively, and in the control group it was 1.69±0.84 and 2.52±1.68 ml, which was not statistically significant between the two groups (P > 0.05). There was no significant difference in duration of ICU and hospital stay between the two groups (P > 0.05). Adding VC to the CPB prime showed a non-significant trend toward reduced postoperative bleeding after CABG. Current evidence from this study is insufficient to recommend routine use; further larger trials are needed.

articles.title: Case Report: Postoperative pulmonary embolism causing obstructive shock and circulatory collapse after gynecologic surgery: successful rescue with VA-ECMO.
articles.abstract: Very-high-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) occurring within hours after major surgery presents a therapeutic dilemma because urgent reperfusion may be required at precisely the time when bleeding risk is greatest. We describe a 45-year-old woman who developed catastrophic bilateral PE approximately two hours after elective gynecologic surgery consisting of myomectomy and ovarian endometriotic cyst excision. Shortly after surgery, she experienced abrupt respiratory failure, profound hypotension, and rapidly progressive circulatory collapse. On arrival at a tertiary intensive care unit, arterial blood gas analysis revealed severe respiratory acidosis (pH 7.019; PaCO2 82 mmHg), and the patient remained unstable despite mechanical ventilation, high-dose vasopressors, and conventional resuscitative measures. Because of refractory obstructive shock and the prohibitive hemorrhagic risk associated with recent pelvic surgery, emergent venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) was instituted before definitive radiological confirmation. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography subsequently demonstrated extensive bilateral pulmonary arterial thrombosis involving both proximal and distal branches. Management was further complicated by ongoing postoperative bleeding during mandatory anticoagulation for ECMO support, requiring repeated transfusion of blood products and frequent adjustment of anticoagulant therapy. During recovery, the patient also developed residual left popliteal deep vein thrombosis, postoperative inguinal hematoma, and surgical-site infection caused by extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli. Despite these challenges, she was successfully weaned from ECMO and mechanical ventilation, transitioned to oral rivaroxaban, and discharged without neurological sequelae. This case illustrates the complexity of managing acute PE when life-saving reperfusion strategies must be balanced against a substantial risk of postoperative bleeding. It also adds to the limited literature describing successful use of VA-ECMO as a bridge to recovery in immediate postoperative PE complicated by obstructive shock and circulatory collapse.

articles.title: Successful application of low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation in CRRT for patients with liver failure: a retrospective case series study of 11 patients.
articles.abstract: To investigate the clinical efficacy, safety and operational feasibility of a low-dose regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) combined with low-dose nafamostat mesylate (NM) mixed anticoagulation regimen in continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for patients with liver failure, so as to provide clinical reference for the selection of CRRT anticoagulation strategies for such special high-risk critically ill patients. A retrospective case series study was conducted. Eleven patients with liver failure who received CRRT in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University were enrolled. All patients were treated with CVVHDF mode and uniformly implemented the low-dose citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. CRRT treatment parameters, anticoagulant drugs, and infusion doses of calcium and sodium bicarbonate were standardized. The monitoring frequency of peripheral blood gas and activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and the criteria for dose stratification adjustment were standardized. Data including patients' demographic baseline data, CRRT treatment duration, filter service life, blood gas electrolytes, dynamic changes of APTT, pipeline and filter coagulation, bleeding and metabolic adverse events, organ function and clinical outcomes were collected for summary and analysis. A total of 11 patients with liver failure undergoing CRRT in CVVHDF mode were enrolled in this study, using the low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. After treatment, the median filter life of patients reached 48 (38, 68.75) hours, with no severe pipeline or filter coagulation; there were no significant abnormalities in systemic coagulation indicators. One case (9.1%) had mild oral mucosal bleeding; no severe massive bleeding occurred. Hypocalcemia and metabolic alkalosis were observed in several patients but were not severe, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred. PCT was lower than baseline (P = 0.005) and APACHE II score was improved (P = 0.011) over the course of ICU treatment; however, all patients simultaneously received antibiotics, vasopressors, source control, and other ICU supportive care, and these changes therefore cannot be attributed to the mixed anticoagulation regimen. Liver and kidney function showed no obvious deterioration. In this small, single-center retrospective case series, a low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen was feasible to implement in patients with liver failure receiving CRRT. In this cohort, the median filter life was 48 h, no severe filter or pipeline coagulation was observed, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred; one case (9.1%) had mild bleeding. Because no comparator group was included, whether these observations reflect a benefit of the mixed regimen over conventional RCA, nafamostat alone, systemic heparin, or no anticoagulation cannot be determined. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered, multicenter, prospective controlled trials.

articles.title: Meta-analysis of the effect of nafamostat mesilate versus no-anticoagulation regimens in adult patients undergoing continuous renal replacement therapy.
articles.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is a critical treatment for critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. However, effective anticoagulation of the extracorporeal circuit remains a clinical challenge. Nafamostat mesilate (NM), a serine protease inhibitor, possesses localized anticoagulation properties; however, its efficacy and safety in high-bleeding-risk populations have not been systematically evaluated. To compare the efficacy and safety of NM anticoagulation and no-anticoagulation regimens in patients undergoing CRRT. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies were retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, MEDLINE, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, the Cochrane Library, Wanfang Database, Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database. We included studies on adult patients receiving CRRT where the intervention and control groups were treated with NM anticoagulation and no-anticoagulation regimens, respectively. Primary outcomes included filter lifespan, number of filters used, coagulation indicators, bleeding events, and in-hospital mortality. The meta-analysis was conducted using RevMan 5.4 software. Eight studies involving 969 patients were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that, compared with the control group, the NM group had a significantly prolonged filter lifespan (P = 0.01) and a reduced number of filters used (P < 0.0001). The activated partial thromboplastin time (P = 0.89), prothrombin time (P = 0.88), and international normalized ratio (P = 0.60) showed no significant differences. Both groups demonstrated clinically similar risks of bleeding events (P = 0.53). However, the NM group demonstrated a significantly reduced in-hospital mortality, compared with the control group (P = 0.02). The NM anticoagulation regimen effectively extended the CRRT filter lifespan, reduced resource consumption, and improved patient survival outcomes without increasing the bleeding risk, demonstrating particular value for high-bleeding-risk populations. Future multicenter RCTs are warranted to validate applicability of NM in non-East Asian populations. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261399024, identifier: PROSPERO CRD420251077578.

articles.title: Time-dependent associations of documented low-dose aspirin administration with 28-day mortality and early safety outcomes in adults with sepsis: a MIMIC-IV cohort study.
articles.abstract: Associations between aspirin use and sepsis outcomes may reflect treatment timing and clinical selection. This retrospective Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) study included 31,888 adults with Sepsis-3. T0 was defined as the later of intensive care unit (ICU) admission or suspected infection; sepsis ascertainment could occur subsequently. Piecewise time-dependent Cox models evaluated actual enteral aspirin administration of 75-100 mg and 28-day restricted in-hospital and ICU mortality. Baseline sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) measurements were restricted to T0 or earlier. Sensitivity analyses examined exposure history, eligibility timing, and a 24-h matched landmark cohort. A continuous-time marginal structural model (MSM) incorporated lagged clinical information. Modified Poisson models evaluated laboratory and transfusion outcomes. Eligible aspirin administration was recorded at or after T0 for 4,771 patients, including 3,646 within 24 h. Adjusted in-hospital mortality hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.48 (95% CI 0.31-0.75) during 0-24 h and 0.63 (0.51-0.78) during 24-72 h, without clear associations thereafter. ICU estimates were similar. Qualifying SOFA scores occurred after T0 in 24,916 patients; restriction to the 6,972 patients with qualifying SOFA scores by T0 yielded HRs of 0.54 (0.28-1.03) and 0.62 (0.44-0.88) in the first two intervals. The MSM had residual imbalance and truncation-sensitive early estimates. After multiple imputation, the first two in-hospital HRs were 0.50 (0.32-0.79) and 0.66 (0.53-0.82), close to the primary estimates. A hemoglobin decline of ≥2 g/dL during 0-72 h was associated with early aspirin administration [adjusted risk ratio (RR) 1.10, 1.03-1.17], but 606 early recipients had a qualifying decline recorded before their first dose. The temporality-restricted 24-72-h analysis showed no clear association (RR 1.05, 0.91-1.21). Documented aspirin administration was associated with lower early restricted mortality. Retrospective eligibility, residual confounding, and uncertain prior exposure prevent causal interpretation; these findings do not justify initiating aspirin solely for sepsis.

articles.title: Case Report: Simultaneous continuous renal replacement therapy and endovascular coiling in a poor-grade ruptured distal anterior cerebral artery aneurysm with ESKD and life-threatening hyperkalemia.
articles.abstract: Poor-grade aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) in patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) on maintenance hemodialysis has traditionally been considered futile. Uremic platelet dysfunction and coagulopathy, electrolyte disturbances, and poor multi-organ reserve make these patients poor candidates for aggressive intervention. When a ruptured aneurysm coexists with life-threatening hyperkalemia, the therapeutic window narrows further, because severe hyperkalemia significantly increases the risk of perioperative arrhythmia and cardiac arrest and requires urgent correction. Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) may offer advantages in this setting, but its use during neurointerventional procedures has rarely been reported. A 43-year-old woman with polycystic kidney disease and ESKD on regular hemodialysis presented with sudden coma and was diagnosed with Hunt-Hess grade V aSAH from a ruptured distal anterior cerebral artery (DACA) aneurysm. After 5 days of intensive care, her neurological status improved sufficiently to consider intervention. However, she developed life-threatening hyperkalemia (potassium 7.6 mmol/L). We performed simultaneous continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) and endovascular coiling. No anticoagulation was used in the CRRT circuit; intravenous heparin 0.67 mg/kg was administered separately for the neurointerventional procedure. CRRT was delivered in CVVHDF mode with a net ultrafiltration rate of 1-2 mL/kg/h and a total clearance of approximately 57 mL/kg/h, maintaining hemodynamic and intracranial stability throughout the 2-hour procedure. The aneurysm was completely obliterated (Raymond class I), and potassium decreased to 5.2 mmol/L. The patient recovered neurologically postoperatively but developed refractory bleeding during tracheostomy due to uremic platelet dysfunction and coagulopathy, ultimately leading to airway complications and death at 3 months. Simultaneous CRRT and endovascular coiling was technically feasible in this carefully selected patient with poor-grade aSAH, ESKD, and life-threatening hyperkalemia. However, this is a single-case experience and cannot be generalized, and perioperative bleeding and airway management remained challenging.

articles.title: A simple nomogram for predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with sepsis-induced coagulopathy in the ICU: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract: One typical consequence of sepsis is sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC), which is linked to a significantly higher risk of in-hospital death for patients in the intensive care unit (ICU). The specificity, sensitivity, and usability of current clinical prognostic evaluation techniques are restricted, and nomogram-based models are still not widely used to predict outcomes in patients with SIC. In order to increase the accuracy of forecasting in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with SIC, this study developed and validated a straightforward and user-friendly nomogram based on multicenter retrospective data. 480 SIC patients who were admitted to the ICUs of Hebei General Hospital and Handan Central Hospital (East District) between March 1, 2021, and March 1, 2024, were retrospectively recruited and randomly assigned to a training set and a testing set at a 7:3 ratio. An external validation set consisted of an additional 229 SIC patients who were hospitalized to Chongqing General Hospital's intensive care unit between March 1, 2021, and January 1, 2026. Eight kinds of variables were gathered, such as laboratory values, comorbidities, and demographics. Eight kinds of information were gathered, including laboratory measurements, comorbidities, and demographics. Using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, core predictors were first chosen. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was then used to find independent risk factors linked to SIC patients' in-hospital mortality. Using R's rms package, a nomogram was created based on the final set of chosen predictors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to assess the model's performance in terms of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. Among the 480 SIC patients, the total in-hospital death rate was 42.7%. Five independent predictors-including coronary artery disease, serum potassium levels, prothrombin time-international normalized ratio (PT-INR), platelet count, and platelet transfusion-were identified as being associated with in-hospital mortality among patients with SIC. With area under the ROC curve (AUC) values of 0.873 [95% Confidence Interval (CI): 0.832-0.914] in the training set, 0.776 (95% CI: 0.696-0.856) in the testing set, and 0.756 (95% CI: 0.692-0.819) in the validation set, the nomogram showed high discriminative capacity. DCA demonstrated that the model offered a high net therapeutic benefit over a broad range of threshold probabilities (0.1-1.0), and calibration plots revealed good agreement between projected and observed probability. The nomogram created in this work has strong discrimination, good calibration, and acceptable clinical applicability, making it possible to estimate in-hospital mortality risk in ICU patients with SIC in an understandable and accurate manner. By helping doctors identify high-risk patients early on and provide tailored care plans, this tool may maximize the use of medical resources and possibly lower mortality rates among SIC patients.

articles.title: Cefazolin-associated coagulopathy in a critically Ill patient with MSSA bacteremia: a case report.
articles.abstract: We report a case of cefazolin-induced coagulopathy in a patient with a methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia. Medical intensive care unit at a 1,500-bed, tertiary medical center. A 74-year-old male presented to the medical intensive care unit with septic shock secondary to a left skin and soft tissue infection. Blood cultures resulted positive for and the patient was initiated on cefazolin therapy. Shortly after initiation of therapy, patient lab work showed an increased INR to a max of >9.67. Hematology was consulted, and further work-up revealed a clotting deficiency consistent with a vitamin K-mediated coagulopathy. Intravenous vitamin K was administered, and the patient had rapid correction of their INR. Therapy was switched to oxacillin for the completion of treatment with no further cases of coagulopathy. Cefazolin-associated coagulopathy, though rare, should be considered in patients with unexplained INR elevation during therapy. Early recognition is critical, as discontinuation of the offending agent and administration of vitamin K can rapidly reverse coagulopathy. Clinicians should maintain heightened awareness in critically ill patients, particularly when additional risk factors for coagulopathy are present.

articles.title: Cesarean Myomectomy for Refractory Uterine Atony in an Eclamptic Woman with Multiple Fibroids: A Case Report from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
articles.abstract: Cesarean myomectomy remains a controversial procedure because of concerns regarding severe hemorrhage and peripartum hysterectomy. Recent reports suggest that it may be performed safely in carefully selected patients; however, the certainty of the available evidence remains very low, and reports describing its use for refractory uterine atony in women with eclampsia are scarce. We report the case of a 38-year-old Congolese woman, gravida 3 para 0 abortus 2, admitted to the University Clinics of Lubumbashi with generalized tonic-clonic seizures, severe hypertension (180/120 mmHg), and marked proteinuria, leading to a diagnosis of eclampsia. No ultrasound examination was performed before surgery because of the maternal emergency. After stabilization with magnesium sulfate and nicardipine, an emergency cesarean section was performed. A live female infant weighing 2030 g was delivered but died 30 minutes after birth in the neonatal intensive care unit. Extensive uterine fibromyomatosis was identified, including nine fibroids, the largest measuring 16 × 10 × 8 cm and weighing approximately 1050 g. After hysterorrhaphy, severe uterine atony persisted despite uterine massage and oxytocin administration. Considering the patient's nulliparity and the wish to preserve the uterus, a conservative cesarean myomectomy was undertaken. Five major fibroids were removed, including the giant lower-segment fibroid. Progressive restoration of uterine tone was observed after myomectomy, with satisfactory hemostasis. Estimated blood loss was 900 mL, and total operative time was 90 minutes. Postoperatively, the patient received blood transfusion and recovered without complications. She was discharged in stable condition on postoperative day five. In this patient, removal of the dominant fibroids was temporally associated with restoration of uterine tone and allowed emergency hysterectomy to be avoided. This single observation does not establish the safety or efficacy of the procedure, but suggests that cesarean myomectomy may be considered as a uterus-preserving option in carefully selected patients with refractory uterine atony related to extensive fibromyomatosis, provided that surgical expertise and blood transfusion capacity are available.

articles.title: Cardiac Tamponade Masquerading as Lactic Acidosis.
articles.abstract: An 85-year-old male presented with acute dyspnea and syncope, with pertinent initial vital signs including hypertension, normal heart rate, tachypnea, and hypoxemia requiring oxygen supplementation. The Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU) team was consulted for treatment of acute hypoxic respiratory failure, severe hyperglycemia, and lactic acidosis; on MICU evaluation, bedside point of care ultrasonography (POCUS) revealed a large, circumferential pericardial effusion. Despite ongoing intravenous fluid resuscitation, the patient rapidly developed cardiac tamponade with pulsus paradoxus and hypotension. Given the severe hyperglycemia and likely resultant osmotic diuresis, his atypical presentation may have represented low-pressure cardiac tamponade phenotype. He was emergently taken for pericardiocentesis and drain placement with immediate resolution of clinical tamponade; the etiology of his pericardial effusion was deemed idiopathic, although a hemorrhagic effusion from anticoagulation use cannot be ruled out. Ultimately, this case highlights POCUS as an essential clinical tool that should be utilized upon initial assessment of ICU level of care patients to avoid missing indolent but fatal conditions, such as developing or manifest cardiac tamponade. Once cardiac tamponade is identified, careful intravenous fluid resuscitation may be appropriate under the correct circumstances, although definitive treatment involves emergent pericardiocentesis.

articles.title: Bleeding Complications and Challenges in Establishing a Diagnosis of AL Amyloidosis of the Lymph Nodes: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Light-chain amyloidosis (AL) is an uncommon, multisystem disorder in which lymphadenopathy is a rare presentation in the absence of other organ involvement. Establishing a diagnosis can be extremely challenging due to bleeding complications stemming from coagulopathy and capillary fragility caused by amyloid vascular deposition. Bleeding complications lead to higher morbidity and mortality and lower diagnostic yield. We present a case of a thirty-six-year-old man who required prolonged hospitalization to establish the diagnosis of AL amyloidosis of the lymph nodes due to severe bleeding after surgical interventions. He underwent an endoscopic ultrasound (US) with fine-needle aspiration (FNA) of mesenteric lymph nodes and an endobronchial US with FNA of paratracheal lymph nodes. Both pathology reports showed mature lymphocytes admixed with blood and fibrin. Large hemoperitoneum and hemorrhagic shock ensued after the mesenteric lymph node biopsy. A subsequent excisional biopsy of an inguinal lymph node was normal. A surgical thoracoscopy with mediastinal node biopsy became necessary and was complicated by hemothorax requiring a thoracostomy tube insertion, a transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU), and an emergent video-assisted thoracoscopy (VATS) due to uncontrollable bleeding. During the hospital stay, the patient required multiple transfusions of blood products and coagulation agents to achieve hemostasis and hemodynamic stability. The diagnosis of amyloidosis was made after the mediastinal lymph node biopsy revealed Congo red positive tissue deposits with characteristic apple-green birefringence. After confirmation of the diagnosis, treatment was initiated with daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone. Subsequently, the patient was released from the hospital. He remains on this regimen in the outpatient setting and has shown a positive therapeutic response. He is now being considered for high-dose chemotherapy followed by autologous stem cell transplant.

articles.title: Bleeding complications in critically ill COVID‑19 patients receiving anticoagulation in a tertiary hospital intensive care unit.
articles.journal: The Southern African journal of critical care : the official journal of the Critical Care Society
articles.abstract: Coronavirus disease‑2019 (COVID‑19) is associated with a heightened inflammatory response, leading to thromboembolic events that influence patient outcomes. Complex anticoagulation strategies are often required to mitigate these complications. However, severe illness combined with such strategies may be associated with bleeding at multiple sites. To describe the incidence of bleeding and venous thromboembolism (VTE) in critically ill COVID‑19 patients receiving anticoagulation. Secondary objectives were to determine the incidence of transfusion in bleeding patients, and the association between inflammatory markers, coagulation parameters, and bleeding and/or VTE. Length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay and patient outcomes in the same cohort were also investigated. Participants included adult patients with confirmed COVID‑19 by positive polymerase chain reaction (PCR), admitted to the ICU from 1 April 2020 to 30 April 2021. A p‑value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. The study population comprised 103 patients. The anticoagulant of choice was low‑molecular‑weight heparin at therapeutic doses (median 80 mg/day). Bleeding occurred in 39.8% (n=41) of patients, predominantly from the oral mucosa (20.4%; n=21) and the gastrointestinal tract (13.6%; n=14). Of the patients who bled, 46.3% (n=19) received blood transfusions. Two patients (1.9%) developed grade 1 deep vein thrombosis. The median length of ICU stay was 7 days. Survival dropped below 50% (n=51) after 10 days of admission, and 25% (n=25) of patients survived beyond 28 days. Overall mortality was high at 65.0% (n=67). COVID‑19‑positive critically ill patients receiving therapeutic anticoagulation exhibited an increased incidence of bleeding, accompanied by a high mortality rate. This study provides South African data demonstrating a high burden of bleeding among critically ill patients with COVID‑19 receiving therapeutic anticoagulation. Bleeding risk was not explained by anticoagulation intensity alone but was associated with markers of thrombo‑inflammatory disease severity. These findings highlight the complex coexistence of thrombotic and haemorrhagic risks in severe COVID‑19 and challenge a simplistic approach to anticoagulation based solely on anticoagulant exposure. The study supports the need for individualised, dynamic, risk stratified anticoagulation strategies that incorporate clinical status, inflammatory markers and platelet trends.

articles.title: Severe tsutsugamushi disease complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and multiple organ dysfunction: a case report.
articles.abstract: Tsutsugamushi disease (scrub typhus), caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi and transmitted by chigger mites, classically presents with fever, eschar, and lymphadenopathy. However, cases lacking an eschar often face delayed diagnosis and can rapidly progress to severe hyperinflammatory conditions like sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS), carrying high mortality. A previously healthy adult male chef residing in Shenzhen, China, presented with a 10-day history of recurrent fever (peak 40.3 °C) and myalgia of the limbs and lower back. He reported unknown arthropod bites but had no typical eschar. On admission, he had thrombocytopenia (70 × 10^9/L) and elevated C-reactive protein (102.61 mg/L). He rapidly deteriorated to a platelet nadir of 33 × 10^9/L, complicated by DIC, ARDS, liver injury, and myocardial damage. Physical examination revealed a crater-like round ulcer on the left scrotum. The diagnosis was confirmed by positive O. tsutsugamushi antibodies at the Shenzhen Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and peripheral blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). Treatment included doxycycline, empirical meropenem and vancomycin, low-dose dexamethasone, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma transfusion, and comprehensive organ support. He stabilized and was discharged after 9 days. Severe tsutsugamushi disease can trigger a hyperinflammatory response leading to DIC, ARDS, and MODS, with a rapid and fulminant course. The absence of a typical eschar is a major cause of delayed diagnosis. In patients with unexplained fever, thrombocytopenia, and multi-organ injury even without an eschar careful inspection for atypical ulcers or eschars in concealed areas such as the perineum and axillae is warranted, especially in those with a history of exposure to endemic areas or bites of unknown arthropods. Diagnosis should rely primarily on clinical features and conventional serology. For critically ill patients with negative routine tests, metagenomic NGS may be considered as a supplementary diagnostic approach. Prompt recognition and timely administration of targeted antibiotic therapy are critical for improving prognosis.

articles.title: Emergency VA-ECMO-assisted PCI in a 95-year-old: a nursing case report.
articles.abstract: Advanced age has historically been considered a relative contraindication to extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) due to poor reported outcomes. However, contemporary guidelines advocate for comprehensive geriatric assessment over chronological age alone. Nevertheless, nursing literature on standardized care for ultra-elderly patients (≥90 years) requiring ECMO support remains scarce. A 95-year-old woman presented with acute inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) complicated by refractory cardiogenic shock (Killip class IV) and third-degree atrioventricular block. Given her extreme age, the family initially hesitated to consent to ECMO, prompting the placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) as a bridge while emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) commenced. Following renewed consent, VA-ECMO was established via the right femoral artery and vein, running in parallel with the IABP to ensure hemodynamic stability during the procedure. The patient was successfully weaned from ECMO after 13 h of support and decannulated. The IABP and tracheal tube were successfully removed the following day. The nursing care was retrospectively reviewed and organized into four domains, informed by the Iowa Model of Evidence-Based Practice and Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory. On admission, the patient already had severe coagulopathy (PT 17.6 s, INR 1.44, PT activity 57.00%, TT >240.0 s, fibrinogen 1.87 g/L, APTT >180.0 s, D-dimer 4.38 mg/L, FDP 18.46 μg/mL), anemia (Hb 60 g/L), and hypoalbuminemia (23.9 g/L). During hospitalization, she developed right lower limb hypoperfusion (unmeasurable toe oxygen saturation, right groin ecchymosis) despite the use of a distal perfusion catheter, and a nosocomial worsening of a pre-existing pneumonia on day 4. VA-ECMO support lasted 13 h 15 min with concomitant IABP; she was successfully weaned and discharged on day 6 at the family's request. Discharge diagnoses included a puncture-site hematoma and suspected ischemic changes of the right toes. This case documents real complications, including severe coagulopathy requiring transfusion, right lower limb hypoperfusion, right groin ecchymosis, and hospital-acquired pneumonia-together with a puncture-site hematoma and suspected toe gangrene recorded at discharge. These were managed without unplanned decannulation, major device-related infection, or pressure injury. It is presented as a hypothesis-generating, educational resource; causality cannot be inferred from a single case. The decision trajectory in this case-initial refusal of ECMO, IABP bridging, and family-initiated weaning-is itself instructive for ultra-elderly mechanical support. Multicenter prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: Outcome-Gap Analysis of High-MELD Deceased-donor Liver Transplantation Using Institutional Reference Values from Living-donor Liver Transplantation.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology
articles.abstract: Benchmarking in liver transplantation has largely relied on low-risk deceased-donor or multicenter cohorts. We derived living-donor liver transplantation (LDLT)-based institutional reference values and evaluated domain-specific outcome gaps in high-Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) deceased-donor liver transplantation (DDLT) in an LDLT-dominant setting. Adult liver-transplant recipients treated at a high-volume tertiary center between June 2016 and December 2024 were analyzed. A predefined low-risk LDLT cohort was used to derive institutional reference values. Continuous cutoffs were defined as the 75th percentile of the LDLT distribution, and binary endpoints as observed LDLT event rates. High-MELD DDLT outcomes were assessed across clinical resource use, global morbidity, organ/graft dysfunction, survival/graft outcomes, and biliary-vascular complications. The cohort included 423 LDLT reference recipients and 203 high-MELD DDLT recipients. LDLT-derived cutoffs were 7.39 h for operation duration, 2 red blood cell (RBC) units, 4 intensive care unit (ICU) days, and 24 hospital days. High-MELD DDLT exceeded reference values for transfusion, ICU stay, 30-day Clavien-Dindo (C-D) grade ≥ III morbidity (49.8% vs 29.3%; gap +20.4 percentage points [pp]), acute kidney injury (AKI) stage ≥3 (6.9% vs 1.7%; gap +5.2), and early allograft dysfunction (EAD) (40.4% vs 8.7%; gap +31.6). One-year graft and patient survival were lower in high-MELD DDLT (73.6% vs 92.1% and 76.9% vs 94.5%). Biliary complications showed negative gaps, indicating graft-type-dependent morbidity that required separate interpretation. LDLT-derived institutional reference values identified high-MELD DDLT outcome gaps, mainly in clinical resource use, major morbidity, organ/graft dysfunction, graft loss, and mortality. These values may help describe excess burden without serving as exclusion thresholds.

articles.title: Fibrinolytic Response to Protein C Zymogen and Plasma in Sepsis-Associated Purpura Fulminans: A Case Series of Nine Consecutive Patients.
articles.journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
articles.abstract: Purpura fulminans (PF) is a rare and life-threatening manifestation of disseminated intravascular coagulation, leading to multiorgan failure. Protein C (PC) zymogen supplementation has a strong pathophysiological rationale, but its effects on the viscoelastic fibrinolytic profile have not been described. We retrospectively analyzed nine patients (six adults, three children) admitted to our intensive care units between 2017 and 2025 with PF associated with septic shock, treated with PC zymogen concentrate and fresh frozen plasma (FFP). In the six adults, PC and fibrinolysis were measured before and a median of 13 hours after the PC loading dose, fibrinolysis with modified viscoelastic hemostatic assays (urokinase-modified thromboelastography [UK-TEG] in three, tissue plasminogen activator test [TPA-test, ClotPro] in three). Median (interquartile range) PC rose from 23 (10-31)% to 102 (63-137)% and Lysis, the percentage of clot lysis at the modified assays, from 15 (0-47)% to 78 (60-100)%. All six patients had fibrinolysis resistance before treatment. Lysis increased in five and returned within the reference interval in one; in the three TPA-test patients, lysis time became measurable after treatment but remained above 300 s. Three patients died and four required surgery for necrotic skin or soft tissue lesions. PC and FFP administration was followed by a partial recovery of the fibrinolytic response, which cannot be attributed to PC alone, since plasma was given at the same time. Modified viscoelastic assays may help monitor the response to PC and plasma therapy.

articles.title: Association Between Sepsis-Induced Coagulopathy Score Trajectories and 28-Day Mortality in Sepsis: MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD.
articles.journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
articles.abstract: BackgroundSepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) is clinically heterogeneous, and the prognostic value of its dynamic score trajectories remains unclear. This study used latent class growth modeling (LCGM) to identify distinct SIC trajectory subphenotypes and examined their associations with 28-day mortality, together with an exploratory assessment of treatment response.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included patients with sepsis from the MIMIC-IV (version 3.1) and eICU-CRD databases. SIC trajectories were built based on the mean daily SIC scores on ICU days 1-7, and at least three SIC measurements per patient were needed. Latent class growth modeling (LCGM) was then applied to determine the different trajectory groups. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was conducted to determine the risk of 28-day mortality, adjusted by age, sex, SOFA score, lactate level, WBC count, hemoglobin level, platelet count, RDW, PT, INR, comorbidities (Chf, COPD, liver disease, renal disease, diabetes, and malignancy), vasopressor use, and mechanical ventilation. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted to determine whether the association between SIC trajectories and mortality differed across subgroups. Exploratory analyses were performed to assess treatment responses to the use of vitamin C, statins, aspirin, and delayed heparin, and were evaluated using a 48-hour landmark analysis. Delayed heparin administration was defined as the first heparin order placed at least 48 hours after ICU admission.ResultsA total of 2,123 patients from the MIMIC-IV database and 807 patients from the eICU database were included in the analysis. LCGM found three groups of trajectories: Low-stable (37.7%), Moderate-to-low (41.4%), and High-risk stable (20.9%). The mortality rate of 28 days rose steadily in these groups, 15.4% to 32.4%, and 54.3%, respectively. This gradient was still present in both cohorts following complete adjustment. In the MIMIC-IV cohort, the adjusted HRs were 1.96 (95% CI, 1.57-2.44) for the Moderate-to-low group and 3.57 (95% CI, 2.74-4.66) for the High-risk stable group. In the eICU cohort, the corresponding adjusted HRs were 2.90 (95% CI, 1.78-4.72) and 4.86 (95% CI, 2.87-8.23), respectively. The addition of trajectory group to the baseline covariates enhanced model discrimination, and the ΔAUCs increased by 0.028 in MIMIC-IV and 0.040 in eICU (both P < 0.001). In the Low-stable group, aspirin use was marginally associated with reduced mortality (adjusted HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.43-1.01; P = 0.060), whereas no significant association was observed in the Moderate-to-low or High-risk stable groups. The same could not be said about delayed heparin administration: patients in the Moderate-to-low group (adjusted HR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.46-0.95) and High-risk stable group (adjusted HR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.42-0.90) had lower mortality. There was no significant association between vitamin C or statin use and better survival. Exploratory analyses (without adjustment for multiple comparisons) suggested that the relationship between trajectory group and mortality was generally similar across clinical subgroups, and interaction tests were not statistically significant in the eICU cohort.ConclusionsThree SIC trajectory subphenotypes identified by LCGM provided more granular stratification of 28-day mortality risk than did baseline SIC assessment alone, allowing identification of patients with persistently high SIC trajectories, who are at the greatest risk of mortality and may warrant closer monitoring and earlier escalation of care. The associations of aspirin use and delayed heparin administration with survival differed across trajectory groups. Nevertheless, due to the observational design and the possibility of residual confounding, future research is justified to confirm these relationships and whether SIC trajectory patterns can be used to inform treatment.

articles.title: Mobilizing the Critically Ill: The Central Role of Nurses in Preventing ICU Complications and Enhancing Recovery.
articles.abstract: The intensive care unit (ICU) is a high-acuity environment where patients with severe illness receive comprehensive care. Immobility is common among patients with critical disease states and contributes to muscle atrophy, development of pressure ulcers, increased risk of thromboembolic events, and acute respiratory insufficiency. Similarly, delirium is another prevalent complication that further contributes to prolonged ICU stays, increased mortality, and long-term cognitive impairments. Reduced mobility, delirium, and other sequelae of critical illness pose significant challenges to patient recovery and often result in poor long-term outcomes. Early mobility has been shown to improve long-term outcomes of critically ill patients by reducing their length of hospital and ICU stay, reducing ICU-acquired weakness, improving functional outcomes, and improving long-term cognitive function. Given their direct patient contact, nurses are uniquely positioned to serve as the primary facilitators of patient mobility in the ICU. As frontline caregivers, nurses can assess a patient's readiness for mobility, monitor vital signs during activity, and provide hands-on support for safe mobilization. They are instrumental in coordinating interdisciplinary efforts, ensuring effective communication among health care team members, and advocating patient-centered mobility goals. Additionally, nurses contribute to delirium prevention and management by closely monitoring cognitive changes, facilitating family engagement, and promoting nonpharmacological interventions such as sleep hygiene and cognitive stimulation. Through their continuous presence and compassionate care, nurses not only address the physical aspects of recovery but also provide emotional support to patients and families, significantly enhancing psychological well-being in the ICU. By leveraging their clinical expertise and patient advocacy skills, nurses are essential in fostering a culture of mobility and comprehensive care in the ICU, ultimately leading to better patient outcomes and quality of life for critical illness survivors.
