No ventilation variable predicted survival, which was primarily determined by disease severity and comorbidities. Changes in ΔP over the first three days were not associated with differences in the number of ventilator-free days.

articles.title: An interpretable machine learning model for predicting the risk of in-hospital death among ICU patients with traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is one of the leading causes of death and disability; early and accurate prediction of a patient's risk of in-hospital mortality is crucial for optimizing treatment and improving outcomes. The aim of this study is to develop and validate a machine-learning-based model for predicting the risk of in-hospital mortality among ICU patients with traumatic brain injury, and to use interpretable methods to identify key predictive factors and assess their clinical utility. Clinical data were retrospectively collected from patients with TBI admitted to the intensive care units (ICUs) of two Grade A, Level 3 hospitals between January 2022 and December 2025; After excluding cases of death due to causes other than TBI and those who were already brain-dead on admission, a total of 874 patients were ultimately included in the study. This was a 24-h milestone prediction study; the predictive model established is applicable only to patients with traumatic brain injury who remained alive 24 h after admission to the ICU. The primary outcome was in-hospital death due to traumatic brain injury; excluding deaths from causes other than traumatic brain injury and cases where brain death had already been confirmed on admission, a total of 381 cases experienced this outcome, representing an incidence rate of 43.59 per cent. Prior to analysis, the dataset was randomly divided into a training group (n = 613) and a testing group (n = 261). Lambda 1-se standard LASSO regression was applied solely to the training set to identify predictive features, resulting in the selection of 17 candidate variables. Seven machine learning algorithms were developed: logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, artificial neural networks, decision trees, support vector machines and naive Bayes. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), recall, accuracy, F1 score, precision and negative predictive value, with 95 per cent confidence intervals calculated for all metrics; interpretability analysis and model pruning were performed using the SHAP method. LASSO regression identified 17 relevant key features; the random forest model demonstrated good predictive performance, with a training set cross-validation AUC of 0.954. The simplified RF model constructed after feature dimensionality reduction included 11 key predictive variables, with AUC on the test set was 0.924 (95% CI: 0.848-0.960). The random forest-based predictive model demonstrated high predictive performance; the simplified model strikes a balance between performance and clinical interpretability and can effectively identify high-risk populations. Key features such as GCS and APACHE II can support early clinical risk stratification and personalized interventions, highlighting the potential of machine learning in the clinical management of TBI.

articles.title: Predictive models for prolonged hospitalization following major hemorrhage: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: This retrospective study aimed to identify the perioperative risk factors associated with prolonged hospital stays in patients undergoing hemostatic resuscitation for intraoperative massive bleeding. The retrospective analysis included clinical data from 119 patients who received intraoperative resuscitation for intraoperative massive hemorrhage. Patients were divided into two groups based on length of hospital stay, using the 3rd quartile as the cutoff (> 26 days vs. ≤ 26 days). The Mann-Whitney U test or independent samples t-test analyzed the influence of categorical variables on hospital stay. Chi-square test was used for count data, and continuous variables were analyzed using Spearman correlation. Risk factors prolonging hospitalization were identified and predictive models developed. Multivariate analysis revealed that independent risk factors for prolonged hospitalization following major hemorrhage comprised unplanned reoperation (OR = 6.743, P = 0.008), admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) (OR = 9.294, P = 0.020), impaired renal function (OR = 11.554, P < 0.001), Postoperative pulmonary inflammation (OR = 4.696, P = 0.018) and body mass index (BMI) (OR = 10.030, P = 0.046). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of the constructed predictive model was 0.908. Our study identified potentially risk factors, like BMI and abnormal kidney function, prolonging hospitalization after intraoperative massive hemorrhage. The predictive model may aid in identifying high-risk patients needing aggressive management to minimize complications. However, it is imperative to conduct prospective, high-quality research in order to validate our findings in the future.

articles.title: Co-occurring leukocytosis and hyperglycemia identify patients at high risk of subsequent mortality after intracerebral hemorrhage: a 24-h landmark analysis in MIMIC-IV and eICU.
articles.abstract: White blood cell (WBC) count and glucose levels may jointly reflect physiological stress after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). We examined their associations with subsequent in-hospital mortality and whether they improved prediction beyond established clinical information. This retrospective study used the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) and the eICU Collaborative Research Database. Adults with ICH identified by diagnosis codes who were alive and hospitalized 24 h after intensive care unit admission were included. WBC > 10 × 109/L and glucose >140 mg/dL defined four groups: neither elevated, WBC elevation only, glucose elevation only, and both elevated. Logistic regression estimated adjusted associations, with bias reduction in the eICU cohort. Restricted cubic splines assessed nonlinear associations. Prediction models used the minimum first-day Glasgow Coma Scale score alone or a clinical baseline model that also included age, sex, blood pressure, and other laboratory measurements. Models were developed on MIMIC-IV and evaluated without updating in the eICU database. The MIMIC-IV and eICU landmark cohorts included 1,606 and 264 patients, with 332 and 42 subsequent deaths, respectively. Adjusted odds ratios for both markers elevated versus neither elevated were 2.98 (95% confidence interval [CI], 2.04-4.36) in MIMIC-IV and 3.34 (95% CI, 0.97-11.54) in eICU. The glucose association in MIMIC-IV was nonlinear (p = 0.005), whereas the WBC curve varied with the spline specification. Among 229 eICU patients with both markers measured, adding the joint category to the clinical baseline model changed the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.796 to 0.811 (difference, 0.014; 95% CI, -0.012 to 0.039) and the Brier score, a measure of prediction error, by -0.0017 (95% CI, -0.0075 to 0.0041). Joint WBC-glucose elevation was associated with subsequent in-hospital mortality in MIMIC-IV, but estimates in the eICU cohort were imprecise. Additional predictive value remained uncertain, and continuous analyses did not establish a stable U-shaped association.

articles.title: Bleeding Complications and Challenges in Establishing a Diagnosis of AL Amyloidosis of the Lymph Nodes: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Light-chain amyloidosis (AL) is an uncommon, multisystem disorder in which lymphadenopathy is a rare presentation in the absence of other organ involvement. Establishing a diagnosis can be extremely challenging due to bleeding complications stemming from coagulopathy and capillary fragility caused by amyloid vascular deposition. Bleeding complications lead to higher morbidity and mortality and lower diagnostic yield. We present a case of a thirty-six-year-old man who required prolonged hospitalization to establish the diagnosis of AL amyloidosis of the lymph nodes due to severe bleeding after surgical interventions. He underwent an endoscopic ultrasound (US) with fine-needle aspiration (FNA) of mesenteric lymph nodes and an endobronchial US with FNA of paratracheal lymph nodes. Both pathology reports showed mature lymphocytes admixed with blood and fibrin. Large hemoperitoneum and hemorrhagic shock ensued after the mesenteric lymph node biopsy. A subsequent excisional biopsy of an inguinal lymph node was normal. A surgical thoracoscopy with mediastinal node biopsy became necessary and was complicated by hemothorax requiring a thoracostomy tube insertion, a transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU), and an emergent video-assisted thoracoscopy (VATS) due to uncontrollable bleeding. During the hospital stay, the patient required multiple transfusions of blood products and coagulation agents to achieve hemostasis and hemodynamic stability. The diagnosis of amyloidosis was made after the mediastinal lymph node biopsy revealed Congo red positive tissue deposits with characteristic apple-green birefringence. After confirmation of the diagnosis, treatment was initiated with daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone. Subsequently, the patient was released from the hospital. He remains on this regimen in the outpatient setting and has shown a positive therapeutic response. He is now being considered for high-dose chemotherapy followed by autologous stem cell transplant.

articles.title: Timely mobilization in acute brain injury: from chronological to physiological timing.
articles.abstract: Early mobilization has become a cornerstone of modern critical care, with demonstrated benefits on neuromuscular function, complication rates, and length of stay. However, its direct application to patients with acute brain injury remains uncertain and insufficiently supported by evidence. In this population, mobilization is constrained by complex and dynamic pathophysiological factors, including intracranial pressure, cerebral perfusion, autoregulation, and brain oxygenation, which may limit tolerance to physical and orthostatic stress. Current approaches, largely derived from the general intensive care unit population, rely on chronological definitions of "early" mobilization that may not adequately reflect the physiological readiness of acute brain injury patients. Emerging evidence suggests that both excessively delayed and prematurely applied mobilization may be harmful, highlighting the need for a more individualized strategy. In this narrative review, we critically appraise the available literature on mobilization in acute brain injury and propose a shift from time-based to physiology-guided decision-making. We introduce the concept of "timely mobilization," emphasizing the importance of integrating systemic and cerebral stability, neuromonitoring data, and patient-specific responses to guide initiation and progression. Ultimately, mobilization in acute brain injury should be considered a targeted therapeutic intervention rather than a routine practice, requiring careful clinical judgment, multidisciplinary coordination, and continuous physiological assessment to balance potential benefits against the risk of secondary brain injury.

articles.title: Longitudinal optic nerve sheath diameter trajectories in neurocritical care patients after mechanical thrombectomy or decompressive craniectomy: A descriptive bedside ultrasound study.
articles.abstract: Longitudinal optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) measurements after neurosurgical procedures remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to describe postoperative ONSD trajectories in selected disease-surgery cohorts. This single-center prospective observational study included 80 patients with clinically and radiologically defined suspected intracranial hypertension: 40 undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for anterior-circulation ischemic stroke and 40 undergoing decompressive craniectomy (DC) for intracerebral hemorrhage or traumatic brain injury. Forty healthy volunteers provided a local reference. Bedside ONSD was measured with a standardized protocol on postoperative days 0-9 and summarized using observed daily means and linear mixed-effects spline models. Of 800 planned patient measurements, 733 were available. Healthy volunteers had a mean ONSD of 4.11 ± 0.54 mm. In the MT group, mean ONSD increased from 5.55 ± 0.62 mm on day 0 to an observed maximum of 5.91 ± 0.77 mm on day 5, then declined. In the DC group, daily means ranged from 5.18 to 5.33 mm. In these selected cohorts, mean ONSD reached its observed maximum on postoperative day 5 after MT and varied within a narrow range after DC. Whether these changes exceeded measurement variability remains uncertain. Further validation is needed before using these observations to infer intracranial pressure changes or guide treatment.

articles.title: Association between early platelet aggregation function and 30-day mortality in patients with cerebral hemorrhage: a retrospective neurocritical care cohort study.
articles.abstract: Cerebral hemorrhage has a high early mortality rate, and platelet function may be related to patient outcomes. However, the prognostic role of platelet aggregation function remains unclear. To evaluate the associations of arachidonic acid (AA)-, adenosine diphosphate (ADP)-, and collagen (COL)-induced platelet aggregation with 30-day mortality in patients with cerebral hemorrhage, and to determine whether these indicators provided additional prognostic information beyond conventional clinical variables and disease severity scores. This retrospective observational study enrolled adult patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage or traumatic cerebral hemorrhage admitted to the neurological intensive care unit (NICU) between September 2022 and April 2026. Platelet aggregation was assessed early after admission using light transmission aggregometry (LTA). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 30 days. Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to generate an integrated AA + ADP + COL PCA score. Candidate covariates were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, Boruta, and random forest methods, and the selected relevant variables were incorporated into multivariable logistic regression models. Supportive analyses examined discrimination, calibration, decision curve, incremental information beyond APACHE II, overlap-weighted estimates, and subgroup consistency. Among 335 included patients, 78 died within 30 days. In the fully adjusted models, higher platelet aggregation values were associated with a lower risk of 30-day mortality for AA (OR 0.978, 95% CI 0.964-0.992, p = 0.002), ADP (OR 0.960, 95% CI 0.942-0.978, p < 0.001), COL (OR 0.960, 95% CI 0.943-0.977, p < 0.001), and the AA + ADP + COL PCA score (OR 0.613, 95% CI 0.494-0.759, p < 0.001). In supplementary model assessment, the fully adjusted models demonstrated good discrimination, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) ranging from 0.839 to 0.857, acceptable bootstrap calibration, and positive clinical net benefit across a wide range of decision thresholds. In supportive analyses, adding platelet aggregation measures to an APACHE II-only model was associated with higher AUCs and favorable NRI/IDI results. Subgroup analyses showed generally consistent results across the pre-specified subgroups. The associations were directionally consistent in extended adjustment and overlap-weighted sensitivity analyses. Reduced AA-, ADP-, and COL-induced platelet aggregation was associated with higher 30-day mortality after multivariable adjustment in patients with cerebral hemorrhage. Platelet aggregation testing may provide supportive prognostic information, but external validation and imaging-based confirmation were needed.

articles.title: Inferior vena cava peak velocity versus collapsibility index to predict volume status in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding: A pilot study.
articles.abstract: Patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) with hemorrhagic shock secondary to acute gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding represent a substantial proportion of the critically ill population. Accurate evaluation of intravascular volume status in these patients is crucial for guiding fluid resuscitation. However, the limitations of invasive methods and inferior vena cava (IVC) diameter/collapsibility measurements in assessing intravascular volume have been widely discussed in the literature. Despite their validation, noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring techniques remain underutilized in the ED. Therefore, the present study aimed to investigate the predictive value of IVC blood flow velocity measured by Doppler ultrasonography in intravascular volume assessment and to compare it with the IVC collapsibility index. Electrical velocity measurement was used as a surrogate marker of volume deficit. Eighteen patients presenting with a preliminary diagnosis of acute GI bleeding were included in the study. The study population consisted solely of patients with suspected hypovolemia; therefore, no normovolemic control group was included in the study. Demographic, vital, and laboratory data were recorded, along with IVC diameter, collapsibility, IVC peak velocity measured by continuous-wave Doppler, and noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring parameters at admission, at the 30th and 60th min, and immediately after completion of fluid replacement. All data were subjected to statistical analysis. A significant correlation was observed between initial IVC peak velocity and stroke volume variation at admission (P = 0.009). The measurement demonstrated a specificity of 100% and a sensitivity of 84%, although the confidence interval was wide due to the small number of patients without volume deficit. No statistically significant differences were detected at the other time points. This can be explained by the ongoing bleeding and the lack of a valid gold standard. Measurement of IVC peak velocity was found to be a significant predictor of hypovolemia, although it showed limited utility for volume monitoring. Furthermore, it demonstrated superior performance compared to IVC diameter and collapsibility measurements. However, the study does not evaluate its ability to distinguish hypovolemia from true normovolemia.

articles.title: Clinical value of a five-predictor nomogram for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after orthopaedic surgery in ICU patients.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the predictive value of a five-predictor nomogram for postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in orthopedic patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU).MethodsClinical data from 224 postoperative orthopedic ICU patients admitted between March 2022 and March 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were divided into a DVT group (n = 73) and a non-DVT group (n = 151). Logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors, and a predictive nomogram was constructed based on these variables. The performance of the model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.ResultsThe incidence of postoperative DVT was 32.59%. Patients in the DVT group had significantly higher age, D-dimer, prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), and a higher prevalence of diabetes, preoperative heart failure, and postoperative infection compared with the non-DVT group (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified age, diabetes, preoperative heart failure, PT, and APTT as independent risk factors for DVT. The nomogram demonstrated good predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.877. The sensitivity and specificity were 82.47% and 76.68%, respectively.ConclusionThe five-predictor nomogram provides individualized estimates of postoperative DVT probability in orthopedic ICU patients and may support risk stratification and targeted prevention.

articles.title: H-shaped sponge positioner prevents pressure injuries during prolonged prone ventilation in acute respiratory distress syndrome: a single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: In patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome, prolonged prone position ventilation is frequently employed to enhance oxygenation but often results in pressure injuries. To protect patients from such injuries, a new H-shaped sponge locator was designed in the study. In this single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial, 60 patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome requiring extended prone position ventilation (≥ 12 hours per session) were recruited from the General Intensive Care Unit at Xiangtan Central Hospital, Hunan Province, China, between May 2023 and May 2024. Participants were randomly allocated to either the intervention group, which received prone positioning with the assistance of the H-shaped sponge positioner, or the control group, which used conventional soft pillows for support. The primary outcomes included the number of anatomical sites affected by pressure injuries and injury severity, classified according to the revised 2016 National Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel/the European Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel staging criteria. Secondary outcomes included mean airway pressure, oxygenation index (PaO2/FiO2), intravesical pressure, and the frequency of support device adjustments. Data from 29 patients in each group were analyzed. Significant group × time interactions were observed for both the number of pressure injury sites and overall incidence. Although pressure injuries increased progressively across all sessions in both groups, patients in the intervention group consistently had fewer injury sites. There were no significant group × time interactions for mean airway pressure or intravesical pressure. However, both measures increased over time in all patients, with significantly lower values in the intervention group. Oxygenation index improved over time, with no statistically significant differences between groups. The intervention group required markedly fewer support device adjustments. In patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome receiving extended prone position ventilation, the H-shaped sponge positioner significantly outperformed standard soft pillow support in preventing pressure injuries. This cost-efficient device not only minimized the number and severity of pressure ulcers but also reduced mean airway and intra-abdominal pressures and decreased the frequency of nursing interventions. Given its ease of use and affordability, the H-shaped positioner holds substantial promise for clinical application, particularly in resource-constrained settings, and warrants further evaluation in broader implementation studies. This trial was registred at National Health Security Information Platform (Medical Research Registration and Information System, https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn, Registration No. MR-43-23-039592) on March 30, 2023.

articles.title: Association between stress ulcer prophylaxis and mortality in trauma ICU patients: A retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV database.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveStress ulcer prophylaxis (SUP) is widely used in intensive care units (ICUs), but its association with outcomes in trauma patients remains uncertain. We examined the association between SUP and mortality in adult trauma patients.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included adult trauma patients in MIMIC-IV (2008-2022). SUP was defined as proton pump inhibitor or histamine-2 receptor antagonist use for ≥3 days. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Propensity score matching (1:1, caliper 0.2 of the standard deviation of the propensity score logit) and sequential multivariable regression were used.ResultsAmong 2,999 patients (median age 66.7 years; 63.6% male), 2,286 (76.2%) received SUP. After matching (409 pairs), SUP was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (OR 1.98, 95% CI 1.30-3.02), 90-day mortality (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.26-2.22), 1-year mortality (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.18-1.94), and hospital-acquired pneumonia (OR 4.77, 95% CI 2.52-9.02). Clostridioides difficile infection was not significant after full adjustment. SUP was also associated with longer ICU (adjusted mean difference 2.88 days, 95% CI 2.08-3.68) and hospital stay (8.24 days, 95% CI 6.42-10.07). In inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) sensitivity analyses, most associations were attenuated; only in-hospital mortality and length of stay remained significant.ConclusionsSUP use was associated with higher mortality, hospital-acquired pneumonia, and longer stay in the matched analysis, but findings were sensitive to the method of confounding adjustment. These results are hypothesis-generating and may reflect residual confounding by indication and illness severity rather than a causal effect.

articles.title: Weekly Multidisciplinary Intensive Care Unit Debriefings Provide Effective Support for Intensive Care Unit Nurses.
articles.journal: Dimensions of critical care nursing : DCCN
articles.abstract: Nursing burnout is a rising crisis, characterized by emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and a diminished sense of accomplishment. Primary drivers include chronic staffing shortages, high-intensity workloads, interpersonal conflict, and inadequate resources to tackle work-related issues. In 2016, we launched daily multidisciplinary debriefings to mitigate the effects of such issues in our 18-bed intensive care unit (ICU). It was very effective, but daily meetings were perceived to be burdensome from a workload perspective. Safety restrictions during the coronavirus disease (2019-2020) pandemic and logistical challenges thereafter forced a suspension of debriefing meetings. To address continued needs, we resumed these operational debriefings in June 2025, electing to hold them on a weekly rather than daily basis. To assess the efficacy and impact of weekly multidisciplinary operational debriefings on ICU staff. Study if once-weekly multidisciplinary operational debriefings provide an effective support system for ICU nurses and are as effective as daily debriefings. Time and schedule permitting, operational debriefing meetings were held in the ICU at least once a week at a mutually convenient time and day of the week. Meetings were brief (∼15 min), informal, and multidisciplinary, involving all ICU staff. The primary objective was to establish a staff-driven support framework that promotes peer validation and tangible improvements within the ICU workspace. Six months after starting this process, attendees were invited to complete an anonymous survey to elicit feedback on the intervention. Survey questions were identical to the prior study in 2016 and were designed to be simple, straightforward, and closed-ended, with answers on a Likert-type scale. Of the 34 potential day-shift ICU staff, 32 completed the survey. Most respondents perceived that the once-weekly process provided them with a safe environment to express work-related concerns/dissatisfactions, nurtured team spirit, provided peer support, and improved overall professional relationships among colleagues. Two-thirds felt that these weekly debriefings led to a decrease in the overall stress level in the ICU. Overall, the results of the study were comparable to the prior study in 2016, with no gross differences in results. An overwhelming majority (90%) wanted the weekly debriefings to continue, but only half of them felt these sessions should be more frequent. Once-weekly informal multidisciplinary ICU operational debriefings provide an effective support system for ICU nurses. It is a realistic and viable method that helps build a positive and supportive work environment, without being burdensome from a workload perspective. A modified model could be replicated by other in-patient units.

articles.title: Alarm Fatigue and Burnout Among Nurses in Critical Care and Technology-Intensive Settings: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Alarm fatigue and burnout are major concerns among nurses in critical care and other technology-intensive settings. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the association between alarm fatigue and burnout in these populations. PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and Web of Science were initially searched from inception to 30 December 2024 and updated to 23 July 2026. Observational studies reporting an association between alarm fatigue and burnout among nurses working in critical care or other technology-intensive settings were eligible. Two researchers independently performed the three fundamental phases: screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to estimate the pooled correlation (r) between alarm fatigue and burnout. Twelve cross-sectional studies with a combined total of 3,716 participants were included (3,595 nurses and 121 intensive care unit physicians from one mixed-sample study); each pooled analysis included only three to five of these studies, so not all participants contributed to every synthesis. Alarm fatigue was positively associated with emotional exhaustion (r = 0.40, 95% CI 0.20-0.56), depersonalization (r = 0.33, 95% CI 0.16-0.48), and lower personal accomplishment (r = -0.27, 95% CI -0.40 to -0.12). For overall burnout, only two studies were available and were not pooled (r = 0.53 and r = 0.37). Secondary analyses showed a positive association between alarm fatigue and ProQOL burnout (r = 0.30, 95% CI 0.18-0.41) and a positive association with secondary traumatic stress (r = 0.29, 95% CI 0.13-0.44); no significant association was observed with compassion satisfaction (r = -0.09, 95% CI -0.30 to 0.12). Alarm fatigue was associated with higher emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and ProQOL burnout, and with lower personal accomplishment among nurses in critical care and other technology-intensive settings; associations with secondary traumatic stress and compassion satisfaction were weaker and less consistent.

articles.title: Music Therapy During Weaning From Invasive Mechanical Ventilation in the ICU: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The study examined the effect of daily music therapy on weaning from invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in the ICU, with a primary focus on weaning duration. Secondary agitation, sedation, and analgesia doses, pain, delirium, and perceived stress after 90 days were assessed. Additionally, total IMV and ICU stay durations and tracheostomy rates were studied. Physiologic parameters were assessed in the music therapy group (MG). The study also aimed to promote the humanization of critical care through a biopsychosocial and creative music therapy approach. DESIGN: Randomized controlled trial with two parallel groups: control group receiving standard care during weaning and MG receiving music therapy additionally. SETTING AND PATIENTS: Adult critically ill patients (n = 100) admitted to a general ICU who received IMV for at least 48 hours. INTERVENTIONS: MG received daily, individualized music therapy sessions averaging 25 minutes, based on patient needs and musical preferences, which included music relaxation, music listening, and clinical improvisation. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: No significant difference in weaning duration was observed between groups (p = 0.97). Patients in the MG group showed significant improvements in agitation and sedation levels (Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale) on days 1 and 3 (p = 0.048, 0.005, and 0.024) and a lower percentage required propofol (p = 0.028). No significant difference in perceived pain (Visual Analog Pain Scale). The MG obtained lower Perceived Stress Scale-14 scores (p = 0.24). Additionally, MG significantly reduced tracheostomy rates (14%; p = 0.025). Median total IMV and ICU stay duration were shorter in the MG group, but not significantly (p = 0.206 and 0.203). Heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and oxygenation showed no significant difference before and after music therapy. CONCLUSIONS: Music therapy may serve as a nonpharmacological complementary adjunct during weaning by reducing agitation, sedation, and tracheostomy rate. It may potentially decrease perceived stress and IMV and ICU stay durations. Further research is warranted.

articles.title: Weaning Strategies for High-Flow Nasal Cannula in Critically Ill Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the efficacy of different high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) weaning protocols in critically ill adults. DESIGN: This multicenter, randomized controlled trial was conducted from December 1, 2022, to August 31, 2024, based on the suggested protocol (SLOWH trial). Experts reviewed the trial between October 2, 2024, and April 15, 2025. SETTING: Randomization was performed by a research coordinator using a sequence of random numbers generated by an independent statistician blinded to both researchers and participants. PATIENTS: Adults (≥ 18 yr old) in the ICU who met the weaning criteria after receiving HFNC were included. Among 102 patients from three tertiary care hospitals, 15 were excluded. INTERVENTIONS: The remaining patients were randomized into three intervention groups: flow reduction (FR) first, Fio2 reduction (OR) first, or simultaneous reduction (SR). The primary outcome was the HFNC weaning success rate, defined as successful transition to conventional oxygen therapy without the need for HFNC reapplication, noninvasive ventilation, or endotracheal intubation within 24 hours. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 87 adults completed the trial (FR, n = 31 [male, 52%]; OR, n = 26 [male, 77%]; SR, n = 30 [male, 53%]). The weaning success rates in the FR, OR, and SR groups were 94%, 81%, and 77%, respectively (p = 0.15). The median [interquartile range] weaning duration was 31.0 hours (29.0-45.8 hr), 29.5 hours (28.0-60.4 hr), and 29.5 hours (26.5-45.0 hr) in the FR, OR, and SR groups, respectively, with no statistically significant difference among groups (p = 0.87). CONCLUSIONS: In this randomized trial, no statistically significant differences were observed among the three HFNC weaning strategies in terms of weaning success or duration.

articles.title: Fluid Therapy in Mechanically Ventilated Critically Ill Adult Patients.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Fluid therapy is ubiquitous in the intensive care unit (ICU) but carries risks, especially in mechanically ventilated patients. Contemporary global practice across dose, indication, and type is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To characterize ICU fluid practices in mechanically ventilated adults. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: International prospective observational cohort study between April 2024 and July 2025, across 206 ICUs in 41 countries on 6 continents. Consecutive adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation within 3 days of ICU admission and ventilated 24 hours or more. Exclusion criteria were age younger than 16 years and transfer under mechanical ventilation from another ICU. EXPOSURES: Fluid volume, indication, and type after intubation. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Key measures included (1) total infused volume and daily fluid balance over 7 days after intubation; (2) the indication for fluid therapy over the first 3 days after intubation; (3) the proportion of total administered fluid volume attributable to each fluid type over the first 3 days after intubation. RESULTS: Among 2454 patients analyzed (median age, 63 years [IQR, 49-73 years]; 63.6% [1560] male), median daily fluid input peaked on day 1 at 3.0 L (IQR, 2.2-4.0 L) and declined to 2.6 L (IQR, 1.8-3.5 L) through day 6. Daily fluid balance (median, 0.9 L; IQR, 0.1-1.9 L on day 1) decreased to less than 0.3 L (IQR, -0.5 to 1.2 L) by day 3 and remained near-neutral through day 6. Maintenance and replacement fluids (to meet daily requirements and to correct ongoing losses; 31.9%) and creep fluids (to deliver medications and maintain catheter patency; 30.9%) were the primary indications, whereas resuscitation (to restore circulating blood volume; 16.0%) accounted for a smaller proportion. Isotonic balanced crystalloids (48.9%) and isotonic saline (0.9% sodium chloride) (27.0%) were common; colloids were rare (1.3%). Substantial between-site variation persisted after adjustment for case-mix. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this prospective international cohort study, fluid therapy varied widely among mechanically ventilated critically ill patients, with maintenance and creep fluids-rather than resuscitation fluids-accounting for most total volume.

articles.title: Distinct weaning phenotypes in patients unsuccessful in weaning from invasive mechanical ventilation: a secondary analysis of the WEAN SAFE cohort.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterise the trajectories and outcomes of patients who enter the weaning process but fail to wean from invasive mechanical ventilation (MV). METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the WorldwidE AssessmeNt of Separation of pAtients From ventilatory assistancE (WEAN SAFE) cohort, we examined weaning duration and intensity, decisions to withdraw or withhold life-sustaining therapy (WLST), and clinical outcomes in patients not weaning from invasive ventilation. The primary outcome was ICU mortality. RESULTS: Of the 5664 patients in the study population, 1270 (22.4%) never underwent a separation attempt (SA), while 4394 (77.6%) had at least one SA; of these, 664 (15.1%) eventually failed weaning from invasive MV at day 90, while 3730 (65.9%) successfully weaned. Failed-Wean patients had the longest duration of invasive ventilation and longest ICU stay of all groups. Compared with Successful-Wean, Failed-Wean patients underwent more separation attempts, but fewer attempted extubations and more reintubations and tracheostomies. ICU mortality was 78% in Failed-Wean compared with 2% in Successful-Wean. Three clinically distinct Failed-Wean phenotypes were identified, distinguished by separation attempt count and WLST timing: Phenotype A (single SA + WLST), Phenotype B (single SA, no WLST), and Phenotype C (> 1 SA). A failed-first SA was strongly associated with WLST decisions. In this cohort, a WLST decision was associated with a higher hazard of ICU mortality and shorter median time to ICU death. CONCLUSIONS: Three weaning failure phenotypes were identified with distinct clinical profiles, weaning trajectories, and outcomes. A strong relationship exists between failed first separation attempts, WLST decision, and the risk of death, which deserves further investigation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03255109.

articles.title: Targeted Temperature Management at 35°C vs. 37°C for Heatstroke in ICU: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Heatstroke Research Group in Southwest China
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of conducting a trial comparing targeted temperature management (TTM) at 35°C-37°C in intubated heatstroke patients, while collecting preliminary data on safety and clinical outcomes. DESIGN: Pilot multicenter randomized clinical trial (June to December 2024). SETTING: Ten tertiary ICUs in China. PATIENTS: Thirty-five intubated adults (18 yr or older) with heatstroke meeting predefined diagnostic criteria. Key exclusions: nonenvironmental hyperthermia, expected death within 24 hours, or contraindications to temperature management. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to two TTM strategies. The therapeutic hypothermia group received protocolized rapid cooling using a combination of ice packs, precooled blankets, and ice-cold IV saline to achieve the target of 35.0°C within 2 hours, which was then maintained for 48 hours. The controlled normothermia group received conventional cooling measures (ice packs, 32°C blankets) only if body temperature exceeded 38.0°C, with the goal of maintaining core temperature between 36.5°C and 37.5°C. Shivering was managed according to a stepwise protocol, with a "lytic cocktail" (chlorpromazine, promethazine, and meperidine) available as rescue therapy for refractory shivering in both groups. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Recruitment rate was 83.7%, retention rate was 97.2%, and protocol adherence exceeded 88%. For clinical outcomes, no significant differences were observed in 28-day poor functional outcome (17.6% vs. 16.7%) or survival (82.4% vs. 83.3%). However, therapeutic hypothermia was associated with significantly higher rates of severe gastrointestinal injury (Acute Gastrointestinal Injury grade 3-4: 52.9% vs. 0%; p < 0.001) and arrhythmias (41.2% vs. 11.1%; p = 0.045). The lytic cocktail was required in 100% of hypothermia-group patients vs. 27.8% in the normothermia group ( p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study confirms the operational feasibility of a large-scale randomized clinical trial. However, therapeutic hypothermia was associated with significantly worse gastrointestinal injury and higher arrhythmia incidence, without evidence of neurologic or survival benefit. The universal requirement for pharmacological shivering control in the hypothermia group raises additional safety considerations. Based on current evidence, this strategy should not be routinely adopted in ICU heatstroke management.

articles.title: A specialist-led interprofessional weaning program to prevent weaning failure in high-risk patients: the PRiVENT study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Effective strategies to prevent weaning failure and prolonged invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in patients at high risk of weaning failure are limited. We evaluated a structured, specialist-led interprofessional weaning program. METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter, non-randomized interventional study, mechanically ventilated patients were screened 96 h to 11 days after intubation. Patients meeting predefined high-risk criteria received a specialist-led interprofessional weaning program, while a parallel control group was derived from health insurance claims data. The primary outcome was successful weaning at ICU discharge. RESULTS: The primary analysis included 349 intervention patients and 1,768 controls. Successful weaning occurred in 58.3% of intervention patients and 51.7% of controls. In the adjusted primary analysis, the odds ratio for successful weaning was 1.46 (95% CI, 0.99-2.17; P = 0.057), and the difference did not reach statistical significance. In prespecified propensity score-matched analysis, successful weaning occurred in 58.3% of intervention patients and 46.4% of matched controls (OR, 2.90; 95% CI, 1.61-5.24; P < 0.001). An exploratory analysis restricted to ICU survivors also showed higher odds of successful weaning in the intervention group (OR, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.09-4.04; P = 0.026). Overall, 16.3% of intervention patients were transferred to a specialized weaning center. These patients had longer ventilation durations, contributing to a longer overall duration of IMV in the intervention group. CONCLUSIONS: The PRiVENT intervention was feasible and successful weaning was numerically more frequent in the intervention group, although the prespecified adjusted primary analysis did not reach statistical significance. These findings suggest a potential benefit of structured, multidisciplinary weaning support. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05260853, registered on March 2, 2022.

articles.title: Sodium Bicarbonate for Critically Ill Adults with Metabolic Acidosis and Shock.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
authors: SODa-BIC Investigators and the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Clinical Trials Group
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic acidosis is common in critically ill patients and is associated with organ dysfunction and death. Sodium bicarbonate is used to correct acidemia, but its benefit in patients with metabolic acidosis who are receiving vasopressors remains uncertain. METHODS: In this pragmatic, adaptive, double-blind, randomized trial, we assigned adults with metabolic acidosis (pH, <7.30; base excess, no more than -4 mmol per liter; and partial pressure of arterial carbon dioxide, ≤45 mm Hg without intubation or ≤50 mm Hg with intubation) who were receiving vasopressors in the intensive care unit (ICU) to receive either sodium bicarbonate or placebo (5% dextrose). Sodium bicarbonate or placebo was infused for up to 5 hours, with the infusion rate adjusted for a target pH of at least 7.30 and base excess of at least 0 mmol per liter. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event, defined as death, use of renal-replacement therapy, or persistent renal dysfunction, within 30 days. RESULTS: A total of 500 patients were enrolled in 55 ICUs across seven countries; 245 patients were assigned to receive sodium bicarbonate and 255 to receive placebo. A major adverse kidney event within 30 days occurred in 98 of 244 patients (40.2%) in the sodium bicarbonate group and in 100 of 254 patients (39.4%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, 1.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -7.1 to 9.4; P = 0.78). Renal-replacement therapy was used within 30 days in 16.8% of the patients in the sodium bicarbonate group and in 20.9% of those in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -3.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -10.6 to 2.7). In-hospital mortality by day 30 was 25.4% in the sodium bicarbonate group and 24.0% in the placebo group (adjusted difference, 1.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.6 to 9.2). Four patients (1.6%) in the sodium bicarbonate group had an adverse effect, as compared with none in the placebo group (P = 0.06). CONCLUSIONS: The use of sodium bicarbonate in critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis receiving vasopressors did not lead to a lower risk of major adverse kidney events within 30 days than placebo. (Funded by the National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia; SODa-BIC ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05697770.).
articles.ai_summary: Researchers conducted a randomized trial of 500 critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis and shock to see if sodium bicarbonate reduced kidney damage. The results showed no difference in kidney damage or mortality between patients who received sodium bicarbonate and those who received a placebo. The study found that sodium bicarbonate did not provide a benefit in reducing kidney damage or improving outcomes in critically ill patients.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings are significant for ICU clinical practice as they suggest that sodium bicarbonate may not be beneficial in reducing kidney damage or improving outcomes in critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis and shock. Clinicians may need to reconsider using sodium bicarbonate in these patients.

articles.title: Induction Agents for Tracheal Intubation of Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tracheal intubation is a common yet high-risk procedure in critically ill patients, with as many as one-half experiencing peri-intubation adverse outcomes. RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the comparative effectiveness and safety of various sedative agents used for endotracheal intubation of critically ill patients in the emergency department (ED), ICU, operating room, and prehospital setting? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a network meta-analysis and systematic review of randomized controlled trials. We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, Cochrane, and trial registries from inception through December 10, 2025, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing ≥ 2 sedative agents in critically ill adults or children undergoing endotracheal intubation. Outcomes of interest were hemodynamic instability during intubation, hypoxemia, cardiac arrest, mortality, ICU and hospital length of stay, vasopressor use, adrenal insufficiency, and first-pass success. Reviewers screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool independently and in duplicate. We performed frequentist random-effects model network meta-analysis and used the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach to rate certainty in estimates. RESULTS: We included 21 RCTs enrolling 6,031 patients across ICU, ED, operating room, and prehospital settings. Compared with etomidate, more hemodynamic instability exists during intubation with ketamine (relative risk [RR], 1.31; 95% CI, 1.15-1.48; moderate certainty). Ketamine-propofol may decrease hemodynamic instability during intubation compared with etomidate (RR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.27-0.72; low certainty) and ketamine (RR, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.21-0.56; low certainty). Compared with etomidate, ketamine may decrease the need for the initiation of postintubation continuous infusion vasopressors (RR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.50-1.28; low certainty). Etomidate caused increased adrenal suppression compared with other agents. INTERPRETATION: Our results show that when considering sedation agents for endotracheal intubation of critically ill patients, etomidate probably causes less hemodynamic instability during intubation when compared with ketamine. However, etomidate may increase the need for the initiation of postintubation continuous infusion vasopressors when compared with ketamine and increases adrenal suppression. The clinical importance of these competing effects remains uncertain. Ketamine-propofol may decrease hemodynamic instability during intubation when compared with etomidate and ketamine, although the available evidence is too limited and uncertain to support firm conclusions, and further randomized trials are needed. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews; No.: CRD42024600739; URL: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/.

articles.title: Rocuronium dose and first-attempt intubation success in the critically ill: secondary analysis of two multicenter trials.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: The neuromuscular blockade dose may affect intubation success on the first attempt, thereby impacting outcomes for patients undergoing emergency tracheal intubation. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between rocuronium dose and tracheal intubation outcomes among adults undergoing emergency tracheal intubation in the emergency department (ED) and intensive care unit (ICU). METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of data from two multicenter randomized controlled trials studying airway management in the ED and ICU. We compared patient characteristics and intubation outcomes between patients receiving high-dose (>1.2 mg/kg) versus standard-dose (≤1.2 mg/kg) rocuronium. The primary outcome was successful intubation on the first attempt. We used propensity matching to account for measured potential confounders, stratified by setting. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Participating sites included 9 EDs and 24 ICUs in the United States. Among 2440 patients in the trial datasets, we included the 1822 (74.7%) patients who received rocuronium in the current analysis. Of these, 720 (39.5%) received high-dose rocuronium, and 1102 (60.5%) received standard-dose rocuronium. Participants receiving high-dose rocuronium had a higher probability of successful intubation on the first attempt (adjusted relative risk [RR] 1.07, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02-1.12). This difference in the primary outcome was not present for ED intubations (adjusted RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.89-1.04) but was present for ICU intubations (adjusted RR 1.13, 95% CI 1.06-1.20). CONCLUSIONS: In this secondary analysis, high-dose rocuronium (>1.2 mg/kg) was associated with higher first-attempt success. Given the potential for unmeasured confounding, these findings warrant evaluation in a randomized controlled trial.

articles.title: Operational Integration and Temporal Validation of a Continuously Deployed ICU Prediction Model.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To operationalize and temporally validate an electronic medical record (EMR)-integrated machine learning system (Big data-driven Evaluation of Survival and Treatment in Acute Illness [BEST-AI]) that generates hourly predictions for multiple ICU outcomes, with emphasis on discrimination, calibration, and workflow integration. DESIGN: Single-center hybrid study with stepwise clinical deployment and forward-in-time temporal validation. SETTING: Thirty-bed tertiary mixed medical-surgical ICU in Japan. PATIENTS: All ICU admissions from August 2017 to March 2025. Exclusions: age younger than 16 years or ICU stay less than 4 hours. Development cohort ( n = 11,176; from August 2017 to July 2024) and temporal validation cohort ( n = 1,127; from August 2024 to March 2025). INTERVENTIONS: EMR-integrated deployment of BEST-AI providing hourly probabilistic predictions to clinicians within the EMR; no protocolized clinical interventions were mandated. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Six prediction tasks (in-hospital mortality, ICU mortality, ICU discharge ≤ 72 hr, intubation ≤ 72 hr, extubation ≤ 72 hr, tracheostomy at ICU discharge) were evaluated. In temporal validation, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curves ranged from 0.856 to 0.960, and the area under the precision-recall curves from 0.302 to 0.786. Decile-based calibration showed overall good agreement; hospital mortality was slightly overestimated at higher predicted probabilities, whereas ICU mortality remained well aligned. The intubation task had comparatively lower discrimination and greater deviation from perfect calibration, consistent with low event counts and heterogeneous timing. A 24-hour landmark sensitivity analysis (one prediction per patient at 24 hr after ICU admission) preserved discrimination and calibration relative to the main analysis, supporting robustness beyond repeated-measures evaluation. The system was successfully maintained with automated hourly updates and EMR-embedded patient- and unit-level visualizations, without prescriptive alerts. CONCLUSIONS: A continuously deployed, EMR-integrated ICU prediction system achieved strong temporal discrimination and generally good calibration. Embedding real-time predictions into routine workflow was feasible, and the system was maintained with automated hourly updates. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted to assess transportability and clinical impact.
articles.ai_key_stats: n=11,176 (development cohort), n=1,127 (temporal validation cohort), AUROC 0.856-0.960, AUPRC 0.302-0.786, p-values not reported
articles.ai_summary: Researchers developed and validated a machine learning system that generates hourly predictions for ICU outcomes, such as mortality and discharge. The system was integrated into the electronic medical record and showed strong performance in a single-center study. The system was maintained with automated updates and visualizations.
articles.ai_significance: This study demonstrates the feasibility of embedding real-time predictions into ICU workflow, which could improve patient care and outcomes. Further studies are needed to assess the system's transportability and clinical impact.

articles.title: Is postoperative ARDS different from medical ARDS?
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postoperative patients have been underrepresented in randomized controlled trials of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Whether postoperative ARDS differs from medical ARDS in its clinical trajectory, outcomes, and prognostic determinants remains unclear. We aimed to compare postoperative and medical ARDS with respect to early trajectory, mortality, and risk factors for mortality. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data in a tertiary ICU from 2003 to 2023. All consecutive intubated adults fulfilling the ARDS New Global Definition were included. ARDS cases were labeled as postoperative when onset occurred within 15 days after surgery. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality, assessed with multivariable Cox analysis. Early ARDS trajectories were assessed at day 3. Multivariable Cox analyses were used to identify factors independently associated with mortality. RESULTS: Among 1,077 intubated ARDS patients, 455(42%) had postoperative ARDS. Compared with medical ARDS, postoperative ARDS showed more favorable early trajectories (p = 0.03) and lower 90-day mortality (36% vs. 49%, p < 0.001). Postoperative ARDS remained independently associated with lower 90-day mortality after adjustment (adjusted hazard ratio[aHR] = 0.68, 95%CI:0.56-0.83, p < 0.001). Prognostic determinants differed markedly. In postoperative ARDS, mortality was independently associated with extrapulmonary organ dysfunction (non-respiratory SOFA score: aHR = 1.10, 95%CI:1.05-1.15; bicarbonate: aHR = 0.81 per 5mmol/L, 95%CI:0.69-0.96) and surgical context, (esophageal surgery: aHR = 0.41, 95%CI:0.24-0.70; upper abdominal surgery: aHR = 0.64, 95%CI:0.46-0.91 versus lower abdominal surgery), while no marker of respiratory failure was independently associated with mortality. In medical ARDS, mortality was independently associated with respiratory failure, including PaO2/FiO2 ratio (aHR = 0.88 per 50mmHg, 95%CI:0.81-0.96) and driving pressure (aHR = 1.13 per 5cmH2O, 95%CI = 1.01-1.27), and extrapulmonary organ dysfunction. CONCLUSION: Postoperative ARDS differs from medical ARDS in its early clinical trajectory, outcomes, and prognostic determinants. These findings support postoperative ARDS as a distinct clinical subtype, mainly driven by extrapulmonary and surgery-related factors rather than by the lung injury itself, supporting a management approach focused on perioperative prevention and early identification of surgery-related complications.
articles.ai_summary: Researchers compared outcomes of 1,077 ICU patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) who developed ARDS after surgery (postoperative ARDS) to those who developed ARDS due to medical reasons. They found that postoperative ARDS had a more favorable early trajectory and lower 90-day mortality. The study suggests that postoperative ARDS is a distinct clinical subtype driven by extrapulmonary and surgery-related factors.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings have significant implications for ICU clinical practice, suggesting that postoperative ARDS may require a distinct management approach focused on perioperative prevention and early identification of surgery-related complications.

articles.title: Personalized automatic management of tracheal cuff pressure and subglottic secretions drainage to prevent pneumonia in critically ill intubated patients. The MICROINHALO multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The MICROINHALO trial investigated whether personalized management of endotracheal tube cuff pressure (Pcuff) based on exhaled CO2 measurement combined with automatic subglottic space drainage (SSD) may prevent tracheal colonization in critically ill intubated patients. METHODS: This cluster-randomized, international, open-label trial (NCT05403320) enrolled adult patients at 10 ICUs. They were randomly assigned to receive either an endotracheal tube equipped with automatic Pcuff management and SSD, or a conventional one with manual Pcuff management and manual SSD. The primary endpoint of the study was the rate of bacterial tracheal colonization (> 103 CFU/mL) on day 3 after intubation. RESULTS: Among 270 randomized patients, 250 were included in the analysis: 127 allocated to the automatic management group and 123 to the manual management group. Bacterial tracheal colonization on day 3 occurred in 47 (37%) patients in the automatic management group and in 51 (41.5%) patients among controls (absolute difference - 4% [95% CI - 16 to 8], P = 0.52). The rate of clinically diagnosed (12.6% vs. 24.4%, P = 0.016) and microbiologically confirmed ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) (10.2% vs. 19.5%, P = 0.039) was significantly lower in the automatic management group, along with a lower percentage of Pcuff values outside the safety range (10.2% vs. 24.4%, P < 0.001) and a higher daily SSD volume (25 [8-41] mL vs. 10.5 [6-17] mL, P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Among critically ill intubated patients, personalized automatic management of tracheal cuff pressure and subglottic secretion drainage was not superior to manual management to prevent tracheal colonization. Further research is warranted to confirm the observed effect on VAP rate reduction.

articles.title: Airway management in critically ill patients with obesity.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a global health challenge. An increasing number of patients with obesity are admitted to an intensive care unit. Airway management in these patients represents a unique challenge due to significant anatomical and physiological alterations. Increased adipose tissue in the face, cheeks, pharynx, hypopharynx, and neck narrows the upper airway, renders soft tissues more collapsible, and complicates airway management. In addition, the functional residual capacity is reduced, resulting in markedly shortened safe apnea time, contributing to severe hypoxemia during intubation. Non-invasive ventilation is effective in mitigating this risk and should be applied from pre-induction to laryngoscopy. Peri-intubation physiological optimization should include assessment of preload and cardiac contractility, with careful consideration of right ventricular strain. The transition from negative to positive intrathoracic pressure should be closely monitored, with cautious titration of positive end-expiratory pressure. Recognition of these anatomical and physiological challenges may prompt clinicians to consider awake intubation in selected patients. When rapid sequence induction is performed, both ketamine and etomidate are appropriate options; the choice between them should be guided by the clinical context, patient characteristics, local practice patterns and availability. Videolaryngoscopy increases the incidence of successful intubation on the first attempt and should be adopted routinely in the population with obesity. Several questions remain unanswered, including the safety and efficacy of pre-emptive vasopressor use to prevent post-intubation cardiovascular collapse and the optimal dosing of hypnotic agents to achieve ideal intubation conditions, while minimizing adverse events.

articles.title: Effect of a Lower Vs. Higher Positive End-Expiratory Pressure Strategy on Clinically Relevant Outcomes in ICU Patients Without Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Bayesian Re-analysis of the REstricted Vs. Liberal Positive End-Expiratory Pressure in Patients Without Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RELAx) Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: REstricted vs. Liberal positive end-expiratory pressure in patients without Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RELAx)—investigators and the PRotective Ventilation (PROVE) Network
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The "REstricted vs. Liberal positive end-expiratory pressure in patients without Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)" (RELAx) trial compared lower vs. higher positive end-expiratory pressures (PEEP) in invasively ventilated critically ill patients without ARDS, concluding non-inferiority of lower PEEP in frequentist analysis. This study aimed to perform a Bayesian re-analysis of RELAx to assess probabilities of clinically meaningful differences between lower and higher PEEP. DESIGN: A post hoc Bayesian analysis of RELAx data. SETTING: RELAx was a non-inferiority multicenter trial conducted between October 2017 and March 2019 in eight ICUs. PATIENTS: The trial included 980 ICU patients expected to require invasive mechanical ventilation greater than or equal to 24 hours for reasons other than ARDS. All patients included in the original analysis entered the Bayesian re-analysis. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to the lowest possible PEEP between 0 and 5 cm H 2 O or to a higher PEEP of 8 cm H 2 O. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was ventilator-free days at day 28 (VFD-28). Secondary outcomes were 28-day mortality and ventilation duration. The odds ratio for higher VFD-28 with lower PEEP was 1.08 (95% credible intervals, 0.87-1.35), with consistent estimates across priors and with a probability of superiority ranging from 75% to 78%. For 28-day mortality and duration of ventilation, the probability of benefit of the lower-PEEP strategy ranged from 72% to 89%, and from 11% to 28%, respectively. In patients admitted for other reasons than cardiac arrest or intubated for other reasons than respiratory failure, probabilities of benefit with lower PEEP exceeded 90%. CONCLUSIONS: Although the probability of benefit in the overall population was modest, the analysis suggested a higher probability of benefit in selected subgroups, particularly patients admitted for other reasons than cardiac arrest or intubated for other reasons than respiratory failure. These findings highlight potential heterogeneity of treatment effect and support further investigations.
