Whether targeted contact precautions are as effective at preventing nosocomial infection as contact precautions for all patients with MRSA and VRE is uncertain. Compared with standard contact precautions, are targeted contact precautions able to reduce the number of days patients spend in contact precautions and are they as effective at preventing hospital-acquired infection with MRSA and VRE? A pragmatic, single-center, single-cluster, crossover pilot and feasibility trial in which all adults admitted to a single medical ICU alternated every 2 months between targeted and standard contact precautions for MRSA and VRE for a total of 8 months. In targeted periods, patients received contact precautions only for highly transmissible MRSA or VRE infections, including open wounds, uncontrolled diarrhea, or pneumonia. In standard periods, patients received contact precautions for any MRSA or VRE infection or colonization. The primary pilot outcome was hospital-acquired infection with MRSA or VRE. The primary feasibility outcome was the number of patients per day removed from contact precautions in the targeted group. The trial enrolled 2,230 adults. During targeted months, 0.56 additional patients/d remained without contact precautions. Thirteen hospital-acquired infections with MRSA or VRE occurred during targeted months compared with 13 infections during standard months (P = .95). MRSA acquisition was higher in the targeted group (6.5% vs 3%; P = .03). Despite a slight reduction in patient-days spent with contact precautions during the targeted contact precautions periods, no statistically significant difference was found in hospital-acquired MRSA or VRE infections when comparing targeted with standard contact precautions in this pilot trial. Larger, multicenter trials should examine the benefits and risks of these interventions. ClinicalTrials.gov; No.: NCT03268122; URL: www.clinicaltrials.gov.

articles.title: Conflict in intensive care units: a conceptual framework for patient, family, team, and inter-service disagreement.
articles.abstract: For clinicians, conflict in the intensive care unit (ICU) is both common and expected owing to the nature of critical illness and its treatment. Examination of conflict in this context has been conceptually diffuse. Studies of moral distress, psychological safety, ethical climate, and other fields offer valuable insights that can be challenging to synthesize cohesively, due to differences in concepts, methods, and disciplinary perspectives. This narrative review integrates this literature using a task-process-relationship framework from organizational psychology. Conflict in the ICU arises in two principal arenas: between clinical teams and patients, families, or surrogates, and within and across clinical teams. Patients who retain decision-making capacity are a distinct and often overlooked party to conflict, as the focus has primarily been on the families and surrogates who speak for those who cannot. The task-process-relationship framework suggests a recurring escalation pattern for both arenas. Genuine task disagreements about treatment, prognosis, or goals of care can become destructive in the presence of process gaps or failures. These include role ambiguity, inconsistent messaging, and perceived unfairness. From there, conflict can enter the relationship domain wherein mistrust or identity threat makes resolution far harder, and two implications follow. First, much of what clinicians may describe as a "difficult family" can often be a response to antecedent process failures rather than a purely interpersonal problem, emphasizing the importance of engineering robust processes and systems in the ICU to avoid conflict reaching the relationship domain. Second, family and team conflict are linked in that unresolved team disagreement can reach families as contradictory recommendations and mixed messaging. Challenging family situations can expose team misalignment and damage collegial relationships. Evidence-based interventions, organized by conflict type and escalation stage, suggest that the most promising investments are structural, namely those built into rounds, improving role clarity, ensuring pre-conference team alignment, and fostering ethical climate. When conflict becomes entrenched, formal supports such as mediation and ethics consultation are matched to the nature of the dispute. While disagreement in intensive care is inevitable, destructive conflict is not.

articles.title: Accelerating tracheostomy decannulation with intermittent oro-esophageal feeding in neurogenic dysphagia: a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Neurogenic dysphagia frequently constitutes a major barrier to decannulation for tracheostomized patients. Conventional nasogastric tube (NGT) feeding may promote disuse atrophy of swallowing musculature and persistent aspiration risk. Intermittent oro-esophageal tube (IOE) feeding, a physiologically oriented modality mimicking natural swallowing, may accelerate decannulation, yet high-quality evidence is lacking. In this multicenter randomized controlled trial conducted at three tertiary academic centers in China, tracheostomized adults with neurogenic dysphagia were randomly assigned 1:1 to IOE or NGT. All participants received standardized pharmacological treatment, pulmonary rehabilitation, and structured swallowing training, and entered an institutional decannulation protocol with predefined readiness criteria. The primary outcome was time from protocol entry to actual decannulation. Secondary outcomes included the 30-day successful decannulation rate, nutritional indices, swallowing function, and swallowing-related quality of life. Outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to allocation. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. A total of 140 patients were randomized to IOE (n = 70) or NGT (n = 70). Time to decannulation was shorter with IOE (22.16 ± 1.86 vs. 26.33 ± 1.30 days; between-group difference, 4.17 days; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.90-6.44; p < 0.001; log-rank p = 0.005). The 30-day successful decannulation rate was higher with IOE (65.71% vs. 47.14%; absolute difference, 18.57% points; 95% CI, 2.43-34.71; p = 0.028). At 1 month, the IOE group demonstrated greater improvements in body mass index, serum albumin, serum prealbumin, swallowing function, and swallowing-related quality of life (all p < 0.001). Pharyngeal discomfort was less frequent with IOE (14.06% vs. 34.21%; p = 0.006); no Grade Ⅲ or higher adverse events occurred. Intermittent oro-esophageal tube feeding shortens time to decannulation and improves nutritional, swallowing, and quality-of-life outcomes compared with nasogastric tube feeding in tracheostomized patients with neurogenic dysphagia. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06791590, registration date January 19, 2025.

articles.title: Parental perspectives on clinician guidance in value-laden NICU conversations: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract: Value-laden decisions about life-sustaining treatment for critically ill infants in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) present profound emotional and ethical challenges for parents and clinicians. In such situations, clinicians must balance providing guidance with respecting parental autonomy. We explored parental perspectives on clinician guidance and effective communication during these decisions. We conducted a secondary qualitative analysis within a randomized clinical trial using parental free-text responses to a simulated neonatal decision-making scenario. The study was carried out online between February and April 2024 in Switzerland, Germany, and Austria. Eligible participants were German-speaking parents of preterm infants with prior NICU experience, recruited through patient and parent organizations. Data were analyzed using qualitative content analysis. Among 128 participants (84% female), parents emphasized the importance of clear, detailed, and evidence-based information about their child's condition and treatment options, as well as empathetic, honest, and individualized communication. They valued sufficient time for discussion and reflection, access to second opinions, and attention to the child's quality of life. Parents appeared to retain a sense of decision ownership, while differing in their preferences regarding clinician guidance. Some welcomed explicit recommendations, whereas others preferred neutral, value-sensitive communication that preserved space for independent deliberation. Parents facing complex medical decisions value both high-quality information and empathetic and honest communication. While they generally retain decision ownership, preferences regarding clinician guidance vary, suggesting that clinicians should actively explore how much direction parents want and tailor their communication accordingly. ISRCTN registry under number ISRCTN16123073, registration date: 17/01/2024, ( https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN16123073 ).

articles.title: The effect of propolis oral care on oral mucositis in intensive care patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the preventive effect of adding a propolis gargle to standard oral care on the development of oral mucositis in critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. This randomized controlled trial included 60 critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Both groups received the institutional standard oral care protocol with 0.2% chlorhexidine gluconate three times daily. The intervention group additionally received a propolis gargle three times daily for 15 days. Oral mucosal status was evaluated using the total oral mucosa score. There was no significant difference in oral mucosa scores between the groups at baseline, whereas oral mucosa scores were significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group at the 7- and 15-day follow-ups (p<0.001). Adding propolis gargle to standard oral care significantly reduced the development of oral mucositis in critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. However, because the intervention group received additional oral care exposure, the independent effect of propolis cannot be determined and requires further investigation.Clinical Trial Registration Number: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07426198.

articles.title: Prevalence of depressive symptoms among intensive care unit nurses: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.abstract: Despite the extensive body of literature on the prevalence of depressive symptoms among intensive care unit (ICU) nurses, the reported rates have exhibited marked inconsistency across studies. This meta-analysis aimed to determine the pooled prevalence of depressive symptoms and to explore potential sources of between-study variation in ICU nurses. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and PsycINFO was conducted from database inception to September 30, 2026. The pooled prevalence of depressive symptoms was calculated using a random-effects model, with heterogeneity evaluated using the I2 statistic. Subgroup analyses and meta-regression were employed to identify the potential sources of heterogeneity. A total of 38 studies comprising 22,474 ICU nurses representing 21 countries were included. The pooled prevalence of depressive symptoms in ICU nurses was 38.6% (95% CI: 31.2-46.3%, 95% PI: 2.8-84.6%, I 2 = 98.9%, τ2 = 0.23). In exploratory univariate and multivariable meta-regression analyses, economic status and data collection period were associated with the prevalence of depressive symptoms among ICU nurses (all p < 0.05). Although the depressive symptoms among ICU nurses are common, the substantial heterogeneity and the wide 95% PI indicate that the true prevalence varies considerably across settings. This pooled estimate should therefore not be interpreted as a stable global prevalence. Instead, the findings highlight the marked variability in the prevalence of depressive symptoms across populations, economic contexts, and data collection periods. These findings highlight the need for increased attention to ICU nurses' mental health and for context-sensitive organizational support to promote long-term psychological well-being in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Enhancing High-Fidelity Simulation Flight-Based Training for Critical Care Paramedics in EMS Aviation: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: High-fidelity simulation (HFS) is used with critical care paramedics (CCPs) to enhance preparedness in high-stake scenarios. This systematic review aims to assess the evidence on the role and effectiveness of HFS flight-based training, evaluating its application in education for CCPs operating within emergency medical services aviation settings. A systematic literature search was performed using a set of inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in 7 articles which were appraised using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme tool. HFS training equips learners with skills relevant to their practice. CCPs register improved expertise, engagement and motivation, responsiveness, and general mood. There was insufficient evidence on whether this modality enhances self-awareness. HFS learning is feasible in training CCPs in emergency medical services aviation. However, there is limited evidence on the performance of CCPs trained using HFS learning in the prehospital setting. The findings suggest that standardizing training and assessment methods is recommended to optimize skill acquisition, improve team performance, and enhance patient safety in high-acuity emergencies.

articles.title: Patient- and Family-centred Nursing Communication in the Intensive Care Unit: A Bibliometric Analysis.
articles.journal: Dimensions of critical care nursing : DCCN
articles.abstract: As a fundamental component of critical care, patient- and family-centred nursing communication in the intensive care unit is not merely an information exchange process, but a professional behaviour that requires practical skills. This study aims to employ bibliometric analysis to elucidate the prevailing research focal points and trends within patient- and family-centred nursing communication. Relevant articles were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. CiteSpace and VOSviewer were used for bibliometric analysis and visualization of countries, institutions, authors, and keywords. From 2006 to 2025, annual publications showed a fluctuating upward trend. A total of 925 publications were included, authored by 4048 authors from 1651 institutions. Research hotspots included the impact of communication, communication management, and context-specific communication. The long-term communication needs of intensive care unit survivors and the development of augmentative and alternative communication tools are likely to emerge as future research trends in this field. This study provides an overview of the research in the field of patient- and family-centred nursing communication over the past 2 decades. This research offers valuable references and guidance for the future trends and research paths in this area.

articles.title: Development and Pilot Psychometric Testing of the ICU-HQI to Assess Handover Quality in Intensive Care Units.
articles.journal: Dimensions of critical care nursing : DCCN
articles.abstract: Effective information handover during shift changes is critical for patient safety in intensive care units (ICUs). Despite extensive research on handover practices, measurement instruments with preliminary psychometric evidence applicable across different nursing roles and ICU contexts remain limited. To develop and conduct a preliminary psychometric evaluation of the ICU-HQI questionnaire for assessing ICU nursing professionals' perceptions of handover quality. A pilot cross-sectional methodological study was conducted in 2 ICUs with different physical layouts (open-box and closed-box) in a tertiary hospital in Spain. Content validity was assessed through a Delphi process. The questionnaire was administered to nursing staff, and exploratory dimensionality analysis using principal components analysis was performed to examine the internal structure of the instrument and its internal consistency. Exploratory subgroup analyses were conducted according to professional role, gender, age, and ICU experience to examine the instrument's preliminary discriminatory behavior. A total of 101 professionals participated (response rate: 94.3%). Principal components analysis supported a 3-dimensional structure (handover methodology, environment, and quality-safety), resulting in a final 12-item instrument with acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach α=0.72). Exploratory differences were observed for selected items across professional roles, gender, and ICU experience. No statistically significant differences were detected between ICU layouts. The ICU-HQI demonstrates satisfactory preliminary psychometric properties as a pilot instrument for assessing perceived nursing handover quality in ICUs. While exploratory subgroup patterns were identified, further validation using common factor methods and confirmatory approaches in larger, multicenter samples is required before substantive comparisons across professional groups or unit contexts can be established.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics of unregulated psychoactive supplement exposures: a 15-year multicenter study of kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine.
articles.abstract: Unregulated psychoactive "supplements" including kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine are readily accessible, raising concern for toxicity and dependence owing to their GABA and opioid receptor activity; however, clinical features associated with their use are poorly characterized. We describe hospital presentations and management of kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine exposures. We analyzed data from the Toxicology Investigators Consortium (ToxIC) Core Registry, which prospectively collects information on patients managed by medical toxicologists (1 January 2010-31 December 2024). All cases involving kratom, phenibut, and/or tianeptine exposures were included. Demographics, exposure circumstances, clinical presentation, management, and outcomes were examined. We identified 152 patient encounters involving kratom (n = 97), phenibut (n = 44) and/or tianeptine (n = 11), with case counts increasing over time. Median age was 35 years (IQR 26-42 years), and 127 (83.6%) were male. Co-ingestions were common (n = 73; 48.0%) frequently involving other psychoactive supplements (n = 27; 17.8%), stimulants (n = 23; 15.1%) and/or opioids (n = 22; 14.5%). Most consultations involved intentional use (n = 131; 86.2%), including euphoria (n = 60; 39.5%), perceived therapeutic/wellness benefit (n = 18; 11.8%) and withdrawal self-management (n = 13; 8.6%). Thirty-five encounters (23.0%) resulted in intensive care admission and one patient died. Addiction treatment infrequently involved buprenorphine/naloxone (n = 15; 9.9%). At hospital discharge 16 (10.5%) patients received naloxone overdose prevention kit education and/or prescription. Psychoactive supplement exposures evaluated by medical toxicologists were associated with substantial morbidity, with nearly one-quarter requiring intensive care unit admission. Withdrawal was common, and nearly half of encounters involved co-ingestants. Hospital presentations involving kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine increased over time, supporting recognition of these substances as emerging drugs of misuse rather than benign supplements. These findings highlight opportunities to strengthen addiction-focused care, regulatory oversight and public education.

articles.title: An ICD-10-based algorithm for identifying the cause of acute respiratory failure in mechanically ventilated patients.
articles.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
articles.abstract: Acute respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation is a common reason for admission to an intensive care unit. Epidemiological research is limited by the lack of scalable approaches for identifying the primary cause of acute respiratory failure in these patients. To develop and validate an algorithm for classifying mechanically ventilated patients by the primary cause of acute respiratory failure using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) diagnosis and procedure codes. We identified adult patients undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation in the electronic health record of a multi-hospital health system in the United States. Using this cohort, we created a preliminary classification schema that assigned patients to one of eight mutually exclusive causes of acute respiratory failure (stroke, chronic lung disease, heart failure, trauma or overdose, pneumonia, non-pneumonia sepsis, post-operative, and other) based on the presence or absence of pre-specified ICD-10 codes. We compared the preliminary classifications to a clinical reference standard ascertained via manual chart review in a stratified random sample of the development cohort, refining the schema to optimize concordance. We then assessed content validity by examining clinical characteristics and outcomes across diagnosis categories, both in the development cohort and in an external all-payer claims dataset. Of 8,130 hospitalizations in the development sample, all were successfully categorized into eight mutually exclusive groups. Compared to the reference standard of manual chart review (n=206), overall agreement was moderate (kappa = 0.44, 95% confidence interval: 0.39-0.49). After refinement, overall agreement improved slightly (kappa = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.41-0.52). The final positive predictive values ranged from 78.6% (pneumonia) to 32.3% (stroke). The largest diagnostic category was non-pneumonia sepsis (26.1%), and the smallest diagnostic category was heart failure (6.2%). Clinical characteristics and outcomes approximated those expected from prior literature and were similar in the external dataset. A novel ICD-10-based algorithm for determining the primary cause of acute respiratory failure in patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation was moderately accurate. This algorithm is potentially useful for facilitating large-scale epidemiological research in this population.

articles.title: Patterns, outcomes and predictors of severe hospital course among people in prison admitted for poisoning in northwest Iran: a retrospective analytical cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: People in prison may be at heightened risk of poisoning and overdose because of substance use, psychiatric morbidity and the stresses of incarceration. This study aims to describe the demographic, toxicological and clinical characteristics of people in prison who required hospital admission for poisoning in northwest Iran. A retrospective cross-sectional review was conducted using hospital records of all people in prison admitted to the poisoning service of Taleghani Hospital, Urmia, Iran, from 12 January 2017 to 31 December 2020. Demographic variables, poisoning agent, route and intentionality of exposure, psychiatric history, previous poisoning-related admission, intensive care unit admission, length of stay and treatment outcome were summarised descriptively. The study included 276 admissions. Most patients were male (98.2%), and the mean age was 35.05 ± 10.43 years. Opioids (30.0% of recorded substances), benzodiazepines (21.0%) and stimulants (17.0%) were the leading recorded agents. Oral exposure was most common (84.1%), and 66.7% of episodes were documented as intentional. Psychiatric history was recorded in 47.8%, previous poisoning-related admission in 54.7% and ICU admission in 15.6%. Most patients were discharged (94.2%); in-hospital mortality was 2.2%. This was a single-centre retrospective study based on hospital records, which may have involved incomplete documentation and limited generalisability. The small number of deaths limited mortality-specific modelling. Findings should be interpreted as exploratory and require validation in larger multicentre studies. The findings support structured clinical risk assessment at admission, closer monitoring of patients with decreased consciousness, supervised medication access in correctional settings and routine psychiatric and substance-use assessment after poisoning. Strengthened communication between hospitals and prison health services may help reduce recurrent poisoning and improve continuity of care. Poisoning among people in prison represents an important public health and social concern. Improving prevention, timely identification and continuity of care may help reduce avoidable harm and support better health outcomes for this vulnerable population. This study adds regional evidence on hospital-treated poisoning among people in prison and extends the descriptive thesis data set with exploratory outcome analysis. The findings highlight the need for integrated prison mental health, substance-use, medication-safety and emergency transfer pathways.

articles.title: Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System Therapy in Severe Amlodipine Overdose: Two Cases and Review of the Literature.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCalcium channel blocker (CCB) overdose is a significant cause of cardiovascular drug overdose-related mortality, with amlodipine emerging as the most frequently implicated agent in serious intoxication. Current management strategies for CCB poisoning include vasopressors, high-dose insulin therapy, and other adjunctive treatments. The unique pharmacodynamic profile of amlodipine can lead to severe and persistent vasoplegic shock that is refractory to conventional therapy. The Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System (MARS), an albumin dialysis technique capable of removing protein-bound toxins, has been proposed as a potential adjunctive therapy in cases of refractory vasodilatory shock associated with severe amlodipine poisoning.MethodsWe report two cases of severe amlodipine poisoning complicated by refractory vasodilatory shock treated with the Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System (MARS). A targeted PubMed search was also performed to identify published reports of calcium channel blocker intoxication with severe shock treated with MARS. Only reports describing amlodipine ingestion, either alone or with co-ingested agents, were included.ResultsBoth cases involved severe amlodipine poisoning complicated by refractory vasodilatory shock with multiorgan dysfunction requiring multiple vasopressors, high-dose insulin therapy, mechanical ventilation, and renal replacement therapy. Initiation of MARS was temporally associated with progressive hemodynamic stabilization, including reductions in vasopressor requirements and improvement in lactate levels. In the first case, MARS was successfully continued during prone ventilation for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome. In the second case, persistent cardiopulmonary failure required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Reinitiation of MARS during ECMO support was associated with improved lactate clearance and reduced vasopressor requirements.ConclusionsSevere amlodipine poisoning can result in profound and persistent vasodilatory shock with multiorgan dysfunction despite multiple conventional and adjunctive therapies. MARS may represent a useful adjunctive therapy in selected cases and can be integrated into complex critical care strategies, including prone ventilation and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

articles.title: Local complications of peripheral intravenous vasopressor use with phentolamine as an antidote: a retrospective review.
articles.abstract: Prior studies have indicated that peripheral administration of vasopressors, particularly norepinephrine, can be considered safe, with local complications occurring in 0% to 1.8% of patients. Our study further explored the local skin complications from peripheral vasopressor administration treated with phentolamine in a large health care system. A retrospective chart review was performed on patients who received phentolamine for effects of local infiltration of pressors. Data were collected for demographics, vasopressor dose and duration of use, phentolamine dose and time after extravasation until administration, peripheral intravenous characteristics, as well as outcomes such as length of stay and mortality. Data on patients who did and did not require central venous catheter placement postextravasation were compared. Of 92 patients with infiltrated vasopressor intravenous access who required phentolamine, the mean age was 69, with 65% being female and a mean body mass index of 28 kg/m2. The most common sites of intravenous access were the antecubital fossa (33%) and forearm (27%). Mean number of hours prior to extravasation of peripheral vasopressors requiring phentolamine administration was 21 hours. Mean number of minutes prior to phentolamine administration after extravasation was 131 minutes. Seventy-six percent of patients did not any have significant ischemic tissue injury with extravasation, and 24% of patients had only minor bruising and erythema. Two significant reactions occurred, including deep vein thrombosis and local skin necrosis. Fifty-two percent of patients required a subsequent central venous line placement. The mean length of stay was 5.4 days in the intensive care unit and 11.8 days in the hospital, and in-patient mortality was 17%. In our large cohort of patients with extravasation from peripheral vasopressors managed with local phentolamine administration, severe tissue skin or soft tissue injury was rare.

articles.title: Gender differences in acute poisoning: a 35-year cohort study.
articles.abstract: Drug overdose is an increasingly common cause of death, more commonly in males. In contrast, women present more commonly to emergency departments with overdose. We therefore aim to investigate gender differences in the characteristics and severity of acute poisoning. Adult (18-64 y) poisoning admissions to a tertiary toxicology service were reviewed (1990-2024), and females were compared to males. Data were extracted from a prospective database, including drug/toxin ingested, clinical effects, treatment, length of stay, intensive care admission and death. Primary outcomes were death, intensive care admission and intubation. There were 22,316 (75%) deliberate self-poisonings - 14,101 females (63%), 8,178 males and 37 transgender; 2,101 (7%) recreational overdoses - 695 (33%) females and 1,406 (67%) males. Females ingested more paracetamol/analgesics, antidepressants and quetiapine, while males ingested more alcohol, amphetamines and opioids. Median age for deliberate self-poisoning in females (33 years [IQR:24-44 years]) was similar to males (34 years [IQR:25-44 years]). There were 1,268 females (9.0%) admitted to intensive care, compared to 912 males (11.2%), which was significantly different (absolute difference 2.2%;95% CI:1.3-3.0%; P < 0.001). Less females were intubated than males (790 [5.6%] vs 549 [6.7%]; P = 0.001). Inpatient mortality was similar for females (32; 0.2%) and males (24; 0.3%), and no difference in length of stay. More females had hypotension, while more males developed coma and hepatotoxicity. Males were more likely to receive sedation and naloxone. Gender differences were similar for recreational poisoning, except greater mortality in males. Gender remained an independent predictor of intensive care and intubation in a multivariate logistic regression model, with males more likely to be intubated and admitted to intensive care. More males took recreational overdoses, including opioids, and females had more deliberate self-poisoning, with less toxic medications. Female deliberate self-poisoning patients were less commonly intubated and admitted to intensive care. Drug type did not account for the gender difference in outcomes. We found only minor differences between inpatient morbidity and mortality for females compared to males. Males were more likely to be admitted to intensive care and be intubated, mainly due to higher rates of coma.

articles.title: Age and intensive care unit admissions following opioid overdose.
articles.abstract: Older adults are increasingly impacted by the opioid crisis, yet age-related differences in overdose presentation, management, and outcomes leading to intensive care unit (ICU) admission remain poorly characterized. This study examined age-related variations in drug exposures, interventions provided, and hospital utilization among patients experiencing an opioid overdose. The Toxicology Investigators Consortium (ToxIC) Fentalog Study was conducted at 10 US medical centers and collected data on patients who presented to emergency departments with confirmed non-fatal opioid overdose, and available waste serum samples between 9/21/2020-4/14/2026 were included. Chart reviews captured presentations, treatments, and hospital utilization. Toxicologic analyses were performed at the Center for Forensic Science Research and Education. Nested multivariable logistic regressions assessed whether age improved predicted ICU admission, after accounting for sociodemographic characteristics and drug classes detected. Among 1930 patients, 15.3% were admitted to the ICU, 7.8% received cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and 5.8% were intubated. Length of hospital stay varied by age, with patients 65 + years old staying longest (median: 22.0h, IQR: 87.0, p < 0.001). Illicit opioids were less commonly detected in older adults (p < 0.001), while prescription opioids were more common (p < 0.001). Age cohort did not significantly predict ICU admission, although prescription benzodiazepine (AOR: 1.4, 95% CI: 1.1, 1.9) and opioid (AOR: 0.7, 95% CI: 0.5, 0.9) detection did. Older age was associated with longer hospital stays but did not predict ICU admission after adjustment for relevant covariates. Benzodiazepine and opioid exposures showed a modest association with ICU utilization. Further work should clarify how pharmacologic combinations influence clinical severity across age groups.

articles.title: Management of the Critically Ill Patient with Opioid Use Disorder.
articles.journal: Emergency medicine clinics of North America
articles.abstract: The management of critically ill patients with opioid use disorder presents a unique challenge, as overdose, withdrawal, or concomitant intoxication, due to an unregulated drug supply, leads to physiologic changes that potentially impact standard treatment. This review article outlines an emergency medicine-focused approach for early recognition and stabilization of opioid overdose or withdrawal. Topics include naloxone, use of medications for opioid use disorder, recognition of concurrent intoxication, treatment of α2-agonist withdrawal, multimodal analgesia, and sedation for opioid-tolerant patients. The acute management of opioid use disorder is an opportunity to prevent withdrawal-related decompensation, improve comfort, and support ongoing engagement in treatment.

articles.title: Profound Hyperbilirubinemia During Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning and Subsequent Multiorgan Failure: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Carbon monoxide poisoning is classically associated with neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, while severe exposure may also cause systemic toxic-hypoxic injury. Profound direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia without mechanical biliary obstruction is rarely described. We report a 55-year-old woman with alcohol use disorder, chronic tobacco use, COPD, and hepatic steatosis who presented with altered mental status and jaundice after suspected household carbon monoxide exposure. Her carboxyhemoglobin level was > 30%, and she required intubation, intensive care, vasopressor support, and three hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Initial testing showed total bilirubin of 23.1 mg/dL and direct bilirubin of 13.1 mg/dL, despite only mild AST elevation and near-normal ALT and alkaline phosphatase. Imaging showed hepatic steatosis and cholelithiasis without convincing biliary obstruction, and the documented workup for viral, autoimmune, metabolic, hemolytic, and vascular causes was unrevealing. Her liver dysfunction was considered multifactorial, with possible carbon monoxide-related toxic-hypoxic injury superimposed on underlying steatotic or alcohol-related liver vulnerability. After transient improvement, she developed coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, recurrent shock with clinical and imaging concern for acute cholecystitis, worsening hyperbilirubinemia peaking near 49-50 mg/dL, encephalopathy, respiratory failure, and multiorgan failure. Cholecystostomy yielded dark green bile without documented purulence, and aspirate cultures showed no growth; biliary sepsis was therefore not microbiologically confirmed. She died in the hospital after goals-of-care discussions. The initial bilirubin-predominant pattern was atypical for classic hypoxic hepatitis and may have reflected overlapping hepatic insults. This case emphasizes broad evaluation and cautious causal interpretation; it does not establish that carbon monoxide exposure alone caused the initial hyperbilirubinemia.

articles.title: Methiodone (IC-26) a case series: an old, but novel, opioid substance causing severe toxicity.
articles.abstract: Methiodone (IC-26; 4-ethylsulfonyl-N,N-dimethyl-4,4-diphenylbutan-2-amine) is a synthetic opioid derivative of methadone that has recently emerged on the designer drug market. Data on its clinical toxicity and pharmacokinetics remain limited. We describe four cases of severe methiodone intoxication requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission, taking place between July and November 2025. Clinical presentation, treatment, and outcomes were evaluated. In addition, systematic toxicological analysis was performed including Liquid Chromatography - High Resolution Mass Spectrometry (LC-HRMS) and targeted Liquid Chromatography - tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). All patients presented with a classical opioid toxidrome, characterized by respiratory depression, miosis, and decreased consciousness. Naloxone administration resulted in clinical improvement in all cases. Methiodone plasma concentrations ranged from 0.20 to 0.64 mg/L. The elimination half-life in plasma was estimated at approximately 13 h based on one case. Metabolite analysis revealed N-dealkylation as an important metabolic pathway, with additional hydroxylation and limited glucuronidation. Methiodone was variably detected in routine immunoassays, depending on assay specificity. No electrocardiogram (ECG) clinically relevant abnormalities were observed, in contrast to observations in methadone intoxications. Methiodone is an emerging opioid capable of causing severe, but treatable, intoxication. Increased clinical and analytical awareness is essential, as further cases are likely to emerge with the ongoing evolution of the new psychoactive substance market.

articles.title: Cardiac toxicity and dysrhythmias in acute poisoning: a ten-year cohort study.
articles.abstract: Cardiac toxicity is frequently cited as an important cause of morbidity and mortality following acute drug overdose. The true incidence of direct drug related clinically significant cardiac complications and malignant dysrhythmias in more recent toxicology practice remains poorly defined. We aim to determine the frequency, nature, and outcomes of cardiac complications in patients presenting with acute poisoning. We conducted a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained clinical toxicology database over a 10-year period. Patients with acute poisoning managed by a specialist toxicology service were included. Cardiac complications were defined as hypotension (systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg) or a primary cardiac dysrhythmia considered temporally related to the poisoning. Sinus tachycardia was excluded. Demographics, exposures, treatments, and outcomes were extracted. A total of 9,743 poisoning presentations were included. Cardiac complications occurred in 473 patients (4.9%). Hypotension occurred in 368 patients (3.8%), primary dysrhythmias in 164 patients (1.7%), and both hypotension and dysrhythmia in 59 patients (0.6%). Most dysrhythmias were isolated bradycardia (139/164, 85%), commonly associated with clonidine (40%) and beta-blocker/calcium channel blocker poisoning (35%). Only 25 patients (0.3% of all poisoning presentations) developed primary dysrhythmias: atrial dysrhythmias (3), conduction abnormalities/delays (10), ectopic rhythms (5), asystole (1) or ventricular dysrhythmias (6; 0.06%). Malignant ventricular dysrhythmias occurred in six patients and were associated with sotalol, methadone, escitalopram, dothiepin, and nortriptyline poisoning. Twenty-one deaths occurred during the study period, but no death was attributable to a primary dysrhythmia temporally related to poisoning.Discussion: In this large cohort of almost 10,000 poisoning presentations, cardiac complications occurred in approximately one in twenty patients. However, almost 95% of these were either hypotension or isolated bradycardia. Only six patients (0.06%) had ventricular dysrhythmias. Our findings support previous studies demonstrating that clinically significant ventricular dysrhythmias are uncommon among unselected populations presenting with acute poisoning. We found that only a few individual drugs, such as sotalol, methadone, tricyclic antidepressants, and escitalopram, were associated with ventricular dysrhythmias, and that such events were rare overall. Cardiac effects occur in approximately 5% of acute poisoning presentations but are predominantly hypotension or sinus bradycardia. Clinically significant ventricular and supraventricular dysrhythmias are uncommon, occurring in less than 0.3% of cases. Death directly attributable to a primary poisoning-related dysrhythmia is rare.

articles.title: Serum ammonia improves early risk stratification beyond West Haven criteria in acute liver failure.
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
authors: US Acute Liver Failure Study Group
articles.abstract: The prognosis of patients with acute liver failure (ALF) presenting with low grade hepatic encephalopathy (HE) defined by the West Haven criteria (WHC) is difficult to establish. We studied the association between HE severity, assessed by WHC and serum ammonia, with outcomes across different age groups. Retrospective analysis of the prospective multicentre United States ALF Study Group registry (2000-2016). Exposures were WHC and serum ammonia on day 1 post inclusion. Endpoints were transplant-free survival (TFS) and mortality due to cerebral events on day 21. Findings were validated in a different and more recent (2010-2023) European cohort. Among 1092 patients, median age was 39 years and 526 (48.2%) had acetaminophen toxicity. On day 1, 968 (88.6%) patients were in the intensive care unit and 669 (61.3%) were receiving any specific organ support (ventilation vasopressors, or renal replacement therapy). TFS and cerebral mortality on day 21 were 45.2% and 6.3%, respectively. Patients with hyperammonemia (≥50 µmol/L) on day 1 had lower TFS on day 21 than others, both for WHC grades 1-2 (53.0% vs. 65.2%) and 3-4 (31.8% vs. 60.9%). Higher ammonia on day 1 was independently associated with lower TFS on day 21, irrespective of WHC grade (odds ratio of 0.958 per each 10 µmol/L increment). Ammonia on day 1 of ≥100 µmol/L showed a significant threshold effect for TFS or cerebral mortality on day 21. Patients with <40 years had the highest probability of cerebral mortality on day 21. In ALF, serum ammonia may help to define HE and assess prognosis earlier, irrespective of WHC grade. Patients with early serum ammonia of ≥100 µmol/L require optimized monitoring and treatment.

articles.title: Principles of drug dosing for obese patients in the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The increasing prevalence of severe obesity in intensive care unit (ICU) patients has led to several challenges with medication dosing. Doses listed in product labels or tertiary references typically do not account for the pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic variability encountered with obesity, leading to the potential for treatment failure or an adverse effect. The purpose of this review is to provide guidance for ICU clinicians when crafting pharmacotherapy regimens in critically ill patients with extreme obesity. METHODS: A literature search was performed to identify relevant articles pertaining to the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of medications in obese patients. Articles describing both general treatment principles and medication specific assessments were retrieved. Bibliographies were searched for additional publications. RESULTS: Evidence guiding medication use in critically ill obese patients is limited by the small number of patients with more extreme forms of obesity, the lack of clinical outcome measurements, and the few studies that are specific to the ICU. Obesity-related alterations in pharmacokinetic parameters, such as apparent volume of distribution and drug clearance, may hinder attainment of pharmacodynamic targets. Individualized dosing strategies are essential to optimize therapeutic outcomes. This review provides dosing recommendations for selected ICU medications and proposes a practical framework to guide medication dosing decisions in this patient population. CONCLUSION: Drug dosing in critically ill obese patients should be individualized by assessing pharmacokinetic variability and whether pharmacodynamic goals can be achieved. Selecting the correct weight for weight-based calculations or dose for fixed regimens is paramount for achieving these goals. Consultation with a clinical pharmacist may be beneficial.

articles.title: Music Therapy During Weaning From Invasive Mechanical Ventilation in the ICU: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The study examined the effect of daily music therapy on weaning from invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in the ICU, with a primary focus on weaning duration. Secondary agitation, sedation, and analgesia doses, pain, delirium, and perceived stress after 90 days were assessed. Additionally, total IMV and ICU stay durations and tracheostomy rates were studied. Physiologic parameters were assessed in the music therapy group (MG). The study also aimed to promote the humanization of critical care through a biopsychosocial and creative music therapy approach. DESIGN: Randomized controlled trial with two parallel groups: control group receiving standard care during weaning and MG receiving music therapy additionally. SETTING AND PATIENTS: Adult critically ill patients (n = 100) admitted to a general ICU who received IMV for at least 48 hours. INTERVENTIONS: MG received daily, individualized music therapy sessions averaging 25 minutes, based on patient needs and musical preferences, which included music relaxation, music listening, and clinical improvisation. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: No significant difference in weaning duration was observed between groups (p = 0.97). Patients in the MG group showed significant improvements in agitation and sedation levels (Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale) on days 1 and 3 (p = 0.048, 0.005, and 0.024) and a lower percentage required propofol (p = 0.028). No significant difference in perceived pain (Visual Analog Pain Scale). The MG obtained lower Perceived Stress Scale-14 scores (p = 0.24). Additionally, MG significantly reduced tracheostomy rates (14%; p = 0.025). Median total IMV and ICU stay duration were shorter in the MG group, but not significantly (p = 0.206 and 0.203). Heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and oxygenation showed no significant difference before and after music therapy. CONCLUSIONS: Music therapy may serve as a nonpharmacological complementary adjunct during weaning by reducing agitation, sedation, and tracheostomy rate. It may potentially decrease perceived stress and IMV and ICU stay durations. Further research is warranted.

articles.title: Ex Vivo Assessment of Lamotrigine Clearance During Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy.
articles.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) provides renal support for unstable ICU patients but significantly alters drug concentrations. For patients on long-term antiepileptics such as lamotrigine, CRRT may increase risk for breakthrough seizures due to subtherapeutic levels. Conversely, CRRT may aid in lamotrigine overdose. While partial clearance of lamotrigine by intermittent hemodialysis has been reported, CRRT clearance is not well studied. This study determined lamotrigine extraction by CRRT in an ex vivo system. Medication was administered at two concentrations: one therapeutic and one supratherapeutic to closed-loop, blood-primed, ex vivo CRRT circuits. Drug concentrations were measured in plasma, hemofiltrate (effluent), and matching control samples at specific time points. For each time point, percent recovery of lamotrigine was calculated, and differences between CRRT circuits and controls were analyzed using two-sample t-tests. Plasma lamotrigine concentrations decreased rapidly, with 10% (n = 3, SD = 4%) and 17% (n = 2, SD = 3%) recovery at four hours for therapeutic and supratherapeutic doses, respectively. Although lower starting concentrations trended toward greater clearance, differences were not statistically significant (P = .13). Control concentrations remained stable, with approximately 100% recovery. Lamotrigine concentrations were significantly affected by CRRT circuits. Patients receiving lamotrigine who require CRRT may need dosing adjustments to maintain clinical efficacy. Additionally, CRRT effectively clears lamotrigine, suggesting potential utility in overdose management.

articles.title: Developing Models for Complicated Outcomes in Acutely Intoxicated ICU Patients With and Without Toxicity Information.
authors: and the INTOXICATE Study Investigators Group
articles.abstract: To assess the prognostic value of the mean Lethality Risk Score (LRS), reflecting the toxicity of substances involved in an exposure, and to develop prediction models for complicated outcomes in ICU patients with acute intoxication. Multicenter prospective cohort study. Seventy-eight ICUs in Europe, Australia, and the Eastern Mediterranean (2020-2023). A total of 2265 adult patients were admitted to the ICU with acute intoxication as the main reason for admission for at least 4 hours. None. The primary outcome was defined as ICU complications or death (22.5%). Clinical data were collected in an electronic capture system. We developed two prediction models: one incorporating laboratory variables ("Laboratory Model"), and one including the mean LRS ("Expo Model"). The mean LRS was calculated as the average of the individual LRS values assigned to the toxicants involved in the exposure. Key predictors were age, severity at presentation, systolic blood pressure, Glasgow Coma Scale score, and hospital type. The mean LRS remained significant only when laboratory variables were not considered. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC), calibration plots, likelihood ratio tests, and decision curve analysis. Internal validation demonstrated good performance for both models (AUROCs of 0.79 and 0.77; calibration slopes of 0.94 and 0.95; intercepts of -0.06 and -0.06), with minimal overfitting. Decision curve analysis revealed clinically relevant threshold probability ranges of 0-50% for the Laboratory Model and 0-40% for the Expo Model. The mean LRS had prognostic value only in the absence of laboratory test results. Both models may aid decision-making regarding the management of acutely intoxicated patients in the ICU.

articles.title: Harm reduction opportunities following ICU admission for prescription opioid overdose: An 8-year comparative audit at the Royal Melbourne Hospital.
articles.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) admission following prescription opioid overdose represents an important opportunity for multidisciplinary intervention and harm reduction, yet Australian data describing inpatient management are limited. A retrospective audit was conducted of 70 adults admitted to the ICU at the Royal Melbourne Hospital with prescription opioid overdose between 2021 and 2024. The primary outcome was provision of take-home naloxone (THN) before discharge among patients meeting institutional eligibility criteria. Secondary outcomes included opioid education, multidisciplinary involvement and discharge opioid management, with comparison with the previous institutional audit where comparable data were available. Only five patients (7.5%, 95% confidence interval 3.2-16.3) were supplied with THN despite all meeting institutional eligibility criteria. Polypharmacy overdose was common (77%). Most patients received at least one specialist referral (83%), although 15% received no inpatient specialist referral. Opioid education was documented in 58 patients (87%) compared with 17% previously (P <0.001), although content and documentation were inconsistent. These findings demonstrate persistent gaps in THN provision, structured opioid education and coordinated discharge planning, highlighting ICU admission as an important opportunity for prescription opioid harm reduction. Strengthening guideline-based multidisciplinary interventions during admission may improve patient outcomes and inform harm reduction strategies nationally.

articles.title: Immobilized Neuroglobin Scavenges Carbon Monoxide From Circulating Carboxyhemoglobin.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning is responsible for around 50,000 emergency department visits per year in the United States alone. Currently, there is no available antidote for CO poisoning. We have previously developed an antidotal therapy based on an engineered hemeprotein, human neuroglobin (Ngb-H64Q-CCC). Intravenous infusion of Ngb-H64Q-CCC removes CO from circulating red blood cells and improves survival in a lethal CO poisoning mouse model. However, the infusion of heme-containing proteins has inherent heme toxicity risks that may limit the dose that can be used safely without liver or kidney toxicity. To overcome these problems, we have investigated the development of immobilized Ngb in a solid matrix. This approach allows for the development of a CO removal system using an extracorporeal blood-circulating system coupled with a stationary matrix with immobilized Ngb-H64Q-CCC. Such a system avoids drug infusion and possible organ injury, allows for antidote recycling, and provides advantages for storage and handling of the antidote. Here we have developed Ngb-H64Q-CCC covalently bound to N-hydroxysuccinimide agarose. The immobilized protein shows preserved heme redox activity and retains its CO removal capacity after successive regeneration cycles. We expect that this novel approach will advance the development of new scavenger-based therapies for CO poisoning.

articles.title: Association between leukocytosis and adverse clinical outcomes in thrombocytopenic patients with acute pesticide poisoning: a cross-sectional study from a referral poisoning center in Iran.
articles.journal: International journal of environmental health research
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the association between leukocytosis and adverse clinical outcomes in patients with pesticide poisoning who also had thrombocytopenia. This cross-sectional study used medical records of patients who presented between 2016 and 2021, including 241 adult patients with confirmed pesticide poisoning. We extracted demographic data, clinical signs, laboratory parameters, and outcomes. We categorized hospitalization duration as >72 hours, 24-72 hours, and <24 hours. Leukocytosis was present in 43.2% of patients (n = 104). The overall mortality rate was 25.3% (n = 61), with 49.8% requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission (n = 120) and 44.4% requiring intubation (n = 107). Patients with elevated WBC had higher odds of prolonged hospitalization than those with normal counts: OR = 3.36, p = 0.004 for 24-72 h; and OR = 4.63, p < 0.001 for hospitalizations longer than 72 h. Leukocytosis was also strongly associated with intubation (OR = 3.50, p < 0.001) and ICU admission (OR = 3.58, p < 0.001). After adjustment, only ICU admission and leukocytosis remained significantly associated (OR = 2.20, p = 0.024). Leukocytosis may be a valuable parameter in predicting ICU admission and hospitalization duration in thrombocytopenic patients with acute pesticide poisoning. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed.

articles.title: Fulminant multi-organ failure associated with cereulide-producing Bacillus cereus after consumption of improperly stored rice.
articles.abstract: A male in his 20s with no medical history was found with generalised seizures and profound hypoglycaemia after consuming improperly stored, reheated rice.Initial laboratory tests showed acute liver failure with hyperammonaemia, acute kidney injury and lactic acidosis, which rapidly progressed to multi-organ failure requiring urgent liver transplantation evaluation.With maximal supportive therapy, including glucose, ammonia and glutamine scavengers, renal replacement therapy, haemodynamic and respiratory support, he gradually improved, avoiding transplantation and achieving full neurological recovery. Toxicological analysis of the rice and serum revealed high concentrations of cereulide, a toxin produced by Bacillus cereus This case illustrates that cereulide intoxication can be associated with potentially fatal multi-organ failure, particularly after ingestion of improperly stored starchy foods.Early recognition through targeted dietary history, focused laboratory evaluation and prompt supportive therapy are essential. Increasing awareness among healthcare professionals and safe food storage practices are key preventive measures.

articles.title: Key principles for rehabilitation of critically ill patients with obesity.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Patients with obesity who are admitted to an ICU bring specific challenges for rehabilitation during and after critical illness. This narrative review explores impact of differences in body compositions and pathophysiology on outcomes to summarise interprofessional, patient-centred rehabilitation strategies across the trajectory of recovery. METHODS: The interprofessional expert panel reviewed major trials and guidelines, integrating their clinical expertise with the current evidence. RESULTS: Three distinct phenotypes potentially influence outcomes for survivors. Whilst patients with preserved muscle mass may have a survival advantage, the phenotypes characterised by ectopic visceral fat or sarcopenia are frequently complicated by multimorbidity and polypharmacy, likely increasing the risk of adverse effects such as suboptimal sedation, prolonged ventilation and immobilisation, malnutrition, and impaired recovery. Targeted respiratory interventions, including secretion-clearance techniques and appropriate patient positioning to prevent atelectasis, reduce the work of breathing. Optimisation of communication and swallowing function is an essential component for facilitating safe oral intake and promoting active patient participation in rehabilitation. Concurrently, targeted nutrition strategies combined with early, targeted, progressive mobilisation might mitigate ICU acquired weakness and support functional recovery. The availability of appropriate weight‑based equipment is fundamental to ensuring safe mobilisation for both patients and healthcare professionals. CONCLUSION: Interprofessional collaboration is central to optimising outcomes and should extend beyond the ICU to structured post-ICU follow-up to address persistent, worsening, or newly emerging health impairments. Early rehabilitation in critically ill patients with obesity should integrate physiological, logistical, and psychosocial considerations to support equitable and functional recovery.
articles.ai_summary: This study reviewed rehabilitation strategies for critically ill patients with obesity, identifying three distinct phenotypes that influence outcomes. Targeted interventions, including respiratory, nutrition, and mobilization strategies, can mitigate complications and support functional recovery.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings highlight the importance of interprofessional collaboration and early rehabilitation in critically ill patients with obesity, emphasizing the need to address physiological, logistical, and psychosocial considerations to support equitable and functional recovery.

articles.title: Decades of intensive care medicine trials: what randomised evidence has changed, corrected, and still questions to resolve.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) have reshaped intensive care medicine (ICM), a discipline defined by acute, interacting organ failures, time-sensitive decisions, biological uncertainty, and heterogeneous recovery trajectories. Many interventions supported by strong physiological rationale failed to improve patient-centred outcomes, whereas durable advances often emerged from optimisation of supportive care, avoidance of iatrogenic harm, and reassessment of established practices. METHODS: We conducted an interpretive historical review of landmark multicentre RCTs in adult ICM from the early 1990s onwards. PubMed searches, reference lists from major trials and reviews, and international guidelines were used to identify trials with conceptual influence on practice, guidelines, physiological reasoning, therapeutic strategy, research priorities, de-implementation, or outcome framing. Evidence was organised into overlapping paradigms rather than rigid chronological periods. FINDINGS: Across haemodynamic support, mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy, antimicrobial treatment, nutrition, glucose control, transfusion, and sedation, landmark RCTs describe more than therapeutic expansion. Early biological and haemodynamic trials exposed the limits of reductionist strategies in syndromic critical illness. Protocol-driven approaches improved timeliness and consistency, but later pragmatic trials showed that rigid targets and invasive algorithms often added little once high-quality usual care was established. More recent trials challenge the assumption that greater intervention intensity improves outcomes, emphasising timing, disease phase, baseline risk, heterogeneity, patient selection, and treatment-related harm. Modern ICM RCTs have clarified not only what works, but what can be reduced, delayed, avoided, or applied selectively. Future progress requires biologically informed, context-sensitive trials focussed on meaningful survival, recovery, and long-term function.

articles.title: Antiseizure medication dosing and monitoring in the intensive care unit: a practical narrative review.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Antiseizure medications (ASMs) are commonly used in the intensive care unit (ICU) and often exhibit pharmacokinetics that differ substantially from those in healthy volunteers or in the outpatient setting. Organ dysfunction, polypharmacy, exogenous devices, and greater severity of illness all influence ASM pharmacokinetics, dosing decisions, and monitoring parameters. It is essential for critical care clinicians to familiarize themselves with the pharmacokinetics, dosing considerations, effects of exogenous devices, and therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM)-all covered in this narrative review-to incorporate in their approach to ASMs in the critical care setting. METHODS: We identified relevant literature from MEDLINE from inception to March 2026 related to ASMs in the ICU. Data on pharmacokinetics, dosing in the ICU, the effect of renal replacement therapy, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), and plasmapheresis (PLEX) on ASM exposure, and the role of TDM in the ICU were collected and summarized. RESULTS: Considerations for 15 ASMs (brivaracetam, cannabidiol, carbamazepine, cenobamate, clobazam, lacosamide, lamotrigine, levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine, perampanel, phenobarbital, phenytoin, topiramate, valproate, and zonisamide) were included in the review. Dosing considerations for TDM, including indications and target reference ranges, and specific settings such as organ dysfunction, illness severity, renal replacement therapy, ECMO, and PLEX are discussed. CONCLUSION: The use of ASMs in the ICU require a distinct approach from outpatient settings. Severity of illness, organ dysfunction and replacement devices, and frequent drug-drug interactions warrant tailored agent selection, dosing, and monitoring.

articles.title: Ethylene Glycol Poisoning Without Fomepizole in a Regional Australian Intensive Care Unit: The Lactate Gap as the Diagnostic Key and the Consequences of Nasogastric Ethanol Therapy.
articles.abstract: A 62-year-old man presented comatose with pH 6.88 and no ingestion history. A point-of-care lactate above 31 mmol/L with a laboratory lactate of 0.8 mmol/L revealed a lactate gap, diagnosing ethylene glycol poisoning despite a near-normal osmolar gap. High-dose continuous renal replacement therapy corrected the acidosis; he survived.

articles.title: Integrated Use of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation and Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System for Refractory Cardiotoxic Ingestion: A Single-Center Case Series.
articles.abstract: Cardiotoxic ingestions of calcium-channel blockers and beta-adrenergic antagonists are highly lethal, often causing refractory vasoplegic shock and noncardiogenic pulmonary edema. While venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a recognized rescue therapy for cardiogenic shock, the roles of venovenous ECMO and albumin dialysis-specifically the molecular adsorbent recirculating system (MARS)-as well as the effectiveness of linking patients to therapy through a coordinated referral process remain underexplored. We describe five consecutive patients with severe cardiotoxic ingestions managed via a regionally triggered transfer pathway. Patients presented with profound hypotension and respiratory failure despite standard therapies. All five patients received MARS for drug clearance and vasoplegia management; two required venovenous ECMO for refractory hypoxemia. One patient died due to profound myocardial poisoning; four survived to discharge. Complications included continuous renal replacement therapy filter clotting and catheter-associated thrombosis. A coordinated regional protocol enabling early access to ECMO and MARS is feasible in massive cardiotoxic ingestions.

articles.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound Detection of Acute Myocardial Dysfunction Following Bupropion Overdose: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Bupropion overdose is associated with significant morbidity and mortality due to severe neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, including seizures and life-threatening arrhythmias. Early recognition of electrocardiographic, clinical, and echocardiographic abnormalities is critical for prompt intervention and prevention of clinical deterioration. We present a case of a 21-year-old female who presented to the emergency department following an intentional polysubstance overdose involving suspected bupropion ingestion. The initial electrocardiogram (EKG) demonstrated sinus tachycardia. However, during continued monitoring, the patient developed QRS widening and seizures. Treatment included benzodiazepines, calcium, and sodium bicarbonate. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) revealed a reduced ejection fraction (EF) of less than 30%, which was later confirmed on formal transthoracic echocardiography. These findings prompted escalation of care, intubation for airway protection and deep sedation, and transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU). During admission, she developed torsades de pointes (TdP), resulting in cardiac arrest. Despite her critical presentation, repeat echocardiography upon resolution of overdose toxicity demonstrated recovery of left ventricular systolic function, with improvement of EF to 50-55% during hospitalization. This case demonstrates the potential role of POCUS in the early recognition of myocardial dysfunction associated with bupropion toxicity. Together with serial EKG monitoring, these findings identified a patient at high risk for clinical deterioration and supported early escalation of care.

articles.title: Role of the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) Score in Predicting Outcomes in Paraquat Poisoning.
articles.abstract: Background and aims Paraquat poisoning is associated with high mortality and progressive multiorgan dysfunction. Early prognostic assessment remains difficult where toxin-specific assays are unavailable. This study evaluated the role of the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score in predicting mortality in patients with paraquat poisoning. Patients and methods This prospective observational study included 80 patients with confirmed paraquat poisoning who were admitted to a tertiary care hospital. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data; organ dysfunction; organ support; estimated ingested dose; and APACHE II scores within the first 24 hours of ICU admission were recorded. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with mortality, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed the discriminatory ability of APACHE II. Results Of 80 patients, 27 (33.8%) survived and 53 (66.2%) died. Renal dysfunction was the most frequent organ abnormality (75.0%), followed by respiratory (63.8%) and hepatic dysfunction (62.5%). Mortality increased with estimated ingested dose, from 21.1% for <20 mL to 62.5% for 20-50 mL and 91.4% for >50 mL (p < 0.001). PaO2 was significantly lower among non-survivors than survivors (median 86 vs. 88 mmHg, p = 0.034). Median APACHE II scores were 15 in survivors and 16 in non-survivors (p = 0.205). APACHE II was not significantly associated with mortality on univariable analysis (OR 1.11, 95% CI 0.99-1.24; p = 0.080), and ROC analysis showed poor discrimination (AUC 0.587, 95% CI 0.461-0.712). In a sensitivity analysis excluding four patients with unknown or difficult-to-interpret dose estimates, recorded estimated dose showed greater discriminatory performance than APACHE II. Conclusion APACHE II demonstrated poor discrimination for in-hospital mortality in this cohort of patients with paraquat poisoning (AUC 0.587, 95% CI 0.461-0.712) and was not significantly associated with mortality on univariable analysis. Mortality increased with estimated paraquat dose, while lower PaO2 was associated with mortality on univariable analysis. In the sensitivity analysis, recorded estimated dose showed greater discriminatory performance than APACHE II in the restricted patient subset. These findings indicate that APACHE II had limited discriminatory ability in the present cohort and should not be used as a stand-alone predictor of mortality. As paraquat poisoning may involve progressive organ dysfunction, a single APACHE II assessment within the first 24 hours may not fully reflect the subsequent clinical course. Future studies should evaluate whether serial APACHE II assessments provide additional prognostic information beyond the initial score. Larger prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate clinically useful prognostic models.

articles.title: Comparison of two automated pupillometry indices in patients with acute brain injury: the prospective multicentre LYNX cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Automated pupillometry quantifies the pupillary light reflex in acute brain injury. The neurological pupil index (NPi) is the established composite index and carries prognostic value. A second index from a different device, the quantitative pupil index (QPi), has recently become available, but whether it conveys equivalent information in non-anoxic acute brain injury is unknown. METHODS: LYNX was a prospective cohort study in three European intensive care units (September 2022-July 2024). Consecutive adults with traumatic brain injury, subarachnoid or intracerebral haemorrhage, or ischaemic stroke ventilated for more than 12 h were enrolled and followed for 6 months. Paired NPi (NPi-300) and QPi (NeuroLight) measurements were obtained at least every 6 h to day 7. Ancillary cohorts of healthy volunteers (dark vs. bright light) and surgical patients (before and after sufentanil and propofol) were also studied. The primary outcome was the correlation between the two indices; secondary outcomes were their association with intracranial hypertension and unfavourable 6-month outcome (Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended ≤ 4). Values below 3 were considered abnormal, with QPi thresholds of 2 and 4 as sensitivity analyses; multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, admission Glasgow Coma Scale score and focal deficit. RESULTS: Among 108 patients (median age 57 years [IQR 44-67], 60.2% male), 7089 paired measurements were obtained. The two indices were moderately to strongly correlated (r = 0.717, 95% CI 0.705-0.730). Each 10-percentage-point increase in abnormal values independently predicted unfavourable outcome (NPi: OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.09-2.04, p = 0.013; QPi: OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.31-2.37, p < 0.001). QPi was associated with intracranial hypertension (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.04-1.82, p = 0.025), whereas NPi was not. Ambient lighting and contralateral eye opening had no meaningful effect in 75 volunteers. In 20 sedated non-brain-injured patients, propofol reduced QPi to a median of 1 (IQR 1-3) and NPi to 4.0 (IQR 3.6-4.3). CONCLUSIONS: NPi and QPi were correlated and both predicted 6-month outcome, but QPi was far more sensitive to anaesthetics, which probably confounds its association with intracranial hypertension. The indices are not interchangeable in sedated critically ill patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05567978. Registered 5 October 2022.

articles.title: Suicide attempt methods among patients referred for psychiatric evaluation at an advanced emergency and critical care medical center in Japan: associations with sex, age, and psychiatric diagnosis: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Suicide attempts requiring emergency care provide a critical opportunity for psychiatric assessment and prevention. However, contemporary evidence from advanced emergency settings remains limited, particularly regarding how suicide attempt methods vary according to sex, age, and psychiatric diagnosis. This single-center retrospective study included 344 patients who were transported to an advanced emergency and critical care medical center after suicide attempts and were subsequently referred for psychiatric evaluation between April 2014 and March 2024. Psychiatric diagnoses and suicide attempt methods were classified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision-based categories. The primary analyses examined sex-, age-, and diagnosis-specific patterns of suicide attempt methods. Secondary analyses compared high- and low-lethality attempts. Drug overdose was the most common method and was more frequent among female patients. Substance use disorders were more frequent among male patients. Age-specific analyses showed that drug overdose was more frequent among patients aged < 20 years, whereas pesticide poisoning was more frequent among patients aged ≥ 65 years. Diagnosis-specific analyses showed that jumping from height was more frequent among patients with schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders. In secondary analyses, patients in the high-lethality group were older, although high- and low-lethality attempts were observed across diagnostic categories. Suicide attempt methods among patients referred for psychiatric evaluation after emergency transport varied according to sex, age, and psychiatric diagnosis. These findings support post-attempt assessment in general hospital settings that integrates demographic and diagnostic context, the observed suicide attempt method, and medical severity rather than relying solely on categorized lethality.

articles.title: Hemodynamic Effects of Interfacility Dexmedetomidine Infusions During Transport of Patients with Alpha-2-adrenergic Agonist Withdrawal.
articles.journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: In the Philadelphia region, there has been an increase in the potency of illicit opioids as well as the addition of nonopioid adulterants. Currently, medetomidine, a veterinary anesthetic that acts as an alpha-2-adrenergic agonist, is a common adulterant in the illicit opioid supply, causing both unique overdose and withdrawal syndromes. Although opioid withdrawal alone is not deadly, with added adulterants, especially medetomidine, this is no longer the case. Dexmedetomidine is an alpha-2-adrenergic agonist frequently used for sedation in the emergency department and intensive care unit. Dexmedetomidine is also used off-label to treat the life-threatening withdrawal from alpha-2-agonists. This study describes the dosing and hemodynamic effects associated with the interfacility administration of dexmedetomidine in patients with alpha-2 adrenergic agonist withdrawal. Secondarily, we describe the safety of dexmedetomidine in this patient population. We conducted a retrospective case review of patients receiving dexmedetomidine infusions in the interfacility setting for presumed alpha-2-adrenergic agonist withdrawal. Demographic data, dosing, and vital signs were analyzed descriptively. Over a six-month period, of 217 cases identified, 182 contained complete hemodynamic data. The average age was 39.5 years, and 67% were male. The average transport time was 15.7 minutes (range, 5-40 minutes). The mean dexmedetomidine infusion rate was 1.32 (0.31) mcg/kg/hr. The average mean arterial pressure decreased from 122.1 mm Hg (21.7) at the time of initial patient contact to 118.3 mm Hg (21.7) (mean difference, 3.80; 95% CI, 1.96-5.64) at final patient interaction. Heart rate also showed a minimal change from 104.9 (23.7) to 103.6 (21.8) beats/min (mean 1.3; 95% CI, -0.48 to 3.08). No cases of severe hypotension or clinically significant bradycardia requiring intervention were documented (one-sided 95% CI, 0-1.7%). In this case series of patients, prehospital dexmedetomidine infusions to treat alpha-2-agonist withdrawal were associated with stable hemodynamics without significant bradycardia or hypotension. These findings support the safety of dexmedetomidine infusions for interfacility transport and provide a rationale for examining whether advanced life support clinicians can safely transport patients receiving dexmedetomidine infusions for this indication.

articles.title: Impact of Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System Therapy on Piperacillin Concentration in Critically Ill Patients: An Observational Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To assess the impact of Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System (MARS) therapy on total plasma piperacillin concentrations in critically ill patients with acute liver failure or acute-on-chronic liver failure.
